## 382. D391 · the Chinese sentence's category is now READ from the signals the extractor resolved (`nlu/understand`, §7.1 / §8 / §141)

**The gap D381 left.** D381 fixed the hard-filter defect: `occasion=date` no longer became a JSONB
containment clause that deleted every row. But the sentence still extracted `category=null`, and a
sentence with no category is a sentence the search cannot answer: §141 wanted the Chinese phrasing to
return cards, and a null category is why it could not.

**The fix.** `_infer_category_from_signals` reads the category from the signals the extractor DID
resolve, and it runs twice: once in `_fill_category` (for the signals the category pass itself
produces) and once after `_fill_preferences` (for the preference signals). The maps are data, not
logic: `_OCCASION_CATEGORY_MAP` (date/group/family/business/solo), `_PREFERENCE_CATEGORY_MAP` keyed by
the `(key, value)` pairs `PREFERENCE_RULES` actually emits, and `_CUISINE_CATEGORY_MAP` for a named
cuisine.

**The confidence discipline (§8).** An inferred category is never as certain as a named one: the
direct hit is 0.95, the inference is capped at 0.75, and the inference only fires when the score
reaches 0.5. A negative preference (`polarity=-1`) contributes -0.5, so a dislike can never name a
place the user did not ask for. A category the query actually names is never overridden.

**Measured, on the sentence that started this (18 cases in `tests/test_category_inference.py`):**
`帮我找一个适合情侣约会的地方` -> `restaurant` (0.5) instead of null;
`想找个适合独自用餐的咖啡厅` ->
`cafe`; `想找个通定营业的地方` -> `bar`; `想找个热震的地方` -> `bar`;
`想找个户外的地方` -> `attraction`; `想找个有停车位的地方` ->
`mall`/`restaurant`; `下雨天想找个室内的地方` -> `restaurant`/`cafe`/`mall`.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_category_inference.py` -> **18 passed**; full `apps/ai`
suite -> **686 passed, 4 skipped** (live-DB tests skip; the Docker engine is down on this machine).

**Discipline note.** The first implementation of this unit put the preference-key lookup in a long
`elif` chain that tested `key == "mtr_near"` where the extractor emits `key == "access",
value == "mtr_near"`, so four of the access preferences never matched; the map is now keyed by the
pair the lexicon emits and the lookup is one dict access. One test premise was also wrong and was
corrected rather than the code: "嗯" is not a discovery turn, so its `unknowns` list names the intent
alone and not a category.

## 383. D392 · the card names the preference that matched, not merely that one did (`search/cards`, §18 / §99)

**The gap D381-D383 left.** The pipeline could rank a merchant higher because of a preference
(occasion=date, ambience=quiet, near the MTR), and the card's reason bullet said only
"配合你的偏好" / "matches your preferences". A bullet that says something happened without saying what is
not checkable against the user's own stated preference, which is the whole point of §18: every
bullet carries a fact id, and this one carried a fact id for a claim nobody could verify.

**The fix.** The search pipeline now records WHICH preference fired for which subject
(`preference_labels` on the candidate's raw), the label is a per-locale name in the user's own words
(`_PREFERENCE_LABEL_COPY` for a boolean preference, `_PREFERENCE_VALUE_LABEL_COPY` for an enum-valued
one, where the value is what the user asked for: "安静" not "气氛"), and the bullet reads
"配合你的偏好：安静" / "matches your preference: quiet".

**The honesty rule.** A preference that scored BELOW neutral (a penalty) names nothing: the card must
not claim a preference match for a merchant the user does not want. A preference the pipeline could not
name falls back to the generic claim rather than inventing a name. Duplicate names are collapsed.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_preference_reason.py` -> **7 passed**; full `apps/ai`
suite -> **693 passed, 4 skipped** (live-DB tests skip; the Docker engine is down on this machine).

**Discipline note.** The first implementation passed the whole JSONB preference value to the label
helper, so an enum-valued preference was named by its container rather than by its content ("气氛" where
"安静" was what the user asked for); the helper now reads the inner value. A second slip was a variable
name: the reason builder's locale parameter is `locale`, not `lang`, and the copy table is indexed by
`locale` — the first draft used the other spelling and raised `NameError` on every card.

## 384. D393 Â· a negated preference is a DISLIKE, not a like (`nlu/polarity`, Â§7.1 / Â§8)

**The gap D381-D392 left.** The lexicon's `PREFERENCE_RULES` carry a fixed polarity of +1 for every
rule, so "å´å¥½å®é" (not quiet) and "å®é" (quiet) extracted the SAME
preference with the SAME sign. The ranking lane could then boost exactly the merchant the user had
asked it to demote, which is the difference between "the page says the wrong thing" and "the page
says the opposite of what the user asked".

**The fix.** A new module `nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py` decides the sign from the SENTENCE, and
`_fill_preferences` calls it after the lexicon pass. The rule is deliberately narrow: a negation cue
must GOVERN the token. A cue immediately before the token (modulo short filler: "å´å¥½çå®é") governs that token
alone; a cue elsewhere in the sentence governs the turn, EXCEPT when other words separate it from
the token by more than a filler, in which case the two belong to different clauses and the token
keeps its positive polarity. A sentence carrying two preferences and one negation is therefore not
silently turned into a dislike of both.

**The token, not the canonical value.** The lexicon's canonical value ("quiet") is not in a Chinese
sentence; the surface token that matched it ("å®é") is. So the extractor remembers which token
matched each rule and the polarity is decided against THAT token.

**The effect, measured end to end.** "å´å¥½å®éçåº" now extracts `ambience=quiet` with
`polarity=-1`; the category inference reads the sign and contributes -0.5, so no category is
inferred from a dislike; and the pipeline ranks the LOUD merchant above the quiet one (the two
merchants' scores separate where they were tied before).

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_preference_polarity.py` -> **12 passed**;
`pytest tests/test_polarity_effect.py` -> **2 passed**; full `apps/ai` suite -> **709 passed, 4
skipped** (live-DB tests skip; the Docker engine is down on this machine).

**Discipline note.** The first version of the polarity rule negated a preference whenever a cue
appeared ANYWHERE in the sentence, which made "å´å¥½è¾£ æ³æ¾åå®éçåå¡ååº" dislike the ambience as well as
the spice. The rule now distinguishes the two clauses, and the test that pins that distinction is
`test_a_cue_far_from_the_token_does_not_negate_it`.

## 385. D394 · the cuisine the user names and the cuisine the seed writes are two vocabularies (`nlu/lexicon`, §7.1 / §99)

**The gap D384 left.** The NLU says "japanese"; the seeded taxonomy writes the leaves
"sushi", "ramen" and "izakaya". The matcher compared the two by SUBSTRING, so a cuisine preference
that WAS satisfied by the merchant never fired â "japanese" is not a substring of "sushi" â and
"dim_sum" (the NLU's spelling) is not a substring of "dimsum" (the seed's). A satisfied preference
and an unsatisfied one produced the same score, which is the same failure D381 found in a
different shape: a signal that cannot fire is not a signal.

**The fix.** `nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py` owns the vocabulary now: `CUISINE_LEAVES` maps a named cuisine to
the leaves that satisfy it, `cuisine_leaves` resolves a name (an unknown cuisine falls back to
matching by its own name, which is right â a cuisine the taxonomy does not know is still a word a
merchant may carry), and `cuisine_matches` compares the two sides by LEAF, normalized for case and
for the `_`/`-`/space separators, rather than by substring. Both the stored preference and the typed
one go through it.

**A weight inconsistency, fixed on the way.** The stored-cuisine matcher was returning a hard 1.0
for a match while every other matcher returns the preference's own weight, so a preference the user
holds at 0.9 was scoring as a certainty. The cuisine matcher now uses the weight like the rest
("w" on a match, "1 - w" on a disliked cuisine, "0.5" for a cuisine that is simply absent).

**Measured.** "japanese" now matches the sushi, ramen and izakaya leaves; "dim_sum" matches
"dimsum"; "seafood" matches the "seafood-grill" leaf and the "Seafood & BBQ" category; "thai"
matches neither a sushi nor a ramen merchant, and a merchant with no such cuisine scores the neutral
0.5 rather than a match.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_cuisine_vocabulary.py` -> **5 passed**; full `apps/ai`
suite -> **714 passed, 4 skipped** (live-DB tests skip; the Docker engine is down on this machine).

**Discipline note.** The first version of the vocabulary test asserted the exact score (0.9) for a
match, and the matcher returned 1.0 â because it ignored the weight. The test premise was right and
the code was wrong: a preference the user holds at 0.9 must not score as a certainty. The matcher
now uses the weight, and the test pins the number rather than a threshold.

## 386. D395 · the "X-style" form is how a HK user asks for a cuisine (`nlu/lexicon`, §7.1 / §111)

**The gap the live plane found.** With the Docker engine back up, the end-to-end probe against the
seeded `nexus` database (470 published merchants, 202 under `restaurant`) showed the Chinese
sentence answering with **5 items** where D381 left it at **0** â the fix holds on the live plane. The same
probe then found a second hole: "æ³é£æ¥åðfè" ("I want Japanese-style food") resolved to
`category=None` with **no preferences at all**, so the page answered with the search's first five
merchants rather than the Japanese ones the user asked for.

**Why.** Only two of the eleven `CUISINE_TERMS` rows carried the "X-style" form (日式, 泰式, 韓式)
â the rows had 日料, 日本菜, 豝菜 but not 日式, and "日式菜" is how a Hong Kong user actually asks
for Japanese food. A vocabulary row is a promise about what the users will type, and this one had
promised less than it delivered.

**The fix.** `_CUISINE_STYLE_FORMS` names the style form for each cuisine, and the forms are
APPENDED to the rows themselves, so the rows stay the single source of truth: a form that is not
IN the row is a form the matcher cannot see, and the test pins that.

**Measured.** 日式 / 日式菜 -> japanese; 泰式 / 泰式菜 -> thai; 中式 -> cantonese; 西式 ->
western; 意式 -> italian; 馬来西菜 -> malaysian; 素菜 -> vegetarian. On the live database
"我想食日式菜" now extracts `category=restaurant` (0.92) with `cuisine=japanese`.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_cuisine_style_forms.py` -> **14 passed**; full `apps/ai`
suite -> **728 passed, 4 skipped**; the live-DB integration tests -> **4 passed** with
`NEXUS_TEST_DATABASE_URL` pointed at the seeded `nexus` database.

**Discipline note.** The first probe of this unit was read off the console, and the console's
GBK encoding made every Chinese term unreadable â one probe used the wrong codepoint for 泰 and
appeared to show that the Thai row was missing its own style form. The probe was rewritten to
print codepoints, which showed the row was fine and the probe was wrong. A measurement read
through a lossy display is not a measurement.

## 387. D396 · a preference TYPED in this query and one the user DECLARED earlier are different claims, and the card says which (`search/cards` + `search/service`, §18 / §32-33 / §99)

**The gap D392 left.** The card named the preference that fired, but not WHERE it came from. The
`user_preferences.source` column already carries the answer (`declared` = the user told us,
`inferred` = the platform's reading of their behaviour, `transaction` = something they did), and
a preference typed in THIS query is neither: it is a request, not a standing preference. The card
said the same words for both, which is a claim the user could not check: "matches your preference"
and "matches what you just asked for" are different promises.

**The fix.** The label travels with its source: `preference_labels` entries are now
`{label, source}`, the stored path takes the source from the row and the transient path marks it
`typed`, and the card picks its copy by source â `preference_named` ("配合你的偏好：安靜" /
"matches your preference: quiet") for a standing preference, `preference_typed` ("符合你這次的要求：安靜" /
"matches what you asked for: quiet") for this turn. When both fired, the bullet names both.

**The honesty rule.** A label that carries no source is not a claim about anything, so the generic
copy is the honest answer rather than an invented one â a legacy string label still reads as
"matches your preferences", not as a typed preference.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_preference_source.py` -> **8 passed**; full `apps/ai`
suite -> **736 passed, 4 skipped** (live-DB tests skip; the Docker engine is up but the gate run
holds the database).

## 388. D396 · a favourite could point at an offering the consumer cannot open (`data/seed/generate.py`, D58 / §35)

**What the fresh gate found.** The 18-step gate ran to step 5 on the live plane and filed 216
assertions with **1 red**: "favourites point at a renderable row". The seeded `nexus` database was
clean â the same query over it returned 0 bad rows â because that database was seeded
from an earlier RNG stream. The gate's own fresh seed was not clean.

**The cause.** The generator sampled the four saved OFFERINGS from *every* offering:
`self.rng.sample(self.offerings, k=4)`. The seeded catalogue holds 5,170 active offerings and 376
that are `draft` or `out_of_stock`, so the sample could bookmark a row the consumer screen hides.
Only an `active` offering is renderable, and the check asserts exactly that. The merchant branch
one line above already did it right (`if m["status"] == "published"]`); the offering branch did not.

**Why it had not been seen.** The sample only fails when one of the four draws lands on a
non-active offering, and the probability of all four being active is (5170/5546)^4 â 75%, so the
check failed on roughly one run in four. It passed the earlier runs by luck of the RNG stream, and
D383's attribute work shifted that stream enough for the latent defect to surface. A check that
passes three times out of four is not a passing check.

**The fix.** The offering branch now samples from the active offerings only, so the seed cannot
ship a bookmark whose click is a 404 â which is the same §35/D35 failure in the opposite
direction, as the check's own comment says.

**Verified, not claimed.** `python data/seed/generate.py --counts ci` -> RESULT: PASS (FK integrity,
bounds, naming, density, language mix); the 18-step gate re-run is in flight and its verdict is
the next entry.

---

## 389. D397 · the better evidence wins: a declared preference is not diluted by a weak history (`search/service`, §6 / §32-33 / §99)

**The gap D382-D396 left.** The preference signal and the feedback signal answer the SAME
question ("does this fit this user") from two different kinds of evidence: one is what the user
SAID, the other is what they DID. The pipeline averaged them, and the average let a weak click
history pull a preference the user DECLARED at 0.95 down to 0.675. That is the platform saying
"you told us you want quiet, but we think you do not" — a claim it has no standing to make, and
one the `source` column exists to prevent: `declared` is the user telling us, `inferred` is the
platform's reading of their behaviour, `transaction` is something they did.

**Measured, before the change.** preference alone (0.95) -> 0.95; preference + 3 weak clicks
(0.4) -> **0.675**; preference + 3 strong clicks (0.9) -> 0.925; 3 weak clicks alone -> 0.4;
nothing -> none.

**The fix.** The two signals combine by MAXIMUM, not by average. Both are on the same 0..1
scale ("how well this fits this user"), and the best evidence about a question is the strongest
answer to it: a declared 0.95 beats a 0.4 history, and a 0.9 history still beats a preference the
user holds at 0.5. A history below `min_signals` is not evidence at all and stays absent.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_preference_evidence.py` -> **6 passed**; full
`apps/ai` suite -> **742 passed, 4 skipped**.

---

## 391. D398 · the live-DB proof of the Chinese-sentence chain became a gate, and the CI job that runs it (`apps/ai/tests/test_live_preferences.py` + `.github/workflows/ci.yml`)

**The gap D381-D397 left.** Every defect in that chain was verified offline and by probe, and a
probe is a file nobody runs. D381's fix — a soft preference rendered as a hard filter — was the
kind of defect that passes on an empty database: with no rows, the query returns nothing, which is
what the defect does too. The live suite skipped every seed-dependent case.

**What the tests now prove, on the live plane (6 cases, all passing against the seeded `nexus`):**

- the Chinese date sentence answers with **cards** (it answered with 0 before D381);
- it resolves a **category** (`restaurant`, inferred at 0.5, below the 0.95 a named category gets);
- it **keeps the preference soft** (the preference survives, and the attribute filter does not);
- the "X-style" cuisine sentence resolves a cuisine (`japanese`) and a category;
- the quiet sentence resolves the cafe category;
- the category the NLU infers is the category the **taxonomy holds** (202 merchants under
  `restaurant`, 84 under `cafe`, 45 under `bar` on the seeded plane).

**The CI job had to grow a step.** The AI job provisioned the SCHEMA and the role split but never
seeded, so every seed-dependent case skipped — the tests were green precisely where they could
not fail. The job now generates and loads the demo seed before the suite, and **asserts** that the
seed published at least one merchant: a seed that loaded nothing would leave the live suite
skipping its own regressions while the job stayed green.

**Verified, not claimed.** The step was run exactly as CI runs it, against a throwaway database
(`nexus_ci_seed_check`): schema applied from `infra/db/migrations/*.sql`, `generate.py --counts ci`
-> PASS, the 23 seed files applied in FK order -> **112 published merchants**, the guard -> PASS, and
`tests/test_live_preferences.py` against that database -> **6 passed**. The log is the evidence.

**Discipline note.** The first run of the step failed with `relation "_seed_tenants" does not
exist`, and the cause was not the CI step but the SEED's staging tables: each seed file stages its
rows in a `TEMP TABLE ... ON COMMIT DROP`, so a psql that autocommits between statements drops the
staging table before the INSERT that reads it. `data/seed/load.sh` has always passed
`--single-transaction` for exactly this reason; the CI step now does too, and says why in a comment.

## 392. D398 · a verification script that changed the shared database's roles, and what it cost (`verify_ci_seed_step.sh`)

**What happened.** The D398 verification script applied `infra/postgres/init/00_roles.sql` to a
throwaway database to prove the CI seed step. The ROLES are cluster-wide, not per-database, so that
file's `ALTER ROLE nexus_ai WITH LOGIN PASSWORD %L` reset the password the LOCAL `nexus` database's
AI role was using. The next live run failed with
`password authentication failed for user "nexus_ai"` on every test that touched the database — nine
of them — while the offline suite stayed green, which is the honest shape of the failure: the local
plane's database access was broken, and only the live tests said so.

**The repair.** The role passwords were restored from `.env`
(`nexus_ai` -> `nexus_dev_ai_only`, `nexus_app` -> `nexus_dev_app_only`) and the live suite went
back to **752 passed**. The script now passes the LOCAL passwords, which makes the cluster-wide
`ALTER ROLE` a no-op, and says why in its header: in CI the cluster is disposable, so the step is
safe there; on a shared machine it is not.

**The lesson, stated so it is usable.** A verification script that touches a shared server is a
change to that server. `00_roles.sql` is safe in CI because CI's Postgres is disposable and it is
NOT safe on a machine that holds a database other people use — and the file does not say so, because
from where it was written every cluster was disposable. The script now states the hazard rather
than rediscovering it, and the CI step it mirrors is unchanged (CI's cluster IS disposable, and the
step's own `ci_nexus_ai` password is the point of it).

**Verified, not claimed.** The repaired script was re-run end to end against a throwaway database:
schema -> `generate.py --counts ci` PASS -> 23 seed files applied -> **112 published merchants** ->
the guard PASS -> `tests/test_live_preferences.py` -> **6 passed**; and the seeded `nexus` database
was re-checked afterwards with the live suite -> **752 passed**.

---

## 393. D399 · the product's own e2e sentence crashed the search with a 500 (`search/service` + `search/sql`, §7.1 / §8)

**What the product's own acceptance test says.** The vertical slice's headline test asks
"帮我找沙田适合情侣约会的餐厅，预算500港币，安静一点，周六晚上" and expects ranked cards with
verifiable explanations, results actually near Sha Tin, and every slot the sentence filled
resolved. Run against the live plane, that sentence returned:

```
asyncpg.exceptions.DataError: invalid input for query argument $7: '18:00:00'
  ('str' object has no attribute 'hour')
```

**The cause.** The sentence's clock time ("周六晚上") produced an open-at-time filter, and the
value was carried as the STRING "18:00:00" and bound to a `time` COLUMN. asyncpg encodes a
`time` parameter from a `datetime.time`, so the bind raised before the query ever ran — a 500 on
the product's headline sentence, and one no offline test could see, because the offline path
never reaches a driver. The filter was correct; the VALUE'S TYPE was not.

**The fix.** The plan carries a `datetime.time` (`plan.at.astimezone(HK_TZ).time()`) and the query
binds it as one. The filter's SQL is unchanged.

**Measured, on the live plane, after the fix.** The same sentence now answers with **8 cards**,
every one carrying a distance (410m from Sha Tin) and the reasons `near_you`, `top_rated`,
`within_budget`, `preference_match`; the intent resolves `category=restaurant` (0.7),
`location=Sha Tin` (resolved, 22.3809/114.1861), `budget.max=500 HKD`,
`time=range` (Sat 2026-10-24, 18:00–15:00, quality `night`), the preferences `ambience=quiet` and
`occasion=date`, and `unknowns: []` — every slot the sentence filled, resolved.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_open_time_binding.py` -> **5 passed** (the plan
carries a `time`, the query binds a `time`, and the open-at-time clause is still there);
`pytest tests/test_live_preferences.py` against the seeded `nexus` -> **8 passed**, including the
product's own sentence; full `apps/ai` suite -> **759 passed** with the database and **747
passed / 12 skipped** without it.

**Discipline note.** The offline test that pins the plan carries a `time`, and the live test pins
the sentence's five slots and its eight answers. The first draft of the offline test read
`extract_intent(...)` and handed the rule engine's own shape to `plan_from_intent`, which reads
the contract shape — the premise was wrong, not the code, and the test was corrected to go through
`validate_intent(extract_intent_dict(...))` the way the pipeline does.

## 394. D400 · the product's own non-negotiable rules, checked on the live plane (`apps/ai/tests/test_live_ai_contract.py`, README rule 1 / §18 / §109)

**What was checked and where.** The README's FIRST rule is "Real data or nothing: every price,
rating, hour and distance shown to a user traces to a `facts` row ... Unverifiable = rendered as
unverified", and the e2e suite asserts it ("cards never render an ungrounded number"). But the
e2e assertion lives in the BROWSER run, which needs the whole stack, so the rule was only ever
checked when the stack was up — which is most of the time, not.

**The three cases, now on the AI service's own suite:**

1. **No card renders an ungrounded number** — for every card the live search returns: a price
   needs a `price` fact, a rating needs a `rating` fact, an open state needs an `opening_hours`
   fact, and the synthetic inventory must carry `flags.demo` (the e2e spec's own assertions,
   run against the database).
2. **Every reason carries a fact id** — §18: a bullet without a fact id is a claim nobody can
   check, and the card rendered 1 reason per card on the live plane (all with fact ids).
3. **A sponsored card is labelled** — §66-67: a promoted card must say so.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_live_ai_contract.py` against the seeded `nexus` ->
**3 passed**; full `apps/ai` suite -> **762 passed** with the database, **747 passed / 15
skipped** without it.

**Why this unit exists.** D399 found a 500 on the product's headline sentence with a probe and
a live test. The rules above had the same exposure and no gate at all: they were asserted only
in a run that needs three services. A rule that is only checked when the whole stack is up is a
rule that is checked rarely.

## 395. D401 · the comparison grid had no distance row, no district row, and two rows of "unverified" (`api/routes_discover` + `search/sql`, §37 / §18)

**What the product says the comparison is.** §37: three merchants from real rows only, and the
e2e spec asserts the compare table shows **Price, Rating and Distance**. The live grid, measured
against the seeded plane, produced five rows — `price`, `rating`, `category`, `district`,
`open_state` — and NO distance row at all.

**The three defects, and what each was:**

1. **No distance row.** A distance needs a reference point, and `CompareRequest` had none, so the
   grid could not compute one. The request now accepts an optional `geo` (the point the
   comparison is measured from) and the grid grows a `distance` row when it is given. The
   distances come from the same PRIMARY location the search's geo lane reads, so the two lanes
   cannot disagree about how far a merchant is. Without a `geo` there is no distance row — the
   grid never invents one.
2. **No district row.** The grid built a `district` row and dropped it EVERY time, because
   `entities_for` selects no district column, so the cells were always empty and the row was
   filtered out. The district now comes from the same primary-location read.
3. **Two rows of "unverified".** A compare cell with no `fact_id` renders as the unverified
   marker (`CompareTable`: `factBacked ? ... : labels.unverified`), so the `category` and
   `district` rows rendered as "unverified" in the product's comparison table. Both are the
   MERCHANT'S OWN CLAIM (its own `category_primary` column, its own location row), so both now
   get a fact with the source and the timestamp — exactly the way the `open_state` row already
   did.

**Measured, on the live plane, after the fix.** The compare of three merchants now answers with six
rows — `price`, `rating`, `category`, `district`, `open_state`, `distance` — and EVERY cell carries a
fact id: price 354.55 / 187.11 / 280.36, rating 4.57 / 4.59 / 4.30, category Steakhouse /
Italian / European Bistro, district Sha Tin / Sha Tin / Tai Wai, open_state Opens 12:00 x3, and
distance 410m / 410m / 1.4km.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_compare_grid.py` -> **9 passed** (the request takes a
point, the query reads the distance and the district, the grid keeps both rows, and the cells are
fact-backed); `pytest tests/test_live_ai_contract.py` against the seeded `nexus` -> **4 passed**,
including the grid carrying price, rating and distance with no empty cell; full `apps/ai` suite ->
**772 passed** with the database, **756 passed / 16 skipped** without it. `docs/API_CONTRACT.md` §7
now documents the optional `geo`.

**The other half, and whose it is.** The grid's row headers are the RAW attribute keys
(`price`, `rating`, ...), and the e2e spec looks for `/Price|价格|人均/` — so the table's row LABELS
have to be localized by whoever renders them (`packages/ui/src/trust/CompareTable.tsx` renders
`row.attribute` raw). That is the web lane's file, so it is reported, not edited. The AI lane's half
is the rows and their facts, and that is what landed here.

## 397. D403 · the RAG retrieval could not find a Chinese chunk, and the corpus plainly has one (`search/sql` + `api/routes_rag`, §7 / RAG)

**What the corpus holds and what the retrieval found.** The seeded corpus has **79 chunks whose
text contains 咖啡**, and the retrieval answered **nothing** for the query 咖啡. The merchant lane
found the same merchants by trigram (D366), but the CHUNK lane had only two:

```
SELECT count(*) FROM chunks WHERE text LIKE '%咖啡%'                  -> 79
SELECT count(*) FROM chunks WHERE search_tsv @@ plainto_tsquery('simple','咖啡') -> 0
SELECT count(*) FROM chunks WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL             -> 0
```

**Why.** `to_tsvector('simple', ...)` cannot SEGMENT Chinese: a CJK run with no spaces becomes
ONE token, so 咖啡 is a SUBSTRING of a token like 咖啡及茶 and never equals one. The vector lane
cannot cover it either â the seeded chunks carry no embedding â so the retrieval had no lane left, and the
merchant agent's answers (grounded on chunks) had nothing to ground on for a Chinese question.

**The fix, in two halves that both had to land:**

1. **The query gained a trigram lane.** `similarity(c.text, :text)` is the trigram function that
   DOES work on CJK: the `%` OPERATOR does not, because it needs three-character trigrams and a
   two-character Chinese word has none (`text % '咖啡'` -> 0 rows, `similarity(...) > 0` -> 82). The
   parameter is cast (`::text`) because `similarity(text, $1)` leaves the type ambiguous and
   Postgres answers `could not determine data type of parameter $1` â a hard error, not a soft one.
2. **The route's threshold learned to count it.** The route scored a chunk by `kw_score` and
   `vec_score` only, so the chunks the trigram lane DID match were dropped as sub-threshold
   noise. The trigram score is now part of the score and of the threshold's evidence.

**Measured, on the live plane, after the fix.** 咖啡 -> 3 chunks; 蛋糕 -> 3; 素食 -> 3; 全日菜單 -> 3;
menu -> 3. Before the fix, 咖啡 and 蛋糕 answered 0.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_rag_chinese.py` -> **6 passed** (5 offline + the live
one); full `apps/ai` suite -> **779 passed** with the database, **762 passed / 17 skipped** without
it.

**Discipline note.** The first attempt at the trigram lane changed the query and the retrieval still
answered 0 â because the route's threshold dropped the chunks the new lane had found. The
probe that found it read the route's own scoring line rather than assuming the query was the whole
story; a lane that only SCORES cannot widen a result set, and this one had to widen a FILTER too.

recovery source immediately before staging, and `recover` restores from the copies alone when the process that

## 396. D402 · the search field's accessible name was an example sentence, and the product's own MVP test could not find the front door (`components/search-box` + `lib/i18n/dict`, §141 / §34)

**What the surface promised and what it rendered.** The consumer front door is one input: the
product's whole pitch is "say what you want in a sentence". `SearchBox` had ONE string for two jobs.
`dict.home.searchPlaceholder` — `例如：帮我找沙田适合约会的餐厅，预算 500，安静一点`, an EXAMPLE —
was passed both to the input's `placeholder` attribute and rendered inside the `<label>` element,
so the field's accessible name was an example sentence. Two things follow from that, and only one
of them is an accessibility complaint: a screen reader announces "for example: help me find a
restaurant in Sha Tin" where it should announce what the field wants, and the accessible name
changes whenever marketing rewrites the example. The example is the volatile string; the name is
the contract.

**The contract that was already written down.** `tests/e2e/specs/consumer/vertical-slice.spec.ts` is
the file the repo calls "the definition of MVP complete", and it locates the field by its NAME:
`getByLabel(/想要|需要|Tell me|What are you looking for/i)` — a question, in both locales. On the live
plane that locator resolved to ZERO elements in six of the suite's nine cases, and the failure text
said only `waiting for getByLabel(...)`. A consumer journey that cannot type its first sentence is
not a partial pass; the whole front door was unaddressable by the product's own acceptance test.

**The remedy, in the order it fell out.**
1. `dict.ts` gains `home.searchLabel` beside `searchPlaceholder`, declared in the `Dict` interface so
   a locale that skips it fails to compile: `你想要什么？` for `zh-HK`, `What are you looking for?` for
   `en`. The interface carries the distinction as a comment — the name is a question, not an example.
2. `SearchBox` gains an optional `label` prop and computes `const name = label ?? dict.home.searchLabel`
   beside the existing `hint`; the sr-only `<label>` renders `{name}` and `placeholder` keeps `{hint}`.
   The two strings are now separately overridable, which is what the results page needed anyway.
3. The follow-up box on the results page is a different question from the first one, so it passes
   `label={dict.search.followUpLabel}` and keeps its own placeholder. No new key: `followUpLabel`
   already existed (`继续追问` / `Keep refining`) and was only ever rendered as visible prose above the
   box, never as the field's name.

**The witness.** The same command on the same live plane (`apps/web` production build served on
127.0.0.1:3002, AI on :8010, platform on :8090, `playwright test specs/consumer --project=desktop
--workers=2`), before and after: **6 failed / 2 passed** → **5 failed / 3 passed**, exit 1 both ways,
and the case that turned green is `:141 MVP success test: first meaningful action inside 5 minutes
(§141)`. `:40` also moved — it used to die at the `fill()`, and now dies three assertions later, so
the fix unblocked it rather than healing it. The DOM evidence is Playwright's own aria snapshot
(`error-context.md`), which reads `textbox "你想要什么？"` with the example on its own line beneath it
as `/placeholder: 例如：…` — the name and the hint are two strings in the served markup, which is
exactly the split this unit was about.

**What this unit measured and deliberately did NOT fix.** Four separate defects remain in the five
reds, each named by its own reading rather than by inference:
- `:27` — the home rails. `page.getByText(/附近熱門/)` finds nothing because the `zh-HK` dictionary
  spells them in Simplified (`为你推荐`, `附近热门`). Whether `zh-HK` should be Traditional is a locale
  decision with a population behind it, not a locator bug, and it needs its own census.
- `:40` — a race the card hook makes invisible. `cards()` is `article[data-card-type]`, and the home
  page's rail cards carry the same attribute. Measured in the browser: the moment Enter is pressed the
  home page shows 28 articles, then the route lands on `/search` with 0, then 8 arrive ~2.5s later.
  The assertion `found.first()` toBeVisible passed on the HOME page's rails and `found.count()` ran on
  the results page — the test is not page-scoped, and the product's stages were never frozen.
- `:85` — the §34 refinement has no surface. `getByRole('button', {name:/太贵了| cheaper/i})` waits out
  the whole 30s. The server half works (measured earlier: budget 500 → 350, and only 3 of 8 slugs
  survive the turn), so this is a missing affordance, with a catch the next unit has to be honest
  about: `state_merger._adjust_budget` returns `op: budget_relative, applied: false, note: "no stated
  budget to scale — do not invent one (§8)"` when the first turn never named a budget, and the e2e's
  own sentence (`帮我找附近适合朋友聚会的餐厅`) is exactly that case.
- `:100` — `getByRole('button', {name:/对比|Compare/i})` resolves to 12 elements. The compare tray
  gives every selected chip's remove button the SAME label as the clear-all button
  (`cards.tsx` `CompareTray`: `aria-label={dict.search.compareClear}`), so four of those twelve say
  "清除对比" and none of them says which merchant it removes.
- `:111` — `section[aria-labelledby="reviews-title"]` is absent on the merchant page; separate unit.

- changed  `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/dict.ts` (the `Dict` interface + both locales),
  `apps/web/src/components/search-box.tsx` (the `label` prop and the name/hint split),
  `apps/web/src/components/search-results.tsx` (the follow-up box's label)

  18 steps; the last recorded reading on this plane is `## 395`'s (`step 8 0 offenders · step 9 91/30

## 398. D404 · the conversation's two refinements had no surface, and the refusal to invent a budget threw away the whole refinement (`search/nlu/state_merger` + `components/search-results` + `lib/i18n/dict` + `lib/mock`, §34 / §8)

**What §34 promised the consumer could say.** Two of the refinements the conversation contract names
are ordinary Chinese phrases a user types on a second turn: 太贵了 ("too expensive") and 近一点 ("a bit
closer"). The server already understood both — `nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py` matches them in
`CHEAP_CUES`/`NEARER_CUES` and rewrites the merged intent — and `tests/e2e/specs/consumer/vertical-slice.spec.ts`
is written as if the surface offered them as one-tap actions: `getByRole('button', {name:/太贵了| cheaper/i})`,
then `getByRole('button', {name:/近一点|closer/i})`. On the live plane no such control existed anywhere, so
the case spent its whole 30 s action timeout waiting and failed with `element(s) not found`. A contract
sentence the product cannot offer a button for is not a UX preference; it is the acceptance test's own
locator, in the file the repo calls "the definition of MVP complete".

**The §8 trap inside the honest refusal.** Adding the button made a second defect visible, and this is
the part a `applied: false` note hides. `太贵了` scales the stated budget by `CHEAP_FACTOR = 0.7`. When the
first turn never named a budget — which is exactly the sentence the e2e test uses, `帮我找附近适合朋友聚会的餐厅` —
`_adjust_budget` returned `applied: false` with the note `no stated budget to scale — do not invent one
(§8)` and did **nothing else**. The refusal is right (§8: a rendered number needs a source), but the user
asked for cheaper and got a page that could not possibly look cheaper, because the refinement's only
effect was the number it would not fabricate. `_tighten_radius` already had the shape of the answer: with
no radius to scale it sets `sort_preference = "distance"` and reports `radius_applied: False`. Saying "too
expensive" without a number to cut has the same honest effect — put the cheap ones first.

**The remedy, in the order it fell out.**
1. `state_merger._adjust_budget`, no-budget branch: set `base["sort_preference"] = "price_low"`, keep
   `op: "budget_relative"` and `applied: False` so the pre-existing witness at
   `tests/test_state_merger.py:43` (`…_is_not_invented`) still holds, and add `sort_preference` to the
   change record so the merge is auditable from `changes` alone.
2. `dict.search` gains `refineCheaper`/`refineCloser`, declared in the interface so a locale that skips
   them fails to compile. The strings ARE the utterances — `太贵了`/`近一点` in `zh-HK`, `Cheaper`/`Closer` in
   `en` — so a chip prints exactly what it submits, and the cue matcher on the server reads the same text
   it always read. No new cue vocabulary was introduced by this unit.
3. `search-results.tsx` renders the two as a labelled `role="group"` in the follow-up region, wired to
   the existing `setQuery`, which is the path that already carries `previous_intent` (§34's client half).
   Nothing new submits a search; the chips only fill the box the user would have typed in.
4. `lib/mock/index.ts` had the cheaper arm as `next.budget?.max ?? 400` — the offline plane inventing a
   number the live plane's own comment refuses to invent. It now branches the way the service does:
   scale when there is a stated budget, sort by price when there is not.

**The witness.** `apps/ai`: `pytest tests/test_state_merger.py -q` → **21 passed**, with the new case
`test_cheaper_with_no_budget_still_orders_by_price`. The case is behavioral, not textual: reverting the
branch to the no-effect return makes it **1 failed / 20 passed**, and restoring makes it 21 again.
`apps/web`: `npm run build` → `✓ Compiled successfully in 73s`, 0 error lines, production server on
127.0.0.1:3002 against AI :8010 and platform :8090. `playwright test specs/consumer/vertical-slice.spec.ts
--project=desktop -g "conversation refinement keeps state"` → **1 passed (52.5s), exit 0**, where the same
command on the same plane was the 30 s `element(s) not found` before.

**What the live three-turn measurement showed, and what it did not fix.** Driving the BFF's
`/api/nexus/ai/stream` with the merged intent threaded back, exactly as the browser does:
turn 1 `帮我找附近适合朋友聚会的餐厅` → `sort_preference: distance, budget: null, radius: null`;
turn 2 `太贵了` → `sort_preference: price_low, budget: null` (the new effect, and §8 still unbroken —
no number appears); turn 3 `近一点` → `radius_m: 1000` (the nearby default 2000 × `RADIUS_TIGHTEN`). The
state merge works end to end. **The answer set did not change: 8 cards, and the same first four slugs in
all three turns.** That is a separate, precisely located defect: `search/service.py:585` writes
`plan.sort_preference` from the intent and nothing downstream reads it — `organic_rank()` sorts by
`(-organic_score, candidate.key())` and `plan.radius_m` is the only planning field the retrieval honours.
So a refinement can be correctly remembered and still produce an identical page; the chip that this unit
made tappable cannot yet visibly re-order. The reader is the next unit, not this one's claim.

**The measurement error this unit made, filed with the rest.** The first run of the same e2e case failed
three lines earlier than the defect it was written to catch: `:87` timed out with 0 cards and the page
printed `流式搜索失败，已降级为确定性搜索结果` over an empty result list, and `/ai/v1/search` answered

`http://127.0.0.1:8080`, which is not where this repo's platform answers (8090). Launching the repo's own
`apps/ai/start_ai.py` (which sets them) gives
`strategy: hybrid_v1+postgres+vector`, 12 items, `degraded: false` on the same four sentences. Invocation
is part of the measurement; no product defect is claimed on the strength of my own command line.

**One thing found while reading that launcher, deliberately left alone.** `apps/ai/start_ai.py` is a
**tracked** file and its first six lines are literal assignments of `NEXUS_AI_DB_URL` (with the AI role's
password) and `NEXUS_JWT_SECRET` — credentials in the repository, while `.env` is gitignored for exactly

**Also noticed on the plane this entry appends to.** The other lane's RAG entry landed in `fdc67be` as
