- **a point to measure from gives a distance** (§37's grid ✗ — and §401 added the row ✓).

**Measured before writing it, on the live plane.** The filters hold ✓ (`max_price: 60` -> the
dearest card is 60.00 ✓, `min_rating: 4.5` -> the lowest rating served is 4.52 ✓, the district
filter -> every subtitle carries "Sha Tin" ✓), and every card carries an open state ✓ — so this
unit is a **gate for a promise that already holds** ✓, which is the cheapest kind of gate there
is ✓: it turns six things that were true today into six things that cannot stop being true
tomorrow ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_live_search_contract.py` -> **6 passed** on the
live plane **and 6 passed** on the plane seeded from the current generator ✓ (§422's second
plane ✓ — the gate is measured on both ✓, so a corpus that cannot show a behaviour says so
instead of passing quietly ✓); the full `apps/ai` suite -> **935 passed / 37 skipped**;
`ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 52
source files**; the eval gate -> **`RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing`**.

**Discipline note.** A gate written for a promise that already holds is worth more than one
written for a promise that does not ✗ — a red gate trains people to ignore gates ✓, and the
lane's readers are only worth their reading if they are mostly green ✓ and their reds are real ✓.
This unit's reds are the ones that would matter ✗: a filter that stops filtering ✗, a card that
stops saying whether it is open ✗, a number that loses its fact ✗.

## 425. D431 · the merchant agent's chat wrote NO run, so its turns were invisible to the conversation timeline (`api/routes_stream`, AGENT_CONTRACT §8)

**What the contract asks for and what the plane had.** AGENT_CONTRACT §8: every task writes an
`agent_runs` row ✓, and the runs of one conversation link together ✓. The chat's request
**requires** a `conversation_id` ✓ — the caller has already paid for the linkage ✓ — and the turn
was invisible:

```
the chat: 200
the runs recorded for the conversation: 0
the five most recent runs on the plane: all "search"
```

So a conversation that contains a merchant chat shows nothing but the searches ✓, and
`GET /ai/v1/conversations/{id}` — the surface that answers "what happened in this
conversation" ✓ — could not show the agent's own turns ✓.

**The fix.** The chat records its run the way the search records its own ✓: the in-process ledger
first ✓ (so the timeline answers offline ✓) and the table best-effort ✓ (so a persistence
failure never breaks a response ✓). The run carries the **conversation** ✓, the **merchant** ✓,
the **message** ✓, the **answer** ✓, the grounded/degraded distinction ✓ (a handoff is a
different outcome from an answer ✓, and the run says which one it was ✓) and the **chunks** the
answer was grounded on ✓ — in the `retrieval` column ✓, not in `fact_ids` ✓, because a chunk id
is not a fact id ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_merchant_agent_run.py` -> **2 passed** (the chat
writes a run for the conversation it was given ✓, carrying the conversation ✓, the merchant ✓,
the question ✓ and the answer ✓; and a handoff is recorded as degraded ✓ with
`fallback_used: no_grounded_chunks` ✓); the full `apps/ai` suite -> **937 passed / 37
skipped**; `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues
found in 52 source files**; the eval gate -> **`RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing`**; and
on the live plane the probe now reads **1** run for the conversation ✓ (it read 0 ✓).

**Discipline note.** Two of the three surfaces that make a product operable — the timeline ✓ and
the observability ledger ✓ — were blind to one of the product's own features ✓, and the feature
still answered perfectly ✓. A response that works and a record of the response are two
different promises ✓, and only the first one was being kept ✓. The contract asks for the second
one in the first line of §8 ✓, and it is the line that is easiest to skip ✓ because nothing
fails when it is ✓.

## 426. D432 · three more surfaces wrote no run, and the recommendation handed out a run id that resolved to nothing (`api/runs` + the three routes, AGENT_CONTRACT §8)

**The census.** §431 found that the merchant agent's chat wrote no `agent_runs` row ✗, and the
same question — *which surfaces record the work they do?* — has an answer for every endpoint ✗.
Walking the service's endpoints and counting what each leaves in the in-process ledger ✓:

```
/ai/v1/search               200  runs: 1
/ai/v1/search/stream        200  runs: 1
/ai/v1/merchant-agent/chat  200  runs: 1
/ai/v1/rag/retrieve         200  runs: 0    <- this unit
/ai/v1/query/understand     200  runs: 0    <- this unit
/ai/v1/recommend            200  runs: 0    <- this unit
/ai/v1/feedback             200  runs: 0    (correct: the feedback EVENT is its record)
```

And the recommendation was worse than "no run": its response carries an **`agent_run_id`** ✓ —
the id of a run ✗ — and **no run row ever carried that id** ✓, so the caller was handed a
pointer to a row that did not exist ✗.

**The fix.** One shared recorder (`api/runs.py::record_run`) — the ledger first ✓ (so the
timeline answers offline ✓) and the table best-effort ✓ (so a persistence failure never breaks
a response ✓) — and three calls to it ✓: the **retrieval** ✓ (`retrieval` ✓ — the chunks it was
grounded on ✓, which are not facts ✗ and do not go in `fact_ids` ✓), the **intent extraction**
✓ (`intent_extract` ✓ — the contract's roster name ✓) and the **recommendation** ✓
(`recommendation` ✓, carrying **the response's own `agent_run_id`** ✓, so the id resolves ✓).

**The one that is right to write no run.** The **feedback** ✓: a signal is not a task ✗, and it
records itself in `feedback_events` ✓ — a run there would be a second, redundant record of the
same thing ✗. That case is pinned too ✓, because "every endpoint writes a run" would have been
the wrong rule ✗.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_runs_census.py` -> **5 passed** (the search ✓, the
intent extraction ✓, the retrieval ✓, the recommendation ✓ — including that **its response's
`agent_run_id` resolves to a run** ✓ — and the feedback ✓, which writes its event and **no**
run ✓); the full `apps/ai` suite -> **942 passed / 37 skipped**; `ruff check .` -> **All checks
passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 52 source files**; the eval gate ->
**`RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing`**.

**Discipline note.** §8's first line is a promise that **nothing fails on** when it is broken ✗ —
the responses were all 200 ✓, the answers were all right ✓, and the records were missing ✗. A
contract clause that only a human reading the ledger would notice ✗ is a clause that gets
noticed once and then never again ✗; a census that counts the records ✗ makes it a **number**
✗, and a number can be a gate ✓. The census is now a test ✓ — five cases ✓, one per surface ✓,
including the surface that is right to be absent ✓.

## 427. D433 · the product's two-turn refinement had never been measured on the live plane, in either spelling (`apps/ai/tests/test_live_conversation_refinement.py`, §34)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** A user says what they want, then says "太贵了"
(too expensive) or "近一点" (a bit closer) on the second turn ✓, and §34 promises what the second
turn does ✓. The two units that carry it were measured **offline** ✓: D406 wired the sort
preference (`plan.sort_preference` was written and never read ✓) and D421 made the merge's cues
answer to either spelling ✓ (the cues are a second vocabulary the canonical table did not cover ✓).
Neither asked the live plane ✓.

**What the live plane answers, measured now.**

```
turn 1  拉麵                      sort='relevance'   8 cards
turn 2  太貴了 (traditional)        sort='price_low'   8 cards, prices ASCENDING
turn 2  太贵了 (simplified)         sort='price_low'   8 cards, prices ASCENDING
turn 2  近一點 (traditional)         sort='distance'   8 cards, the radius tightened to 1000
```

**The words in the test come FROM the vocabulary** ✓ — `L.CUISINE_TERMS["japanese"][5]` ✓ and
`M.CHEAPER_CUES` / `M.NEARER_CUES` ✓ — because D421's lesson is that a writer's memory of a CJK
code point is not a reference ✓, and a test that hard-codes one inherits the mistake ✓. (It is not
hypothetical: while writing this unit the probe's own 拉麵 and 近一點 were **wrong code points** ✓
and the probe reported a refinement that did not fire ✗ — the vocabulary was the only thing that
had it right ✓.)

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_live_conversation_refinement.py` -> **2 passed** on
the plane seeded from the current generator ✓; the full `apps/ai` suite -> **981 passed** with the
database, **942 passed / 39 skipped** without it ✓; `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**;
`mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 52 source files**; the eval gate ->
**`RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing`**.

**Discipline note.** Two units, two fixes ✓, and the question that would have caught the next one
was never asked ✗ on the plane where the answer is served ✗. A fix measured offline is a fix
measured on a **model** of the product ✗ — and the difference between the model and the product
showed up here in the form of a probe that could not spell 拉麵 ✗. The test that takes its words
from the vocabulary ✓ cannot make that mistake ✓, which is a stronger property than a test that
happens to spell them right ✓ today ✓.

## 428. D434 · the evaluation's own price case was written with three wrong code points, and it still PASSED (`apps/ai/tests/test_vocabulary_is_the_reference.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/eval/data/intent_v1.jsonl`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §405 (D411) built the eval gate: a suite of
intent cases and a suite of injection cases that run without a database and fail the build when
a behaviour regresses. The cases are DATA, and DATA is written by hand. §403 (D409) and §408
(D414) already paid for that lesson once - a hand-written CJK code point is not a reference, and
the fix that time was to check the vocabulary against the Unihan database. But the CASES were
never checked against anything. They were only ever checked against their own expectations.

**The defect.** The intent case `sort-price-low-zh` asks for something cheaper in Cantonese and
expects the price ordering. Its query was written with **three wrong code points**:

```
written    U+6709 U+4EC0 U+9EBC U+5E73 U+55AE U+5605 U+9910 U+5EF3
           有    什    麼    平    (variant) 嘅    餐    廳
right     U+6709 U+54A9 U+5E73 U+5572 U+5605 U+9910 U+5EF3
           有    咩    平    啲    嘅    餐    廳
```

`什` is not `咩` (the Cantonese question particle, U+54A9 - "the bleating of sheep; (Cant.) an
interrogative particle" in the Unihan readings), `麼` is not `啲` (U+5572), and U+55AE is a
variant of `啲` rather than `啲` itself. Every one of the three was verified against the Unihan
database and the compatibility pages before it was written down.

**The part that matters.** The case **PASSED** - all along, and after the fix. It passed because
the sort's cue list contains the single character `平` on its own, and the query's `平` matched it.
So the case was not testing the phrase it claimed to test; it was testing a loose one-character
cue, and the three wrong characters were decoration. A gate that asks only "does the case pass?"
cannot see that. The gate was reporting coverage the suite did not have, and the coverage it
reported was the coverage of the cheapest possible way to pass.

**The fix, and the reference that makes it hold.** The case's query is now the real words. And
the repo now carries a reference that does not need the Unihan data shipped with it: **the
product's own vocabulary**. `apps/ai/tests/test_vocabulary_is_the_reference.py` requires every
Chinese character in the intent cases to be one the lexicon, the canonical table or the merge's
cues already carry - after the canonicalisation the product actually performs on the text
(§411, D417). The injection suite is deliberately out of scope: an attack is SUPPOSED to use words
the platform has never heard of. The handful of grammatical words the vocabulary does not carry
are DECLARED in the test, each with its verified code point.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- `pytest tests/test_vocabulary_is_the_reference.py` -> **1 passed**
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **982 passed** with the database (the one before was 981)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 52
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** (`intent_v1` 31/31, `safety_injection_v1`
  27/27) - with the case's query fixed, so the suite now asserts the phrase it names
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** §427 (D433) made a live test take its words FROM the vocabulary, so that a
test cannot inherit a writer's misspelling. This unit applies the same rule to the DATA: a case
file must take its characters from the vocabulary too. The general form of the lesson is worth
stating, because it is easy to get backwards: **a test that passes for the wrong reason is worse
than a test that fails**, because a failing test is a task and a passing test is a claim. The
three wrong code points sat in the suite for the whole of §405's life, and every run of the gate
reported the suite's coverage as complete. The gate was measuring the right thing; the QUESTION
it asked was not the right one.

## 429. D435 · the word for "now" set NOTHING: two vocabulary tables were left out of the canonicalisation list, and the locale's markers did not know the canonical table's 96 Simplified forms (`apps/ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_vocabulary_canonical_coverage.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_live_vocabulary_spelling.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** Two facts about a Chinese character are kept in
this product, and they are the SAME fact:

* its **canonical spelling** - the one the vocabulary is written in and the one every comparison
  is made in, because the query is canonicalised before it is compared (§411, D417);
* whether it is the **Simplified or the Traditional** one - which is what the locale detection
  votes on, on the text as the user wrote it (§420, D420).

They were kept twice, by hand, in two different modules, and nothing checked they agreed.

**The first drift: two tables were left out of the canonicalisation list.** `nlu/lexicon.py`
already holds the mechanism - `_CANONICALISED_TABLES`, a list of the tables that are rebound in
the canonical spelling at import (§411, D417). The list is kept BY HAND, and the two urgency cue
lists were not on it. So the cue for "now" was compared against a spelling it could never have:

```
现在  U+73B0 U+5728   ->  urgency='normal'    (the cue was compared in the wrong spelling)
現在  U+73FE U+5728   ->  urgency='normal'    (the word is not in the list at all)
得闲  U+5F97 U+95F2   ->  urgency='normal'
得閒  U+5F97 U+9592   ->  urgency='flexible'  (the one spelling that worked)
```

**A user who typed 现在 was told nothing about urgency - in either spelling.** The word "now" was
in the cue list in the Simplified spelling only; the Traditional spelling of the same word was
never there, and the Simplified entry could not fire because the query's character is rewritten
before the comparison.

**The second drift: the locale's markers did not know the canonical table.** The detection votes
on Simplified and Traditional characters, so it needs its own list of them - `_TRAD_SIMP_PAIRS`,
144 pairs. The canonical table already knows 229 Simplified forms. The two lists overlapped on 133
of them, so **96 Simplified forms the product already rewrites did not vote as Simplified**: a
Simplified user whose query used one of them was read as a Hong Kong user and answered in the
Traditional locale. The same query, 现在, came back `language='zh-HK'` - the user wrote
Simplified and was addressed in Traditional.

**The fix - one fact, one place.**

* `URGENCY_NOW` and `URGENCY_FLEXIBLE` (and the cuisine style forms, which hold a mixed
  spelling of their own) are now on `_CANONICALISED_TABLES`, so every cue is written in the one
  spelling the comparison happens in;
* the marker sets are now DERIVED from the canonical table - the detection's Simplified set is
  the canonical table's keys and its Traditional set is the canonical table's values, unioned with
  the pairs the canonical table does not carry (适/適, 麵/麺). The two tables can no longer
  disagree, because one of them is now computed from the other.

**The gate - a census, so the next table left out is caught.**
`apps/ai/tests/test_vocabulary_canonical_coverage.py` requires that every vocabulary table
holding Chinese is either canonicalised at import or already holds the canonical spelling (a
table that holds a character the canonicalisation rewrites is a table whose cues can never match),
that the canonicalised tables hold only canonical characters, that **every one of the 229
canonical pairs votes for its own locale**, and that the product's own word for "now" is
understood in both spellings. `apps/ai/tests/test_live_vocabulary_spelling.py` asks the live
stream the same question - the fix was measured offline first, and an offline measurement is a
MODEL of the product (§427, D433).

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the census -> **5 passed**; the live plane -> **1 passed** (the stream's intent frame reports
  `urgency='now'` and `language='zh-CN'` for the Simplified spelling, `zh-HK` for the Traditional)
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **988 passed** with the database, **948 passed / 39 skipped** without it
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 52
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note, and a residual that is filed rather than fixed.** The general form of the
lesson is not "be careful with the Chinese": it is that **a fact kept in two places is a fact
that will drift**, and the fix is not vigilance but DERIVATION - one place computed from the
other. Here the two facts drifted in opposite directions at once: the vocabulary forgot two
tables and the markers forgot 96 characters, and both defects made the SAME user - someone
typing Simplified - wrong in two different ways at the same time.

The residual is measured and left alone on purpose: 37 of the canonical forms have a VARIANT the
table does not join (Unihan's variant data names 閒 as both U+9591 and U+9592, and the table
rewrites 闲 to only one of them). Joining variants is a word-level decision - §411's own lesson
is that 座位 must not become 庢位 - so it is a decision to make with the ledger in front of it,
not a change to make silently.

## 430. D436 · the Simplified spelling of the two-turn refinement was NEVER RUN: the test read "the two spellings" out of a list that holds one spelling (`apps/ai/tests/test_live_conversation_refinement.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_refinement_spellings.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §427 (D433) measured the product's own
two-turn refinement on the live plane and reported a table with a row for each spelling:

```
turn 2  太貴了 (traditional)   sort='price_low'   8 cards, prices ASCENDING
turn 2  太贵了 (simplified)    sort='price_low'   8 cards, prices ASCENDING
```

The second row was never run. The test took its two words from the merge's own cue list:

```python
CHEAPER_TRADITIONAL = M.CHEAPER_CUES[1]
CHEAPER_SIMPLIFIED  = M.CHEAPER_CUES[0]
```

and **those two entries are the same string** - `U+592A U+8CB4` and `U+592A U+8CB4`. They are
the same because §415 (D421) canonicalises every cue list at import (`_canonicalise_cues`), so
the list holds ONE spelling per word - and the two entries are the two spellings of the source
text, collapsed into one. The test looped over the same query twice, measured the Traditional
spelling twice, and reported both spellings as covered.

**The property itself is true; the evidence was hollow.** The merge does answer to either
spelling - the turn is canonicalised too (§415, D421), so the user's Simplified word and the
cue's Traditional one meet. That was never the question. The question was whether the product
was MEASURED in both, and it was not.

**The fix.** The two spellings now come from the place that holds two spellings - the canonical
table, whose keys are the Simplified forms and whose values are the Traditional ones:

* `apps/ai/tests/test_live_conversation_refinement.py` derives the other spelling from the
  canonical table and **asserts that the two differ** - a guard, not a hope - and the closer
  cue is measured in both spellings too (§427's table had only the Traditional one);
* `apps/ai/tests/test_refinement_spellings.py` holds the property itself as a gate over EVERY
  cue the merge compares against: the canonical spelling and the other spelling must produce
  the SAME refinement, and the canonical table must hold both spellings of every pair.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **4 passed**; the live plane -> **2 passed** (the refinement now fires in the
  Simplified spelling as well: `sort_preference='price_low'`, prices ASCENDING, and the closer
  cue tightens the radius in both spellings)
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **992 passed** with the database, **952 passed / 40 skipped** without it
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 52
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** A green test can still measure nothing, when the thing it names was
canonicalised under it. §415's fix was right - one spelling per word, the user's text rewritten
to meet it - and it silently removed the evidence for §427's claim, because the two units read
the same list for different purposes. The general form: **when a test names two things, the
source it reads them from must hold two things.** Reading both spellings out of a list that
holds one is the same mistake as reading a case file's expectation out of the case file - the
assertion is about itself.

## 431. D437 · the cost ledger was an EMPTY table: the router built the row for it and nobody ever called the builder (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/runs.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/models/router.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_live_cost_ledger.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The AI service may write five tables; `llm_calls`
is the cost ledger - OBSERVABILITY.md §3: *"llm_calls is the ledger: provider, model, purpose,
tokens, cost_usd, latency, cache_hit"* - and §1 lists it as *"llm_calls per model call"*.

Measured on the seeded live plane, before this unit:

```
the llm_calls rows: 0
the agent_runs rows: 446   prompt_tokens 0 (446/446)   completion_tokens 0   cost_usd 0
   of which 138 runs had used the mock provider
```

**The defect.** The router builds the exact row for that ledger - `RoutedCall.as_llm_call_row()`,
whose own docstring says *"One routed LLM call, ready to be recorded into `llm_calls`"* - and
**nothing ever called it**. The table was in the AI service's own write grant
(`AI_WRITE_ALLOWED_TABLES`) and empty. So the model layer measured every call - the
`CostMeter` counts the calls and sums the tokens, the cost and the latency - and the
measurement was thrown away: the `agent_runs` row wrote `prompt_tokens=0`,
`completion_tokens=0`, `cost_usd=0` whatever the model layer had measured. AGENT_CONTRACT §8
says a run carries *"tokens, cost_usd"*.

**The fix - the ledger and the run are written together, in that order.**

* the `CostMeter` keeps the CALLS, not only their totals, so the recorder has the rows to
  write;
* the recorder that owns the run writes the run first and the ledger row second - because
  `llm_calls.agent_run_id` refers to `agent_runs(id)`. The foreign key taught the order: the
  first attempt wrote the ledger row first and every insert was rejected, which is why the
  table could look "written but empty" for a while;
* the run row now carries the tokens and the cost the model layer measured - the intent
  extraction's, the summary's and the merchant agent's chat's.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the live gate -> **3 passed**: a model call leaves a row in `llm_calls` (provider, model,
  purpose, tokens, latency), the run that made it carries the tokens, and the ledger and the
  run agree about them
- the live plane, after the fix -> **`llm_calls` 3 rows** (it was 0) and **6 runs carrying
  tokens** where the table had 446 runs carrying none. The 446 older rows keep their zeros:
  the fix applies to the runs written after it
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **995 passed** with the database, **952 passed / 43 skipped** without it
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 52
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note, and one honest caveat.** The general shape of this defect is old and familiar:
*the builder existed and the call did not*. `as_llm_call_row()` was written to the exact shape
of the table, documented as "ready to be recorded", and never recorded - so the cost ledger was
a schema and a docstring, and every cost dashboard built on it (§160) would have divided by a
sum of nothing.

The caveat is about the numbers themselves: the mock provider ESTIMATES its token counts
(`estimate_tokens`), so a row written by the mock carries an estimate, not a measurement. The
row says which provider wrote it, so the reader can tell - but a ledger whose rows can be
estimates has to say so on the row, and today it says so only by naming the provider.

## 432. D438 · the contract module modelled the error body and seven places hand-built it instead; one request shape has been dead since the first commit (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/errors.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/contract.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_contract_shapes_are_used.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** `nexus_ai/contract.py` is the AI service's own
shape vocabulary - the request bodies the routes parse, the response bodies they return, the
error body they answer with. It declares **14 shapes**. The census of the package (every
definition, and whether anything mentions it - the same sweep that found §431's unused row
builder) says:

```
the contract module declares 14 shapes
   AiSearchRequest    -> (nowhere)
   ErrorEnvelope      -> (nowhere)
   the other twelve   -> wired to a route
```

**The first defect: the error body was modelled and then copied.** `ErrorEnvelope` and
`ErrorBody` describe the §1 error body, and **seven places across five route modules
hand-built the same dict** instead: `api/app.py`, `api/routes_search.py`,
`api/routes_conversations.py`, `api/routes_discover.py` (three of them), `api/routes_rag.py`
(three of them). A shape written once and copied seven times is a shape that drifts - and a
drift there is invisible, because the copy still *looks* like an envelope.

**The second defect: a request shape nobody ever sent.** `AiSearchRequest`
(`query`, `conversation_id`, `context`, `limit`) has been dead since the first commit
(`e237f6d`, "M1 wave 1"): the search's own shape is `SearchRequest`, and the platform never
sent this one - it only ever calls `/ai/v1/imports/extract` (service to service) and the
browser uses the stream. Its `conversation_id` was the interesting part: the non-streaming
search still cannot join a conversation, and its runs are still invisible to the
conversation timeline.

**The fix.**

* `api/errors.py` builds the envelope from the contract's own model, and every route calls
  it - one place, and the place the contract points at;
* `AiSearchRequest` is removed: a shape no route accepts is a promise nobody keeps, and the
  alternative - letting the non-streaming search carry a `conversation_id` - is a contract
  decision (the documented request shape, the SDK's type, the platform's caller), not a
  change to make silently in a unit about dead code. **Filed, not done.**

**The gate - a census, so the next unused shape is caught.**
`apps/ai/tests/test_contract_shapes_are_used.py` requires that every shape the contract
module declares is used by the package (a shape mentioned only by its own definition is
unused), and that every error the service answers with - four error paths, exercised - is
accepted by the contract's own `ErrorEnvelope` model.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **3 passed**; the full `apps/ai` suite -> **998 passed** with the database,
  **955 passed / 43 skipped** without it
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 53
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** §431's lesson ("the builder existed and the call did not") had a second
half that this unit found: **the model existed and nobody called it either** - and the thing
that happened instead was not a bug but a copy. Seven hand-built envelopes looked fine,
passed every test, and meant that the contract's model described a shape the service did not
produce. A model that is not used is not a contract: it is a comment with a type annotation.

## 433. D439 · §8's follow-up question was computed in the user's language and delivered NOWHERE: the endpoint's `follow_up_question` was always null (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/pipeline.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_follow_up_question.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** API_CONTRACT §7.1 carries the intent's
`"unknowns": ["party_size"]  // §8 - never guess; ask in one follow-up only`. The question
itself is written - `nlu/state_merger.py` holds it in the user's language, one question, never
an interrogation - and it was delivered nowhere.

Measured on the live plane, before this unit:

```
'拉麵'        -> follow_up_question=None   unknowns=['location']   language=zh-HK
'餐廳'        -> follow_up_question=None   unknowns=['location']   language=zh-HK
'coffee'      -> follow_up_question=None   unknowns=['location']   language=en
'安靜的地方'  -> follow_up_question=None   unknowns=['location']   language=zh-HK
```

The intent always knew something was missing (`unknowns=['location']` ✓) and the question was
always null ✗. The reason is a seam: **only the merge path ever asked for the question** - the
second turn of a conversation - and the endpoint that carries the field
(`/ai/v1/query/understand`) never merges, because the merge needs a `previous_intent` the
endpoint does not accept. So the field existed, was documented in the response model, and was
null in every response the service ever gave.

**The fix.** The question is asked on EVERY turn now: the pipeline computes it on the model
path and on the deterministic floor, in the user's language - which, since §429 (D435), is the
language the user's own spelling asked for. The question function became public (`question_for`),
because every turn needs it and not only the ones that follow another turn.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **4 passed** (3 offline + 1 on the live plane): the endpoint asks the one
  question the intent leaves open, the question is in the user's language (the English query
  gets an English question, the Traditional and the Simplified queries get their own), and an
  intent with nothing unknown gets no question
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1002 passed** with the database, **958 passed / 44 skipped**
  without it
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 53
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note, and a filed residual.** The general shape is the D435 shape one layer up: a
fact the product knows (what is missing) and a promise the product makes (ask about it, once)
that were never JOINED - the question lived behind a seam only one caller went through. The
field was not a bug in the field: it was a field whose value was decided by which code path
happened to run.

The residual is filed: **the stream does not carry the question either.** The merge path
computes it (`IntentResult.follow_up_question` ✓) and the stream yields the intent, the
results and the summary - the question is dropped ✗. Delivering it needs a frame the
documented SSE list does not have (`API_CONTRACT` §7's six frames), so that is a contract
decision, not a silent change.

## 434. D440 · a run said when it started and never when it finished: the timeline's documented shape promises `finished_at` (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/runs.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_live_run_timestamps.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** API_CONTRACT §7's conversation-timeline row
names the fields each run carries, and two of them are the ends of the run:

> Each run is its `agent_runs` row (`agent_run_id, agent, model, provider, status, plan,
> input_summary, output_summary, tool_calls, retrieval, fact_ids, tokens, cost_usd,
> latency_ms, error, fallback_used, started_at, finished_at, parent_run_id`)

Measured on the seeded live plane before this unit:

```
the agent_runs table: 25 columns, 446 rows
   started_at    null in    0/446
   finished_at   null in  446/446
```

**The defect.** `finished_at` has no default, and no caller ever passed one: the run's clock
was a monotonic millisecond counter (`latency_ms` ✓) and the wall clock was never stamped, so
every run on the plane - every search, every intent extraction, every chat turn - carried a
NULL end. The `started_at` was there, but only because the recorder back-solves it from the
measured latency (a caller passing NULL had overridden the column default and every insert
had been rejected). So one end of every run was invented and the other was missing.

**The fix - the write IS the finish.**

* the recorder stamps `finished_at` when the caller has none, and back-solves `started_at`
  from the measured latency, so the two ends of the in-process run agree with each other;
* the SQL stamps `finished_at` itself (`COALESCE($22::timestamptz, now())`), which keeps the
  durable row and its back-solved start exactly `latency_ms` apart - the same clock, not two.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the live gate -> **3 passed**: a run carries both ends, the two ends agree with the latency
  the run measured (within 50ms), and the in-process ledger carries the end too - the offline
  timeline would otherwise show runs that never finished
- the live plane, after the fix -> `finished_at` null in **624 of 686** rows: the 62 rows
  written after the fix carry it, and the 624 older rows keep their NULL - the ledger's
  history is not rewritten to look better than it was
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1005 passed** with the database, **958 passed / 47 skipped**
  without it
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 53
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** This is the same defect §431 (D437) found in the cost ledger, one column
over: **a column the product's own documented shape promises, and nothing ever wrote.** The
column was there, the schema was there, the timeline read it - and because a NULL end is a
legal value, nothing failed and nothing looked wrong. The run looked complete in the
observability surface: an agent, a status, a plan, a latency. It just never ended.

The residual is filed: `parent_run_id` is NULL in every row too, and that one is honest - the
product runs one task per turn and has no sub-agent runs to link - but the roster's
parent/child tree (§8's "sub-agents link via parent_run_id") is not there yet.

## 435. D441 · the documents pointed at a layout the repository never had: `apps/ai/app/...` instead of `apps/ai/nexus_ai/...` (`apps/ai/tests/test_doc_paths_are_real.py`, 15 documents)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The lane's documents name the files a
reader is expected to open - the router, the state merger, the search SQL, the tool registry.
Those names had drifted: the documents said `apps/ai/app/...` and the repository says
`apps/ai/nexus_ai/...`. The census (every `apps/...` path the documents mention, and whether
it is there) found **73 paths that do not exist**, of which **10 name a file that exists
elsewhere** - the reader follows the path and finds nothing.

```
AGENT_CONTRACT.md: apps/ai/app/models/router.py      -> apps/ai/nexus_ai/models/router.py
AI.md:             apps/ai/app/nlu/state_merger.py    -> apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py
AI.md:             apps/ai/app/models/router.py        -> apps/ai/nexus_ai/models/router.py
API_CONTRACT.md:   apps/ai/app/nlu/state_merger.py    -> apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py
ARCHITECTURE.md:   apps/ai/app/search/sql.py          -> apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/sql.py
DATABASE.md:       apps/ai/app/nlu/state_merger.py    -> apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py
PLAN.md:           apps/ai/nlu/lexicon.py              -> apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py
PRODUCT.md:        apps/ai/app/nlu/state_merger.py    -> apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py
TRACEABILITY.md:   apps/ai/app/search/sql.py          -> apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/sql.py
TRACEABILITY.md:   apps/ai/app/nlu/state_merger.py    -> apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py
```

The `apps/ai/app/` prefix is a layout that was never built - the package is `nexus_ai` - and
the drift reached the documents an AGENT reads before it touches the code (`AGENTS.md` points
at the registry and the planner; `AI.md` points at the router and the merger).

**The fix.** The paths are rewritten in the fifteen living documents. The ledgers are NOT
rewritten: `docs/STATUS.md` and `docs/DECISIONS.md` are history, and a record is not edited
to look tidier than it was.

**The gate - the rule, and the reason it is not "every path must exist".**
`apps/ai/tests/test_doc_paths_are_real.py` distinguishes three cases:

* a path that exists -> fine;
* a path that does not exist **while the same file exists elsewhere** -> STALE, and that is
  the defect;
* a path that does not exist and has no counterpart -> **a promise about the future** (the
  tool registry, the orchestrator, the eval gates) - a promise, not a drift.

The gate reads the living documents only, and only the paths that name the AI lane's own
files: another lane's path is that lane's to fix, and this lane reports it rather than
touching it.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **1 passed** (it failed with all ten findings before the fix)
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1006 passed** with the database, **959 passed / 47 skipped**
  without it
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 53
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** A path in a document is a promise too - a small one, and the cheapest to
break: nothing fails when a path rots, and the reader who follows it is usually an agent that
has no way to tell "not built yet" from "moved". The three-way rule above is the general form
worth keeping: **a missing path is only a defect when the thing it names is somewhere else.**

## 436. D442 · the service-to-service door was IN the public OpenAPI document: §7.0 says it must not be (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_rag.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_service_to_service_is_hidden.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** API_CONTRACT §7.0 states three things about
the paths that exist only between our own services:

> These paths exist only between our own services. The BFF must not proxy them, **they are
> absent from the public OpenAPI document**, and a request that arrives from an edge is
> rejected for missing the shared secret.

Two of the three held. The secret stands (D7: an unconfigured token is a closed door, and a
wrong one is a 401 ✓). The third did not:

```
the OpenAPI document lists 13 paths:
   get   /                                  post  /ai/v1/compare
   get   /ai/v1/conversations/{id}          post  /ai/v1/feedback
   get   /ai/v1/health                      post  /ai/v1/imports/extract     <- the door
   post  /ai/v1/merchant-agent/chat         post  /ai/v1/query/understand
   post  /ai/v1/rag/retrieve                post  /ai/v1/recommend
   post  /ai/v1/search                      post  /ai/v1/search/stream
   get   /ai/v1/tools
```

`/ai/v1/imports/extract` - the door the platform calls to hand raw text to the extractor -
was in the document any client could read. The secret still guarded it, but the document was
telling the world where the door is.

**The fix.** `include_in_schema=False` on that one route: the door is still there, still
guarded, and no longer advertised.

**The gate - and it reads the paths from the contract, not from a list.**
`apps/ai/tests/test_service_to_service_is_hidden.py` takes the service-to-service paths out
of `API_CONTRACT.md`'s §7.0 section itself - a hand-kept list would be the same fact in two
places, and the two would drift (§432, D438) - and then checks all three halves of the
sentence: the paths are absent from the public document, the door is still closed without the
secret (401/501), and the door still opens with it (200).

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **3 passed**
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **998 passed** with the database, **951 passed / 47 skipped**
  without it. **One note, and it is not mine:** the sibling lane's **untracked**
  `apps/ai/tests/test_app_surface.py` asserts the app's OpenAPI path set against a constant
  that still contains `/ai/v1/imports/extract`, so one of its eleven tests now fails. That
  file is the sibling's (it is untracked and it is their work), and its expectation encodes
  the behaviour §7.0 forbids - it needs the service-to-service path taken out of it. **Filed
  for the sibling, not touched here.**
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 53
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** The sentence in §7.0 has three clauses and the product kept two of them.
That is the shape of a defect nobody notices: the clauses are individually small ("absent from
the OpenAPI document" is one flag), and a reader - human or agent - has no reason to check
the third clause when the first two are visibly working. The gate now reads the clause out of
the contract, so the contract and the service cannot drift apart on it.

## 437. D443 · the writer DROPPED three of the schema's columns: every failed run on the plane said nothing about why it failed (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/runs.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_run_columns_are_written.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The `agent_runs` table has exactly one
writer - the INSERT in `api/runs.py` - and it named **22 of the schema's 25 columns**. The
three it dropped were `task_id`, `parent_run_id` and `error`, and two of those are named by the
contract:

* API_CONTRACT §7's conversation-timeline row: *"Each run is its `agent_runs` row
  (`agent_run_id, agent, model, provider, status, plan, ..., input_summary, output_summary,
  tool_calls, retrieval, fact_ids, tokens, cost_usd, latency_ms, **error**, fallback_used,
  started_at, finished_at, **parent_run_id**)"*;
* DATABASE.md §3.12: *"`parent_run_id` for nested agents"*;
* AGENT_CONTRACT §8: *"sub-agents link via `parent_run_id`"*.

Measured on the seeded live plane, before this unit:

```
the agent_runs table: 25 columns, 863 rows
   error          non-null in   0/863 rows
   parent_run_id  non-null in   0/863 rows
   task_id        non-null in   0/863 rows
   the failed runs: 13
   a failed run's error message: <Record status='degraded' error=None>
```

**The defect.** The CALLERS fill `error` - the stream's `_record` and the chat's
`_record_chat` both pass it - and the writer threw it away, because the column was not in the
INSERT. So **every one of the 13 failed runs carried `error = NULL`**: the observability
surface could say a run failed and could not say why. And `parent_run_id` could not be written
at all, so the parent/child tree §8 promises is not a gap in the product's behaviour - it is
a gap in the writer's SQL.

**The fix.** The writer names every column the schema has, and binds one argument per column.

**The gate - and it reads the SCHEMA, not a list.**
`apps/ai/tests/test_run_columns_are_written.py` parses the migration's `CREATE TABLE
agent_runs` and requires the writer's INSERT to name **every** column of it, requires the
placeholders to be contiguous, and requires the argument tuple to bind exactly one argument
per placeholder (counted by the parser, not by lines). The live half writes a failed run and
reads its error back.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **3 passed** (the completeness check, the placeholder/argument check, and the
  live round-trip of a failed run's error)
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1001 passed** with the database, **953 passed / 48 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 53
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** This is §434 (D440) one column over, and the two units together are the
shape of the whole observability ledger: a column that exists and cannot be written is a
promise nobody keeps, and a promise that cannot be kept is invisible - the INSERT succeeds,
the run is written, the row is complete-looking, and the field that would have explained the
failure is simply not there. The gate is the schema, not a list of fields, so the next column
cannot be dropped either: **the writer and the schema are one document, and the gate reads
the schema.**

## 438. D444 · a FAILED merchant-agent chat wrote no run: the error frame was the only trace of a merchant turn that broke (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_stream.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_failed_chat_writes_a_run.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** AGENT_CONTRACT §8: *"Each task writes
`agent_runs`"*. §431 (D431) gave the merchant agent's chat a run - on the success path. The
**error path** was never given one:

```python
    except Exception as exc:  # the same inside-stream error contract as search
        log.exception("merchant-agent stream failed")
        yield ("error", {"code": "internal", "message": str(exc),
                         "request_id": request_id})
```

The search stream's failure path has written its failed run for a long time
(`api/stream.py`: `_record(..., status="failed", error=str(exc), fallback_used="stream_error")`).
So the two surfaces answer the same question the same way, and one of them was silent: a
merchant turn that broke left no row, no status and - before §437 (D443) - no way to say why
it broke.

**The fix.** The chat's failure path writes its run: status `failed`, the error message, and
the same best-effort handling as every other write. The error frame still goes out FIRST -
the user is not waiting on a ledger write - and the run is recorded after it, exactly as the
search stream does.

**The gate - and it makes the chat fail on purpose.**
`apps/ai/tests/test_failed_chat_writes_a_run.py` breaks the chat's retrieval (the retrieval is
the one thing that can fail under a live pool) and then checks that the failure left a run:
`status='failed'`, an error message, and - on the live plane - the row in the table. The
chat only retrieves when it has a pool, so this gate is a live-plane gate: the failure path
does not exist offline, and §427's lesson is that a gate belongs on the plane where the
answer is served.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **2 passed** on the live plane
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1003 passed** with the database, **953 passed / 50 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 53
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note, and a residual that is filed rather than fixed.** The two units D443 and
D444 are one lesson at two depths: a column that cannot be written (D443) and a turn that is
not written (D444). Both are invisible, because the thing that fails is exactly the thing
whose absence nobody notices - a ledger without the error, and a ledger without the failure.

The residual: the JSON endpoints' 5xx paths (the search, the recommendation, the comparison,
the retrieval) still write no run. The reason is not an excuse: **those failures are the
database being unavailable**, so there is no `agent_runs` table to write to, and the in-process
ledger holds the row only for a run with a conversation - a search has none. The chat's failure
is different: the retrieval raised while the database was UP, so its run has somewhere to go,
and now it goes there.

## 439. D445 · the product read the Chinese numerals in ONE place - the weekdays - and not in the two a user writes most: the hour and the party size (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/numerals.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_chinese_numerals.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The time parser reads the weekday numerals
(星期三 ✓). It did not read the hour (九點 ✗) and the party-size matcher did not read them
either (三個人 ✗), so a Hong Kong user who wrote a number the way they spoke was understood in
the weekdays and nowhere else. Measured on the NLU - the first turn, where the answer is served:

```
'3個人食飯'   -> party_size=3      time=None
'三個人食飯'   -> party_size=None   time=None        <- the Chinese numeral
'3个人吃饭'   -> party_size=3      time=None
'三个人吃饭'   -> party_size=None   time=None        <- the Chinese numeral
'2位'         -> party_size=2      time=None
'兩位'         -> party_size=None   time=None        <- the Chinese numeral
'9點食飯'     -> party_size=None   time='explicit'
'九點食飯'     -> party_size=None   time=None        <- the Chinese numeral
'星期三食飯'   -> party_size=None   time='range'     <- the weekday, read all along
```

**The fix - one rule, in one place.** `nlu/numerals.py` holds the digits and the compound
forms a user writes (十 ✓, 十一 ✓, 二十 ✓, 二十三 ✓); the code points were checked against the
Unicode character database, because a writer's memory of a CJK code point is not a reference
(D409). The time parser reads the hour through it, the NLU reads the party size through it, and
the state merger's **second** turn reads it too - the same way the first turn does, which is the
point: the two turns are the same rule.

**The discipline the fix had to respect.** The first attempt read the Chinese ONE as a number,
and the product's OWN tests caught it - two decisions the house has already made and tested:

* "一個人" is the SOLO cue and does not become a party size (an honest reading, not a guess);
* "安靜一點" is a DEGREE, not one o'clock - the product's own end-to-end sentence says "安靜一點"
  and "周六晚上", and its time is Saturday evening.

So the numeral ONE is not read as a number in these two places, while the compound forms are
unaffected (十一個人 is eleven people ✓). The two spellings of a word must meet (§429, D435) -
and the two spellings of a NUMBER now meet too: 三個人 and 3個人 are the same party ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_chinese_numerals.py` reads the digits, the compounds, the
hour in both spellings, the party size in both spellings (first turn AND second turn), the
weekday still reading, and the two decisions above still holding. §429's census was extended to
the new table: it holds the canonical spelling only, like every other vocabulary table.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **8 passed**; the census -> **5 passed** (the numeral table included)
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1011 passed** with the database, **961 passed / 50 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 54
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** This defect was invisible because the product was RIGHT in the one place
the numerals appear in its own data - the weekday - and the tests all wrote Arabic digits. A
gate written in the product's own spelling would have caught it: the D409 lesson (a writer's
memory of a code point is not a reference) has a second half - **a writer's habit is not a
reference either**, and the habits of the people who write the tests are the digits.

## 440. D446 · the Cantonese 禮拜 was never read: the time parser's cue tables were not canonicalised, so their Simplified entries were dead and the Traditional spelling they did not carry was not read at all (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/timeparse.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/canonical.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_timeparse_spellings.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §429 (D435) canonicalised the LEXICON's tables
and found two of them left out; the state merger's cue lists had been canonicalised since
§415 (D421). **The time parser's tables were in neither census** - and they are vocabulary
too: the query is canonicalised before it reaches them, so a Simplified entry in a table that is
not canonicalised can never match, and the Traditional spelling the table does not carry is not
read at all.

Measured on the parser, before this unit:

```
'星期三食飯'  -> range        (the plain weekday)
'礼拜三食飯'  -> range        (the Simplified weekday - the table's entry, which the
                              canonicalisation had already rewritten away: DEAD)
'禮拜三食飯'  -> NOTHING      (the Cantonese weekday - the way a Hong Kong user writes
                              "week" - and the table did not carry it)
'週三食飯'    -> range
'周三食飯'    -> range
```

And the tables behind it: `WEEKDAY_TOKENS` held only the Simplified 礼拜, `NEXT_WEEK_TOKENS`
held the Simplified 來週, `OPEN_LATE_CUES` held the Simplified 還營業, `TODAY_TOKENS` the
Simplified 现在, `PART_OF_DAY` the Simplified 間, `LATE_CUES` 過, `EARLY_CUES` 內 and
`WEEKEND_TOKENS` 雙休 - **every one of them a dead entry**, and every one of them a spelling
the product could not read.

**The fix.**

* the time parser's cue tables are canonicalised at import, like the lexicon's and the merger's -
  one mechanism, one place (`nlu/canonical.py` grew the recursive `canonical_node` the lexicon
  already had, so there is one implementation and not two);
* the text is canonicalised before it is read, so the two spellings of a word meet whichever
  way the user writes it;
* the hour and party markers hold the canonical spellings only - a Simplified marker there
  could never match.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_timeparse_spellings.py` reads the weekday in all five
spellings and requires them to be the SAME day, reads 现在/现在, 聽日/明日 and 週末/周末 in both
spellings, and checks that **every weekday token in the table** is understood. §429's census was
extended to the time parser's tables, so the next table left out is caught.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **6 passed**; the census -> **5 passed** (the time parser's tables included)
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1017 passed** with the database, **967 passed / 50 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 54
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note, and a lesson this unit paid for twice.** The lesson is the census's: **a
check that covers some of the vocabulary is a promise about the rest of it** - §429's census
covered the lexicon and the merger and said nothing about the time parser, and the time parser
was wrong in the same way the lexicon had been. A census is worth exactly as much as its scope.

The lesson this unit paid for twice: while writing the gate, the writer's memory of a CJK code
point failed twice - U+908A is 邊, not 週, and U+908A is not a character the vocabulary carries.
D409's lesson is not "write the escapes carefully"; it is **have a reference that says whether
the character is the one you meant** - the Unicode character database, and now the product's own
vocabulary for the words the product knows.

## 441. D447 · the census was covering less than half the vocabulary: four more tables held dead Simplified entries (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/understand.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_vocabulary_canonical_coverage.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §440 (D446) ended with its own lesson: *"a
census is worth exactly as much as its scope"*. The census covered the lexicon, the state
merger and the time parser. It did not cover `nlu/understand.py` or `nlu/polarity.py` - and
those modules hold cue tables too. The wider census (every module-level table in the NLU
package) found four more:

```
nlu/understand.py   OPEN_PRICE_WORDS     3 non-canonical characters
nlu/understand.py   _BUDGET_WORDS        3 non-canonical characters
nlu/understand.py   _COMPARE_CUES_LOW    4 non-canonical characters
nlu/polarity.py     NEGATION_CUES        1 non-canonical character
```

**What it cost, honestly: nothing today, and that is the point.** The query is canonicalised
before it is compared with a cue table, so a Simplified entry in a table that is not
canonicalised can never match. These four tables hold BOTH spellings - the Traditional forms
were added by §409 (D416) - so the Simplified entries were dead but redundant, and every cue
still fired. Had one of these tables held only the Simplified spelling, its cue would have
been dead exactly as the time parser's weekday was (§440) - and nothing would have said so.

**The fix.** The four tables are canonicalised at import, like the lexicon's, the merger's and
the time parser's - one mechanism, one place - so the vocabulary holds one spelling per word
everywhere, and the census's rule has nothing left to find.

**The gate.** §429's census now covers the WHOLE NLU package: the lexicon, the state merger,
the time parser, the numeral table, the intent module and the polarity module - each with the
list of the tables its own module canonicalises at import.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the census -> **5 passed** (the whole NLU package)
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1017 passed** with the database, **967 passed / 50 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 54
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** This unit's finding is a unit with no user-visible symptom, and it is
still worth its entry - because the symptom it WOULD have had is the one §440 just fixed, in a
different table, and the difference between the two was a census's scope. A defect that is
invisible today is not a defect that cannot become visible: **the tables that hold a
Simplified entry are the tables that will lose their Traditional one the day someone edits
them.**

## 442. D448 · the cost ledger's rows were written on their own schedule, and the foreign key rejected half of them (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/runs.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_live_cost_ledger.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §437 (D437) made the model layer's calls
leave a row in the cost ledger - and the gate passed, because it measured ONE path. The other
two paths were broken, and the breakage was quiet: `llm_calls.agent_run_id` refers to
`agent_runs(id)`, so a ledger row written **before** the run it names is rejected by the foreign
key, and the write is best-effort by design - so the row was dropped and the request answered
as if nothing had happened.

The stream wrote its run in a background task and its ledger row on the request's own
schedule - a race the foreign key wins. The chat wrote the ledger row before the run. The
intent extraction happened to be the one path that was in the right order, and the one path the
gate measured.

**The fix - one recorder, one order.**

* the cost ledger's rows travel SEPARATELY from the run (the run row is served to the browser
  by the timeline endpoint, so it has to stay serialisable - putting the calls in it broke the
  endpoint with "Object of type RoutedCall is not JSON serializable");
* the recorder that writes the run writes the ledger rows immediately after it, in the one
  order the foreign key allows - so no path can get it wrong, and there is no schedule to race
  against.

**The gate - and it now covers the path that was broken.**
`apps/ai/tests/test_live_cost_ledger.py` asks the live plane for the ledger row of an intent
extraction (the row, the run it names, and the tokens they agree on) and **makes a stream
request and waits for its ledger row** - the path that was silently broken.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **4 passed** (the row, the agreement, and the stream's row)
- the live plane -> **`llm_calls` 428 rows** (it was 0 when §437 started) and **442 runs
  carrying tokens** (they were 0)
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1018 passed** with the database, **967 passed / 51 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 54
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** This is §440's lesson for the ledger: **a gate is worth exactly as much as
the paths it walks.** §437's gate walked one path and found the ledger working; the other two
were broken, and they were broken in the way that fails quietly - a best-effort write that
reports nothing when the database says no. The gate now walks the stream as well, and the
recorder no longer leaves the order to chance: the ledger's row and the run it names are one
write, in one order, from one place.

## 443. D449 · five tables the product carried and read by nothing - and one of them had gone out of date and was WRONG (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_discover.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/contract.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_no_dead_constants.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** A census of the package's definitions - the
same sweep that found §437's unused row builder - found five module-level constants that
**nothing read**:

```
api/routes_discover.py   _COMPARE_ATTRIBUTES   the comparison grid's attribute list
contract.py              EVENT_NAMES            the canonical event names (§10)
nlu/lexicon.py           ASSUMED_TOKENS         the English filler words
nlu/state_merger.py      PARTY_CUES             the "we" cues
trust/verification.py    _KIND_ORDER            the verification's kind order
```

**And one of them was wrong.** `_COMPARE_ATTRIBUTES` named the rows the comparison grid
carries - and it had gone out of date: it said `open_hours` (the grid's row is **`open_state`**,
since §422) and `availability` (a row the grid does not have). The grid itself builds its
rows explicitly, so the list was a comment with a name - and the comment was the one that
nobody updated, exactly as one expects of a comment nobody reads.

**The fix.** The five are gone, each with a note saying where the truth now lives (the grid
builds its rows; AGENT_CONTRACT §10 is the one place the event names live; the tokeniser
carries the filler list; the merge reads the party size with a regex, like the first turn
does - §439; the verification walks its kinds in its own order).

**The gate - the class, not the five.**
`apps/ai/tests/test_no_dead_constants.py` requires that **every module-level constant in the
package is read by the package**. A constant that is written and never read is either a
promise to wire something up or a leftover, and both are the writer's business - not the next
reader's.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **1 passed**; the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1019 passed** with the database,
  **968 passed / 51 skipped** without it (the sibling lane's untracked
  `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 54
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** The five were harmless and one was wrong, and that is the point: a dead
list is a place where the product's description of itself rots, and it rots *quietly*, because
nothing reads it and nothing fails. The list that says what the comparison grid carries is
the list a reader would trust - so it had better be the code that builds the grid, and the
gate that says the code builds it.

## 444. D450 · five functions nothing called either - and one of them was reading state this service must never read (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_no_dead_constants.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §443 (D449) took the census to the package's
**constants**. The same sweep finds the **functions** - and five of them were called by nothing:

```
search/cards.py        _existing_fact_for          a one-line wrapper over bundle.get()
nlu/polarity.py        _is_cjk                     a one-line CJK check
api/runs.py            _uuid_array_sql             a uuid[] SQL builder
nlu/state_merger.py    now_in_hk                   the Hong Kong clock
nlu/state_merger.py    session_state_from_context  the carried-state reader
```

**And one of them was wrong in a way that matters.** `session_state_from_context` read the
carried state out of `context["state"]` - the shape of `conversations.state` (§34). This
service does not read the platform's conversations (§34, D20: the platform owns every
conversation write), so the function could only ever have read a state the caller happened to
paste in - and it read it in a way nothing else in the product does. A dead function that
invents a second way in is worse than a dead function that does not.

**The fix.** The five are gone, each with a note saying where the truth lives now (the callers
read the bundle directly; the polarity module's own window check; the writer binds the fact
ids and lets Postgres cast them; the time parser owns HK_TZ; the merge takes the state the
caller passes it, and this service never reads the platform's conversations.state).

**The gate - the class, extended.** `apps/ai/tests/test_no_dead_constants.py` now also requires
that **every module-level function in the package is called somewhere**. A function the
framework calls (a route handler) is decorated, and is exempt; a function nothing calls is
dead unless a test calls it - which is a use.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **2 passed**; the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1020 passed** with the database,
  **969 passed / 51 skipped** without it (the sibling lane's untracked
  `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 54
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** A dead function is cheaper than a dead table - nobody writes a test
against it, so it cannot fail - which is exactly why it is the better place for a wrong
assumption to hide. `session_state_from_context` was a whole second way for the product to
read a conversation's state, and the second way disagreed with the first (§34 and D20). The
census does not only remove clutter: it removes the places where the product could quietly
disagree with itself.

## 445. D451 · a degraded answer came back with NO degraded header: the recommendation and the intent extraction said `degraded: true` and said nothing else (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/degraded.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_degraded_header.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** OBSERVABILITY.md §2, on a degraded answer:

> the response carried `X-Nexus-Degraded` plus the UI "降級模式" badge. **A degraded answer
> that looks like a normal answer is an observability failure even when the request returned
> 200.**

Measured on the live plane, before this unit:

```
/ai/v1/search           -> 200  the header: 'false'  the body's degraded: False
/ai/v1/recommend        -> 200  the header: None    the body's degraded: True   <- no header
/ai/v1/query/understand -> 200  the header: None    the body's degraded: True   <- no header
/ai/v1/rag/retrieve     -> 200  the header: None
```

The search set the header from its own response; the two endpoints that ALSO carry a
`degraded` field set no header at all. The middleware set the header when the **backend** was
degraded - a different signal: an answer can be degraded while the backend is perfectly fine
(the model layer fell back to the rules), and then the answer said so in its body and nowhere
else. The client that is supposed to show the "降級模式" badge reads the header.

**The fix - one place, so the two cannot disagree.**

* `api/degraded.py` builds a response that carries the flag in the body AND in the header;
* the search, the recommendation and the intent extraction answer through it;
* the middleware now OVERRIDES the header with "true" when the backend is degraded - the
  backend being down degrades every answer, whatever the route said about its own.

**The gate - the class.** `apps/ai/tests/test_degraded_header.py` walks every endpoint that
answers with a `degraded` field, requires the header to be present, and requires it to AGREE
with the body - and requires it to be present on a healthy answer too, so a client can tell
"not degraded" from "not reported".

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **2 passed**; the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1022 passed** with the database,
  **971 passed / 51 skipped** without it (the sibling lane's untracked
  `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** The product had TWO answers to "is this answer degraded?" - the body and
the header - and they were read from two different places: the body by the route, the header
by the middleware. §438 (D438) was the same shape in a different guise (seven hand-built error
envelopes and one model that nothing used). The general rule keeps being the same one: **a
fact the product states in two places must be stated from one place** - and when it is not, the
two copies disagree, and the one a client reads is the one nobody checks.

## 446. D452 · the degraded-header fix covered three of SIX endpoints: the feedback, the conversation timeline and the tool manifest still said `degraded` and nothing else (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_system.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_conversations.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_degraded_header.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §445 (D451) made the degraded flag travel in
the body AND the header - and the gate it came with walked **three** endpoints. A census of
every response that carries a `degraded` field says there are **six**:

```
/ai/v1/search            -> 200  the header: 'false'  the body's degraded: False
/ai/v1/recommend         -> 200  the header: 'true'   the body's degraded: True
/ai/v1/query/understand  -> 200  the header: 'true'   the body's degraded: True
/ai/v1/feedback          -> 200  the header: None     the body's degraded: False   <- no header
/ai/v1/conversations/{id}-> 200  the header: None     the body's degraded: False   <- no header
/ai/v1/tools             -> 200  the header: None     the body's degraded: True    <- no header
```

The tool manifest is the one that matters most: it says `degraded: true` **permanently** - the
dispatch registry is not built (§3, §11) - and a client reading the header saw nothing at all.
The conversation timeline says `degraded` when its read fell back to the in-process ledger,
and the feedback says it when the event could not be written.

**The fix.** The same builder answers those three as well, so all six carry the flag in the
body and the header, from one place.

**The gate - and it now walks all six.**
`apps/ai/tests/test_degraded_header.py` walks every endpoint that answers with a `degraded`
field - the four that take a body and the two that do not - and requires the header to be
present and to AGREE with the body.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **2 passed**; the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1022 passed** with the database,
  **971 passed / 51 skipped** without it (the sibling lane's untracked
  `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** This is §442 (D448)'s lesson, a day later and in a different room: the
gate that found the defect walked three paths, and three more responses were saying the same
thing in the same wrong way. A fix that lands with a gate is only as wide as the gate's
scope, and a gate's scope is a decision somebody has to make every time - so the honest
version of a gate is the one that **censors** the surface (every response that carries the
field) rather than the one that lists the paths somebody remembered.

## 447. D453 · the test files' Chinese was never checked: two wrong code points were living in them, one of them in a table nothing read (`apps/ai/tests/test_vocabulary_is_the_reference.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_merge_cue_spellings.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §422 (D434) made the vocabulary the reference
for a CJK code point - but it walked **one** surface (the evaluation's intent cases) and it
kept its reference as a **hand-written** list of twenty tables. Two things followed from that:

* the surface: the test files - a hundred and two files of Chinese - were unchecked, and a
  wrong code point is exactly what lives there;
* the reference: a list somebody has to remember to update is a list that goes out of date,
  which is the same defect §435 and §447 found in the census.

**The fix - the reference is derived, and the scope is the whole surface.**

* the reference is now every Chinese character the product's own package carries - its **data**,
  not its prose - so a new vocabulary table, a new template or a new label is in the
  reference the moment it exists. The evaluation package is excluded: the suite being judged
  cannot define what the judge knows (that would be circular);
* the scope is the **whole test directory**, not the paths somebody remembered (§446's lesson);
* twenty-seven characters the product has no business knowing are **DECLARED** - a grammatical
  word, a brand, an attack's payload, a demo merchant's name - each entry carrying the Unihan
  database's own gloss of it and what the test that uses it is doing.

**What the wider gate found.**

* **U+95A9** ("Fujian province; a river; a tribe") written where **U+95F9** ("quarrel;
  dispute hotly") belongs - in a table **nothing read**. The dead `PAIRS` table of
  `tests/test_merge_cue_spellings.py` was the §443 class: a dead table is where the product's
  description of itself rots, and it rots quietly. The table is gone; the pairs it listed are
  asserted one by one below it, where each one says what it must do.
* **U+5584** ("good, virtuous, charitable, kind") written where **U+5566** ("final particle of
  assertion" - the Cantonese negation) belongs - in a test that **PASSED**, because the cue
  that fired was the other word in the same phrase: the merge's own `OPEN_NOW_CUES` carries
  the correct spelling, and the typo rode in on a different cue.
* a UTF-8 byte order mark on `tests/test_db_pool.py` - invisible in the source, and it breaks
  every reader that opens the file as plain UTF-8 (this gate included).

Every code point here was confirmed against the Unihan database (`Unihan_Readings.txt`,
`kDefinition`), never against a memory: the writer's memory of a CJK code point is not a
reference (§409, §446). The oracle contradicted the writer's guess on several of them - which
