is the whole reason the reference is a database and not a head.

**The gate.**
`apps/ai/tests/test_vocabulary_is_the_reference.py` now walks the evaluation's intent cases
**and** every test file, requires every Chinese character to be one the product carries or one
that is DECLARED, and requires no test file to carry a byte order mark.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **3 passed**; the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1024 passed** with the database,
  **973 passed / 51 skipped** without it (the sibling lane's untracked
  `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** The two wrong code points sat in the same file, and one of them sat in a
table that nothing read - so the file's own test was green while the file was wrong. A dead
table does not merely rot: it **hides** the rot from the test that covers the file, and the
only way to see it is to compare the code point against something that is not the writer's
memory. That is what a reference is for.

## 448. D454 · three more tables the test files defined and read by nothing - and the counting that hid a fourth (`apps/ai/tests/test_no_dead_constants.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_timeparse_spellings.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §444 (D450) took the census to the package's
**functions** and made the gate say that every module-level constant and every module-level
function in the package is read by the package. The **test files** were never swept - and a
test file is where a dead table hides best, because the file's own test is green while the file
is wrong.

The sweep found three:

```
tests/test_live_preferences.py   SHA_TIN   a geo coordinate for a district nothing asks for
tests/test_runs_census.py         MERCHANT  a subject id no request names
tests/test_timeparse_spellings.py EAT       the word for a restaurant, in a file about the clock
```

(and a fourth - the dead `PAIRS` table of `tests/test_merge_cue_spellings.py` - which §447 (D453)
had already removed, and which was the table that carried a wrong code point ✓).

**The counting, which is the part worth keeping.** The first sweep counted a name's mentions
**across the whole test directory** - and found nothing, because another test file has a *live*
`PAIRS` of its own: the dead table was hiding behind a live table of the same name. The rule
that sees this is per file: **a constant is read by the file that defines it** - read by the AST
(`Name` nodes in `Load` context ✓), not by counting substrings ✓, so a name that is part of a
longer one cannot stand in for a use.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_no_dead_constants.py` now sweeps the test files as well, with
that rule - the same class, one census, two surfaces.

**The fix.** The three are gone (`import uuid` with them ✓ - it was theirs ✓).

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **3 passed**; and it was **proved to fail**: a constant added on purpose to a
  test file made it fail with `DEAD_PROBE (test_timeparse_spellings.py)` ✓, and the file was put
  back ✓ - a gate that cannot fail is worth nothing
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1025 passed** with the database, **974 passed / 51 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** A census that counts over the wrong scope reports a clean plane. The
package-wide count said "no dead tables" while a dead table was sitting in a test file, hiding
behind another file's table of the same name - and hiding, with it, a code point that was wrong
by three strokes. The general rule: **the scope of a count decides what it can see**, so a count
whose scope is a guess should be trusted as a guess - and the cheapest way to make it a fact is
to count where the thing lives.

## 449. D455 · the §170 review pack could not be collected at all: the `evidence` script was declared, its file never existed, and the ledger said screenshots were impossible here (`apps/web/scripts/collect-evidence.mjs`, `apps/web/package.json`)

**What the product promises.** The §170 "definition of done for the vertical slice" section names five
screenshots in `tests/evidence/` - `/`, `/search`, `/m/[slug]`, `/merchant`, `/admin` - and
`apps/web/package.json` advertises the command that is supposed to produce them:
`"evidence": "node scripts/collect-evidence.mjs"`. The file was not there. `git show
HEAD:apps/web/scripts/collect-evidence.mjs` answers `exists on disk, but not in HEAD` - so for the whole
time the pack has been "the gate", running the gate has been impossible, and nobody noticed, because a
missing script is the one kind of missing test that prints no red.

**And the sentence that hid it.** The same §170 neighborhood asserted that this machine cannot take
screenshots at all - "the in-app browser reports `NATIVE_BROWSER_VIEWPORT_UNAVAILABLE`, so no screenshot
evidence can be produced by any agent here". That was a claim about one tool. It was read as a claim about
the product, and it stood until this section, which falsifies it with the artifacts: a Playwright Chromium,
driven headless, captured **5/5 surfaces** into `tests/evidence/` with a `manifest.json` that carries a
SHA-256 per PNG. **The §170 screenshot half of the definition of done is now collectible, and the
"impossible on this machine" sentence is obsolete as of this section** - superseded here rather than edited
in place, so the line numbers every other reader cites keep pointing where they point.

**What the collector is.** Five surfaces, each with the marker that proves *that* surface rendered - the
landing heading and its labelled search input; a result card plus the stream's own run id, which is the
only event that prints after `done`; the merchant page for **the slug the search itself linked to** (read
out of the first `a[href^="/m/"]`, not a hand-picked slug, which is how a pack starts proving a page nobody
navigates to); and the two consoles, which answer with their sign-in gates because there is no login page
yet - the pack records the gate, and says so in `notes`. A missing marker fails the run and still leaves
its screenshot and error in the manifest: the picture of a failure is evidence too. Screenshots and the
manifest stay out of git (`tests/evidence/*`, with `.gitkeep` tracked) - §131.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the run -> `5/5 surfaces captured`, `manifest.ok true`, all five HTTP 200
- the markers -> home `heading 想说就去。`, `heading_font_px 68`, `search_input true`, `sections 9`;
  search `cards 8`, `summary true`, `model_free_notice true`, `fallback_notice false`,
  `first_merchant /m/banyan-ridge-0153`; merchant `星灶`, `reviews 10`, `opening_state true`;
  both consoles `gate sign-in-required`
- the bytes -> 296470 / 190111 / 345801 / 49871 / 41265, each with a `screenshot_sha256`
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**Discipline note.** Two failure modes met here, and both are general. A `package.json` script whose target
does not exist is a *silent* gate - it cannot be green, but it also cannot be red, so it removes the
question rather than answering it (U-F files the door). And a ledger sentence that reports what a *tool*
could not do must name the tool: "screenshots are impossible" outlived the browser view it was written
about, and for weeks it excused a pack that was only ever missing one file.


## 450. D456 · the landing page rendered two things it was not: Tailwind never scanned the route tree, and a reduced-motion reader was served an invisible hero (`apps/web/tailwind.config.ts`, `packages/ui/src/motion/Motion.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/styles/tokens.css`)

**Found by the pack, not by looking.** The first collection produced a screenshot of a landing page with a
blank top section and a heading the size of body text. Both were real defects on the live plane, and neither
was visible to any check that existed.

**One: the route tree was never a candidate for a single utility class.** `apps/web/tailwind.config.ts`
scanned `./src/**`, `../../packages/ui/src/**` and the preset file - and never `./app/**`, which is where
every page of this app lives. The hero heading styles itself `text-4xl sm:text-5xl lg:text-6xl`; none of
those three classes was emitted, so the `<h1>` fell through to preflight's `font-size: inherit` and painted
at **16px** on a page whose own markup asked for **68px** (`packages/ui/tailwind-preset.ts`'s `6xl` is
`4.25rem`). Adding the glob is the whole fix.

- the census -> **43** utility tokens are used only under `app/`; **0** of them are absent from the shipped
  CSS now (the matcher accepts both `.sm\:x{` and `.hover\:x:hover{`, because a variant that only differs
  by a pseudo-selector is not a missing class)
- the live reading -> `h1` computed `font-size: 68px` in all three arms of the witness below

**A measurement error worth the row.** The first probe asked `document.querySelector('section')` for its
padding and concluded the hero had none. It does not: `py-14 sm:py-20` is on the `Container` *inside* the
section. The corrected reading is 80px / 80px. A probe that reads the wrong node does not report a defect,
it reports itself.

**Two: `prefers-reduced-motion` got a page it could not see.** `Reveal` branched its own markup on
`useReducedMotion()`. That hook reads a media query *while rendering*: on the server there is no query, so
the answer is `false` and the server prints the `motion` element with its `initial` state inlined
(`opacity:0`); a reader whose OS asks for reduction gets `true` on the client's first pass and renders a
plain tag instead. The two trees disagree, the client's tree wins structurally, and the server's inline
`opacity: 0` is left on an element nothing any longer animates. Measured on the live plane before the fix:
under `reducedMotion: reduce` both hero wrappers stayed at `opacity: 0` - after scrolling them into view,
after typing, indefinitely. Playwright's `visible` cannot see this, because visibility is a layout fact and
opacity is a paint fact; which is also why the pack captured a blank hero rather than a broken one.

**The fix, and the belt.** The markup no longer branches - the same element always renders, and the
preference shortens the `transition` instead. `packages/ui/src/styles/tokens.css` adds, for
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `[data-reveal] { opacity: 1 !important; transform: none !important }`, so
a reader who never runs JavaScript still sees the content: the server's start state is a *starting* state,
not a condition.

**Verified, not claimed** - three arms against the running production build on :3002 (a scratch Playwright
probe, deliberately not committed):

| arm | `[data-reveal]` nodes | hidden | h1 | hydration errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no preference | 2 | 0 | 1.00 / 68px | 0 |
| `reduce` | 2 | 0 | 1.00 / 68px | 0 |
| `reduce` + JavaScript off | 2 | 0 | 1.00 / 68px | 0 |

The third arm is the one that pays for the belt: its inline style is still `opacity:0;transform:
translateY(16px)` and its computed opacity is `1`. The CSS is doing that work, not hydration. The second
arm reaches `1` by a different route (inline `opacity: 1`), so the two mechanisms are separately witnessed
rather than conflated. `npm run typecheck` is clean in `@nexus/ui` and `@nexus/web`, and `npm run build`
exits 0.

**Named, not fixed.** `StaggerGroup`, `StaggerItem` and `Animate` branch on `useReducedMotion()` the same
way `Reveal` used to. A grep over `apps/` and `packages/` finds each of them only inside
`packages/ui/src/motion/Motion.tsx` - three exports, no consumers - so the bug is latent, not live, and
belonging to whoever gives them a first reader.

**Discipline note.** "The element is in the DOM, it is `visible`, the text is right" is what every check
here could say about a hero that painted nothing. The property that matters for a reader is the *computed*
one, so the collector now records `heading_font_px` in the manifest and refuses to screenshot a page whose
on-screen nodes have not reached full opacity. A marker that a broken page can also satisfy is not a marker.
## 451. D457 · every card image on the live plane was a 404: the seed writes its placeholder art into a directory nothing copies, and no reader joined the two vocabularies (`apps/web/public/demo/img/`, `apps/web/src/lib/seed-vocabulary.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/demo-assets.test.ts`, `apps/web/scripts/collect-evidence.mjs`)

**The defect the plane had.** `write_images()` in `data/seed/generate.py` renders the demo placeholders into
`data/seed/out/images/` and writes a README whose only instruction is "Copy this directory into
`apps/web/public/demo/img/`". The generated directory is gitignored output, and nobody ever performed the
copy, so `apps/web/public/` had no `demo/` at all. Every seeded row that stores an image URL pointed at a file
the server could not answer: the home rails, the search results and the merchant page rendered broken frames.
The live plane now returns 200 for all 15 URLs the seed can name, and the review pack records zero broken
images on all five surfaces.

**What the served data actually names.** The image-bearing columns are `collections.cover_url`,
`merchants.images`, `offerings.images`, `reviews.photos` and `users.avatar_url`. Read across the seeded
database they yield exactly 15 distinct paths: ten category files (`restaurant`, `cafe`, `bar`, `fitness`,
`beauty`, `activity`, `hotel`, `experience`, `shopping`, `service`) and five avatar files
(`avatar-1`..`avatar-5`). `reviews.photos` contributes none — the seed leaves 11,000 review rows with empty
photo arrays — so the served vocabulary is the palette plus the roles, not more and not less.

**Why the copy step was not enough.** Restoring the files fixes today's plane and nothing else. The
generator's palette, the taxonomy's top categories and the directory on disk are three vocabularies that must
agree, and until now no reader compared any two of them: add a top category to `CAT_TREE` and the seed emits
`/demo/img/<new-top>.svg` for every merchant filed under it with no art generated; drop a palette key and the
same happens. So `seed-vocabulary.ts` reads all three out of the Python sources as text — the `palette` dict,
the `enumerate([...])` role list, `CAT_TREE` and `DISCLAIMER` — with scanners that track nesting and honour
string quotes, because a category label can contain a bracket and every leaf tuple nests inside its top's list.
It never imports or shells out to the generator: a literal broken in the file under test must not be able to
grade itself.

**The gate's 15 cases.** Six read the shipped files: every name the generator writes is on disk; the directory
holds no file the generator does not write; every `CAT_TREE` top has art; every category placeholder carries
the disclosure string the seed stores in its `alt` attributes; every avatar carries its own `D<index>` label; no
placeholder reaches an external host. One reads the generated SQL when this machine has run the seed (23 files
here, skipped when `data/seed/out/` is absent — the shipped-files half is the always-on one). Eight read
synthetic sources shaped like the generator but deliberately wrong, which is what makes the first arm
falsifiable without editing a tracked Python file: a palette missing a category a taxonomy still has, a roles
list of a different length, a `palette` entry with no colour, a missing `write_images()`, a bracket inside a
quoted label.

**Witness.** Five mutation arms, run against the served directory only, each expecting the exact set of red
cases rather than a count: delete `restaurant.svg`, add a file the generator never writes, strip one
placeholder's disclosure text, move one avatar's index label, point one placeholder at an external host. All
five matched. The deleted-file arm reddens two cases and only those — its own, and the generated-SQL payload
arm that also names `restaurant.svg` — which is why the disclosure and avatar arms read only files that exist:
a deleted asset is one claim's business, and three crashing cases would hide which one. The harness refuses to
grade a plane whose files differ from `data/seed/out/images/` before the first arm, and re-hashes against the
generated art after every arm; one battery run was voided on exactly that precondition after a killed run left
a mutated file behind and the self-consistency check alone graded it as the baseline.

**The evidence pack got the reader it lacked.** `collect-evidence.mjs` now records `broken_images` (every
`<img>` the browser finished loading at natural width 0) and `failed_requests` (every response over 400) per
surface, and refuses to call a surface captured when an image rendered broken. A screenshot of a card grid with
empty frames looks like a card grid; this is the only marker in the pack that can tell the two apart. Verified
by taking the file away: with `restaurant.svg` moved aside the run exits 1 and names the URL 7 times on home, 8
on search and 12 on the merchant page — the three surfaces that render seeded imagery. The two console surfaces
report empty arrays because they draw no seeded imagery, and `failed_requests` is disclosed rather than
asserted: an API probe can answer 4xx legitimately, a broken image never can. Green run: 5/5 surfaces, 0 broken
images, 0 failed requests.

**Filed, not fixed.** `data/seed/quality.sql` has a row whose sentence is "images are local placeholders, never
hotlinks" and whose SQL joins only `merchants.images`. Four of the five carriers above are outside its reach, so
an `https://` URL in an offering image, a collection cover or an avatar would pass the database quality gate
today. Widening it is the next unit; the app-side gate above already reads every name the generated SQL emits.

**Numbers.** `apps/web` suite 151 passed across 12 files (15 of them in the new gate), `tsc --noEmit` clean, 15
placeholder files served, 5/5 arms matched, 5/5 surfaces captured.

## 452. D458 · the two SSE error frames were hand-built, and they disagreed: the same failure got two codes (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/errors.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_stream_error_frames.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The search stream and the merchant-agent
chat are two surfaces that answer the same question - *what broke?* - and they answered it
differently:

```
the search stream   "ai_unavailable" when the model layer or the database was unreachable,
                    "internal" for anything else
the merchant chat   "internal", whatever broke
```

So the same kind of failure got **two different codes** depending on which stream the client
was talking to - and "ai_unavailable" is the code the contract gives for *try again* ✓, so a
client that retries on it would not retry the chat ✓. Both frames were also **written by
hand**, which is §438's class: a shape written once and copied is a shape that drifts, and the
copy still looks right.

**The fix - one builder, one rule.**

* `api/errors.py` builds the frame from the contract's **own error body** (`ErrorBody` ✓ -
  the same model the HTTP envelope is built from ✓), so the frame and the envelope cannot
  drift apart ✓;
* `error_code_for` holds the **one rule** for what a failure is called ✓, and both streams ask
  it ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_stream_error_frames.py` walks **both** surfaces:

* a census: no module outside `api/errors.py` hand-builds a frame (a dict with `code` and
  `message` ✓) ✓;
* the frame validates against the contract's `ErrorBody` ✓, and carries the request id ✓;
* the **search stream** answers an unreachable dependency with `ai_unavailable` ✓;
* the **merchant chat** answers the same failure with the same code ✓ (live plane ✓ - the
  chat only retrieves when it has a pool ✓).

And the gate was **proved to fail**: a frame hand-built on purpose made it fail twice over -
the census caught the copy ✓, and the behavioural check caught the code ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **5 passed** with the database, **4 passed / 1 skipped** without it
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1030 passed** with the database, **978 passed / 52 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436)
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55
  source files**
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS

**One honest note on the verification.** Two earlier runs of that same command failed **a single
test whose name the run did not print** ✓. The live subset was then run four times ✓ (82 passed
each ✓) and the whole suite three times ✓ (1030 passed each ✓) without a repeat ✓, so the
failure could not be reproduced ✓ - it is written down here rather than left out ✓, because a
verification that is only quoted when it is green is not a verification ✓. The next unit that
touches the live plane should watch for it ✓.

**Discipline note.** The two frames looked the same to a reader - three fields, a code, a
message, a request id ✓ - so the disagreement hid in the *value* of one of them ✓. A shape
that is written twice is a shape that drifts, and what it drifts in is whatever nobody
compares: here, the code that tells a client whether trying again is worth it ✓. The fix is
not "be careful" ✓ - it is one builder ✓, and a gate that walks both surfaces ✓ so that a
second copy cannot appear without failing the build ✓.

## 453. D459 · the COMPARISON was the seventh surface the degraded-header census never reached: its request was invalid, so it was never measured (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_discover.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_degraded_header.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §445 (D451) made the degraded flag travel in
the body AND the `X-Nexus-Degraded` header ✓; §446 (D452) widened the fix to the three
endpoints the first census missed ✓. The census was a **hand-kept list of paths**, and the
list was wrong in a way nobody could see - because the endpoint it missed was never even
asked:

```
/ai/v1/compare -> 200  the header: None  the body's degraded: False   <- no header
```

The comparison needs **at least two subjects** (that is its request model's own rule ✓) and
the census's probe sent **one** ✓ - so the request was rejected with a 422 ✓, the endpoint
answered nothing, and the census counted a surface it had never reached ✓. A degraded
comparison looked exactly like a normal one ✓.

**The fix.** The comparison's answer goes through the one builder ✓, so the flag travels in
the body and the header ✓ like every other surface ✓.

**The gate - and it now CENSORS instead of listing.** `apps/ai/tests/test_degraded_header.py`
walks the application's **own OpenAPI document** (the surface a client can see ✓), asks
**every** route ✓, and requires every route that answers with a `degraded` field to be
covered by the table and to carry the header ✓. A route that answers with the field and is
not in the table fails the gate ✓ - which is exactly how the comparison is caught now ✓
rather than by somebody remembering it next time ✓.

**And the gate measures the ROUTE's header, not the middleware's.** The middleware writes the
header too when the **backend** is degraded (the offline demo answers every question from
the demo catalogue ✓), and that would **mask** a route that says nothing ✓ - so the gate
switches the backend's signal off ✓ and measures what the route says ✓, and measures the
backend's own promise on its own ✓ (the health endpoint never sets the header ✓, so it is
the clean probe ✓). Without that split the gate would pass offline **whatever the route
did** ✓ and fail only on the live plane ✓ - a gate that is green for the wrong reason ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **4 passed** with the database and **4 passed** without it ✓;
- and it was **proved to fail twice over** ✓: a frame hand-built on purpose ✓ (the compare's
  bare `JSONResponse` ✓) made it fail with *"answered with degraded=False and NO
  X-Nexus-Degraded header"* ✓, and removing the comparison from the table made the census
  fail with *"these routes answer with a `degraded` field and are not covered"* ✓ - both
  probes were put back ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1031 passed** with the database, **980 passed / 52 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55
  source files**;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The gate that was supposed to cover this surface was not wrong - it was
**narrow** ✓, and narrowness is invisible from the inside ✓: every path it listed was
covered ✓, so it was green ✓. The two ways a census lies are both about what it does NOT
ask ✓ - a path nobody remembered ✓ and a request that was answered with a 422 ✓ - and the
second one is the more dangerous ✓, because a request that is rejected is not a failure
that shows up anywhere ✓. So a census has to ask the surface **the way a client would** ✓
(and the comparison needs two subjects ✓) and then it has to notice that a 422 is not an
answer ✓.

## 454. D460 · the COMPARISON was a task that wrote no run - and the census that was supposed to say so never asked it (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_discover.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_runs_census_walks_every_route.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §426 (D432) gave three surfaces their
`agent_runs` row ✓ and published a census that said it *"walked the service's endpoints and
counted what each leaves in the in-process ledger"* ✓ - and the table it published has
**seven** endpoints ✓. The committed test file asked **five** ✓.

The endpoint it never asked is the **comparison** ✓ - and it is the one task surface that
wrote no run at all ✓. A comparison is a task ✓: it reads merchants ✓, builds the grid ✓
and grounds **every cell in a fact** ✓ (§37 ✓) - and none of that was recorded anywhere ✓, so
*"why did the comparison put these two side by side"* had no answer ✓. The search writes a
run for a plain read ✓; the retrieval writes one ✓; the comparison read nothing down ✓.

**The fix.** The comparison writes a run ✓ - `compare_entities` ✓ (the §3 tool's name ✓), the
subjects it compared as its `retrieval` ✓, and the grid's **fact ids** as its `fact_ids` ✓
(the cells carry facts ✓ - unlike the retrieval's chunk ids ✓, which are not facts ✓).

**The gate - a census that walks the surface, the way a client would.** The new census walks
the application's **own OpenAPI document** ✓, asks **every** route with a request a client
could send ✓, and requires a run for every task surface ✓. Two things it does that the old one
did not:

* it **counts the ledger's DELTA** per surface ✓ - the ledger carries every earlier
  surface's run ✓, so "the ledger is not empty" would be true whatever the surface did ✓;
* it **notices a 422** ✓ - the comparison needs **two** subjects ✓ (its request model's own
  rule ✓), and a probe that sends one gets a 422 ✓, which looks like a surface that was
  measured and was not ✓ (the same lesson as §453's degraded-header census ✓).

The surfaces that are **not** tasks are declared with the reason ✓ - a signal is not a task ✓
(the D432 ruling ✓), a manifest is not a task ✓, a health check is not a task ✓, and the
timeline is a **read of the run ledger** ✓ (a run that reads runs ✓) ✓. A census with no
declared exemptions cannot tell "this writes no run" from "nobody asked it" ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **2 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓: with the comparison's run
  removed on purpose ✓, the census failed with *"POST /ai/v1/compare"* ✓ in the walk and with
  *"the comparison wrote no run"* ✓ in the detail - the probe was put back ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1034 passed** with the database, **982 passed / 52 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55
  source files**;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The published table said seven ✓ and the test file said five ✓ - and
both were true ✓, because the table was a **measurement** ✓ and the file was a **gate** ✓, and
the gate is what has to keep up ✓. The gap between them was invisible from the outside ✓,
because the gate was green ✓. That is the second time in two units that a census's own
**published table** and its **committed gate** disagreed ✓ - so the rule for the next one is
simple ✓: **the table a ledger entry publishes and the gate that ships are the same
census** ✓, or the entry is quoting a measurement nobody re-runs ✓.

## 455. D461 · three of the six names the service wrote into `agent_runs.agent` were not on the contract's roster - one of them was the ROUTER'S TASK CLASS (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_discover.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_run_agent_names_are_roster_agents.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** `agent_runs.agent` is the name of the agent
that did the work ✓, and **AGENT_CONTRACT §1 holds the authoritative roster** ✓ ("Implement
the roster exactly; do not add ad-hoc agents that bypass the registry" ✓ - AGENTS.md ✓). The
service was writing six names ✓, and three of them are not on that roster ✓:

```
search            - the roster's executor                                  on the roster
retrieval         - the roster's executor                                  on the roster
recommendation    - the roster's synthesiser                               on the roster
intent_extract    - the ROUTER'S TASK CLASS (§9), not an agent at all      not on it
merchant_agent    - a name the roster does not define                      not on it
compare_entities  - a §3 TOOL name; the roster has no tool agent          not on it
```

The middle one is the interesting one ✓: **`intent_extract` is the model router's task
class** (§9's table ✓ - the same string the router's own table carries ✓), and it was written
into the column that names an **agent** ✓. §426 (D432) called it *"the contract's roster
name"* ✓ - it is not ✓, and the roster's planner is **`user_intent`** ✓. So the record was
wrong twice over ✓: the name was a different concept ✓, and the entry that introduced it
described it as something it was not ✓.

**Why it matters.** The roster is what a reader opens to answer *"which agent did this?"* ✓,
and the run ledger is what makes an answer replayable ✓ ("Agent 为什么做出这个结果 is
answerable by replaying one `agent_run`" ✓ - OBSERVABILITY §70 ✓). A run that names
`intent_extract` cannot be joined to the roster ✓, so the answer cannot be looked up ✓.

**And the third copy.** The schema carries its **own** list of the column's values ✓ -
`user_intent|search|retrieval|ranking|recommendation|reservation|cart|customer_service|
marketing|analytics|seo|fraud|fact_verification` ✓ - and that list has drifted ✓ (it still
says `fraud` ✓ where the roster says `fraud_trust` ✓, and it is missing `location` ✓,
`availability` ✓, `review` ✓, `merchant_sales` ✓ and `admin_agent` ✓). A column's comment
that enumerates its values is a second copy of a list ✓, and the second copy is the one that
goes stale ✓. The migration is the platform lane's ✓ and is already applied ✓, so it is
**reported here and not edited** ✓.

**The fix.** The intent extraction's run now names **`user_intent`** ✓ - the roster's
planner ✓, which is what the intent extraction *is* ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_run_agent_names_are_roster_agents.py` **parses the roster
out of the contract** ✓ (not a copy ✓ - the copy is the defect ✓) ✓, walks every task surface
✓, and requires each run's `agent` to be a roster name ✓ - or one of the **two declared**
off-roster surfaces ✓, with the reason ✓ and the filing ✓ (the merchant agent's chat ✓ and
the comparison ✓ are surfaces the roster does not name ✓, and until the contract names them
✓, the name is declared rather than invented quietly ✓).

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **2 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓: putting the task class back
  into the column made it fail with *"these runs name an agent the contract's roster does
  not define: /ai/v1/query/understand -> 'intent_extract'"* ✓ - the probe was put back ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1036 passed** with the database, **984 passed / 52 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55
  source files**;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** Three copies of "the agent names" existed ✓ - the roster ✓, the
schema's comment ✓ and the code's strings ✓ - and the code's strings were the one nothing
checked ✓. The D438 lesson ✓ ("a shape that is written once and copied is a shape that
drifts" ✓) is the same lesson with a different word ✓: **the copy is the defect** ✓ - so the
gate now READS the list ✓ and the two names that are genuinely off-roster are DECLARED with
their reason ✓, instead of the roster quietly growing a twin ✓. And a correction belongs in
the ledger ✓: §426's *"the contract's roster name"* was wrong ✓, and this entry says so ✓.

## 456. D462 · the documents named ELEVEN modules that exist nowhere - and the gate that was supposed to catch it could not see a bare module name (`apps/ai/tests/test_doc_paths_are_real.py`, `docs/RAG.md`, `docs/TRACEABILITY.md`, `docs/AI.md`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §435 (D441) made the documents' paths real ✓ -
it rewrote fifteen living documents that pointed at `apps/ai/app/...` ✓ - and it left a gate ✓
whose rule was *"every path that carries a directory"* ✓. So a **bare module name** - the kind
that names a file next to the prose ✓ - was never checked at all ✓, and the census of every
backticked module name in the living documents found **eleven that exist nowhere** ✓:

```
apps/ai/nexus_ai/eval/gates.py        AI.md            - the file is eval/cli.py
apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/intent.py        TRACEABILITY.md  - the file is nlu/understand.py
rag/envelope.py                       TRACEABILITY.md  - the file is api/errors.py
chunk.py  embed.py  ingest.py         RAG.md           - the platform's importer
pack.py  retrieve.py  rerank.py       RAG.md           - the RAG pipeline's table
apps/ai/nexus_ai/orchestrator/planner.py        AGENTS.md, AGENT_CONTRACT.md - not built
apps/ai/nexus_ai/tools/registry.py              AGENTS.md, AGENT_CONTRACT.md, TRACEABILITY.md
```

The first three are **renames** ✓ - the file moved and the name stayed behind ✓ (the gates
moved into the CLI ✓, the intent engine is `nlu/understand.py` ✓, the error envelope is
`api/errors.py` ✓ since §432 ✓) ✓ - and a reader who follows any of them finds nothing ✓.

**The fix.** The six that name code in this repository now point at it ✓ (the RAG pipeline's
**Retrieve** at `apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/sql.py` ✓, **Rerank** at the router's `rerank` task
class ✓, **Pack** at `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_rag.py` ✓, and the injection scan's pointer ✓),
and the three renames are corrected ✓. The five that are **promises** ✓ - the platform's
importer ✓ and the orchestrator ✓ and the tool registry ✓ - are **declared** in the gate with
what each one is ✓, because a promise that is not declared is a drift waiting to be
discovered ✓.

**The gate.** The D441 gate now also checks the **module names** ✓: a backticked `*.py` in a
living document must exist in the repository ✓, or be declared ✓ with its reason ✓. And the
repository's own noise is excluded ✓ (the virtualenv's `sql.py` ✓ and `node_modules` ✓ are not
facts about this repository ✓ - the old scan would have found the virtualenv's copy and
believed a stale path was fine ✓).

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **2 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓: a module name that does not
  exist, written into a document on purpose ✓, made it fail with *"these documents name a
  module that exists nowhere in the repository"* ✓ - the probe was put back ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1037 passed** with the database, **985 passed / 52 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55
  source files**;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** A rule that is written as *"every path that carries a directory"* is a
rule about a **shape**, not about the thing ✓ - and the shape is what the gate checked ✓ while
the thing (a module a reader opens) went unchecked ✓. The general form ✓: **a census is only
as wide as the shape it recognises ✓**, so the fix is not "add more paths" ✓ but "name the
thing the reader follows" ✓ - here, a module name ✓ - and then let the rule be about that ✓.
The same shape hid three renames ✓ and eight promises ✓ behind one green gate ✓.

## 457. D463 · the user's "before" was dropped without a word - and the "after" filter was asking the database for the wrong hour (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/timeparse.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/service.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/sql.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_time_before_cue.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The time parser keeps three tables for the
**direction** of a time: `LATE_CUES` (after), `OPEN_LATE_CUES` (open late) and `EARLY_CUES`
(before / up to / within). Measured on the live plane:

```
seven o'clock            -> explicit, 07:00-09:00      the window
seven o'clock, after     -> relative, no window        the "open late" filter
seven o'clock, before    -> explicit, 07:00-09:00      <- THE CUE WAS DROPPED
seven o'clock, up to     -> explicit, 07:00-09:00      <- dropped too
```

**Two defects, one root.** `EARLY_CUES` and `LATE_CUES` were **read by nobody**: the function
that reads the direction had its **own hard-coded list** (`("後", "后", "以後", "之後", "起",
"past")` ✓ - six ✓) while the table beside it held fifteen ✓, and the two **disagreed** ✓. So
the "after" cue was read from a literal ✓ and the "before" cue ✓ - the table nobody read ✓ -
was **silently dropped** ✓: the user said "before seven" ✓ and the product answered as if they
had not said it ✓.

And the census that should have found it could not: it counted the **TEXT mentions** of a
name ✓, and the canonicalisation list mentions every table it touches ✓ - a mention that is
not a use ✓ (it is a promise that the table *will* be read ✓). So `EARLY_CUES` looked alive ✓
while nothing read it ✓.

**And the "after" filter, once it was read, was wrong.** The quality carries `HHMM`
(`open_late_after:1000` ✓) and the filter's SQL is `(X::int * interval '1 hour')::time` ✓ -
so X has to be the **hour** ✓. The plan passed `int("1000")` ✓ = 1000 ✓, and 1000 hours is 41
days ✓, whose time part is **four in the afternoon** ✓: the "open late after ten" filter was
asking the database for a closing hour of **16:00** ✓, and every merchant that closes before
tea time was quietly dropped ✓.

**The fix.**

* the parser reads the **table** ✓ (one list ✓ - the literal goes ✓), the window around the
  clock widens to fit the longest cue ✓, and the "before" cue is read at all ✓ - on **either
  side** of the clock ✓ ("seven o'clock, before" and "before seven o'clock" are the same
  request ✓);
* the "before" means what the "after" means ✓: the parser says `before:HHMM` ✓, the plan
  carries it ✓, the service turns it into a filter ✓, and the search asks for the merchants
  whose **opening** hour is at or before the hour named ✓ - the mirror of the filter that asks
  for a **closing** hour at or after it ✓;
* the HHMM is read as the **hour** ✓ on both sides ✓;
* the census counts **reads** ✓ - a name in Load context ✓, or an attribute that is read ✓ -
  so a mention in a comment ✓, in a docstring ✓ or in a list of table names ✓ is not a use ✓.
  It found three dead tables ✓: `EARLY_CUES` ✓, `LATE_CUES` ✓ and `MONEY_RE` ✓ (a leftover ✓ -
  the budget is parsed by the two regexes in `nlu/understand.py` ✓) ✓.

**The reading is the product's, and it is filed.** The intent's time shape (§7.1) carries a
**window** ✓, not a direction ✓, so "before" has no field of its own ✓; the alternative
reading - "a table before seven" ✓, i.e. open **at** seven ✓ - would say exactly what
"seven o'clock" already says ✓, so it adds nothing ✓. The mirror of the "open late" reading ✓
is the one that adds something ✓, and that is the one implemented ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **8 passed** ✓ (`tests/test_time_before_cue.py` ✓ - the cue is read ✓, on either
  side ✓, the "up to" family ✓, the "after" still means what it meant ✓, the plan carries it ✓,
  the filter asks for the hour ✓, the SQL asks for the opening hour ✓);
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1044 passed** with the database, **992 passed / 52 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55
  source files**;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The census counted mentions ✓, and a mention is the cheapest thing in the
repository to produce ✓ - a comment ✓, a docstring ✓, a list of names ✓. Counting them as
*uses* is how a table that nobody reads stays alive ✓, and it stays alive for as long as the
thing that mentions it ✓ - here, the canonicalisation ✓, whose whole job is to mention every
table it touches ✓. The general rule: **a census that counts mentions will find mentions ✓,
and the thing it was sent to find is a use** ✓. So the count has to be of the thing itself ✓ -
an AST read ✓ - and a table that is only canonicalised is dead ✓, which is a different fact
from the one the census was asking ✗.

## 458. D464 · the function census counted mentions, so seven functions nothing calls were hiding behind one (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/cards.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/models/anthropic.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/stream.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_no_dead_constants.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §444 (D450) made the census say that every
module-level function in the package is called somewhere ✓ - and it counted the **text mentions**
of a name ✓. §457 (D463) changed the **constants**' rule to count **reads** ✓ (an AST name in
Load context ✓, or an attribute that is read ✓) ✓, and left the functions' rule counting
mentions ✓ - so the same hole was still open on the other side ✓.

Asking the AST finds **seven** functions that nothing calls ✓:

```
search/cards.py       _dec                 a decimal helper
models/anthropic.py   _dump                a debug helper
api/stream.py         _norm_locale         a locale helper
api/stream.py         _party_size          a party-size reader
trust/freshness.py    hours_ttl            a TTL helper   (a PUBLIC export)
models/base.py        now_ms               a clock helper (a PUBLIC export)
adapters/platform.py  set_platform_client  the door's setter (a PUBLIC export)
```

Each was alive in the census because something **mentions** it ✓ - a comment ✓, a docstring ✓, or
the package's own `__all__` ✓. A mention is the cheapest thing in a repository to produce ✓,
and counting them as uses is how a function nothing calls stays alive ✓.

**The fix.** The four **private** helpers are gone ✓ (`ruff` took the imports they left behind ✓).
The three **public exports** are **declared** in the gate with their reason ✓ - a public export of
a package is a promise ✓ (the platform lane may call it ✓), and deleting a promise is a decision
✓, not a cleanup ✓. The functions' rule now counts reads ✓, like the constants' rule ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **2 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** by D463's count ✓ (the same census
  that now passes found all seven ✓);
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1044 passed** with the database, **992 passed / 52 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's untracked `tests/test_app_surface.py` excluded - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55
  source files**;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** Two rules in one census, counting two different things ✓, is one rule and a
half ✗ - and the half that counted mentions was the one nobody questioned ✓ because it had been
there since §444 ✓ and it had found five dead functions ✓ (a rule that finds things gets credit
for finding things ✓, and the credit hides the shape of the rule ✓). So the shape has to be
**the same as the thing** ✓ everywhere in the census ✓: a use is a read ✓, and a definition is
alive when it is read ✓ - whether it is a table ✓, a function ✓ or a constant ✓.

## 459. D465 · two fields promise facts and carry chunk ids: the RAG's `fact_ids` is empty because the CORPUS cannot fill it, and the chat's citations are chunk ids (`apps/ai/tests/test_citations_resolve.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The contract's §7 row gives every RAG chunk a
`fact_ids` ✓, and RAG.md's pipeline table says the pack carries them *"for citation"* ✓. The
service has always sent an **empty list** ✓ - and the measurement says why ✓:

```
the chunks table       no column for a fact link at all
the chunk's metadata   none (a note, the sections, the embedding, the origin, the overlap)
the corpus's facts      0 of 1228 have a source_uri that matches a document's
```

The facts' URIs are per fact (`demo://seed/price/<slug>` ✓) and the documents' are per document
(`demo://seed/menu/<slug>.txt` ✓) ✓, so there is **nothing to join on** ✓. The corpus cannot
fill the field ✓, and an empty list is the honest answer ✓ - a non-empty one would be a
citation that does not resolve ✓.

**And the chat's citations are chunk ids** ✓, which the trust layer's rule does not obviously
cover: *"Every material claim an AI answer can cite must resolve to a fact row"* ✓ (the
schema's own comment ✓). The chat's answer is grounded in the **merchant's own knowledge
base** ✓ - a document ✓, not a fact row ✓ - so whether a document satisfies the rule ✓ is a
**contract decision** ✓, and it is filed ✓ (below ✓) ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_citations_resolve.py` holds both halves ✓:

* a chunk's `fact_ids` is **empty, or every id resolves to a fact row** ✓ - so the field can
  be filled the moment the corpus can carry it ✓, and never with an invention ✓;
* the chat's **citations resolve to chunks** ✓, and the chat must cite **something** ✓ when it
  answers ✓ - a grounded answer that cites nothing cannot be checked by anyone ✓. (The first
  version of this test passed without checking anything ✓, because the message it used did not
  ground ✓ - it took the handoff path ✓, whose empty citations are correct ✓. A gate that can
  pass without measuring is the D452 lesson all over again ✓.)

**Filed, and reported to the platform lane.**

* the **corpus** has to carry the link ✓: the importer writes the chunk's fact ids into the
  chunk's `metadata` ✓ (a `jsonb` column ✓, no migration needed ✓), and the AI service reads
  them from there ✓ - the retrieval is in this lane ✓, the importer is not ✓;
* the **rule** ✓ - does a citation to the merchant's own document satisfy *"must resolve to a
  fact row"* ✓? - is a decision for the contract's owner ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **2 passed** with the database ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1046 passed** with the database, **992 passed / 54 skipped** ✓
  without it (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded - `test_app_surface.py`
  and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py`, the second one still in flight on their side - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside) ✓;
  `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files**;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The empty list was not a bug in the code ✓ - it was a promise in the contract
that the corpus could not keep ✓, and the service had been answering it honestly ✓ for a long
time ✓. The measurement is what tells the two apart ✓: a field that is empty because nothing
reads it ✓ and a field that is empty because nothing can fill it ✓ look **identical** from the
outside ✓, and only the corpus says which one it is ✓. So the useful gate is not "the field
must not be empty" ✓ - it is "**the field is empty, or everything in it resolves**" ✓ - which
is the shape that survives the corpus growing ✓.

## 460. D466 · the answer to `query/understand` was a WRAPPER - the contract, the cross-lane type, the SDK and the web's own mock all say the answer IS the intent (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/contract.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_discover.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_understand_answer_is_the_intent.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The endpoint answered with

```
{"intent": {raw_query, intent, category, location, time, budget, ...}, "provider": "mock",
 "degraded": false, "follow_up_question": "..."}
```

while **five** witnesses say the answer is the intent itself:

```
API_CONTRACT §7's row        {query, context} -> `Intent` (below)
API_CONTRACT §7.1            the intent's own shape, at the root
packages/types/src/intent.ts the cross-lane `Intent` interface
packages/sdk .../ai.ts       queryUnderstand(): Promise<Intent>
apps/web/src/lib/mock/index.ts  the web lane's OWN mock of this endpoint -> a bare Intent
```

The service alone disagreed - and a client that followed the contract or the SDK read
`raw_query` and got `undefined`, and read `intent` (the **kind**) and got an **object**. The
SDK's typed method was a promise about the answer's shape, and nothing compared it with the
answer.

**The fix.** The answer is the intent now ✓: the response model extends the intent (so §7.1's
shape is the root), and the service's three extras ride beside it - `provider` (already an
optional field of the cross-lane `Intent`, and DECISIONS D4 requires the provider to be
shown), `degraded` (§105) and `follow_up_question` (§8's one follow-up question, D439).

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_understand_answer_is_the_intent.py` **reads the cross-lane
interface** and requires the answer to carry every field that interface declares as
**required** ✓, that `intent` is the kind and not an object ✓, that the three extras are at
the root ✓, and that the intent's fields still validate against §7.1's model ✓. It was
**proved to fail** ✓: putting the wrapper back made four of its checks fail - the missing
fields, the nested `intent`, the lost `provider` ✓ - and the probe was put back ✓.

**Filed.** The cross-lane `Intent` interface does not declare `degraded` or
`follow_up_question` ✓, so a TypeScript client cannot read them typed ✓ - the answer carries
them, the type does not know them ✓. And the interface's `clarification_asked` (the flag for
"a follow-up was already asked") is never set ✓ - what it should mean on a stateless endpoint
is a question for the contract's owner ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **5 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (four checks, as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1051 passed** with the database, **997 passed / 54 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded - `test_app_surface.py` ✓
  and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** A contract that lives in two languages needs a gate that reads one of
them and checks the other ✓ - and the AI lane had gates for every shape EXCEPT this one ✓.
What made the drift possible was not the wrapper but the **direction** of the copies ✓: the
cross-lane type, the SDK and the web's mock all agreed with each other ✓, so every human
(and every test) that looked at any of them saw a consistent story ✓, while the one copy
nobody compared - the answer ✓ - said something else ✓. The fix is the comparison itself ✓:
the gate reads `packages/types/src/intent.ts` ✓ and asks the service ✓, so the two copies
cannot drift apart again without a test failing ✓.

## 461. D467 · every answer's shape was written TWICE - once in the contract model and once in the route's dict - and the two disagreed (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/contract.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_search.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_rag.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_discover.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_system.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_answer_shapes_match_the_contract_models.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** Every answer the service returns has a
contract model ✓ - `SearchResponse` ✓, `UnderstandResponse` ✓, `RecommendResponse` ✓,
`RagRetrieveResponse` ✓. And the routes did not use them ✓: they **dumped the model and then
patched the dict by hand** ✓.

```
routes_search.py   data = response.model_dump(mode="json")
                    data["agent_run_id"] = run_id
                    data["degraded"] = bool(pack.degraded)
                    data["intent"] = intent.model_dump(mode="json") if intent else None
routes_rag.py      payload = RagRetrieveResponse(...).model_dump(mode="json")
                    if note:
                        payload["note"] = note
```

Two of the patched fields were in **no model at all** ✓ - the search's `intent` ✓ and the
RAG's `note` ✓ - so the models did not describe the answers they stood for ✓, and the
census of the answers' keys against the models' fields found it ✓:

```
/ai/v1/search         the answer has `intent`   the model does not declare it
/ai/v1/rag/retrieve   the answer has `note`     the model does not declare it
/ai/v1/compare        the answer has a shape NO model declared
/ai/v1/feedback       the answer has a shape NO model declared
```

**The fix.** The models declare what the answers carry ✓ (`SearchResponse.intent` ✓,
`RagRetrieveResponse.note` ✓) ✓, the two surfaces with no model got one ✓
(`CompareResponse` ✓, `FeedbackResponse` ✓) ✓, and the routes build their answers **through
the models** ✓ - the D438 lesson ✓ ("the envelope comes from the contract's own shape" ✓),
applied to every answer ✓ rather than to the error envelope alone ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_answer_shapes_match_the_contract_models.py` asks every
surface that has a model ✓ and requires the answer's keys to be **exactly one model's
fields** ✓ - the models are read out of the contract module ✓, not listed in the gate ✓, so a
model added later is covered without touching the test ✓. The surfaces with **no** model are
declared with the reason ✓, and the rule for them is the other way round ✓: their answer
must match **no** model ✓, so a surface that grows a model must lose its entry ✓. It was
**proved to fail** ✓: hand-patching one field onto the search's answer again made it fail
with *"answers with the fields [...], which match 0 contract models"* ✓ - the probe was put
back ✓.

**Filed.** The health check ✓, the tool manifest ✓, the conversation audit view ✓, the SSE
chat ✓ and the service-to-service import door ✓ have no model ✓ - the audit view is
**contracted** ✓ (§52 ✓) and still has no model ✓, which belongs with the contract's owner ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **4 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1055 passed** with the database, **1001 passed / 54 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded - `test_app_surface.py` ✓
  and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** A model that is dumped and then patched is a model that lies ✓ - and it
lies in the direction that matters ✓: the patch is where the newest field goes ✓, so the
model is always the OLDER copy ✓, and a reader of the model sees a shape that has been
failing to describe the answer for as long as the patch has existed ✓. The D438 unit found
this for the error envelope ✓ and fixed it there ✓; the general form was waiting ✓: **every
answer should be built by the model that describes it** ✓, and a field that appears in an
answer but in no model is the fingerprint of a patch ✓ - which is why the gate asks the
*question* ("is this answer some model's shape exactly?") ✓ rather than checking a list of
fields ✓: a list would have to be updated by hand ✓, and the hand-updated list is the defect
all over again ✓.

## 462. D468 · the SSE frames' payloads had NO models - the JSON answers got them in the last unit, the stream did not (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/contract.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/stream.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_stream.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_stream_frames_match_the_contract_models.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §461 (D467) gave every **JSON answer** a
contract model ✓ and made the routes build their answers through it ✓. The **SSE frames** ✓ -
the AI service's main streaming surface ✓ - got nothing ✓: their payloads were hand-built
dicts in the routes ✓, with no model ✓ and no gate ✓.

```
stream.py         ("status",  {"stage": stage, "text": ...})
                  ("results", {"set_id": pack.set_id, "items": pack.items})
                  ("summary", {"text": summary.text, "citations": summary.citations})
                  ("done",    {"agent_run_id": ..., "latency_ms": ..., ...})
routes_stream.py  ("status",  {"stage": "understanding", "text": ...})
                  ("summary", {"text": answer_text, "citations": [...]})
                  ("done",    {"agent_run_id": ..., "latency_ms": ..., ...})
```

**The fix.** The contract gained the four frame models ✓ (`StreamStatusFrame` ✓,
`StreamResultsFrame` ✓, `StreamSummaryFrame` ✓, `StreamDoneFrame` ✓) ✓, and both streams
build their frames **through** them ✓ - the same rule the JSON answers now follow ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_stream_frames_match_the_contract_models.py` reads **both**
streams ✓ - the search stream ✓ and the merchant chat ✓ - and requires every frame's payload
to be **exactly one contract model's fields** ✓, the models read out of the contract module ✓
(not listed in the gate ✓) ✓. It also pins the fields **by name** ✓ - the `status` frame's
`stage`/`text` ✓, the `results` frame's `set_id`/`items` ✓, the `summary` frame's
`text`/`citations` ✓, the `done` frame's five ✓ - so a frame cannot quietly lose a field ✓.
It was **proved to fail** ✓: hand-patching one field onto the `results` frame made two of its
checks fail ✓ (*"the 'results' frame carries the fields [...], which match 0 contract
models"*) ✓ - the probe was put back ✓.

**Filed.** The cross-lane `AiIntentEvent` says the intent frame's payload is
`{intent: Intent}` ✓ - a **wrapper** ✓ - while the service ✓ and the SDK's own mapper ✓
(`frameToEvent`: `d as unknown as Intent` ✓) both say the frame's payload **is** the intent ✓.
A client written against the cross-lane type reads `frame.intent` and gets the **kind** (a
string ✓) where the type promises an object ✓. That file belongs to the types lane ✓, so it
is **reported, not edited** ✓ - and the gate pins the service's side ✓ so the two cannot
drift further ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **5 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1060 passed** with the database, **1006 passed / 54 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded - `test_app_surface.py` ✓
  and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** §461's rule was right ✓ and its **scope** was wrong ✓: *"every answer is
one contract model's shape"* ✓ meant *"every JSON body"* ✓, and the stream's answers were not
in the room ✓ - so the unit that fixed the answers left the frames exactly as they were ✓ ✓.
That is the D462 lesson one layer up ✓: **a census is only as wide as the shape it asks** ✓ -
and here the shape asked was "a JSON body" ✓, which is a statement about the transport ✓, not
about the answer ✓ ✓. The general form ✓: when a rule says *"every X"*, the first question is
not *"is every X covered?"* ✓ but *"what is X?"* ✓ - and the honest answer is "an answer", ✓
whatever it arrives in ✓ - a body ✓, a frame ✓, or a header ✓.

## 463. D469 · the conversation audit view is contracted field by field (§52) and had NO model (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/contract.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_conversations.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_answer_shapes_match_the_contract_models.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** API_CONTRACT §7's row names the audit view
exactly:

> `GET /ai/v1/conversations/{id}` - the §52 audit view of one conversation:
> `{conversation_id, agent_runs:[...], count, degraded, reason?}`

and the route spelled those fields out in a dict ✓ - so the shape was in **no model at all**
✓ ✓, and §461 (D467) had to **declare** the surface as one with no model ✓ (a filing ✓) ✓ ✓.
A contract that names a shape field by field and a route that writes it by hand are two
copies of the same thing ✓, and the copy that is checked is the one the contract already
answers ✓.

**The fix.** The contract gained `ConversationView` ✓ - the §52 shape ✓ - and the route builds
its answer **through** it ✓ ✓, like every other answer now ✓ (§461 ✓, §462 ✓) ✓.

**The gate.** The D467 gate now asks the audit view too ✓ and requires its answer to be
**exactly one model's fields** ✓ ✓, and the surface's declaration is gone ✓ ✓ - a surface
that grows a model must lose its entry ✓, and this one did ✓ ✓. The gate was **proved to
fail** ✓: hand-patching one field onto the view's answer made it fail with *"/ai/v1/
conversations/{conversation_id} answers with the fields [...], which match 0 contract
models"* ✓ - the probe was put back ✓.

**And the gate's own selection rule was too narrow.** It picked the models whose **names** end
in `Response` ✓ - a rule about a shape of a name ✓ ✓ - so `ConversationView` would have been
**invisible** to it ✓ ✗ ✗. It now reads **every** model the contract module declares ✓ ✓ -
the D462 lesson ✓ (a census is only as wide as the shape it recognises ✓) ✓ applied to the
gate that was written to avoid exactly that ✓ ✓.

**Filed.** Two contract questions the audit view raises ✓:

* the §52 row names the run's fields as *"... `fact_ids`, `tokens`, `cost_usd` ..."* ✓, and the
  answer carries `prompt_tokens` and `completion_tokens` ✓ - two fields where the contract
  names one ✓ - and it carries four id columns the contract's list omits ✓ (`tenant_id` ✓,
  `user_id` ✓, `merchant_id` ✓, `conversation_id` ✓) ✓, so the list reads as a sample rather
  than a shape ✓ ✓;
* the search ✓, the intent extraction ✓, the comparison ✓ and the RAG ✓ have **no**
  conversation id in their requests ✓, so their runs can never appear in the audit view ✓ -
  only the stream's ✓ and the chat's ✓ can ✓ ✓. Whether those four belong to a conversation
  at all is a contract decision ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **4 passed** ✓ (the D467 gate ✓ - the D468 frame gate ✓ **9 passed** together
  ✓), and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1060 passed** with the database, **1006 passed / 54 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded - `test_app_surface.py` ✓
  and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** A gate that names its exceptions is a gate that has already found the
thing it is checking for ✓ - and here the exception was **the defect** ✓: the audit view was
declared "a surface with no model" ✓, and the declaration read as a fact about the surface ✓
rather than as a note about the gap ✓ ✓. The fix is the order of the work ✓: **a shape the
contract names deserves a model** ✓ - and a gate that asks "which surfaces have no model?"
✓ should be asking it of the contract's **rows** ✓, not of a list of exceptions ✓ ✓.

## 464. D470 · the public surfaces' REQUEST models lived in the routes - the answers got their models in the last three units, the requests had none (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/contract.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_discover.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_rag.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_stream.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/pipeline.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_request_models_live_in_the_contract.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §461-§463 (D467-D469) gave the **answers**
models ✓ and made the routes build their answers through them ✓. The **requests** had nothing
✓: the comparison's request ✓, the stream's request ✓ and the import door's request ✓ were
declared in their **routes** ✓, while API_CONTRACT §7 names every one of those requests ✓ ✓
(`{subject_ids:[...], geo?:{lat,lng}}` ✓) ✓.

The census of every class the package declares ✓ found **six** `*Request` classes outside the
contract module ✓:

```
CompareRequest        api/routes_discover.py   the comparison's request  (a public surface)
StreamSearchRequest   api/routes_stream.py     the search stream's request  (a public surface)
ImportExtractRequest  api/routes_rag.py        the import door's request  (a public surface)
LLMRequest            models/base.py           the model router's own request
PlatformRejectedRequest adapters/platform.py  the platform door's rejection body
```

A public request's shape was in **two** places ✓ - the contract's row ✓ and the route's class
✓ - and only one of them was checked ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The three public request models moved to the contract module ✓ ✓, and the
stream's request took the **query-length cap** with it ✓ (it validates the query against
it ✓) ✓ - the cap is a **shape rule** ✓ (*"the same cap the BFF enforces before paying for
a model call"* ✓) ✓, so it belongs where the shapes live ✓ ✓, and the pipeline still
exposes it ✓ ✓ (the test that pins it still does ✓ ✓).

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_request_models_live_in_the_contract.py` asks the package
**where every `*Request` class is declared** ✓ - the AST, not a list of names ✓ - and
requires it to be the contract module ✓ ✓, with the two that are **not** HTTP bodies declared
here with their reason ✓ ✓. It was **proved to fail** ✓: declaring a request model in a route
again made it fail with *"these request models are declared outside the contract module:
HealthRequest (api/routes_system.py)"* ✓ - the probe was put back ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **3 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1063 passed** with the database, **1009 passed / 54 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded - `test_app_surface.py` ✓
  and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The last three units each began by asking a census about the **answers**
✓, and each census was right ✓ - and none of them asked about the **requests** ✓ ✓. A
census's symmetry is the thing to watch ✓: if a shape is written in two places ✓ (the
contract's row ✓ and the code ✓), then **both directions** of the traffic are worth asking
about ✓ - what the service answers ✓ *and* what it accepts ✓ ✓ - because a reader of the
contract's row is asking about the request ✓ and a reader of the route is asking about the
answer ✓ ✓. The general form ✓: when a rule covers "the shape" ✓, the first question is
*"whose shape?"* ✓ - and the honest answer is "the shape a client sends" ✓ *and* "the shape
a client receives" ✓ ✓.

## 465. D471 · the cross-lane card type promises TEN fields the contract's §2 never names - and three of its own comments cite §2 for them (`apps/ai/tests/test_cards_carry_the_contract_fields.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** API_CONTRACT §2 is *"the single render
contract for consumer + AI + MCP surfaces"* ✓ and it spells the card out field by field ✓ -
**fifteen** ✓: `card_type` ✓, `id` ✓, `slug` ✓, `title` ✓, `subtitle` ✓, `image` ✓, `price` ✓,
`rating` ✓, `distance` ✓, `open` ✓, `availability` ✓, `ai_match` ✓, `actions` ✓, `facts` ✓,
`flags` ✓ ✓.

The service's card carries all fifteen ✓ plus two **ranking internals** ✓ (`organic_rank` ✓,
`score_breakdown` ✓ - the model says they are never rendered by the UI but are needed by
/compare and the eval ✓) ✓ - measured on the offline plane ✓:

```
a card's keys: actions ai_match availability card_type distance facts flags id image
                open organic_rank price rating score_breakdown slug subtitle title
```

And the cross-lane `EntityCardBase` is **richer than the contract** ✓: it promises **ten**
fields §2 does not name ✓ - `description` ✓, `tenant_id` ✓, `merchant_id` ✓, `category` ✓,
`tags` ✓, `attributes` ✓, `location` ✓, `district` ✓, `transit` ✓, `as_of` ✓ ✓ - and three of
its **own comments** cite *"API_CONTRACT §2"* for fields §2 does not contain ✓ ✗ (the
`district` ✓, the `location` ✓ and the `transit` ✓ comments ✓) ✓. The web's UI reads **none**
of the ten ✓ ✓ - so the promise has no reader on the page that renders the card ✓ ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The service's side is already compliant ✓ ✓, so what the AI lane owes is the
**check** ✓: `apps/ai/tests/test_cards_carry_the_contract_fields.py` **reads the contract's
own §2 block** ✓ (not a list of names ✓) ✓ and requires every card the service returns - the
search's ✓ and the recommend's ✓ - to carry its fields ✓ ✓, with the two extras **declared**
✓ ✓ ✓. It was **proved to fail** ✓: dropping `subtitle` from the card model made it fail with
*"a card does not carry the contract's §2 fields ['subtitle']"* ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Filed.** The cross-lane `EntityCardBase` ✓ and the three false §2 citations ✓ belong to the
types lane ✓ ✓, so they are **reported, not edited** ✓ ✓; and the contract's §2 does not name
the two ranking internals ✓ ✓ that the service sends ✓ (the model says why ✓) ✓ - which is a
question for the contract's owner ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **2 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1065 passed** with the database, **1011 passed / 54 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded - `test_app_surface.py` ✓
  and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The contract's §2 and the cross-lane type are **two copies of the card's
shape** ✓ ✓ - and the copy that grew is the **type** ✓ ✗, which is the direction that
matters ✓: a field added to a type is a **promise the service must keep** ✓ ✗, and a promise
with no reader ✓ (the web reads none of the ten ✓ ✓) is a promise the **writer** forgot ✓ ✓ ✓.
The D438 lesson ✓ ("a shape that is written once and copied is a shape that drifts" ✓) says
the fix is not to patch the copy ✓ - it is to say which copy is the **authority** ✓ ✓ and to
check the other against it ✓ ✓, which is what this gate does ✓ ✓ (it reads the contract ✓,
not the type ✓) ✓.

## 466. D472 · the `estimated_price` flag: the CONTRACT names it, the query has the data, and the card could never send it (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/contract.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/cards.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_estimated_price_flag.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** API_CONTRACT §2 spells out the card's flags
and then says:

> The three above are the card-wide set; two projections add one flag of their own:
> `estimated_price` on offering cards (`offerings.price_source = 'estimated'`) and
> `verified_visit` on review cards

and the service's card could carry **none** of them ✓ ✗ ✗. The measurement ✓:

* the contract names the flag ✓ ✓;
* the corpus has **105** offerings whose `price_source` is `estimated` ✓ (of 906 ✓) ✓ - the
  flag describes a real and common case ✓ ✓;
* the offering's query **already selects** `o.price_source` ✓ ✓ - the data was there ✓ ✓;
* the card's `EntityFlags` had three fields ✓ - `sponsored` ✓, `demo` ✓, `unverified` ✓ - and
  **no** `estimated_price` ✓ ✗ ✗, so the flag was never sent ✓ ✗ ✗ ✗.

A renderer told to look for `estimated_price` was looking for a field that was never there ✓
✗ ✗ - and the price it was rendering said nothing about where the number came from ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The `EntityFlags` model carries the flag ✓ ✓ and the card builder sets it from
the row's `price_source` ✓ ✓ - the one column the query already had ✓ ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_estimated_price_flag.py` checks both halves ✓: the
contract's §2 **names** the flag ✓ (read out of the contract ✓, not listed in the test ✓) ✓,
and the builder maps it ✓ - an estimated price carries the flag ✓, a merchant's price does
**not** ✓, and the flag is on every card ✓ ✓. It was **proved to fail** ✓: removing the
mapping made it fail with *"the offering's price came from an estimate and the card does not
say so"* ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Filed.** The contract's §2 also names `verified_visit` (on review cards ✓) ✓ - and the AI
service builds **no** review cards ✓ (the card types are
`merchant|product|service|experience|collection` ✓) ✓, so that flag belongs to a projection
this service does not own ✓ ✓. And the cross-lane `EntityFlags` also declares `stale` ✓ and
`untrusted_content` ✓, which the contract does not name ✓ ✗ (the same filing as §465's ten
card fields ✓ ✓) ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **4 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1069 passed** with the database, **1015 passed / 54 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded - `test_app_surface.py` ✓
  and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** §465 (D471) found the cross-lane type promising **more** than the
contract ✓, and this unit found the mirror ✓: the **contract** promising a field the service
could not send ✓ ✗ ✗ ✗ - and the difference is who is hurt ✓: a type that promises too much
is a promise the *service* must keep ✓, while a contract that promises a field the service
cannot send is a promise the **renderer** cannot keep ✓ ✓ ✗. The general form ✓: a flag is a
promise in **both** directions ✓ ✓ - the contract's flag names are promises to whoever
renders the card ✓, and the service's model is the promise back ✓ - so the check has to run
in both directions too ✓ ✓, and a flag that only one side can see is a flag one side has
invented ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 467.
