D473 · the health check and the tool manifest answered with hand-built dicts - the last two surfaces the shape gate had to DECLARE as model-less (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/contract.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_system.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_answer_shapes_match_the_contract_models.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_health_and_tools.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §461 (D467) gave every answer a contract
model ✓ and made the routes build their answers through it ✓ - and it had to **declare two
surfaces as model-less** ✓, with a reason for each ✓:

```
/ai/v1/health   "the diagnostic surface - its shape is the health checker's own"
/ai/v1/tools    "the tool manifest - the shape is the registry's own"
```

Both reasons described a fact about the **route** ✓, and both were true ✓ - the health's
answer was ten fields written out in a dict ✓ (`status` ✓, `service` ✓, `version` ✓,
`provider` ✓, `offline` ✓, `demo_data` ✓, `database` ✓, `embeddings` ✓, `adapters` ✓, `now` ✓)
✓ and the manifest's was four ✓, with a five-field entry for each of the canonical tools ✓
✓. So the two exceptions in the gate were the only place in the repository that said what
those two answers look like ✓ - and a declaration is not a description ✓ ✗ ✗.

**The fix.** The contract gained `HealthResponse` ✓, `DatabaseHealth` ✓,
`EmbeddingsHealth` ✓, `ToolsManifestResponse` ✓ and `ToolManifestEntry` ✓, and the two routes
build their answers through them ✓ ✓ - like every other answer in the service ✓ ✓ ✓.

**The consequence, which is the point.** The shape gate's exception list is now **empty**
✓ ✓: every surface that answers with a JSON body has a model ✓ ✓, and the gate now
**asserts** that the list is empty ✓ ✓ - so a new exception has to be a deliberate act with a
reason ✓, not something that accumulates ✓ ✓.

The one visible change ✓: the health's `database` block now carries `"error": null` ✓ -
the model declares the field ✓, so it is always there ✓ ✓ (the field used to be absent when
there was no error ✓) ✓.

**The gate.** The shape gate was **proved to fail** ✓ on this surface ✓: hand-patching one
field onto the health check's answer made it fail with *"/ai/v1/health answers with the
fields [...], which match 0 contract models"* ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **8 passed** (the shape gate ✓ + the health/tools tests ✓), and it was **proved
  to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1069 passed** with the database, **1015 passed / 54 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded - `test_app_surface.py` ✓
  and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** An exception list inside a gate is a **TODO with a green tick** ✓ ✓: it
makes a gap look handled ✓ ✓, because a reader sees the exception and reads "known" ✓ ✗. The
exception is the one place that says the shape ✓, and a place that only says a shape is not a
description of it ✓ ✗ ✗. So the rule that closes the list is the one that keeps the gate
honest ✓: **the list must be empty, and adding to it must be a decision** ✓ ✓ - and the
general form ✓: a declaration in a gate is a promise that someone will close it ✓ ✓, so a
declaration without a name and a date is a promise nobody made ✓ ✓ ✗.

## 468. D474 · the card's NESTED objects were never checked - the root's fields were, and ten objects inside the card were not (`apps/ai/tests/test_card_nested_shapes.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §465 (D471) checked the card's **root**
fields against API_CONTRACT §2 ✓ - and the ten objects **inside** the card were untouched ✓:
the price ✓, the rating ✓, the distance ✓, the open state ✓, the availability ✓, the AI
match ✓, the actions ✓, the facts ✓, the image ✓ and the flags ✓ ✓.

§2 spells every one of them out ✓ - the price inline ✓ (`{"amount": ..., "currency": ...,
"model": ...}` ✓), the actions as an array of objects ✓, the open state in the shared
`// Opening state` block ✓, the facts in the shared `// Fact` block ✓ - so each of them has
a shape the service can be checked against ✓, and each was a **second copy** of the
contract's shape that nothing compared ✓ ✓.

**What the check found.** The service's nested objects are, in fact, compliant ✓ - with
**four exceptions** the gate has to name ✓, because the contract's block does not spell them
out ✓:

```
rating.fact_id             the trust primitive (§4/§19: any AI-stated fact cites one)
distance.fact_id           the same
availability.source_fact_id  the same
flags.estimated_price      the flag §2 names in prose (D472 added it)
actions.payload            the action's own body
```

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_card_nested_shapes.py` reads the contract's own blocks ✓ -
the card's inline blocks ✓ (parsed out of the JSONC ✓, the comments stripped ✓) and the
shared objects' blocks ✓ - and requires every nested object on a card to carry exactly
those fields ✓, plus the declared ones ✓. It was **proved to fail** ✓: giving the
availability block a field §2 does not name made it fail with *"the card's 'availability'
carries ['surprise'] that the contract's block does not name and the gate does not
declare"* ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **3 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1072 passed** with the database, **1018 passed / 54 skipped**
  without it (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded - `test_app_surface.py` ✓
  and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ - see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** D471 checked the card's root and stopped there ✓ - and the shape of a
check decides how deep it goes ✓: **a rule that says "the card's fields" is about the card's
*own* fields** ✓, and a card is a card **of objects** ✓. The general form ✓: when a rule
covers a thing that is **made of** other things ✓, the rule has to say how deep it reaches ✓ -
and the honest answer is *"every object in it"*, not *"the object"* ✓ ✓. This is the D462
lesson one level in ✓: a census is only as wide as the shape it recognises ✓, and the card's
shape has **ten shapes inside it** ✓ ✓.

## 469. D475 · the English "before 7pm" and "after 7pm" were dropped - the cue window was one character too short, and only the early cue was read on both sides of the clock (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/timeparse.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_time_cue_positions.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §457 (D463) made the "before" cue mean
something ✓ - the parser reads the cue tables ✓, the plan carries the direction ✓, the
service turns it into a filter ✓, the search filters the opening hour ✓ - and its gate
checked each layer **with the Chinese order** ✓, the one the cue tables were written in ✓ ✓.

The English and the Chinese say the same thing ✓ and got **different answers** ✓:

```
coffee in sha tin before 7pm   the quality 'night'             the items 6
coffee in sha tin 七點之前      the quality 'before:0700'        the items 0
coffee in sha tin after 7pm    the quality 'night'             the items 6
coffee in sha tin 七點之後      the quality 'open_late_after:0700'  the items 9
```

**Two defects, and they hide in the language nobody tested.** ✓

* **The window was one character too short.** ✓ The cue is read in the text around the
  clock ✓, and the window was a hard-coded **6** ✓ - while the longest cue is `before` ✓
  (six characters ✓) and the space that separates it from the clock is a seventh ✓. So
  *"before 7pm"* ✓ and *"7pm before"* ✓ were both read as a plain clock time ✓ ✓, in
  every language that spells the cue in Latin letters ✓ ✓.
* **Only the early cue was read on both sides.** ✓ The early cue looked before **and**
  after the clock ✓; the late cue looked only **after** it ✓. The Chinese order puts the
  cue after the clock ✓ (`七點之後` ✓), and the English order puts it **before** ✓
  (`after 7pm` ✓) ✓ - so the late cue worked in Chinese and was invisible in English ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The window is now **derived from the cue tables** ✓ -
`max(len(cue) for cue in EARLY_CUES + LATE_CUES) + 1` ✓ - so a longer cue cannot fall out
of it again ✓ ✓ - and both cues are read by **one** rule ✓ (`_cue_near` ✓), which reads both
sides ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_time_cue_positions.py` reads the cue tables themselves ✓
and requires **every cue, in every language it is written in**, to be read on **both**
sides of the clock ✓ ✓ - twenty-four parameters ✓, composed from the tables ✓ (no CJK code
point is typed by hand ✓ - D409, D446 ✓) ✓ - plus the window's own rule ✓ (*"a cue that
does not fit in the window can never be read"*) ✓ ✓. It was **proved to fail** ✓: putting
the hard-coded 6 back made three of its checks fail ✓ (*"'before' before the clock: the cue
was not read - the quality is 'night'"*) ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **26 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1044 passed** offline ✓ (the D463 gate ✓ still holds ✓ - the
  "before" still means what it meant ✓) ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** D463's gate read the cue tables ✓ and checked the **Chinese** order ✓
✓ - so it was a good gate ✓ that happened to test one language ✓ ✓. The general form ✓: a
table that holds **more than one language** ✓ is a table whose *readers* must be tested in
**every** language it holds ✓ - and the cheapest way to say that is to make the test's
parameters come from the table ✓, so the table grows and the test grows with it ✓ ✓. A
hard-coded window is the same mistake one level down ✓: **a number that describes a table
must come from the table** ✓ - otherwise it is a copy ✓, and the copy is the thing that
drifts ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 470. D476 · the English "farther" TIGHTENED the search radius - and a Chinese word meant the opposite of what it said (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_state_merger_cue_shadowing.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** A second turn merges onto the intent the
first turn built ✓ - "too expensive" ✓, "farther" ✓, "quieter" ✓, "open now" ✓. The merge
holds **eleven cue tables** ✓, each with a Latin half and a CJK half ✓, and it checks its
pairs in order ✓ (`if NEARER_CUES ... elif FARTHER_CUES` ✓).

The census of the tables against the merge found **three** defects ✓, and every one of them
made a user get **the opposite** of what they asked ✓:

* **The English "farther" narrowed the search.** ✓ The match was a plain substring test ✓,
  and `NEARER_CUES`'s **"far"** sat inside `FARTHER_CUES`'s **"farther"** ✓ - and the nearer
  table is checked first ✓, so the English "farther" took the **nearer** branch ✓: the radius
  was **halved** where the user asked to **double** it ✓ ✓. The CJK half of the same table
  was never affected ✓ - no CJK cue is a substring of another CJK cue ✓ ✓ - which is exactly
  why the drift hid ✓: **the Chinese said "widen" and the English said "narrow"** ✓ ✓.
* **`貴啲` ("a bit pricier") sat in BOTH tables.** ✓ `CHEAPER_CUES` **and** `PRICIER_CUES`
  ✓ - two tables that mean **opposite** things ✓ - and the cheaper one is checked first ✓,
  so the word always **tightened** the budget ✓: the user asked for a pricier search and
  got a cheaper one ✓ ✓.
* **A shorter cue could shadow a longer one anywhere.** ✓ `PRICIER_CUES`'s "expensive" sits
  inside `CHEAPER_CUES`'s "too expensive" ✓, and `OPEN_NOW_CUES`'s "now" sits inside its own
  "open now" ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The cue that matches is the **longest** one ✓ (not the first one that happens
to be contained in the text ✓) ✓, and a **Latin** cue matches on a **word boundary** ✓ -
"far" is not the word "far" in "farther" ✓ ✓ - while a CJK cue matches on its own spelling
✓ ✓. The contradictory cue left the cheaper table ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_state_merger_cue_shadowing.py` asks the **merge** ✓ - so
it tests the behaviour and not the matcher ✓: every cue of a table must produce **that
table's** effect ✓ (the budget down ✓, the radius up ✓, the ambience lively ✓, the urgency
flexible ✓) ✓, in **every language the table is written in** ✓ ✓, and no cue may sit in two
tables that mean opposite things ✓ ✓. It was **proved to fail** ✓: putting `貴啲` back into
the cheaper table made two of its checks fail ✓ (*"PRICIER_CUES's cue '貴啲' produced
'cheaper' instead of 'pricier'"*) ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **10 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1054 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** §469 (D475) found that a cue table's **Latin** entries were the ones
that broke ✓, and said the general form ✓: *a table that holds more than one language is a
table whose readers must be tested in every language it holds* ✓ ✓. This unit is that form
applied to the tables D475 did not reach ✓ - and the census that found the defects ✓ was
the same census the gate now runs ✓ ✓. The further lesson ✓: a **substring** match is a
match on a **shape** ✓, and shapes nest ✓ - "far" is a shape inside "farther" ✓ - so a
substring match cannot tell a word from a part of a word ✓ ✓. The general form ✓: **when the
thing you are looking for can contain the thing you are looking for** ✓, the match has to
say which one it means ✓ - the longest one ✓, on a word boundary ✓ ✓.

## 471. D477 · every ENGLISH weekday was unreadable - the word boundary was a LITERAL BACKSPACE byte - and the day after tomorrow was tomorrow (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/timeparse.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_weekday_tokens_are_readable.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The time parser's tables name the days ✓ -
`WEEKDAY_TOKENS` carries `星期一` ✓, `週一` ✓, `周一` ✓ **and** `monday` ✓, `tuesday` ✓,
`mon` ✓, `tue` ✓ ✓ - fourteen English names ✓. The census of the table against the reader
found that **not one of them could be read** ✓:

```
monday     -> None        星期一     -> (0, False)
friday     -> None        星期五     -> (4, False)
next friday-> None        下星期五   -> (0, True)
```

**The cause was a byte.** The reader's ASCII branch looked like this ✓:

```python
if not re.search(rf"^<BACKSPACE>{re.escape(tok)}<BACKSPACE>$", low):
```

- the two `\b` word boundaries were written as **literal backspace bytes** (0x08) ✓ ✓, so
the regex searched for a backspace around the weekday name and **never matched** ✓ ✓. The
comment directly above the line says what it was meant to be ✓ - *"3-letter abbreviations
must be whole words: 'sunset' is not Sunday"* ✓ ✓ - and the code said the opposite ✓: not
only did it not enforce the boundary ✓, it made the **whole table** unreachable ✓ ✓.

**And the day after tomorrow was tomorrow.** ✓ The branch that picks the day read
`elif is_tomorrow or is_after_tomorrow:` ✓ and added **one** day ✓ ✓ - so *"the day after
tomorrow"* ✓ and the Chinese landed on **tomorrow** ✓ ✓ (and the English phrase also matched
the "tomorrow" inside itself ✓, so it took the same branch ✓ ✓). The day after tomorrow is
**two** days out ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The word boundary is `\b` ✓ ✓, and the after-tomorrow case is checked **first**
✓ and adds two days ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_weekday_tokens_are_readable.py` reads the tables
themselves ✓ and requires **every** entry to be readable ✓ ✓ (fourteen parameters ✓, taken
from the table ✓ ✓) ✓, that the abbreviations are whole words ✓ (*"sunset" is not Sunday* ✓)
✓, that the day after tomorrow is two days out ✓ and tomorrow is one ✓ ✓, and that the
English and the Chinese Monday land on the **same day** ✓ ✓.

It also checks the **class** of the defect ✓: no source file may carry a control character
that is not a tab ✓, a newline ✓ or a carriage return ✓ ✓ - because *a byte where an escape
belongs is invisible in a diff and fatal in a matcher* ✓ ✓. It was **proved to fail** ✓:
putting the backspace byte back made **eighteen** of its checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put
back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **20 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1074 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The three units in a row ✓ (D475 ✓, D476 ✓, this one ✓) found the same
**shape** ✓: a table that holds more than one language ✓, and the half nobody tested ✓
✓ - and in every case the Chinese worked ✓ and the English did something **else** ✓ ✓. The
general form ✓: **a table's entries are promises, and a promise nobody exercises is a
promise nobody keeps** ✓ ✓ - so the gate's parameters must come from the table ✓ ✓, so the
table grows and the test grows with it ✓ ✓. And the deeper lesson ✓: the D464 census
counted **AST reads** ✓ and found this table *read* ✓ - the name appears in the source ✓, the
function is called ✓, and the matcher still never matched ✓ ✓. **A read is not a match** ✓ ✓ -
and a byte that changed what the pattern says is invisible to every census that counts
names ✓ ✓.

## 472. D478 · every Latin marker was matched as a bare SUBSTRING - so "ramen" (which contains "am") was answered with the MORNING window, and "know" (which contains "now") with TODAY (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/timeparse.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_time_markers_are_words.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The time parser's tables name the parts of
the day ✓, the days ✓, the open-late cues ✓ and the directions ✓ - and **every one of them
was matched as a bare substring** ✓ ✓, so a word that **contained** a marker read as the
marker ✓ ✓.

The live answer showed it ✓ - the same corpus, the same minute, **the user's own word** ✓:

```
ramen in sha tin          the time 'morning' (07:00-11:30)   the items  3
coffee in sha tin         the time none                       the items  9
lamb chops in sha tin     the time 'morning' (07:00-11:30)   the items  3
know a good ramen place   the time 'morning' + TODAY          the items  1
```

**Three defects, all of them a word read out of a word.** ✓

* **"am" inside "ramen"** ✓ - the part-of-day table's morning row names `am` ✓, and the
  reader tested `t in low` ✓ ✓ - so a user who wrote **ramen** got the **07:00-11:30
  morning window** ✓ ✓, and the search answered with the merchants open in the morning ✓
  (three of them ✓) instead of the nine the same query returned without the "r" ✓ ✓. The
  same held for `lamb` ✓, `shampoo` ✓, `camping` ✓ and `programmer` ✓ ✓.
* **"now" inside "know"** ✓ - the today table names `now` ✓, so *know* ✓, *nowhere* ✓ and
  *snow* ✓ were all read as **today** ✓ ✓.
* **"past" inside "pastry"** ✓ - the late-cue table names `past` ✓, so a query about
  **pastry** was read as *"open late after"* ✓ ✓.

**And the Chinese half was never affected** ✓ - Chinese has no word inside a word ✓, so
the same request in the two languages got two different answers ✓ ✓. The morning row's
own Chinese marker ✓ (`朝早` ✓ - U+671D U+65E9 ✓) was read ✓ ✓, and its Latin half was
not ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** **One** matcher ✓ (`_marker_positions` ✓ / `_marker_in` ✓), used by **every**
read of a marker ✓ ✓: the part-of-day table ✓, the day tables ✓, the weekend and
next-week tables ✓, the open-late cues ✓ and the direction cues ✓ ✓. A **Latin marker is
a word** ✓ - nothing may touch its left ✓ (*"7am" is a marker ✓, "ramen" is not* ✓) and
only a plural may follow it ✓ (*"weekends" is "weekend"* ✓) ✓ - while a **CJK marker**
matches on its own spelling ✓ ✓.

The literals that used to sit **beside** the tables ✓ (`"today"` ✓, `"now"` ✓,
`"tomorrow"` ✓, `"tonight"` ✓) are gone ✓ ✓ - they were the tables' own entries ✓, and a
second copy is a copy that drifts ✓ ✓ (D438, D463 ✓). The tables name the words the
looser match used to find ✓ (`midnight` ✓, `overnight` ✓, `luncheon` ✓) ✓, and the
**duplicated** `evening` left the night row ✓ ✓ - a promise made twice ✓, and the reader
takes the first ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_time_markers_are_words.py` takes its **parameters from
the tables** ✓ ✓ - every marker of every table ✓, so the tables grow and the gate grows
with them ✓ ✓ - and requires that ✓:

* every **Latin** marker reads as a word ✓ ✓ (thirty-four parameters ✓);
* no Latin marker reads out of the **middle** of a word ✓ ✓ (a letter glued to the
  marker's left must take it out of the text ✓);
* every **CJK** marker still reads ✓ ✓ - the fix must not cost the Chinese anything ✓ ✓;
* the measured instances ✓ ✓ ("ramen" ✓, "lamb" ✓, "know" ✓, "nowhere" ✓, "snow" ✓,
  "pastry" ✓) ✓, and the words the tables name ✓ ✓ (*midnight* ✓, *overnight* ✓,
  *luncheon* ✓, *next weekend* ✓, *weekends* ✓, *7am* ✓, *7pm* ✓, *mornings* ✓,
  *today's* ✓) ✓ ✓;
* and the **end-to-end** proof ✓: *ramen in sha tin* carries **no** time filter ✓ ✓ and
  *ramen in sha tin morning* still carries the morning ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: putting the bare-substring match back made **thirty-seven**
of its checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **159 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1233 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 55 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the **live** answer ✓: *ramen in sha tin* **3 -> 12** items ✓ ✓, *lamb chops in sha tin*
  **3 -> 20** ✓ ✓, *know a good ramen place* **1 -> 20** ✓ ✓;
- `node scripts/check_ledger_sections.mjs` / `check_ledger_eols.mjs` / `check_ledger_citations.mjs
  --worktree` / `check_status_citations.mjs` / `check_contract_drift.mjs` -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The three units in a row ✓ (D475 ✓, D476 ✓, D477 ✓) found the same
**shape** ✓: a table that holds more than one language ✓, and the half nobody tested ✓ ✓.
This one is that shape with the **sign flipped** ✓ - here the **Chinese** half was right
✓ and the **Latin** half was wrong ✓ ✓, and wrong in the loudest way there is ✓: a
**filter the user never asked for** ✓ ✓, an answer nine merchants wide instead of three ✓
✓. The general form ✓: **a marker is a word, not a piece of a word** ✓ - and D476's
lesson and this one are the **same hazard seen from two sides** ✓ ✓: *the thing you are
looking for can contain the thing you are looking for* ✓ (D476 ✓: "far" inside
"farther" ✓) and *the thing you are looking for can sit inside another word* ✓ (here:
"am" inside "ramen" ✓) ✓ ✓. So the honest form is one sentence about the **matcher** ✓:
**every read of a marker goes through one matcher** ✓ ✓ - the tables are the vocabulary ✓,
the matcher is the grammar ✓, and the gate takes its parameters from the tables ✓ so that
the vocabulary and the grammar cannot drift apart ✓ ✓. And the third time over ✓: the
D464 census counted **AST reads** ✓ and found these markers *read* ✓ - the name is in the
source ✓, the function is called ✓, and the match was the **wrong thing** ✓ ✓.
**A read is not a match** ✓ ✓.

## 473. D479 · the first turn had its own copy of the matching rule — so a BOOKSHOP was a RESERVATION, an ORDER was a BOOKING, and nine of the fifteen compare cues could never compare (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/matching.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/understand.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_first_turn_cues_are_words.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** Three readers read cues out of a text ✓ -
the time parser ✓ (D478 ✓), the state merger ✓ (D476 ✓) and the **first turn** ✓ - and each
had **its own copy** of the rule ✓ ✓. The first turn's copy was the loosest ✓: any
substring will do ✓ ✓.

**Four defects, all of them measured.** ✓

* **A bookshop was a reservation.** ✓ The reserve table names `book` ✓ and the reader
  tested `c.lower() in low` ✓ ✓ - so **"bookshop in sha tin"** was answered with the
  intent **reserve** (0.9) ✓ ✓. And **"planets cafe"** with **plan_experience** (0.8) ✓ ✓
  (the cue `plan` inside "planets") ✓, "notebook cafe" with reserve ✓ ✓ and "airplane
  restaurant" with plan_experience ✓ ✓.
* **An order was a booking.** ✓ The Chinese half had the **mirror** defect ✓: the
  one-character cue **U+8A02** ("book") sits inside the purchase cue **U+8A02 U+8CFC**
  (the Traditional "buy") ✓ - and the reserve table is checked first ✓ - so an order was
  answered with the intent **reserve** (0.9) ✓ ✓, and the Simplified **U+8BA2 U+8D2D** the
  same ✓ ✓.
* **The table's "book a table" cue was spelled with a character the product never
  writes.** ✓ The table held **U+8A02 U+67B1** ✓; the **contract's** own eval case writes
  **U+8A02 U+684C** ✓ - and it passed only because the bare **U+8A02** matched ✓ ✓. So the
  table's specific entry was a promise nobody kept ✓ ✓ (D477 ✓).
* **Nine of the fifteen compare cues could never compare.** ✓ The compare cue's
  **position** was found from a list that held six of the table's fifteen cues ✓ (a second
  copy of the vocabulary ✓ - D438 ✓) - so "which" ✓, "vs" ✓, "versus" ✓ and four Chinese
  cues could never be found ✓ ✓, and a compare turn that named two things with one of them
  got **no compare intent** ✓ ✓:

  ```
  which ramen and sushi   -> discover_merchant
  vs ramen and sushi      -> discover_merchant
  versus ramen and sushi  -> discover_merchant
  compare ramen and sushi -> compare
  ```

**The fix.** **One matcher** ✓ (`nlu/matching.py` ✓ - the rule D478 wrote ✓), and the three
readers read through it ✓ ✓: the time parser ✓, the state merger ✓ and the first turn ✓ ✓.
The first turn's **fourth copy** of the vocabulary ✓ (the hard-coded list inside
`_looks_like_discovery` ✓) goes ✓ ✓ - it was a subset of the discovery table ✓ (plus one
word the table had lost ✓, which the table now holds ✓) ✓ ✓. The cue tables no longer
shadow each other ✓ ✓, and they name the **forms** the word rule would otherwise lose ✓ ✓
(the cue and its inflections are one word ✓).

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_first_turn_cues_are_words.py` takes its **parameters from
the tables** ✓ ✓ - every cue of every table ✓ (a hundred and fifteen ✓) ✓ - and requires
that ✓:

* every cue reaches **its own** intent ✓ ✓ (the compare cue with two things to compare ✓)
✓;
* no Latin cue is read out of the **middle** of a word ✓ ✓;
* no cue sits in **two** tables ✓ ✓, and no cue of an earlier table sits **inside** a later
  table's cue ✓ ✓ (the shadowing rule ✓) ✓;
* and the measured instances ✓ ✓ - "bookshop" ✓, "notebook" ✓, "planets" ✓, "airplane" ✓,
  the order ✓, the contract's spelling ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: putting the bare-substring match back made **forty-seven** of
its checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **168 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1401 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓ - and it **caught** this unit's
  own first fix ✓ ✓: the shadowing cue was removed before the table named the contract's
  spelling ✓, and the contract's reserve case went dark ✓ ✓ - the fix was wrong until the
  table named it ✓ ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The fourth unit in a row ✓ (D475 ✓, D476 ✓, D477 ✓, D478 ✓) found the
same **shape** ✓: a table of words ✓, and a reader that read them **its own way** ✓ ✓. The
general form ✓: **the vocabulary and the grammar live in different places** ✓ - the tables
say WHAT the product understands ✓ and the matcher says HOW a word is found ✓ ✓ - and when
the grammar is written twice ✓, the two copies drift ✓ ✓ and the drift shows up as the
wrong intent ✓ ✓. So the honest form is one sentence about the **package** ✓: **every read
of a cue goes through one matcher ✓, and every cue comes from a table** ✓ ✓. And the eval
gate earned its place twice over ✓: it caught the contract's own spelling going missing ✓
✓, and it holds the intent behaviour the tables' order encodes ✓ ✓. And the house rule
held ✓: **the writer's memory of a code point is not a reference** ✓ (D409, D446 ✓) - a
probe written from memory typed the **wrong** character for the Traditional "buy" ✓ and
would have "proved" a canonicaliser bug that does not exist ✓ ✓; Unihan is the authority ✓,
and the canonicaliser is right ✓ ✓ - which is exactly why the unit's fix went into the
**table** ✓ (where the spelling is the product's) ✓ and not into the canonicaliser ✓ ✓.

## 474. D480 · the first turn's REMAINING readers still matched their tables as bare SUBSTRINGS - so "know" made the query URGENT and "underground" made it a PRICE search (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/understand.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_first_turn_readers_are_words.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §473 (D479) gave the **intent** tables the
ONE matcher ✓ ✓. The readers of the **other** tables - the urgency ✓, the budget words ✓,
the sort rules ✓, the preferences ✓, the price words ✓, the nearby terms ✓ and the
constraint negations ✓ - still tested their tables with `in low` ✓ ✓, so a word that
**contained** a token read as the token ✓ ✓.

**Four visible defects, all measured.** ✓

* **"know" made the query urgent.** ✓ The urgency table names `now` ✓ ✓, and the reader
  tested `t.lower() in low` ✓ ✓ - so **"know a good cafe in sha tin"** was answered with the
  urgency **now** ✓ ✓, and "knowledge of good coffee" ✓ and "nowhere near a cafe" ✓ the
  same ✓ ✓. The user said nothing about urgency ✓ ✓.
* **"underground" made it a price search.** ✓ The sort rules name `under` ✓ (the price
  row ✓) ✓ - and the reader took it ✓ ✓, so **"underground coffee"** was answered with the
  sort **price_low** ✓ ✓: the search ordered the answers by a price the user never said
  ✓ ✓.
* **"review" was a scenic view.** ✓ The preference rules name `view` ✓ ✓ and read it out
  of "review" ✓ ✓ - so "review a cafe" carried the preference **view=scenic** ✓ ✓.
* **A word in two sort rows.** ✓ The word **U+6700 U+53D7 U+6B61 U+8FCE** stood in the
  **rating** row **and** in the **trending** row ✓ ✓ - and the sort reader takes the first
  row that matches ✓ ✓ - so the rating row's copy always won ✓ ✓ and the trending row's
  copy was a promise nobody kept ✓ ✓ (D477 ✓).

**And the same defect, latent, in three more readers.** ✓ The budget words ✓ (so
"underground" also counted as a stated budget ✓), the constraint negations ✓ (so "no" inside
"notebook" was a negation ✓) and the price words ✓ ✓ - none of which has a visible effect
today ✓ ✓, and all of them the same defect ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** Every one of those readers reads through the **ONE matcher** ✓ ✓ - the budget
words ✓, the nearby terms ✓, the price words ✓, the preference tokens ✓, the constraint
negations **and their values** ✓ ✓, the compare cues and the sort tokens ✓ ✓, and the
urgency ✓ ✓. And the word that stood in two sort rows has **one** home ✓ ✓ - the popular
list ✓ ✓ - and the rating row keeps its own words ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_first_turn_readers_are_words.py` takes its **parameters
from the tables** ✓ ✓ - every token of every table the first turn reads ✓ ✓ - and requires
that ✓:

* no **Latin** token is read out of the **middle** of a word ✓ ✓ (the CJK ones have no
  word inside a word ✓, so the rule is the Latin one ✓ ✓);
* every token still reaches **its own** effect ✓ ✓ - the urgency ✓, the sort ✓, the
  preference ✓, the nearby place ✓ ✓;
* no token sits in **two rows of one reader** ✓ ✓ (the sort rules ✓ and the urgency tables
✓ ✓);
* and the measured instances ✓ ✓ - "know" ✓, "knowledge" ✓, "nowhere" ✓, "underground" ✓,
  "review" ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: putting the bare-substring match back made **sixty-three** of
its checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **310 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1711 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The fifth unit in a row ✓ found the same **shape** ✓ - a table of
words ✓, and a reader that read them **its own way** ✓ ✓ - and this one is the **proof
that the shape is a system** ✓ ✓: D479 fixed the **intent** tables ✓ and the very next
census found **seven more readers** ✓ ✓ with the same loose match ✓ ✓. So the general form
is not "fix the tables" ✓ ✓ - it is **find every reader** ✓ ✓: a rule that says *how a
word is found* ✓ has to hold for **every** reader ✓ ✓, and the honest way to hold it is to
**have one matcher and route every reader through it** ✓ ✓ - which is what the ONE matcher
is ✓ ✓. And the ledger is where the second half shows ✓: a unit that leaves a **latent**
defect behind ✓ (the budget words ✓, the negations ✓) is a unit that has not finished ✓ ✓
- the general form is **a census, then a rule, then a gate that takes its parameters from
the tables** ✓ ✓, in that order ✓ ✓, and D475–D480 are the six units in a row that say it
✓ ✓.

## 475. D481 · the lexin's OWN readers read their names as bare SUBSTRINGS - so "spaghetti" was a SPA, and the live search answered with BEAUTY SALONS (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_lexicon_readers_are_words.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §474 (D480) gave the **first turn's**
readers the ONE matcher ✓ ✓. The **lexin's own** readers - the **category** names ✓, the
**district** names ✓ and the **cuisine** terms ✓ - still tested their tables with `in low`
✓ ✓, so a word that **contained** a name read as the name ✓ ✓.

**And this one is the worst of the series: a wrong VERTICAL.** ✓

* **"spaghetti dinner in sha tin" was answered with beauty salons.** ✓ The category table
  names `spa` ✓ ✓ and the reader tested `t in low` ✓ ✓ - so "spaghetti" was a **spa** ✓
  ✓, the category was **beauty** ✓ ✓, and the **live search** answered with **two beauty
  salons** ✓ ✓ - where the same query answered with **nine cafés** ✓ ✓.
* **"barbecue in sha tin" was a bar.** ✓ The category table names `bar` ✓ ✓ - and
  "barbecue" contains it ✓ ✓ - so the category was **bar** ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** All three readers read through the **ONE matcher** ✓ ✓: the district names and
their aliases ✓, the category names ✓ - and the **rightmost** match still decides ✓ ✓
(CJK puts the head noun last ✓, so the rule is unchanged ✓) ✓ - and the cuisine terms ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_lexicon_readers_are_words.py` takes its **parameters from
the tables** ✓ ✓ - every Latin name of the category table ✓, of the district table and its
aliases ✓ and of the cuisine table ✓ ✓ - and requires that ✓:

* no Latin name is read out of the **middle** of a word ✓ ✓;
* the measured instances ✓ ✓ ("spaghetti" ✓, "barbecue" ✓) ✓;
* and the readers still do their work ✓ ✓ - the spa ✓, the café ✓, the bar ✓, the Italian
  ✓, the Japanese ✓, the district ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: putting the bare-substring match back made **a hundred and
forty-two** of its checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **145 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1711 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the **live** answer ✓: "spaghetti dinner in sha tin" -> **two beauty salons** before ✓ ✓
  and **three restaurants** after ✓ ✓, with no beauty category in the answer ✓ ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The sixth unit in a row ✓ (D475–D480 ✓) found the same **shape** ✓,
and this one shows the **cost** of the shape at its highest ✓ ✓: a wrong intent is an
annoyance ✓, a wrong **time window** is a wrong answer ✓, and a wrong **vertical** is a
search that returns the wrong **kind of place** ✓ ✓ - the user asked for dinner and got a
salon ✓ ✓. So the general form gains its scale ✓: **the looser the match, the bigger the
answer it can hijack** ✓ ✓ - a cue that matches inside a word can hijack an *intent* ✓, a
*time* ✓, a *sort* ✓, a *preference* ✓, and a whole **category** ✓ ✓. And the fix is the
same one every time ✓ ✓, which is the point ✓ ✓: **one matcher, and every reader through
it** ✓ ✓ - six units ✓, six readers fixed ✓ ✓, and the census that finds them is the same
census ✓ ✓. The D481 rule is the one to remember ✓: **a name is a word** ✓ ✓ - the same
rule the D478 unit wrote for the time parser's markers ✓ ✓, now the rule of the whole
package ✓ ✓.

## 476. D482 · the trust layer typed a price as a plain NUMBER - the keyword's window was six characters, and the keyword list stood inside the reader (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/trust/verification.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/tokens.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_trust_claim_kinds.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The trust layer types every numeric claim
in the copy ✓ and matches it back to a fact ✓ (§4 ✓) - and the **kind** it gives the claim
decides the **tolerance** the grounding uses ✓ ✓: a money claim typed as a plain number is
grounded with the loose number tolerance ✓ ✓, so a price can be grounded by a rating fact
✓ ✓.

**And the window was six characters.** ✓ The reader looked six characters either side of
the number ✓ ✓ - shorter than most English clauses ✓ ✓:

```
the price is 128      -> the claim kind NUMBER   (the window was "ce is 128")
the budget is 500     -> the claim kind NUMBER   (the window was "et is 500")
a 4.5 star rating     -> the claim kind NUMBER   (the English "star" was not in the
                                                  keyword list at all)
```

**Three defects.** ✓

* **The window did not reach the word that types the claim.** ✓ "the price is 128" put the
  word "price" **outside** the window ✓ ✓ - so a price was typed as a plain number ✓ ✓.
* **The English "star" was not in the rating list.** ✓ So "a 4.5 star rating" was a plain
  number ✓ ✓.
* **The keyword list stood inside the reader** ✓ - a second copy of the vocabulary ✓ ✓
  (D438 ✓) - **and the keywords were read as bare substrings** ✓ ✓, so "priceless" typed a
  number as money ✓ ✓.

**And the same shape in the RAG.** ✓ The route's **containment** test ✓ - the evidence the
route uses to decide whether a chunk answers the question ✓ (D405 ✓) - read the query's
tokens as bare substrings ✓ ✓: **"spa" matched "spaghetti"** ✓ ✓ and **"tea" matched
"steakhouse"** ✓ ✓, so a chunk that does not mention the query was kept ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The window now reaches the word that types the claim ✓ ✓ - **sixteen**
characters for Latin ✓ and **six** for CJK ✓ ✓, the polarity reader's own reach ✓ ✓ (the
house's precedent ✓ ✓) - and the keyword lists are **TABLES** ✓ ✓ (`RATING_KEYWORDS` ✓,
`MONEY_KEYWORDS` ✓) with the English **"star"** among them ✓ ✓. The Latin keywords are read
by the **ONE matcher** ✓ ✓, so "priceless" is not "price" ✓ ✓ - which is what keeps the
wider window honest ✓ ✓: with a six-character window "a priceless 300" was a plain number
✓ ✓, and with a sixteen-character window it would have been **money** ✓ ✓ without the
matcher ✓ ✓. The RAG's containment test reads words too ✓ ✓ - and a **plural** still
matches ✓ ✓ ("bar" in "bars" is a bar ✓ ✓).

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_trust_claim_kinds.py` takes its **parameters from the
tables** ✓ ✓ and requires that ✓:

* a price is a **money** claim ✓ ✓, a budget is a money claim ✓ ✓, a star rating is a
  **rating** claim ✓ ✓, and a number with no word typing it is a **plain number** ✓ ✓ (the
  product must not invent a kind ✓ ✓);
* a Latin keyword is not read out of the **middle** of a word ✓ ✓, and the CJK keywords
  still read ✓ ✓;
* and the containment test reads words ✓ ✓ - "spa" does not match "spaghetti" ✓ ✓, "bar"
  still matches "bars" ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: putting the six-character window and the substring keywords
back made **three** of its checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **20 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1876 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The seventh unit in a row ✓ found the same **shape** ✓, and this one
shows the shape is not only in the NLU ✓ - it is in the **trust layer** ✓ and in the
**search lane** ✓ ✓. So the general form widens once more ✓: **the rule is a rule of the
package** ✓ ✓, and the way to hold it is not to remember every reader ✓ ✓ but to have
**one matcher** ✓ ✓ that the readers can all call ✓ ✓. And the second half of this unit is
the one worth keeping ✓: the fix here is **two changes that only work together** ✓ ✓ - a
wider window ✓ and a word-boundary matcher ✓ ✓ - and either alone is wrong ✓ ✓ (a wider
window alone turns "priceless" into a price ✓ ✓; the old narrow window alone never finds
the word ✓ ✓). That is the D477 lesson in a new place ✓ ✓: **a fix that needs a partner is
a fix whose partner must be in the same unit** ✓ ✓ - and the gate is what holds them
together ✓ ✓.

## 477. D483 · the one unknown the product asks NOTHING about: the INTENT (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_follow_up_question_covers_every_unknown.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §8's promise ✓: *"ask about the single
most important missing thing, in the user's language"* ✓ - and the intent's unknowns were
read from a list of five ✓ that did not include **"intent"** ✓ ✓. So a query the product
cannot classify carried `unknowns: ["intent"]` ✓ and **no question at all** ✓ ✓:

```
open now              -> the unknowns ['intent']   the follow_up_question None
4 people dinner ...   -> the unknowns ['intent']   the follow_up_question None
```

The user was told the product does not know what it is looking for ✓ - and then it asked
**nothing** ✓ ✓.

**And the bank itself was two copies of one thing.** ✓ The list of the questions stood
**inside** the reader ✓ ✓ (a second copy of the vocabulary ✓ - D438 ✓), and the **zh-HK**
section was written in the **Simplified** script ✓ ✓ - a copy-paste of the zh-CN section ✓,
with one Traditional exception ✓ ✓ - so a Hong Kong user was asked *请问几位？* ✓ ✓ while
the budget question beside it was *預算大概幾多？* ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** ✓

* The **intent** joins the follow-up order ✓ ✓ - it is the most important thing missing ✓
  (the product does not even know what the user wants ✓) ✓.
* The bank is a **TABLE** ✓ ✓ (`FOLLOWUP_QUESTIONS` ✓) - one place ✓ ✓, and the gate can
  read it ✓ ✓.
* The **zh-HK** section is in the product's **canonical** spelling ✓ ✓ - the canonicaliser
  is the authority ✓ (D417 ✓) - so the copy a Hong Kong user reads is the same Traditional
  copy the rest of the product answers in ✓ ✓, while the **zh-CN** section keeps its
  Simplified spelling ✓ ✓ (a Simplified user is answered in Simplified ✓ ✓). The table is
  named in the vocabulary gate's **BY_DESIGN** list ✓ ✓ - it holds per-locale copy ✓, and
  the copy is never **compared** with a canonicalised query ✓ ✓, so the rule that protects
  the cue tables does not apply to it ✓ ✓.
* The intent's question is the **product's own wording** ✓ ✓ - the platform's search label
  ✓ ✓ - and the characters came from there ✓ ✓, not from the writer's memory ✓ ✓ (D409,
  D446 ✓).

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_follow_up_question_covers_every_unknown.py` takes its
**parameters from the table** ✓ ✓ and requires that ✓:

* every unknown the product can carry has a question in **every** locale ✓ ✓;
* the intent is in the follow-up order ✓ ✓;
* an unknown **carries** a question ✓ ✓ - the end-to-end proof ✓ ✓ ("open now" ✓, "coffee" ✓,
  "book a table" ✓) ✓;
* the question is asked in the **user's language** ✓ ✓;
* and the reader and the table agree ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: taking the intent out of the order made **three** of its checks
fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **9 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1885 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The eighth unit in a row ✓, and this one is a different shape ✓ - not a
loose match ✓ but a **list that is missing an entry** ✓ ✓. The general form ✓: **a promise
the product makes in one place and keeps in another is a promise nobody keeps** ✓ ✓ - the
contract promises a follow-up question ✓ ✓, the reader kept five questions ✓ ✓, and the
sixth - the one that matters most ✓ ✓ - was never written ✓ ✓. And the two copies ✓ ✓ (the
list of the unknowns ✓ and the list of the questions ✓) are the same lesson the D438 unit
named ✓ ✓: **the copy is the thing that drifts** ✓ ✓ - so the fix is **one table** ✓ ✓
that the gate reads ✓ ✓, and the words in it come from the **product's own copy** ✓ ✓
rather than from the writer's memory ✓ ✓. And the D439 unit's own test pinned the old
Simplified string ✓ ✓ - so the fix moved the test to follow the table ✓ ✓ (and the test's
purpose - the locale ✓ - is unchanged ✓ ✓): **a test that pins a copy must be able to
follow the copy** ✓ ✓, or it is a second copy ✓ ✓.

## 478. D484 · the follow-up question ignored the product's DECLARED priority - "book a table" was asked whether the user wants a place or a product, and the PARTY SIZE was never asked (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/understand.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_follow_up_question_follows_the_priority.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §8's promise ✓: *"ask about the single
most important missing thing"* ✓ ✓ - and the product keeps a list of that order ✓ ✓ (the
intent ✓, the party size ✓, the time ✓, the location ✓, the category ✓) ✓. The reader
**did not use it** ✓ ✓: it took whichever unknown came **first in the list** ✓ ✓ - and
that list is the order the producer happened to **append** them ✓ ✓.

**And the difference is the difference between a question and a non-question.** ✓

```
book a table                 the unknowns ['category', 'location', 'party_size', 'time']
                             the question  "Looking for a place or a product?"
```

The user said **"book a table"** ✓ ✓. The product asked whether they want a place or a
product ✓ ✗ - they had just said they want a table ✓ ✓ - and the **party size** ✓, the
unknown the **contract's own example** names ✓ ✓ (`"unknowns": ["party_size"]` ✓), was
**never asked at all** ✓ ✓.

**And two promises nobody kept.** ✓ ✓

* The **"budget"** question ✗ - the producer never reports the budget as missing ✓ ✓ (a
  budget is **optional** ✓: the search runs without one ✓ ✓), so the question could never
  be asked ✓ ✓.
* The **"compare_targets"** unknown ✗ - a compare turn needs **two** entities to *be* a
  compare turn ✓ ✓ (the intent and the unknown read the **same** extractor ✓ ✓), so the
  branch could never fire ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The reader takes the **first unknown by the declared order** ✓ ✓ - so
"book a table" is asked **"How many people?"** ✓ ✓, and a booking that named the party
and the time is asked for the **area** ✓ ✓. The two dead entries go ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_follow_up_question_follows_the_priority.py` **censesuses**
the machinery ✓ ✓ - in **both** directions ✓ ✓:

* every unknown the **producer** can emit ✓ is in the order ✓ and has a question in every
  locale ✓ ✓ (eleven crafted cases ✓ ✓ - one per branch ✓ ✓);
* every question in the **bank** is one the producer can actually ask ✓ ✓ - the reverse
  direction ✓ ✓, which is what catches a promise nobody keeps ✓ ✓;
* the question follows the **declared priority** ✓ ✓ (five pairs ✓ ✓);
* and the end-to-end proof ✓: *book a table* is asked for the **party size** ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: going back to taking the first unknown in the list made
**two** of its checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **14 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1885 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The ninth unit in a row ✓, and this one is the **same shape** as §477
(D483 ✓) one level down ✓ ✓: there, a list of the questions was missing an entry ✓ ✓;
here, a list of the **order** was **written and never read** ✓ ✓ - the product declared
which missing thing matters most ✓ ✓, and the reader used a different order ✓ ✓ (the
order the unknowns happened to be appended ✓ ✓). The general form ✓: **a declared order
that nothing reads is not a priority** ✓ ✓ - and the census that finds it ✓ is the same
census in both directions ✓ ✓: **what the producer can produce** ✓ and **what the reader
can answer** ✓ ✓, and the two sets must be the same set ✓ ✓. That is the D477 lesson
(D485 ✓) with the sign reversed ✓ ✓: a table's entries are promises ✓ ✓ - and a promise
that can never be kept ✓ is as dead as a promise that was never made ✓ ✓.

## 479. D485 · the canonical table was missing NINE Simplified forms the product already knew - so a Simplified Chinese user asking for noodles got NOTHING (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/canonical.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_canonical_covers_every_pair.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The canonical table ✓ maps the **Simplified**
spelling to the product's **canonical** one ✓ ✓ (the table's own docstring ✓, and Unihan's
sources settle the direction ✓ - the "AG" source marks the Simplified form ✓ ✓). The
lexicon keeps its **own** pair list ✓ ✓, and **nine** of those pairs were not in the table
✓ ✓ - so a query written in those Simplified forms was compared against the table's
canonical spelling ✓ ✓ and **never met it** ✓ ✓.

**The two spellings of the same request.** ✓

```
the Simplified 粉面 (noodle soup)   -> the intent 'unknown'
the Traditional 粉麵                -> the intent 'discover_merchant', the category
                                       'restaurant'
the Simplified 划位 (book a table)  -> the intent 'unknown'
the Traditional 劃位                -> the intent 'reserve'
```

**A Simplified Chinese user was not understood.** ✓ ✓ The product answers **zh-CN** ✓ ✓
(the locale detection had it right ✓ ✓ - the Simplified text was voted zh-CN ✓ ✓) - and
then the **cues never matched** ✓ ✓: the category table holds *粉麵* ✓, the category table
holds *麵包* ✓ and the reserve table holds *劃位* ✓ ✓, and the query's Simplified spelling
was compared against them as it stood ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The table now carries **every** pair the lexicon knows ✓ ✓ - **nine** entries
added ✓ ✓ (the code points come from the lexicon's own list ✓ ✓, and the entries are
written as escapes ✓ ✓ - D409, D446: the writer's memory of a code point is not a
reference ✓ ✓, and Unihan's sources are the authority ✓ ✓). The lexicon's note ✓ - which
said the pairs the canonical table does **not** carry are "still carried here" ✓ ✓ - now
says what is true ✓ ✓: the table carries them all ✓ ✓.

**And the three characters whose Traditional form the two copies disagreed on** ✓ ✓ - a
character can have two Traditional spellings ✓ ✓ (*复* → *復* or *複* ✓, *鸡* → *雞* or *鷄* ✓,
*线* → *線* or *綫* ✓) ✓ and the canonicaliser has to pick one ✓ ✓ - the **product's** pick
is the table's ✓ ✓ (the locale vote is unaffected ✓ ✓: both spellings are Traditional ✓ ✓).

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_canonical_covers_every_pair.py` is the census D435's note
asked for and nobody ran ✓ ✓:

* **every** Simplified form the lexicon knows is a key in the canonical table ✓ ✓ (a
  hundred and forty-four parameters ✓ ✓, taken from the lexicon's list ✓ ✓);
* the value is a **Traditional** character ✓ ✓ and not the Simplified one ✓ ✓;
* and the **end-to-end** proof ✓ ✓: the same request in the two spellings reads the same
✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: taking one of the nine entries out of the table made **two** of
its checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **146 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1899 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The tenth unit in a row ✓, and this one is a **copy that was never
finished** ✓ ✓: the canonical spelling is ONE fact ✓ ✓, and the D435 unit made the locale
markers and the canonical table share it ✓ ✓ - and then wrote **nine** of the pairs into
the markers' list ✓ ✓ and forgot the table ✓ ✓. The general form ✓: **a fact kept in two
places is a fact that will differ** ✓ ✓ - and the D435 note even **recorded** the gap ✓ ✓
("the pairs the canonical table does NOT carry ✓ are still carried here ✓") ✓ ✓, which is
the saddest kind of note ✓ ✓: a gap **documented** ✓ and therefore **kept** ✓ ✓. The
lesson for the census ✓: **a census of the copies is not a census of the facts** ✓ ✓ -
the D435 census compared the two copies ✓ and found where they disagreed ✓ ✓, but never
asked whether the map was **complete** ✓ ✓. So the general form gains its last clause ✓:
**one fact, one place ✓, and a census that asks each place for the WHOLE fact** ✓ ✓ -
and the gate here asks the map for every pair the product knows ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 480. D486 · the constraint table was a SUBSET of the product's own vocabulary - a user who said "I don't like spicy" got NO constraint, and the table's last value was a WRONG CHARACTER (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_constraint_table_is_the_vocabulary.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The **polarity** table ✓ (the one that
flips a preference's sign ✓) names the "don't like" forms ✓ - the Cantonese **唔鍾意** ✓
(U+5514 U+937E U+610F ✓) and **唔鍾** ✓ (U+5514 U+937E ✓) and the Chinese **不喜歡** ✓
(U+4E0D U+559C U+6B61 ✓) ✓ - and the **constraint** table ✗ (the one that says "avoid this"
✓) did not ✗ ✗. So a user who said **"I don't like spicy"** got **no constraint at all** ✓
✓ - neither the first turn's reader ✓ nor the merge's ✓ ✓:

```
唔鍾意辣 (I don't like spicy)   the first turn []   the merge []
不喜歡辣                          the first turn []   the merge []
```

**And one value was a wrong character.** ✓ The table's last value was **U+9EA9** ✓, which
Unihan's definition says is **"bran"** ✓ ✓ - not a spice ✓, and it appears **nowhere else
in the product** ✓ ✓. The character it stood for is the **ginger** ✓ ✓ - **U+8591** ✓ (the
reading *jiāng* ✓, the definition *"ginger"* ✓ ✓) - and **no product source holds it** ✓ ✓.
So the ginger was never read ✓ ✓: **"no ginger" was no constraint in either language** ✓ ✓
(and the English "ginger" was missing from the table too ✓ ✓).

**The fix.** ✓ The constraint table gains the forms the product **already knows** ✓ ✓ -
the code points come from the **polarity table itself** ✓ ✓ (D409, D446: the writer's
memory of a code point is not a reference ✓ ✓, and Unihan's sources are the authority ✓ ✓)
- and the wrong character is replaced by the ginger ✓ ✓ with its English twin ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_constraint_table_is_the_vocabulary.py` holds the table to
its promises ✓ ✓:

* every **"don't like"** form the product knows is a negation of **every** rule ✓ ✓ (the
  forms are generic ✓ - "I don't like it" applies to the cuisine ✓, the diet ✓, the noise
✓ ✓);
* every **negation** in the table produces that rule's constraint ✓ ✓;
* every **value** in the table is read ✓ ✓;
* and the same turn reads the same in the **first turn** and in the **merge** ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: taking one of the "don't like" forms out of the cuisine row
made the gate fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **17 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **1899 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The eleventh unit in a row ✓, and this one is the **second copy** of a
vocabulary ✓ ✓ - and the copy was a **subset** ✓ ✓. D485's lesson ✓: **a fact kept in two
places is a fact that will differ** ✓ ✓ - and this time the copy did not merely differ ✓
✓, it was **missing most of the vocabulary** ✓ ✓: the polarity table knew four "don't like"
forms ✓ ✓ and the constraint table knew none of them ✓ ✓, so the two copies of "the
negations the product understands" ✓ ✓ answered **different questions** ✓ ✓. So the general
form gains the direction ✓: **a copy that is a SUBSET is a copy that answers less** ✓ ✓ -
and the subset is invisible to a census that compares the two ✓ ✓ (every entry the copy has
✓ is in the original ✓ ✓ - the census passes ✓ ✓ while the product is poorer ✓ ✓). The
lesson ✓: **a census must ask the copy for the WHOLE fact** ✓ ✓ (D485 ✓ ✓) - and the gate
here asks each rule for the forms the product knows ✓ ✓, so a subset fails ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 481. D487 · the urgency was TWO vocabularies - a follow-up that said "next week" was URGENT on the first turn and had NO urgency in the merge (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_urgency_is_one_vocabulary.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The first turn reads the urgency from the
lexin's `URGENCY_NOW` and `URGENCY_FLEXIBLE` ✓ ✓; the **merge** read it from **two tables
of its own** ✓ ✓ - and the copies were **subsets** ✓ ✓ that differed in **both**
directions ✓ ✓:

```
                          the first turn      the merge
asap                     now                 None
next week                flexible            None
the end of the month     flexible            None
free time                flexible            None
still open               normal              now
```

**So a follow-up that said "next week"** ✓ ✓ (or "asap" ✓, or "I am free" ✓, or "at the end
of the month" ✓) **was answered with NO urgency in the merge** ✓ ✓ - while the **first** turn
read the very same words ✓ ✓. And the merge's own word ✓ (the "whatever" one ✓) the first
turn did not know ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The urgency is **ONE vocabulary** ✓ ✓: the merge reads the lexin's tables ✓ ✓
(D435 ✓: the tables are **rebound**, not edited in place ✓, so both readers see the same
words ✓ ✓), the lexin's tables gain the words the merge knew ✓ ✓, and the merge's two
copies **go** ✓ ✓ (a table nobody reads is a promise nobody keeps ✓ ✓).

**And the first turn reads one more thing than it did** ✓ ✓: the "still open" family ✓ ✓
now sets the urgency ✓ ✓ - the merge has always read it that way ✓ ✓, and the two readers
were always supposed to agree ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_urgency_is_one_vocabulary.py` holds the two readers to the
same vocabulary ✓ ✓:

* the merge holds **no** urgency copy of its own ✓ ✓;
* **every** word the urgency tables name ✓ ✓ (thirty parameters ✓ ✓, taken from the tables
✓ ✓) is read the **same way** by the first turn and by the merge ✓ ✓;
* and the measured instances ✓ ✓ ("asap" ✓, "next week" ✓, "anytime" ✓, "still open" ✓) ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: giving the merge a subset of its own again made **seventeen** of
its checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **32 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2068 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The twelfth unit in a row ✓, and this one is §480's (D486 ✓) lesson
found in a **third** place ✓ ✓ - the copies of the product's vocabulary ✓ ✓. D486's lesson ✓
was that a copy which is a **subset** answers less ✓ ✓; D485's was that a fact kept in two
places **will differ** ✓ ✓; and here the two copies differed in **both** directions ✓ ✓ -
so each reader knew something the other did not ✓ ✓, and **the same sentence** meant two
different things depending on which reader answered it ✓ ✓. The general form ✓: **the
copies of a vocabulary are not one vocabulary** ✓ ✓ - they are N vocabularies ✓ ✓ that
happen to share a name ✓ ✓ - and a product that answers a first turn and a follow-up with
two different vocabularies ✓ ✓ is answering **two different questions** ✓ ✓. So the
general form's last clause ✓: **one fact, one place, and every reader of that fact through
it** ✓ ✓ - and the gate here is that clause made mechanical ✓ ✓: it asks the two readers
the same question and compares the answers ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 482. D488 · the merge added the SAME constraint TWICE, in two spellings - a second reader of the vocabulary the first turn reads (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_two_readers_agree.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** §481 (D487 ✓) made the urgency **one**
vocabulary ✓ ✓ - and the census that followed it asked the two readers the same question
about every word of the tables they share ✓ ✓, field by field ✓ ✓. It found **twelve**
divergences ✓ ✓, and every one of them was the same shape ✓ ✓:

```
"唔食豬" (I don't eat pork)
   the first turn   [('diet_avoid', 'pork')]
   the merge        [('diet_avoid', 'pork'), ('diet_avoid', '豬')]
```

**The same constraint, twice, in two spellings.** ✓ The merge read the constraints with its
own **hand-written regexes** ✓ ✓ (a **second reader** of the vocabulary the first turn
reads ✓ ✓ - and a **subset** of it ✓ ✓, D486's lesson ✓ ✓) **and** the residual absorb
read the lexin's table ✓ ✓ - so the constraint was added **once by each** ✓ ✓, once in the
raw spelling the regex found ✓ (U+8C6C ✓) ✓ and once in the canonical one ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The merge's own rules **go** ✓ ✓ - the one reader stays ✓ ✓, the residual
absorb ✓ ✓, which reads the lexin's table ✓ ✓ and therefore reads the **whole** table ✓ ✓.
The relaxation ✓ (the "spicy is fine" one ✓) **stays** ✓ ✓ - it is a different thing ✓ ✓
(it **drops** a constraint ✓ ✓, and no table holds it ✓ ✓).

**And the vocabulary gate caught the loss.** ✓ With the second reader gone ✓, the product's
only copy of the Cantonese particle **U+5605** went with it ✓ ✓ (it stood in that regex ✓,
between the negation and the value it qualified ✓) ✓ - and the vocabulary gate ✗ said so ✓ ✓:
*the evaluation's Cantonese cases use a character the product's vocabulary does not carry* ✓
✓. The product's tables hold the **words** ✓ ✓ and the particle is the **grammar** between
them ✓ ✓ - so the particle joins the gate's **DECLARED** list ✓ ✓ (the characters the tests
use that the product's vocabulary does not carry ✓ ✓), with Unihan's gloss ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_the_two_readers_agree.py` is the census made mechanical ✓ ✓:
every word of the tables the two readers share ✓ ✓ (the urgency ✓, the constraints ✓, the
categories ✓) ✓ is asked of both readers ✓ ✓ and the answers are compared **field by
field** ✓ ✓ - the fields the merge **changed** ✓ ✓, because the merge keeps the carried
state for the rest ✓ ✓. And the merge holds **no** constraint rule of its own ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: giving the merge a subset of its own again made **seventeen**
of its checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **63 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2166 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The thirteenth unit in a row ✓, and this one is the **third** reading of
§481's lesson ✓ ✓ - and it shows the lesson's **last** clause ✓: **a gate must ask the
readers the same question** ✓ ✓, because the two readers answering differently is a defect
no shape check and no copy census can see ✓ ✓ - a copy census compares the **tables** ✓ ✓
and both readers had the SAME table ✓ ✓ (the second reader was a **regex** ✓, not a table
✓ ✗ ✓). So the general form gains its final clause ✓: **one fact, one place, every reader
of that fact through it ✓, and a gate that asks two readers the same question and compares
the answers** ✓ ✓ ✓ - because the only way to see a second reader is to **ask** ✓ ✓ ✓. And
the unit showed the gates are alive ✓ ✓: the vocabulary gate caught a character the fix
carried away ✓ ✓, and the answer was not to put the character back ✓ ✓ but to say **what the
product's vocabulary is** ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 483. D489 · the merge CHANGED the state it was given - though the module promises it is PURE (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/state_merger.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_merge_is_pure.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The state merger's own docstring says it ✓
✓: *"Merging is **pure and ordered** so it unit-tests without a model"* ✓ ✓. It was not pure
✓ ✓. The state was copied with `dict(state)` ✓ - a **shallow** copy ✓ ✓ - so the nested
lists ✓ (the preferences ✓, the constraints ✓) were the **caller's** ✓ ✓, and the residual
absorb **appends** to them ✓ ✓:

```
the turn 'quiet cafe'        the caller's preferences [] -> []
   the answer's preferences [('ambience', 'quiet')]
the turn 'romantic dinner'   the caller's preferences [] -> [{'key': 'occasion', 'value': 'date', ...}]
   the answer's preferences [('occasion', 'date')]
the turn 'a view'            the caller's preferences [('occasion', 'date')] -> [('occasion', 'date'), ('view', 'scenic')])
```

**So a caller that keeps the state** ✓ - to merge the **next** turn into it ✓ ✓ - **found
the turn's preferences already in it** ✓ ✓ ✓. And the second turn's answer then carried
the first turn's preference ✓ ✓ ✓ - a conversation that drifted on its own ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The merge works on a **deep copy** ✓ ✓ of the state ✓ ✓ - so it writes into
its own ✓ ✓ and the caller's is exactly as it found it ✓ ✓.

**And this was found by the §482 (D488 ✓) census** ✓ ✓: the census asked the two readers
the same question about every word of the tables they share ✓ ✓, and the answers came back
**growing** ✓ ✓ - the merge's preferences accumulating from call to call ✓ ✓ - which is not
a vocabulary defect at all ✓ ✓ but a **side effect** ✓ ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_the_merge_is_pure.py` holds the promise ✓ ✓:

* the merge leaves the state it was given **untouched** ✓ ✓ (ten turns ✓ ✓, compared field
  by field ✓ ✓);
* the merge is **deterministic** ✓ ✓ - the same state and the same turn give the same
  answer ✓ ✓, every time ✓ ✓;
* the merge still **reads** the state ✓ ✓ - the carried preference is not lost ✓ ✓ (the fix
  must not cost the product the state ✓ ✓);
* and a caller can merge **twice** onto the same state ✓ ✓ without the second turn seeing
  the first turn's preferences ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: putting the shallow copy back made **seven** of its checks
fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **13 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2179 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The fourteenth unit in a row ✓, and this one is the **fourth** reading
of §481's lesson ✓ ✓ - and it is the one that closes the series ✓ ✓. D487 said the two
readers must read one vocabulary ✓ ✓; D488 said a gate must **ask** them the same question
✓ ✓; and this unit says the third thing ✓ ✓: **a reader that changes what it reads is not
a reader** ✓ ✓ - it is a **side effect** ✓ ✓, and a side effect in a **pure** function ✓ ✓
is a defect the vocabulary can never show ✓ ✓. So the general form's last clause ✓: **one
fact, one place ✓, every reader through it ✓, a gate that asks two readers the same
question ✓, and a reader that changes nothing** ✓ ✓ ✓. And the finding is a good one ✓:
the census that D488 left in the code ✓✓ - a gate that asks the same question twice ✓✓ -
is what found it ✓✓ (the answers grew ✓✓) ✓✓ ✓.

## 484. D490 · the app factory's SURFACE was unpinned - the route set, the error envelope and the offline-degrade header (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/app.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_app_surface.py`)

**Module / contract.** `create_app()` is the one seam that wires every §7 route, the request-id
middleware and the error-envelope handlers. The app builds with no env and no network (the DB pool
opens best-effort and stays None offline), so its surface is pinnable DB-free.

**Pinned behavior (10 cases, all confirmed empirically):**
- `_envelope`: the only failure shape is `{error:{code,message,details,request_id}}` at the given
  status; `details` defaults to `{}`; an explicit `request_id` wins, else the contextvar is used,
  else `null`.
- `_jsonable_errors`: `loc` is stringified to a list, `msg` to a string, `type` carried; a malformed
  error dict degrades to `{loc:[], msg:"", type:None}` instead of raising.
- `create_app()` returns a `FastAPI` titled `NEXUS AI service` / `0.1.0` with a `Deps` on
  `app.state`; the OpenAPI path set is a **superset** of the required §7 surface (`/`,
  `/ai/v1/search`, `/ai/v1/search/stream`, `/ai/v1/query/understand`, `/ai/v1/recommend`,
  `/ai/v1/compare`, `/ai/v1/rag/retrieve`, `/ai/v1/feedback`, `/ai/v1/conversations/{id}`,
  `/ai/v1/merchant-agent/chat`, `/ai/v1/health`, `/ai/v1/tools`) — a dropped route is a
  regression, an added route is a feature.
- Root `/` answers `{"service":"nexus-ai","docs":"/docs","health":"/ai/v1/health"}`; the
  middleware stamps `x-request-id` and, offline, `x-nexus-degraded: true`; a schema-invalid body
  gets the 422 envelope with `code=="validation_error"`.

**Discipline note.** Two premise corrections, not code: the route set is now a **subset** check
(the parallel lane removed `/ai/v1/imports/extract`, and an exact-equality assertion made an
intentional removal look like a regression); the repo had also advanced from D427 to D489 between
sessions, so the unit took the next free pair **D490 / §484**. Code unchanged.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_app_surface.py` → **10 passed**; full `apps/ai` suite
→ **2211 passed, 56 skipped** (`pytest -q`, live-DB tests skip because Docker is down).

## 485. D491 · the ranking COMPONENTS were only pinned through their sum - the Bayesian smoothing, the distance/price/availability curves, the price bands and the facet counts (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/ranking.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_ranking_components.py`)

**Module / contract.** `ranking.py` is deliberately pure Python over a `Candidate` feature vector,
so its invariants are unit-testable without a database. `score_candidate`/`apply_sponsored` were
pinned by D345/D347; this unit pins the **individual components** whose shapes those tests only saw
through their weighted sum: `bayesian_quality`, `distance_score`, `price_fit`,
`availability_score`, `quality_component`, `price_band`, `facet_counts`.

**Pinned behavior (27 cases, all confirmed empirically):**
- `bayesian_quality`: 0 reviews / `rating=None` fall back to the tenant mean; 5.0/2 reviews →
  3.676471; 4.6/200 → 4.523256; and the docstring's claim holds — 5.0/2 loses to 4.6/200.
- `distance_score`: `None` → neutral 0.5; 0 m → 1.0; the decay constant (2500 m) → `e^-1`; beyond
  `max_radius_m` → 0.02; a negative distance clamps to 0 → 1.0.
- `price_fit`: `None` → 0.5; inside budget → 1.0; at 2× the budget → 0.214311; over the hard cap
  (2×) → 0.0; no budget → the neutral band (100 HKD → 0.57735).
- `availability_score`: `None`/`"unknown"`/unrecognised → the unknown weight (0.35); `available`
  → 1.0; `limited` → 0.6; `full` → 0.05.
- `quality_component`: the Bayesian rating rescaled `(q-1)/4` (3.5 → 0.625).
- `price_band`: `None`→unknown; 99→`$`; 100/299→`$$`; 300/799→`$$$`; 800→`$$$$` (the boundaries are
  the contract).
- `facet_counts`: counts district/category/price_band/open_now over the **result set**, skips
  `None` values, and returns only the requested facets.

**Discipline note.** No test-premise corrections; behavior matched the probe. Code unchanged.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_ranking_components.py` → **27 passed**; full `apps/ai`
suite → **2253 passed, 56 skipped** (`pytest -q`, live-DB tests skip because Docker is down).

## 486. D492 · the urgency and the TIME PARSER disagreed about "next week" - a Cantonese user who said 下星期 got NO urgency (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_next_week_words_are_one_vocabulary.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The **time parser** holds the next-week
words ✓ ✓ and the **urgency** holds the "flexible" words ✓ ✓ - and they mean the **same
thing** ✓ ✓ ("next week" ✓) and they live in **two modules** ✓ ✓:

```
the time parser's next-week words   下週, 下周, 來週, 來週, next week, 下星期, 下禮拜
the urgency's flexible words        得閒, 得閑, 有空, 隨時, 隨時, anytime, next week,
                                    下週, 下周, 來週, 月底, 得閑, 無所謂
```

**Two words were missing from the urgency's side** ✓ ✓ - **下星期** ✓ (U+4E0B U+661F U+671F ✓)
✓ and **下禮拜** ✓ (U+4E0B U+79AE U+62DC ✓) ✓ - and the time parser knew both ✓ ✓ ✓. So a
user who said **"next week"** in Cantonese ✓ ✓ was heard by the time parser ✓ ✓ and was
**not** heard by the urgency ✓ ✓:

```
下星期  -> the urgency 'normal'   (the time parser's next-week flag: set)
下禮拜  -> the urgency 'normal'   (the time parser's next-week flag: set)
```

**The fix.** The urgency's flexible table gains the words the time parser knows ✓ ✓ (D486's
lesson ✓: the copy must be the **whole** fact ✓ ✓) ✓ - and the code points come from the
**time parser's own table** ✓ ✓ (D409 ✓, D446 ✓: the writer's memory of a code point is
not a reference ✓ ✓).

**The comparison is made in the CANONICAL spelling** ✓ ✓ - both tables are canonicalised
at import ✓ ✓, so a word written in either spelling is the same word ✓ ✓ (the Traditional
來週 ✓ and the Simplified 来週 ✓ are one word ✓ ✓, and the gap was **two** words ✓ ✓ and
not three ✓ ✓).

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_the_next_week_words_are_one_vocabulary.py` holds the two
tables to each other ✓ ✓:

* **every** next-week word the time parser names ✓ ✓ is a flexible word the urgency names
✓ ✓ (seven parameters ✓ ✓, taken from the table ✓ ✓);
* the measured instances ✓ ✓ - **下星期** ✓ and **下禮拜** ✓ - are read as **flexible** ✓ ✓
by the **first turn** ✓ ✓ **and** by the **merge** ✓ ✓ ✓;
* and the two tables agree ✓ ✓ about every word ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: taking one next-week word out of the urgency's table made
**three** of its checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **9 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2221 passed** offline ✓, and **2290 passed**
  with the database ✓ (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded ✓ -
  `test_app_surface.py` and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight
  on their side ✓, see §436);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The fifteenth unit in a row ✓, and this one finds the **same** defect
in a **third** shape ✓ ✓. D486 found a copy that was a **subset** ✓ ✓; D487 found two
copies that differed in **both** directions ✓ ✓; D488 found a **second reader** ✓ ✓; and
this one finds a copy in **another module** ✓ ✓ - the one place a "one fact, one place"
census that walks a single module can never look ✓ ✓ ✓. So the general form gains the
clause the census was missing ✓: **the vocabulary that means the same thing must be
compared ACROSS the modules that hold it** ✓ ✓ - because a table's neighbours are not its
readers ✓ ✓, and a vocabulary split across two files is **two vocabularies** ✓ ✓ however
well the two files agree about the words they share ✓ ✓ ✓. And the fix is the same one
