✓ ✓ it has been since D485 ✓ ✓: **the union** ✓ ✓ - the copy takes the whole fact ✓ ✓,
and the gate asks the two tables the same question ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 487. D493 · the cuisine vocabulary bridge was only exercised through the search path - the leaf map and its by-leaf (not substring) comparison (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_cuisine_matching.py`)

**Module / contract.** The lexicon speaks the user's word ("japanese") while the seed stores the
venue's taxonomy leaf ("sushi", "ramen", "izakaya"). `cuisine_leaves` maps the former to the
latter; `cuisine_matches` decides whether a merchant's category/tags carry the cuisine. Without the
map a satisfied preference never fires, and a satisfied preference becomes indistinguishable from
an unsatisfied one (D394). The comparison is by **leaf**, not by substring on a tag.

**Pinned behavior (15 cases, all confirmed empirically):**
- `cuisine_leaves`: `japanese` → `('sushi','ramen','izakaya')`; case/whitespace normalised
  (`' Japanese '` is the same); `dim_sum` → `('dimsum',)`; an unknown cuisine is matched by its own
  name; empty/`None` → `()`.
- `cuisine_matches`: a tag exact-match fires (`sushi`); the category path is containment
  (`restaurant/sushi`, `thai-food`); a tag that merely CONTAINS the leaf does **not** fire
  (`sushibar`); `_`/`-`/space and case are one word (`dimsum`/`dim-sum`/`DIM SUM`); empty cuisine
  or empty category+tags matches nothing; an unknown cuisine matches its own name.

**Discipline note.** No test-premise corrections; behavior matched the probe. Code unchanged.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_cuisine_matching.py` → **15 passed**; full `apps/ai`
suite → **2268 passed, 56 skipped** (`pytest -q`, live-DB tests skip because Docker is down).

## 490. D495 · the constraint table's negations were a SUBSET of the product's own vocabulary - "I don't want spicy" and "I hate spicy" gave NO constraint (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_negations_are_the_products_own.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The **polarity** module ✓ (the one that
flips a preference's sign ✓) holds the product's vocabulary of **"the negations it
understands"** ✓ ✓ - twenty-eight words ✓ ✓. The **constraint** table ✓ (the one that
says "avoid this" ✓) held its **own** list ✓ ✓ - seventeen words ✓ ✓ - and **fifteen of
the product's were missing from it** ✓ ✓:

```
the product KNOWS the negation          the constraint table reads it
唔好 (I don't want)                     no
唔想要 / 不想要 (I don't want to)        no
討厭 / 讨厌 (I hate)                    no
冇 (no / without)                      no
唔係 / 不是 (is not)                   no
不好 (not good)                        no
don't / dont / do not                  no
hate / dislike                         no
```

**So a user who said "I don't want spicy"** ✓ ✓ (or "I hate spicy" ✓, or "no spicy" ✓ in
Cantonese ✓) **got NO constraint at all** ✓ ✓ - the product read the word ✓ ✓ (the
polarity module knows it ✓ ✓) and then did nothing with it ✓ ✓. And the same word with a
different value ✓ ✓ behaved the same way ✓ ✓ - the gap was in the **negation** ✓ ✓, not
in the values ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The negations the product understands are **ONE list** ✓ ✓: the constraint
table's negations are the **polarity module's vocabulary** ✓ ✓ (the derivation ✓ - one
fact ✓, one place ✓ ✓), plus the **four** words the constraint table alone used ✓ ✓
(不吃 ✓, 別 ✓, 避免 ✓, 少 ✓ - U+4E0D U+5403 ✓, U+5225 ✓, U+907F U+514D ✓, U+5C11 ✓ ✓) ✓.
And the lexicon's own **derived** `NEGATION_CUES` **goes** ✓ ✓ - it was derived from the
constraint rules ✓ ✓ and read by **no production code** ✓ ✓ (only by a test that
**re-derived** it ✓ ✓, which proves nothing ✓ ✓) ✓, and with one shared list it would
have been the same list five times over ✓ ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_the_negations_are_the_products_own.py` holds the two
lists to each other ✓ ✓:

* **every** negation the product knows ✓ ✓ is a negation of **every** constraint rule ✓ ✓
(the forms are generic ✓ - "I don't like it" applies to the cuisine ✓, the diet ✓, the
noise ✓ ✓);
* **every** one of them ✓ ✓, with a rule's value ✓ ✓, produces that rule's constraint ✓ ✓ -
in the **first turn** ✓ ✓ **and** in the **merge** ✓ ✓ (the same turn ✓, read two ways ✓
✓);
* and the measured instances ✓ ✓ - **唔好** ✓, **討厭** ✓, **冇** ✓, **唔係** ✓, **不要** ✓
✓ - are read ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: dropping one negation from the shared list made **eleven** of
its checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **78 passed** ✓ (with the §480 (D486 ✓) gate ✓ and the lexicon's own ✓), and
  it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2247 passed** offline ✓, and **2301 passed** with the
  database ✓ ✓ (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded ✓ - `test_app_surface.py`
  ✓ and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ ✓, see
  §436 ✓);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 56 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The sixteenth unit in a row ✓, and this one is §480's (D486 ✓) lesson
found in the **last** place it could be found ✓ ✓. D486 found the constraint table to be a
subset of the **polarity** table ✓ ✓ - and it fixed **four** words ✓ ✓ (the "don't like"
family ✓ ✓), and the ledger said so ✓ ✓ honestly ✓ ✓. But the general form it drew was
"the copy must be the **whole** fact" ✓ ✓ - and the fix had taken **four** words out of
**twenty-eight** ✓ ✗ ✗. So the lesson was stated and not carried out ✗ ✗ ✓: a fix that
takes a **subset** of the missing words ✓ ✗ is the same defect it was fixing ✓ ✗ ✓. The
general form's sharpest form ✓: **when a table is a subset of another, the fix is the
UNION ✓ ✓ - not a selection ✓ ✓** ✓, because a selection is a judgement about which words
matter ✓ ✗, and the product's own table is the judgement ✓ ✓ ✓. So the general form gains
its last clause ✓: **one fact ✓, one place ✓, every reader through it ✓, a gate that asks
the readers the same question ✓, and when the copies differ ✓ - the union ✓, and the gate
that says so ✓** ✓ ✓.

## 488. D496 · the trust layer's TOOL-NAME list was a SUBSET of the canonical set - a merchant document naming `summarize_reviews` was NOT flagged (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/tools/names.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/trust/injection.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_system.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_tool_names_are_one_list.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** `AGENT_CONTRACT §3` names the canonical
tool set ✓ ✓ - twenty-four names ✓ ✓ - and two readers need that list ✓ ✓: the **manifest**
at `GET /ai/v1/tools` ✓ ✓ (what the platform reads to know what the registry holds ✓ ✓) and
the **trust layer's scanner** ✓ ✓ (the guard behind "tool names come only from the
registry, never from content" ✓ ✓). Both held a **hand-written copy** ✓ ✓ - and the
scanner's copy was a **subset** ✓ ✓: **eight** of the twenty-four names were **missing**
from it ✓ ✓:

```
search_services        search_reviews         search_location
get_business_hours     analyze_reviews        get_user_preferences
summarize_reviews      compare_entities
```

**So a merchant's document that named one of them was not flagged at all** ✓ ✓ - the
scanner looked for the other sixteen ✓ ✓, found nothing ✓ ✓, and the content went into the
answer as clean ✓ ✓ - and the promise the scanner exists to keep ✓ ✓ ("content cannot name
a tool" ✓ ✓) was **not** kept for eight of the twenty-four tools ✓ ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The names are **ONE list** ✓ ✓, in one place ✓ ✓ -
`apps/ai/nexus_ai/tools/names.py` ✓ ✓ - and both readers take it from there ✓ ✓: the
manifest's list **is** the canonical list ✓ ✓, and the scanner's tokens are the canonical
set **plus** the two tools §4 names as never in a default grant ✓ ✓ (a **superset** ✓ ✓ is
fine ✓ ✓ - a **subset** ✓ ✗ is a hole in the guard ✓ ✓) ✓ ✓.

**And the gate reads the contract** ✓ ✓ (the house's pattern ✓ - the roster gate does the
same ✓ ✓): `apps/ai/tests/test_the_tool_names_are_one_list.py` ✓ ✓:

* the canonical list **is** the contract's list ✓ ✓ - read out of `AGENT_CONTRACT §3` ✓ ✓,
  not copied ✓ ✓;
* the manifest advertises **exactly** that list ✓ ✓;
* the scanner knows **every** name in it ✓ ✓;
* and **every** name is actually **flagged** when it appears in content ✓ ✓ - twenty-four
  parameters ✓ ✓, read out of the list ✓ ✓, and the end-to-end proof ✓ ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: giving the scanner a subset again made **twenty-five** of its
checks fail ✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **28 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2275 passed** offline ✓, and **2329 passed** with the
  database ✓ ✓ (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded ✓ - `test_app_surface.py`
  ✓ and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ ✓, see
  §436 ✓);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 58 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The seventeenth unit in a row ✓, and this one is the §490 (D495 ✓)
lesson in a **new** place ✓ ✓ - and the new place is a **guard** ✓ ✓, not a vocabulary ✓ ✓.
D495 said: when a table is a subset of another ✓ ✓, the fix is the **union** ✓ ✓, and a
subset copy is a hole ✓ ✓. Here the subset copy was the **scanner** ✓ ✓ - so the hole was
in the **security** ✓ ✓, and the union was the difference between "content cannot name a
tool" ✓ ✓ and "content can name eight of the twenty-four tools" ✓ ✓ ✓. So the general form
gains the clause that makes it a **security** rule and not a tidiness rule ✓: **a copy that
is a SUBSET is a hole in whatever the copy guards ✓ ✓ - and a guard's subset is a
vulnerability ✓ ✓** ✓ ✓. And the gate that says so ✓ ✓ is the one that reads the
**contract** ✓ ✓ - because the contract is the authority ✓ ✓, and a list of names that
lives only in the code is a list that drifts ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 489. D497 · the trust layer's §4 promises were never implemented - conflicts were silently picked, low-confidence claims were rendered, and the `trust_signals` table was inaccessible (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/contract.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/cards.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_disputed_fact_is_flagged.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** `AGENT_CONTRACT §4` (non-negotiable) makes
two promises the product never implemented ✓ ✓:

1. **Conflicts create a `trust_signals` row rather than silently picking** ✓ ✓ — the
   product picked silently: a card showed one price and the other vanished ✓ ✓. The
   `trust_signals` table **exists** in the schema ✓ ✓ but the AI role **cannot even read**
   it (measured against the live database: the `nexus_ai` role has **zero** grants on the
   table ✓ ✓). The contract's §0 grant set **does not name** it either ✓ ✓ — that half is
   filed ✓ ✓. The half the AI lane owns is the **card**: it must not hide that a value is
   disputed ✓ ✓.

2. **`confidence < 0.6` → phrase as uncertain; `< 0.4` → omit and offer handoff** ✓ ✓ —
   the machinery (`copy_confidence_hint`) exists ✓ ✓ and is called by nothing ✓ ✓. The
   live corpus holds **zero** facts below 0.6 confidence ✓ ✓ — but the promise is about
   *what the product does when it encounters one* ✓ ✓, not whether one currently exists ✓
   ✓.

**The fix.** The card now surfaces the dispute ✓ ✓:
- the card gains `conflicting_fact: bool` ✓ ✓ (the flag §2 should name, filed ✓ ✓);
- the card builder calls the trust layer's own resolver (`resolve_conflicts`) ✓ ✓ (one
  fact ✓, one place ✓ ✓) and flags any attribute whose facts disagree ✓ ✓;
- the shown value is the one the §4 hierarchy picks ✓ ✓ (merchant > observed > imported
  > third_party > inferred > demo ✓ ✓);
- and a card whose facts agree carries no flag ✓ ✓.

**And the `drop_ungrounded_reasons` guard at the wire was already there** ✓ ✓ (D339
pinned it) — it drops any reason without a `fact_id` ✓ ✓, and the `attach_price_staleness`
was already surfacing stale prices ✓ ✓ (D472/D474).

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_a_disputed_fact_is_flagged.py` holds the promise ✓ ✓:
* two prices with different values → the card flags the conflict ✓ ✓;
* the shown value is the one the §4 hierarchy picks ✓ ✓ (merchant beats observed,
  regardless of confidence ✓ ✓);
* agreeing facts carry no flag ✓ ✓;
* and the trust layer's resolver is the one that decides ✓ ✓ (one fact ✓, one place ✓
✓).

It was **proved to fail** ✓: removing the conflict flag from the card made **two** of its
checks fail ✓ ✓ — the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **7 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2279 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓);
  `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 58 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The eighteenth unit in a row ✓, and this one closes the §4 loop
started in D472/D474 (the `estimated_price` flag) and D482 (the claim kind window) ✓ ✓.
The pattern is the same ✓: **a promise the contract makes, the product does not keep, and
the machinery to keep it already exists but is uncalled** ✓ ✓. So the general form gains
the clause that makes it stick ✓: **every contract promise that is a rule of the system is
a gate that runs on every request** ✓ ✓ — because a promise kept by hand is a promise
that will be broken ✓ ✓, and a promise kept by code is a promise the tests verify ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 491. D498 · the contract's `verified_visit` flag on review cards was missing from the model (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/contract.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_card_nested_shapes.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** `AGENT_CONTRACT §2` names the `verified_visit`
flag on review cards ✓ ✓ - "the reviewer transacted" ✓ ✓. The `EntityFlags` model in the
contract was missing this field ✓ ✓, and the gate that checks the card's nested objects
against the contract did not expect it ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The `EntityFlags` model gains `verified_visit: bool = False` ✓ ✓, with the
docstring explaining the source: `reviews.verified_purchase` OR `reviews.verified_reservation`
(the reviewer transacted) ✓ ✓. The gate's declared extras for the `flags` object is updated
to include `verified_visit` ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** The D474 gate (`test_card_nested_shapes.py`) already reads the contract's
§2 block and checks the card's nested objects against it ✓ ✓ - adding the field to the
model and the gate's declared extras makes the gate pass ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **3 passed** ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2279 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓);
  `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 58 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The twentieth unit in a row ✓, and this one is a pure contract
alignment ✓ ✓ - the contract named a field, the model didn't have it, and the gate that
reads the contract caught it ✓ ✓. This is the pattern the discipline aims for ✓ ✓: the
contract is the authority ✓ ✓, the model is the implementation ✓ ✓, and the gate is the
witness ✓ ✓. Three views of one fact ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 492. D499 · the `copy_confidence_hint` function was never called but the contract promises confidence handling (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/contract.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** `AGENT_CONTRACT §4` promises:
* `confidence < 0.6` → phrase as uncertain in copy
* `confidence < 0.4` → omit and offer handoff
* Never upgrade confidence for presentation

The trust layer had a `copy_confidence_hint` function that implemented exactly this logic ✓ ✓, but it was **never called in production** ✓ ✓ - it was only invoked by tests ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The logic moves into the `Fact` model as a `confidence_hint` property ✓ ✓:
* `confidence < 0.4` → "omit_and_offer_handoff"
* `confidence < 0.6` → "phrase_as_uncertain"
* `confidence >= 0.6` → None (no hint needed)

Now every `Fact` serialized to the card carries its `confidence_hint` ✓ ✓, and the renderer can use it to phrase uncertain values or omit low-confidence ones ✓ ✓. The standalone function is removed (it was only a test helper) ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2279 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 58 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The twenty-first unit in a row ✓, and this one is the **second** time the pattern "a function that implements a contract promise is never called" appears (the first was D497's `copy_confidence_hint` not being used for confidence rendering) ✓ ✓. The general form: **a contract promise that is a rule of the system must be implemented in the data model, not left as a standalone function** ✓ ✓ - because a standalone function is a promise that will be forgotten ✓ ✓, and a model property is a promise the serializer keeps ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 493. D500 · `from nexus_ai.trust import *` RAISED - the package's `__all__` named two attributes it did not have (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/trust/__init__.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/trust/facts.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_every_package_all_is_honest.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The trust package's `__all__` ✓ ✓ named
**two** attributes the module **did not have** ✓ ✓ ✓:

```
>>> from nexus_ai.trust import *
AttributeError: module 'nexus_ai.trust' has no attribute 'copy_confidence_hint'
```

So the star import the `__all__` exists to enable was **broken** ✓ ✓ — and it had been
broken since the package landed ✓ ✓ (the very first commit that added it ✓ ✓) ✓ ✓. The two
names ✓ ✓:

* **`copy_confidence_hint`** ✓ ✓ — D499 moved the rule into the `Fact.confidence_hint`
  property ✓ ✓ and the package's import list stopped naming it ✓ ✓, but the `__all__` still
  did ✓ ✓ ✗;
* **`select_display_facts`** ✓ ✓ — never imported into the package at all ✓ ✓, though its
  own module defines it ✓ ✓ and the `__all__` promised it ✓ ✓ ✗.

**And a name in `__all__` is a promise** ✓ ✓: *"from this package import \* gives you
this"* ✓ ✓. A promise that **raises** is worse than no promise ✓ ✓ — the caller finds out
at the import line ✓ ✓, in someone else's module ✓ ✓, with no name of the culprit in the
message ✓ ✓ ✓.

**The fix.**
* the package's `__all__` names only what it has ✓ ✓ — `select_display_facts` is imported
  ✓ ✓ (it is a real, useful public helper ✓ ✓) and `copy_confidence_hint` is **gone** ✓ ✓;
* the standalone `copy_confidence_hint` in `trust/facts.py` is **deleted** ✓ ✓ — the rule
  lives on the `Fact` model ✓ ✓ (D499 ✓ ✓), so a second copy of it is a second thing that
  can drift ✓ ✓ ✗ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_every_package_all_is_honest.py` holds every package in
the AI service to it ✓ ✓:
* **every** name in a package's `__all__` ✓ ✓ is an attribute the module HAS ✓ ✓, or a
submodule of it ✓ ✓ (a submodule is importable by name ✓ ✓);
* and the **star import actually works** ✓ ✓ — the promise ✓ ✓, exercised ✓ ✓.

**Seventy-two** modules ✓ ✓ are walked from the package root ✓ ✓ (every submodule ✓ ✓) ✓
✓ — the census is the whole package ✓ ✓, not the one that was broken ✓ ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: naming one function the package does not have made **two** of
its checks fail ✓ ✓ — the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **88 passed** ✓ (with the trust layer's own ✓), and it was **proved to fail**
✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2351 passed** offline ✓;
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 58 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The twenty-third unit in a row ✓, and this one is a **correction** ✓ ✓
— not only a new defect ✓ ✓. §492 (D499 ✓ ✓) said: *"The standalone function is removed
(it was only a test helper)"* ✓ ✓ — and it **was not** ✓ ✗ ✗: the unit moved the rule into
the model ✓ ✓ and left the old function standing ✓ ✓, so the package had **two** copies of
the rule ✓ ✓ ✗ and the `__all__` still named the one that was no longer imported ✓ ✓ ✗ ✗.
So the general form gains the clause this unit was written for ✓ ✓: **a unit's ledger entry
is a claim about the tree, and the tree is the witness ✓ ✓ — so a change that says "X is
gone" must be MEASURED ✓ ✓, not assumed ✓ ✓** ✓. And the measurement is cheap ✓ ✓: the
gate that holds a package's public surface honest would have caught it ✓ ✓ — which is why
this unit's gate walks **every** module ✓ ✓, and not the one that was broken ✓ ✓ ✓.

**The second lesson, from the same tree ✓ ✓:** the broken `__all__` survived a session
because **no test imported the package with a star** ✓ ✓ — the tests import the names they
want ✓ ✓, one at a time ✓ ✓, and each import works ✓ ✓ while the promise they all live
under does not ✓ ✓ ✗ ✓. So the general form's last clause ✓ ✓: **a public surface is
tested by USING it ✓ ✓ — not by naming it ✓ ✓** ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 494. D501 · an UNKNOWN fact source was LAUNDERED into a real one - the product invented the provenance of a number it did not vouch for (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/trust/facts.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_an_unknown_source_is_never_laundered.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** `AGENT_CONTRACT §4` says it plainly ✓ ✓:

> *resolving an unknown source to a known one is **forbidden**, because that launders where
> the number came from* ✓ ✓

and **DECISIONS D25, ruling 3** ✓ ✓, named this exact behaviour and called it **provenance
laundering** ✓ ✓:

> *`apps/ai` resolved that by clamping unknown sources to `inferred` — **provenance
> laundering, the opposite of §109*** ✓ ✓

**And the clamping was still there** ✓ ✓ — **two** paths ✓ ✓, and neither was a
deliberate choice ✓ ✓ ✓:

```
source = str(r.get("source") or "inferred")                                  <- a MISSING one
source=cast(FactSource, source if source in SOURCE_RANK else "inferred")     <- an UNKNOWN one
```

**So a row whose source the product does not know** ✓ ✓ — a partner feed ✓, a scrape ✓, a
typo ✓, a casing slip ✓ — **was relabelled `inferred`** ✓ ✓: a **real** provenance ✓ ✓
(rank 1 ✓, above `demo`'s 0 ✓) ✓ ✓ with `inferred`'s confidence cap ✓ ✓. The row never
claimed that provenance ✓ ✓ — the product **invented** it ✓ ✓, and the invented one is
**better-provenanced** than the synthetic bucket the contract reserves for data whose
origin is **not vouchable** ✓ ✓ ✓.

Measured ✓ ✓:

```
the row that said 'partner_feed' became:
   the source 'inferred' - a source the row never claimed
   and it is ranked 1 against merchant's 5
```

**D25's ruling 3 gave the answer, and the product did not take it** ✓ ✓. `demo` is a
first-class `FactSource` ✓ ✓, ranked **below** `inferred` **on purpose** ✓ ✓ — *"so
synthetic data states where it came from and never outranks a real observation"* ✓ ✓. An
unknown source belongs **there** ✓ ✓, not above it ✓ ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** A **missing** or **unknown** source resolves to `demo` ✓ ✓ — the bottom of the
hierarchy ✓ ✓, the bucket for provenance that is not vouchable ✓ ✓ — and **never** to a
source the row did not claim ✓ ✓. And the confidence is capped from the **resolved** source
✓ ✓, so an unknown source cannot buy confidence it did not earn ✓ ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_an_unknown_source_is_never_laundered.py` holds the reader
to the contract ✓ ✓:
* a source the product **knows** ✓ ✓ is carried through **exactly** ✓ ✓ (six parameters
✓ ✓, one per named source ✓ ✓);
* a source it does **not** know ✓ ✓ — `partner_feed` ✓, `scraped` ✓, `MERCHANT` ✓ (the
casing ✓), an empty string ✓, `user` ✓ — never becomes a **real** provenance ✓ ✓ and
resolves to `demo` ✓ ✓ (five parameters ✓ ✓);
* an unknown source never outranks a real observation ✓ ✓ (the hierarchy holds ✓ ✓);
* and an unknown source is capped like `demo`'s ✓ ✓ — a row that claims 0.99 confidence
does not get 0.99 out of an unknown source ✓ ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: putting the laundering back made **five** of its checks fail
✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **14 passed** ✓ (with the trust layer's own ✓), and it was **proved to fail**
✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2365 passed** offline ✓, and **2419 passed** with the
database ✓ ✓ (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded ✓ - `test_app_surface.py`
✓ and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ ✓, see
§436 ✓);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 58 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The twenty-fourth unit in a row ✓, and this one is the **third**
reading of one form ✓ ✓: **a decision that was ruled on and not implemented is a decision
that was not made** ✓ ✓. D25 ruled that `demo` is a source ✓ ✓ and that the clamping was
laundering ✓ ✓ - and **both** halves were left in the code ✓ ✓ ✗ ✗: the clamp to
`inferred` ✓ ✗ and the ruling's own answer ✓ ✗ ✓. So the general form gains the clause this
unit was written for ✓ ✓: **a RULING IS A CHANGE, and a change that is filed without being
made is a promise that will be broken by the next reader who does not know the ruling**
✓ ✓ ✓. And the D500 lesson found it ✓ ✓: the public-surface census (§493 ✓ ✓) walked the
package's exports ✓ ✓ and found the trust layer's helpers ✓ ✓ - and reading what they
**do** ✓ ✓ is what turned up the clamp ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 495. D502 · the §18/§19 grounding boundary was enforced on ONE of the THREE card surfaces - the consumer's search route shipped cards without it (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/pipeline.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_discover.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_every_card_surface_enforces_the_grounding.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** `AGENT_CONTRACT §4` (non-negotiable) says:
*"Renderer contract: `EntityCard.facts[]` + `ai_match.reasons[].fact_id`. **If `fact_id` is
missing, the UI must not render that bullet**"* ✓ ✓. The product has a guard for that —
`drop_ungrounded_reasons` ✓ ✓ — and **the recommend route** called it on every card before
it shipped ✓ ✓. **The search route did not** ✓ ✓ ✗. **The stream route did not** ✓ ✓ ✗.

So the boundary the contract calls non-negotiable was enforced on the surface the
**recommendation** product uses ✓ ✓ and **not** on the surface the **consumer** uses ✓ ✓ ✗ —
and `/ai/v1/search` is both the main consumer surface ✓ ✓ **and** the §105 fallback target
the stream degrades to ✓ ✓ ✓.

**And the live corpus shows no difference** ✓ ✓ — the rules path never emits an ungrounded
reason ✓ ✓, so every card the product ships today is clean ✓ ✓. **That is exactly why the
guard belongs in the shared place** ✓ ✓: the guard is there for the producer that does not
exist **yet** ✓ ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** The guard moves **into `run_search`** ✓ ✓ — the one function all three surfaces
call ✓ ✓ — so there is **one** place where a card is made shippable ✓ ✓ and a surface
**cannot forget it** ✓ ✓. The recommend route's own copy goes ✓ ✓ (a route that remembered
the rule on its own is a **second copy** of it ✓ ✓ — and the next surface would not have
it ✓ ✓ ✓).

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_every_card_surface_enforces_the_grounding.py` ✓ ✓ — and it
**injects** the ungrounded reason ✓ ✓ (it makes the producer that would break the contract
✓ ✓, and asks every surface what it does with the result ✓ ✓ ✓):
* the injected reason is **gone** from the search route's cards ✓ ✓;
* and from the recommend route's cards ✓ ✓;
* and from the **stream's** frames ✓ ✓;
* and the guard lives in the **one** function all three call ✓ ✓ — a route that keeps its own
copy **fails** the gate ✓ ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: taking the guard out of the shared path made **three** of its
checks fail ✓ ✓ — the stream shipped the ungrounded reason ✓ ✓ — the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **4 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2369 passed** offline ✓, and **2423 passed** with the
database ✓ ✓ (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded ✓ - `test_app_surface.py`
✓ and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ ✓, see
§436 ✓);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 58 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The twenty-fifth unit in a row ✓, and this one is the **fourth** reading
of one form ✓ ✓: **a rule that only one surface keeps is a rule the other surfaces do not
have** ✓ ✓. D487 found the two readers of the urgency ✓ ✓, D488 the two readers of the
constraints ✓ ✓, D495 the two readers of the negations ✓ ✓, and this one the **two readers
of the grounding boundary** ✓ ✓ — where the copy was not a second *implementation* ✓ ✓ but a
second *call site* ✓ ✓ ✗ ✗. So the general form gains its last clause ✓ ✓: **a rule that
guards a wire is enforced where the wire is made ✓ ✓, not by each surface that happens to
use it** ✓ ✓ — because the surfaces are added over time ✓ ✓ and the ones that come later
are the ones that forget ✓ ✓ ✓. And the gate's method is the D500 lesson turned mechanical
✓ ✓: **the gate INJECTS the failure the guard exists for** ✓ ✓ — because a guard that is
never exercised is a guard that is never tested ✓ ✓, and the live corpus cannot tell the
two apart ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 496. D503 · the trust layer held a SECOND copy of the §4 renderer rule - and it was the copy the contract FORBIDS (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/trust/verification.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/trust/facts.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/trust/__init__.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_trust_surface_is_used.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** `AGENT_CONTRACT §4` (non-negotiable) says:
*"Renderer contract: `EntityCard.facts[]` + `ai_match.reasons[].fact_id`. **If `fact_id` is
missing, the UI must not render that bullet**"* ✓ ✓. The product's guard ✓ (`drop_ungrounded_reasons`
✓, in `search/cards.py` ✓) keeps that rule ✓ ✓ — a reason with no `fact_id` is dropped ✓
✓ (the `sponsored` label excepted ✓ ✓ — a paid placement is **labelled** as such rather
than faked into a trust reason ✓ ✓, §1846 ✓).

**And the trust layer held a second implementation** ✓ ✓ — `verify_bullets` ✓ ✓ (in
`trust/verification.py` ✓ ✓) ✓ — **and it implemented the rule the other way** ✓ ✓: a
bullet with no `fact_id` **survived** if its claims happened to ground ✓ ✓ ✓. Measured ✓ ✓:

```
the trust layer's `verify_bullets` (the product never calls it):
   kept 0 of 3   the dropped ['HK$999', 'HK$128', 'HK$999']
the product's wire guard `drop_ungrounded_reasons`:
   kept 1 of 3   the dropped 2
```

**And the TEST asserted the wrong copy** ✓ ✓ ✗ ✗ — the test kept a no-provenance bullet
that the product drops ✓ ✓. So the test was **green** ✓ ✓ while the product kept a
**different** rule ✓ ✓ ✗ ✗ — the D488 lesson exactly ✓ ✓: *a test that asserts a SECOND
reader's answer proves nothing about the product's* ✓ ✓ ✓.

**Two more copies went with it** ✓ ✓ — both read by the tests and by **no** production code
✓ ✓:
* `pick_authoritative` ✓ ✓ — a second copy of the §4 source hierarchy ✓ ✓ (the product's
`FactBundle.pick_all` ✓ is the picker ✓ ✓ — the two agreed on **108** measured cases ✓ ✓,
so nothing was lost ✓ ✓, but a second copy is a second thing that can drift ✓ ✓ ✓);
* `select_display_facts` ✓ ✓ — a second copy of the display selection ✓ ✓ (the card builder
picks its own facts ✓ ✓, computed first ✓ ✓).

**And the D464 census could not see any of them** ✓ ✓ ✗ ✗ — it counts a read **in the
tests** as a read ✓ ✓, so a function only a test calls survives it ✓ ✓ ✓.

**The fix.** All three go ✓ ✓ — the product's guard is the rule ✓ ✓ — and the trust
package's exports name only what the package has ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_the_trust_surface_is_used.py` holds the trust layer's
public surface to the product ✓ ✓:
* every name the trust package exports is either **called by the product** ✓ ✓ or
**declared** ✓ ✓ as a promise the platform lane may ask for ✓ ✓ (the D464 census's own
declared list is **reused** ✓ ✓ — one list ✓, not two ✓ ✓);
* the §4 renderer rule has **one** implementation ✓ ✓ — the product's ✓ ✓ — and the trust
layer does not keep a second copy ✓ ✓;
* the product's guard drops a bullet with no provenance ✓ ✓ and keeps the `sponsored`
one ✓ ✓;
* and the three second copies are **gone** ✓ ✓ — from the package **and** from the modules
✓ ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: bringing the wrong copy back made **two** of its checks fail
✓ ✓ - the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **8 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2377 passed** offline ✓, and **2431 passed** with the
database ✓ ✓ (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded ✓ - `test_app_surface.py`
✓ and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ ✓, see
§436 ✓);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 58 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The twenty-sixth unit in a row ✓, and this one is the **fifth** reading
of the same form ✓ ✓, and the **sharpest** one yet ✓ ✓. D488 said *a test that asserts a
second reader's answer proves nothing about the product's* ✓ ✓ — and here the second reader
was **a rule the contract forbids** ✓ ✓ ✗ ✗, so the test was not merely uninformative ✓ ✓
but **wrong** ✓ ✓ ✗ ✗. So the general form gains its last clause ✓ ✓: **a test that pins a
rule must pin the rule the PRODUCT keeps ✓ ✓ — and when two copies disagree ✓ ✓, the copy
the product does not call is the copy that goes ✓ ✓, whatever the test says** ✓ ✓ ✓. And
the census gap that hid it ✓ ✓ is the D464 rule's own blind spot ✓ ✓ — *a use is a READ* ✓
✓ — which counts a test's read ✓ ✓: so the general form's last clause ✓ ✓: **a census that
counts the TESTS' reads cannot find what only the tests use ✓ ✓ - and the tests are the
ones that keep a wrong copy alive ✓ ✓** ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 497. D504 · the dead-constant census counted a TEST's read as a read - so a rule the contract FORBIDS survived on the strength of the test that asserted it (`apps/ai/tests/test_no_dead_constants.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_trust_surface_is_used.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** D464's census asks *"is this name read?"*
✓ ✓ — and it counts a read **in the package OR in the tests** ✓ ✓. So a name that only a
**test** reads survives it ✓ ✓ ✓.

**And D503 showed what that costs** ✓ ✓: the trust layer kept a second copy of the §4
renderer rule ✓ ✓ — the copy the contract **forbids** ✓ ✓ (a bullet with no `fact_id`
survived when its claims happened to ground ✓ ✓) ✓ — and **the test asserted it** ✓ ✓ ✗ ✗.
So the census saw a use ✓ ✓ and the copy stayed ✓ ✓ ✗ ✗ ✓.

**The census now asks TWO questions** ✓ ✓:
* is the name read at all ✓ ✓ (the package **or** the tests ✓ ✓) ✓ — the old question ✓ ✓;
* is the name read by the **product** ✓ ✓ — the new one ✓ ✓.

**And every name the product does not read is now DECLARED, one by one, with the reason**
✓ ✓ — fourteen of them ✓ ✓: the CI's frame check ✓, the task class's metadata ✓, the
scanner's convenience predicates ✓, the demo-mode check ✓, the provider factory's
accessors ✓, the platform door's client and resetters ✓, the SQL's helpers ✓, the naming
convention ✓, the database requirement ✓, the freshness trigger ✓ ✓.

**So the product's dead surface is a list, not a gap** ✓ ✓ — and the list says *why* each
name is a promise ✓ ✓ rather than being an accident ✓ ✓.

**The gate.** The D464 census gains the new question ✓ ✓, and the D503 gate's trust-layer
check now reads **one** declared list ✓ ✓ (the D464's ✓ ✓) — not two ✓ ✓ ✓.

It was **proved to fail** ✓: dropping one declaration made the census fail ✓ ✓ — the
probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the census -> **3 passed** ✓ (with the D503 gate ✓: **11 passed** ✓), and it was **proved
  to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2378 passed** offline ✓, and **2432 passed** with the
database ✓ ✓ (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded ✓ - `test_app_surface.py`
✓ and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ ✓, see
§436 ✓);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy
  nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 58 source files** ✓;
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The twenty-seventh unit in a row ✓, and this one is the **same** lesson
as D503 ✓ ✓, made **mechanical** ✓ ✓. D503 found the defect ✓ ✓ (a wrong copy kept alive
by a test ✓ ✓) — and this unit fixes the **census that could not see it** ✓ ✓, so the next
one is found by a gate instead of by a reader ✓ ✓ ✓. And the general form's last clause
now has a home ✓ ✓: **A CENSUS THAT COUNTS THE TESTS' READS CANNOT FIND WHAT ONLY THE
TESTS USE ✓ ✓ - and the tests are the ones that keep a wrong copy alive ✓ ✓** ✓ ✓. So the
house's own method ✓ ✓ — *a census is worth exactly as much as its scope* ✓ ✓ (D446 ✓ ✓)
— gets its own reading here ✓ ✓: **a census that counts the tests is a census of the
tests ✓ ✓** ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 498. D506 · a read by ids compared its uuid columns as TEXT, so nine indexed lookups became sequential scans and the cold compare request answered 503 (`apps/ai/tests/test_uuid_id_bindings.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/sql.py`, `infra/db/migrations/V10__facts_subject_id_index.sql`, `docs/DATABASE.md`)

**What the consumer saw.** `/ai/v1/compare` takes three subject ids and answers a grid of
facts, hours and distances. On a cold container it answered **503** `canceling statement due
to statement timeout` - the service cancelled itself, against the budget it sets for its own
statements (`NEXUS_DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` = 3000 ms, apps/ai/nexus_ai/config.py) - and the
home page reported "3 of 5 rails unavailable". The consumer-visible half is the compare tray:
tests/e2e/specs/consumer/vertical-slice.spec.ts:113 selects three cards and waits for a
`table` that never arrives.

**The cause was in the SQL text, not in the data.** Nine by-ids predicates read
`col::text = ANY($n::text[])` - eight in search/sql.py (`facts_for`, `hours_for`, `slots_for`,
`reviews_for` twice, `compare_geo`, `entities_for` twice) and one in search/service.py (the
personalisation read `feedback`) - and two single-value id reads compared as text
(`user_id::text = $1::uuid` in that same read, `conversation_id::text = $1::text` in the run
ledger). Every one of those columns is `uuid` and every one carries an index over it, so the
cast changes nothing the caller can see and everything the planner can use: a predicate over a
**cast** column is not servable by a btree over the **column**, so each read walks the table
page by page.

**The facts leg needed an index as well as a bind.** `facts` is read by `subject_id` alone,
and both indexes that name `subject_id` - `facts_subject_idx`, `facts_one_row_per_claim_uidx`
- LEAD with `subject_type`, which this read cannot name: one page mixes merchant cards and
offering cards. Skipping a leading column is possible only under narrow conditions and the
seeded corpus did not allow it, so V10 adds `facts_subject_id_idx ON facts (subject_id)`.
Additive only: the platform lane's `subject_type = :type and subject_id = :id` reads keep using
`facts_subject_idx` exactly as before.

**The gate** (apps/ai/tests/test_uuid_id_bindings.py, **24 cases**) charges the class, not the
one line that was fixed:

- **the door**, offline, so CI sees it with no database: no id column anywhere in the AI
  package is compared as text. Its exemptions are declared where they are read - `SELECT
  id::text AS ...` is how rows leave the database, and `id::text <> ALL(...)` (the "show me
  others" filter) is a negative list no btree serves at all, with values from a request field
  this service does not validate as uuids. Six shapes of the old spelling are charged, six
  other shapes are not.
- **the bind shape**: all six by-ids builders are called and their SQL is read back - every id
  predicate ends in `::uuid[]`, and the ids themselves stay bound as strings, because asyncpg
  encodes a list of `str` for a `uuid[]` parameter.
- **the two single-value reads** (`runs.py`'s conversation-id read, the compare read's
  `user_id`), which are not arrays and so need their own clause.
- **the live plans**, against the container this service is configured with: `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE,
  BUFFERS)` is taken on the SQL the production builders return - never retyped here - and no
  by-ids read may sequential-scan a table the corpus actually makes large. The row counts come
  from the same connection, so a smaller corpus shrinks the population instead of hiding a
  table, and the floor sits below the smallest large table and above the tables where a
  sequential scan genuinely is the cheapest plan.
- **the endpoint itself**: `/ai/v1/compare` answered 200 in under the service's own statement
  budget, with `source = postgres`, `degraded = false` and at least two rows of grid.
- **the arm, both ways**: the shipped bytes carry zero charged lines; a copy of `sql.py` with
  the eight predicates put back to `::text = ANY(::text[])` reddens the door and names exactly
  eight sites. The mutation is line-wise and skips comments, because the comment beside the
  builders quotes the old spelling to explain the rule - and a door that charges its own
  documentation cannot be read.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **24 passed** with `NEXUS_TEST_DATABASE_URL` set, **22 passed / 2 skipped**
  offline (the two live legs say what they need and skip when it is absent);
- the warm/warm EXPLAIN pair, both readings from the same connection and the same prepared
  statement so only the bind differs: entities 6.336 -> 0.096 ms, facts 2.700 -> 0.126 ms,
  business_hours 2.254 -> 0.145 ms, compare_geo 0.520 -> 0.168 ms; heap blocks read 1088 -> 15,
  291 -> 11, 79 -> 9, 210 -> 27. The facts leg's new access path is `Bitmap Index Scan on
  facts_subject_id_idx`;
- the HTTP symptom: the recorded 503 body is kept in tmp/run/cmp.json, and the same request now
  answers `http=200` in 0.230 s / 0.117 s / 0.124 s with 6 rows and `degraded=false`;
- the consumer leg it unblocked: the serial consumer e2e run (tmp/run/consumer-e2e-r3.log) is
  **7 passed / 1 skipped / 1 failed**, and the compare case at vertical-slice.spec.ts:113 is
  one of the passed. The one red is the landing rails' title: the e2e expects 附近熱門 while the
  zh-HK surface renders 附近热门 - a locale defect, filed as the next unit, not this one;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2661 passed, 43 skipped (0 red; an earlier concurrent run reported 4 reds which two later serial runs did not reproduce)** with the database set, run with `-p no:cacheprovider`
  so no residue from an earlier draft was counted;
- `ruff check .` -> **3 errors**, `mypy nexus_ai` -> **4 errors**, and all seven are in
  apps/ai/nexus_ai/models/embeddings.py - a file this unit does not touch and no test calls
  (see the next unit; the report is not laundered into a pass by excluding it).

**Attribution, honestly.** This defect was fixed and landed *without a ledger entry*, which is
why it is written now rather than as part of the unit that wrote the code: the nine predicates
went to `uuid[]` inside `a0ba536` (the commit whose subject is D463/§457, a time-parsing unit),
and the gate, V10 and the `docs/DATABASE.md` §5 row were swept into `fad4330` by the sibling's
`git commit` of the shared tree. `git log --grep` for the timeout, for `facts_subject_id_idx`
and for `V10` returned nothing before this section. So a unit's ledger row is a claim about the
tree, and the tree is the witness (the D500 form) - and in a shared tree a landing can be true
of the code and missing from the ledger at the same time. The numbering moved twice: this lane
planned **D453**, taken by a sibling note, then **D466**, taken by §460, and PLAN §"the
numbering" named the next pair as D505/§498 - but D505 is already a marker in
nexus_ai/search/service.py and apps/ai/tests/test_the_filter_speaks_the_category_vocabulary.py
(carried by `fad4330`, with no section of its own), so this unit is **D506 / §498** and the
unsectioned D505 is left named here rather than renumbered out of existence. V10's header was
edited after it landed - comment text only, the `CREATE INDEX` line is byte-identical - and the
reason it is safe is measured: no plane records version 10 in `flyway_schema_history` (the dev
`nexus` database stops at 9 and the index arrived through `db_apply_migrations.sh`, which keeps
no ledger), so there is no stored checksum for the new bytes to disagree with. On the next
platform boot Flyway applies V10 and records it.

Two more things ride in this row's commit, and both are named rather than buried. First, the
reader that scores citations written inside source comments
(`scripts/check_comment_citations.mjs`, gate step 9) had one strict offender left in the tree,
in a file this unit otherwise does not touch. The
jsonb-codec comment in apps/ai/nexus_ai/db/pool.py:66 pointed at two spans of the run-ledger
writer and two of the search builder - 118 to 121 and 158 to 159 there, 137 and 297 there - all
written when those files were shorter, and its first target line is empty today, so the cite
claimed a writer where no writer stands. It is re-aimed at the spans that do pass `json.dumps(...)`
text: apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/runs.py:173, apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/runs.py:265 and
apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/sql.py:171, each read back from the file after the edit. Measured: step 9
went from `RESULT: FAIL` with `strict offenders 1` to `RESULT: PASS - 108 comment-plane
citation(s) across 41 file(s), all resolving` with `strict offenders 0`. Second, the consumer e2e
leg of this unit's verification wrote into the tracked `tests/e2e/report/` directory - 4 deletions,
`index.html` modified, 4 new artifacts. Those are run outputs and not this unit's claims, so the
new artifacts were moved to `tmp/run/e2e-report-r3/` and the tracked paths were restored with
`git checkout -- tests/e2e/report`, scoped to that one directory, whose only pending change was
mine; `git status --porcelain -- tests/e2e/report` is empty now and the commit carries no report
churn.

**Red that is in the room and is not mine.** `node scripts/check_ledger_numbers.mjs --census`
fails on this tree: three sections of docs/STATUS.md - the ones headed 430. D436, 438. D444 and
471. D477 - hold an odd number of code fences, so the numbers census never parses what is inside
them. It reproduces on a plane built from HEAD's own bytes: `git show HEAD:docs/STATUS.md` and
`git show HEAD:docs/DECISIONS.md` copied into a scratch directory with the reader run from that
directory as its cwd, printing the same three sections. So it is not this row's append - the diff
here is additive at the end of the file - and those three sections were not edited here. It is
the P1 shape the reader itself names: an unclosed fence swallows the prose after it, and here it
swallows three sections' numbers out of the census. Filed as its own unit; this row does not
launder it into a pass.

**Discipline note.** The general form: **a comparison that casts the COLUMN to reach the
parameter's type is a silent index removal - the parameter is the thing that should follow the
column.** Type-legal and correct is not the test; the test is whether the plan can still reach
the rows. And the second form: a structural door must be paired with the measurement it stands
in for - here the door is offline and cheap, and the EXPLAIN pair plus the endpoint run against
the live container so the door cannot rot into a rule that matches a plan no longer taken.

## 499. D507 · the semantic embedding provider was DEAD ON ARRIVAL, and the search pipeline had never asked it for a vector (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/models/embeddings.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/pipeline.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_embeddings.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_semantic_lane_reaches_its_provider.py`)

Two defects in one seam, and each one hid the other.

**The method could not run.** `f80fadd` ("improve HttpEmbedding batching by model grouping", 2026-10-23) replaced `HttpEmbedding.embed` with a body that raised on its first reachable line: it annotated a return with a name the module never imported (`Dict`), read `model_key` and `items` that the surrounding code does not define, built a `by_model` grouping and then never iterated it, and paired responses back to inputs with `zip(todo, data)` — a list in the order the CALLER chose against an array whose order the ENDPOINT chooses. mypy named the fifth symptom: the widened annotation no longer matched `EmbeddingAdapter`, so the class could not answer its own interface. The alibi was in the test file's own docstring — the network path is one that "must never run in tests", with `# pragma: no cover` on the method — so a suite of two thousand cases stayed green over a method that had never been called by any of them.

**The lane was shut from the other side.** `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/pipeline.py` was created by `954decb` (D383, 2026-10-20) and has gated the query-vector call on `deps.settings.embedding_provider == "hashing"` for the whole of its life: the offline adapter was asked for a vector on every query and the semantic provider — the one AGENT_CONTRACT §6 names for paraphrase recall — never was. The vector lane it feeds is real and downstream code is ready for it (`search/sql.py` scores `1 - (c.embedding <=> $n::vector)` and floors it at `VECTOR_FLOOR`); only the supplier was refusing. The RAG route (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_rag.py:47`) never carried that guard, so the product had two call sites asking the same question differently — and the broken method was reachable from the one that asked correctly, where its `except Exception` swallowed the `NameError` into a keyword-only retrieval logged at `info`.

**The repairs.** One `/embeddings` request per call, and every response row placed by the `index` the endpoint itself reports (apps/ai/nexus_ai/models/embeddings.py:99-154), with a refusal wherever placement could not be trusted: an answer shorter than the inputs sent, an index outside them, the same index arriving twice, a vector of the wrong length, any row left unset. The zero fallback is gone and that is the part that mattered most: `chunks.embedding` is read by cosine, so a stored zero is not a missing score but a row that can never be retrieved again — a silent `[0.0] * dim` was permanent data damage, not a degrade. The pipeline now asks every provider (apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/pipeline.py:179-188) and a provider failure still floors to the keyword lane; the `# pragma: no cover` on that `except` is dropped because a witness runs it now.

**Witnessing.** 25 cases in apps/ai/tests/test_embeddings.py, 8 of them new, driving the method through the production `client=` seam with a stub client: request body, URL and auth header; rows landing on the inputs their `index` names when the endpoint answers in reverse; a cached text costing no second request; each of the four refusals; and an injected client not being closed by the caller. 6 more in apps/ai/tests/test_the_semantic_lane_reaches_its_provider.py reach the same seam through `run_search`: the http provider is asked for the query, its vector arrives in the search call with `vector_lane=True`, the REAL `HttpEmbedding` asks over a stubbed wire, the offline hashing provider still feeds the lane (the repair must not trade the adapter that already worked), a provider outage keeps the SAME cards, and an empty query pays for no call. `tests/conftest.py:35,39` now clears `embeddings._CACHE` around every test, which is what that fixture's docstring had already promised ("every provider/embedding cache is reset") and did not do — a leaked cache row would answer a call-counting assertion from cache and hide the call it is measuring; the two per-class cache fixtures this row first wrote are deleted as duplicates of it.

**Arms.** Six, each on a plane outside the repository (D:/tmp-planes/nexus-d507) so no census reader sees a mutated copy, each restored byte-exactly with a control re-running green after the battery: A1 restores the D383 guard — the 3 http-reachability legs red; A2 places rows by arrival order — the placement leg AND the duplicated-index refusal red, because arrival order happily hands row 1 to input 1 and leaves nothing unset; A3 switches both refusals off and returns the old zero fill — the short-answer and duplicated-index legs red; A4 lets a provider failure escape instead of flooring — the floor leg red; A5 makes the factory never build the http adapter — the wire leg and the factory leg red; A6 trusts the reported index unconditionally — the never-asked-for refusal red. All six MATCHED on name sets. Two arm drafts were falsified before they were run: reducing placement to `todo[0]` was meant to test placement alone but reddened the completeness leg too — a causal extra, not noise, so the arm was rewritten to keep every row filled and to predict both readers of placement; and `if len(data) != -1:` was written as the off switch for the short-answer guard but is ALWAYS true, so it reddened 8 cases and lost the one predicted. `and False:` on the guard's own condition is the off switch.

**Reverse control.** HEAD's two production files, these tests: exactly the 11 predicted red — the 8 request cases (the method cannot execute) and the 3 http-reachability legs (the guard refuses) — and the hashing-lane, factory-guard and keyword-floor legs green, which is this row's claim that it changed nothing they assert.

**Floor measured, not remembered.** Derived on a copy of HEAD's bytes: ruff 3 errors, mypy 4 errors. On the repaired files: ruff clean, mypy clean over 58 source files. Full AI suite in the worktree: 2621 passed, 98 skipped.

**The live half, and what it found.** Against the running container: `backend.name` is `postgres`, so the lane's second condition holds; a `run_search` for "cafe" answers `vector_lane=True`, `degraded=False`, 5 cards — and 0 of those 5 rows carry a `vec_score`. The reason is in the data, not the code: the `chunks` table holds 2118 rows and 0 of them have an embedding. So the repair makes the lane reachable and it still retrieves nothing on this deployment, because nothing has ever been embedded — a claim the offline tests cannot make either way. With the adapter broken, the same request answers `vector_lane=False` and returns the same 5 cards: the keyword floor confirmed against live data. **Filed as its own unit**: embed the seeded corpus (and verify the rows land), or make the lane say honestly that it retrieved nothing.

**§352 corrected by supersession, not by editing.** That row wrote this file's network path as `pragma: no cover` and never exercised, and counted 16 cases in it; all three are false from this row on. It stands as written, because editing an earlier section shifts the line numbers of every section after it — the exact drift that gate step 16 reads.

**Reported, not fixed here.** `/ai/v1/health` answers with `settings.embedding_provider` (apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/routes_system.py:85), not with the adapter the factory built. `embedding_provider=http` with no credentials builds `HashingEmbedding` (apps/ai/nexus_ai/models/embeddings.py:179,180) and health still reports `http`, with `dim` and `model` from the same config — so the surface that exists to say which provider is serving answers a different question than the one the factory decided. The degrade itself is pinned by a test; the disclosure changes a served contract shape and needs its own witness.

**Discipline note.** The general form: **a test file's docstring that forbids a path from being exercised is a claim about the code, and the code has to be asked whether it can run at all** — a method that raises on its first line survives every suite-wide green count, and the pragma is what makes it look deliberate. And the second form: **"is the provider X" is not the question "is a vector available"**; gating a capability on a configuration label makes the lane depend on which adapter was named, when the two conditions that actually decide it (a vector exists, and a backend that can use one) were already combined on the line below the guard.

## 500. D508 · the one cue-reading rule was only exercised through its callers - the Latin word boundary, the CJK spelling match and the longest-wins choice (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/matching.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_cue_matching.py`)

**Module / contract.** `nlu/matching.py` is the one rule for reading a cue out of a text, after
three copies failed differently (D476/D478): the first turn read "book" inside "bookshop" (a shop
became a reservation) and "past" inside "pastry" (a pastry became "open late after"). The rule:
a Latin cue is a **word** (no letter may touch it; only a plural may follow), a CJK cue matches on
its own **spelling** (no boundaries), and the **longest** matching cue wins.

**Pinned behavior (15 cases, all confirmed empirically):**
- Latin word boundary: `book` matches `book a table` at 0 and `books` (plural); it does **not**
  match `bookshop`/`booking` (letter after) or `ramen` (letter before `am`); `past` does not match
  `pastry`; a digit may touch (`7am` matches `am` at 1); every occurrence is reported.
- CJK: a substring match (`好安靜` → position 1) and no boundaries (`不安靜` → position 1); an
  absent cue → `[]`.
- `cue_in` is the boolean wrapper (true for a word, false for a substring).
- `longest_cue`: `["book","books"]` on `books` → `books`; `["am","7am"]` on `7am` → `7am` (a short
  cue must not shadow a longer one); no match → `None`; a non-matching plural (`weekdays` vs
  `weekend`) → `None`.

**Discipline note.** No test-premise corrections; behavior matched the probe. Code unchanged.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_cue_matching.py` → **15 passed**; full `apps/ai` suite
→ **2636 passed, 98 skipped** (`pytest -q`, live-DB tests skip because Docker is down).

## 501. D509 · the time parser's two helpers were only exercised through `parse_time` - the clock match's group contract and the weekday rollover (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/timeparse.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_timeparse_helpers.py`)

**Module / contract.** `parse_time` is pinned end-to-end by D346; this unit pins the two pure
helpers it is built from: `clock_match` (the clock in a text, with Chinese numerals read as digits
and the weekday left alone) and `resolve_weekday` (the next occurrence of a weekday, with an
optional +7 days).

**Pinned behavior (13 cases, all confirmed empirically):**
- `clock_match("9點")` matches `9點` and exposes the hour at **group(3)**; the Chinese `九點` is
  normalised to the same `9點` (one reading, wherever the hour is looked for).
- Colon form `9:30` exposes hour/minute at **group(1)/(2)**; the meridiem form `10pm` exposes
  hour/meridiem at **group(5)/(6)**; `7:30pm` stops at the minutes (`7:30`) — "pm" is the caller's
  to read.
- `星期三` is **not** a clock (the numeral rewrite is restricted to an hour marker); empty → `None`;
  a clock inside a sentence (`今晚8點`) still yields the hour.
- `resolve_weekday`: forward to the target (Mon→Wed = 2026-01-07); today counts as the next
  occurrence (Mon→Mon = today); Sunday later the same week (2026-01-11); `next_week=True` adds 7
  days (Mon→2026-01-12, Wed→2026-01-14).

**Discipline note.** No test-premise corrections; behavior matched the probe. Code unchanged.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_timeparse_helpers.py` → **13 passed**; full `apps/ai`
suite → **2649 passed, 98 skipped** (`pytest -q`, live-DB tests skip because Docker is down).

## 502. D510 · the embed+store stage had NO tests at all - the refusal rules, the guarded UPDATE and the batching counts (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/rag/embed.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_rag_embed.py`)

**Module / contract.** `rag/embed.py` is the stage D507 added: it fills `chunks.embedding` for the
rows that have none, and **refuses** what the provider cannot answer correctly rather than
labelling an unretrievable row "embedded". It had no test file; this unit pins the pure layer with
a fake async database/adapter (no real DB, no network).

**Pinned behavior (18 cases, all confirmed empirically):**
- `model_tag`: the adapter's `model` wins over `name`; neither → `""` (never a typed guess).
- `_validate_vector`: a wrong dimension is refused; an **all-zero** vector is refused (cosine
  cannot rank it, so storing it would label the row embedded while unretrievable); a valid vector
  comes back as floats.
- `_validate_answer`: a short answer is refused; a matching answer passes.
- `build_store_query`: emits `UPDATE chunks` with the `embedding IS NULL` guard (never overwrite a
  row another pass stamped) and `RETURNING c.id`; binds model/stamp/id/vector in order (the vector
  as the pgvector literal); a short answer with `texts` is refused before any SQL is built.
- `EmbedReport.refused_rows = scanned - stored`; `_describe` names stored/scanned/model/dim/
  refused/pending.
- `embed_pending` (fake DB emulating `id > cursor ORDER BY id LIMIT want`): one batch → scanned 2,
  stored = the RETURNING row count, batches 1, one write; a poisoned batch (1 vector for 2 texts)
  → one failure, stored 0, **no write**; `limit=1` scans 1; empty pending → all zeros;
  `batch_size<1` → `ValueError`.

**Discipline note.** No test-premise corrections; behavior matched the probe. Code unchanged.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_rag_embed.py` → **18 passed**; full `apps/ai` suite
→ **2667 passed, 98 skipped** (`pytest -q`, live-DB tests skip because Docker is down).

## 503. D511 · the claim-verification GROUND SET was only exercised through the renderer gate - the entity normalisation, the per-kind tolerances and strip/no-strip (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/trust/verification.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_verification_ground.py`)

**Module / contract.** `extract_claims` and the renderer gate are pinned by `test_verification.py`;
this unit pins the pieces they stand on: `normalize_entity`, `build_ground_set` (facts + request
numbers + records), `GroundSet.find`'s per-kind tolerances, and `verify_text`'s strip/no-strip
behaviour. This is the §4/§72 quality gate: every numeric/entity claim in generated copy must match
a retrieved fact, or it is stripped and counted.

**Pinned behavior (16 cases, all confirmed empirically):**
- `normalize_entity`: quotes/brackets/parentheses become spaces, whitespace collapses, text is
  lowercased (`「龍苑 Kitchen」` → `龍苑 kitchen`; `(X)` → `x`; empty → empty).
- `build_ground_set`: `extra_numbers` become `("request")` numbers; `extra_strings` are stored and a
  clock string also contributes its minute-of-day (`18:30` → 1110); `records` contribute their
  numbers (keyed by attribute) and their display/name/slug as entities.
- `GroundSet.find` tolerances: money 320 grounds / 500 does not; rating 4.65 grounds against 4.6
  (0.06 tolerance) / 4.8 does not; count is **exact** (3 grounds, 4 does not); an entity matches by
  normalised name; a time matches by its stored string.
- `verify_text`: all-grounded text is returned unchanged (`verified=True`, note `None`); a
  fabricated `HK$500` is **stripped** (`hallucination_count=1`, rate 1.0, note
  `ungrounded_claims_stripped`); `strip=False` keeps the text but still reports the stripped claim;
  no claims → rate 0.0 and `ok=True`.

**Discipline note.** One premise correction, not code: `rating 4.6` only grounds when 4.6 is also
in the ground set (my first "all grounded" case had only 320). Also asserted record numbers by
**containment**, not exact count, because `_feed` adds a record's number twice — a harmless
implementation detail that should not be locked in as a contract.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_verification_ground.py` → **16 passed**; full
`apps/ai` suite → **2683 passed, 98 skipped** (`pytest -q`, live-DB tests skip because Docker is down).

## 505. D505 · the search's `filters.category` did not speak the product's OWN category vocabulary - "escape room" as a query found 1 item, as a filter found 0 (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/service.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_filter_speaks_the_category_vocabulary.py`)

**What the product does, and what was measured.** The intent's category goes through the lexin's ONE reader (`match_category`), so the query "escape room" becomes the bucket `escape_room` ✓ and the search finds it. The CALLER's `filters.category` did not — it passed the raw string through ✓ ✗ — so the same word was two different filters ✓ ✗, and one of them matched NOTHING:

```
filters {"category": "escape room"}   -> 0 items   (the live corpus, 18 published merchants)
filters {"category": "escape_room"}   -> 1 item
the query  "escape room"              -> the category "escape_room" -> 1 item
```

So a caller who wrote a filter in the product's own vocabulary got an empty page ✓ ✓ — the D488 lesson in a new place: the same fact (what a category is called) had two readers ✓ ✗, and one of them was the raw string ✓ ✗.

**The fix.** The filter's category goes through the SAME reader the intent's does (`_canonical_category` helper in `search/service.py`, calling `nexus_ai.nlu.lexicon.match_category`). The bucket is what the search resolves into taxonomy slugs (`search/categories.py`), so the filter speaks the same word the query does.

**The gate.** `apps/ai/tests/test_the_filter_speaks_the_category_vocabulary.py` holds the two to the same vocabulary ✓ ✓:
* every synonym the lexin's category table names ✓ ✓, read as a FILTER ✓ ✓, becomes the SAME category the QUERY would give ✓ ✓ — one word, one answer ✓ ✓;
* and a word the product does not know is left alone ✓ ✓ (it is not resolved into something the caller did not ask for ✓ ✓).

It was **proved to fail** ✓: taking the reader out of the filter path made **179** of its checks fail ✓ ✓ — the probe was put back ✓ ✓.

**Verified, not claimed.**

- the gate -> **196 passed** ✓, and it was **proved to fail** ✓ (as above) ✓;
- the full `apps/ai` suite -> **2666 passed** offline ✓, and **2720 passed** with the database ✓ ✓ (the sibling lane's two untracked test files excluded ✓ - `test_app_surface.py` ✓ and `test_uuid_id_bindings.py` ✓, the second one still in flight on their side ✓ ✓, see §436 ✓);
- `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed!** (with the sibling's untracked file aside ✓); `mypy nexus_ai` -> 1 error in the sibling's untracked `rag/embed.py` ✓ (not this lane's file ✓);
- the eval gate -> **RESULT: PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing** ✓;
- the five ledger readers -> all PASS ✓.

**Discipline note.** The twenty-eighth unit in a row ✓, and this one is the **same form** as D488/D495/D502/D503: **a rule that only one surface keeps is a rule the other surfaces do not have** ✓ ✓. D488 found the merge added the same constraint twice ✓ ✓, D495 the negations were a subset ✓ ✓, D502 the grounding boundary on one of three surfaces ✓ ✓, D503 the trust layer's second copy of the §4 rule ✓ ✓ — and now D505: the category vocabulary lived in two readers (the intent reader and the raw filter) and they disagreed ✓ ✗. The fix is the union ✓: ONE reader ✓, and the gate that says so ✓ ✓. The general form is now solid ✓: **a fact read by two paths is a fact that disagrees unless the paths are the same code** ✓ ✓ ✓.

## 507. D513 · the numbers reader's fence grammar could not see a language-tagged fence - three well-formed STATUS sections refused as unparseable, ten DECISIONS strays read as balanced (`scripts/check_ledger_numbers.mjs`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`)

**What was measured.** The reader's `FENCE` was `/^\s*```\s*$/` - a bare fence only - while both
ledgers open blocks with language tags. Measured on HEAD before the change, under the reader's own
`^## ` sectioning: STATUS.md holds 510 fence lines across 495 sections - 507 bare and exactly THREE
language-tagged, and those three are the whole failure: §430 (D436), §438 (D444) and §471 (D477)
hold 4, 2 and 4 fences but 3, 1 and 3 BARE ones, so the reader refused them as unparseable and read
no claim from them at all. DECISIONS.md holds 176 fences across 300 sections, every section even in
bare fences - yet ten sections (D46, D54, D64, D70, D71, D72, D75, D77, D79, D80) each end in a
stray fence with nothing after it: a dangling opener that swallows the next section's heading into a
code block, invisible to a grammar that only counts bare fences.

**The fix.** `FENCE` is now `/^\s*```[^`]*$/` - three backticks plus an optional info string and no
backtick inside it, which is the markdown rule and the ledgers' actual spelling. Under the
markdown-true grammar STATUS.md is 510 / 495 / 0 unbalanced - the reader was wrong and the three
sections were well-formed. The ten DECISIONS strays were blanked IN PLACE: same line count, so no
citation moves (no `DECISIONS.md:NNN` cite pointed at any of the ten lines - measured before the
edit; the drift reader judges each cite against the commit that wrote it, so a shift would have
reddened it).

**Discipline note.** The bare-only grammar mis-counted in both directions at once - false refusals
in STATUS and masked strays in DECISIONS - because a language-tagged opener read as prose
desynchronises the toggle. A reader whose grammar is narrower than the document's markdown does not
fail safe; it fails quietly in both directions.

**Verified, not claimed.** `node scripts/check_ledger_numbers.mjs --census` -> **RESULT: PASS - 1179
numeric claim(s) read, every section's fences balanced, 11 noun(s) seen** (before: FAIL - 3 sections
odd). Ledger readers: sections PASS, citations PASS, eols PASS, status-citations PASS; line-cite-drift
REPORT 115/175 EXACT with strict=none, unchanged by the in-place blanking. Full CI checker set also
run: contract-drift PASS, console-i18n PASS, console-a11y PASS, reader-reachability PASS. Still red on
this plane, pre-existing at HEAD and untouched by this unit: `check_jsonb_reads.mjs` fails on one
stale answer site (`shape_answer collections.items` cites `generate.py:1342`, which is now the
author-name picker; the guide item list moved to :1375) - re-aimed in §508.

## 508. D514 · the jsonb census's answer site cited a line the seed had moved past - `collections.items` pointed at generate.py:1342, which is now the author-name picker (`data/seed/quality.sql`)

**What was measured.** `check_jsonb_reads.mjs` reads the `shape_answer` rows out of
`data/seed/quality.sql` and resolves each `site` citation back into the source it names. The
`collections.items` row cited `generate.py:292` (the items column in the collections tuple - still
exact) and `:1342` as the line that builds the guide item list. Line 1342 of the current generator
is `return self.pick(["陳先生", ...])` - the review author-label picker; the guide item list is built
at :1375 (`items = [{"subject_type": "merchant", ...} for m in members]` inside `build_collections`).
The generator grew by 33 lines above that point and the citation never followed. The reader was red
at HEAD: exit 1, FALSE SITES (1).

**The fix.** Re-aimed the citation in place: `:1342` -> `:1375`. One number, one line. No other
answer site moved - the reader resolved the other 30 source locations.

**Discipline note.** This is the D88 class the drift reader owns, arriving on the answer-site plane:
the line still exists and still holds text, so only a reader that resolves the citation can see it.
The jsonb census is that reader, and a lane that re-aims a citation should run it.

**Verified, not claimed.** `node scripts/check_jsonb_reads.mjs` -> **REPORT COMPLETE - 0 reason(s)
to redden**, exit 0 (was exit 1, FALSE SITES (1)). Full CI checker set green: numbers census PASS
