## 525. D531 · a preference the user DECLARES in the NLU's own spelling was unreadable (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/service.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_declared_preference_speaks_the_spelling_the_nlu_emits.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_live_the_declared_preference_speaks_the_nlu_spelling.py`)

**What was measured.** The lexicon's `PREFERENCE_RULES` carries two spellings of the same
fact, and both are the product's own:

    ("ambience", "quiet",  ["安靜", "静一啲", "quiet", ...], 1)
    ("ambience", "lively", ["熱鬧", "lively", ...], 1)
    ("style",   "ambience", ["有情調", "vibe", ...], 1)

The seed's own comment names the first two - "Ambience preferences (NLU: ambience/quiet,
ambience/lively)" - and the seed declares its demo user's ambience row as
`("style", "ambience", {"value": "quiet"}, 0.6, "inferred")`, whose value is the STRING
"quiet". So the stored-preference chain grew a branch for `style/ambience` reading a
string, and never one for `ambience/quiet` or `ambience/lively`, which carry a BOOLEAN.
Measured on this database, a preference stored the way the product itself spells it:

    kind=ambience, key=quiet, value={"value": true}  ->  personalization = None
                                                         for all 470 merchants

The same fact typed into the query box was read correctly, because the intent path
derives `quiet_ambience` and the seed writes it. So the TRANSIENT signal worked and the
PERSISTENT one did not: the preference the user saved was the one that did nothing, and
nothing on any surface said so. §33 says the user can inspect and delete their
preferences; a preference whose effect they cannot see is one they cannot inspect.

This is the D518 shape a fourth time - one fact, two readers, and here the copy serving
the live query was the working one while the stored copy was the broken one - and the
mirror image of D530, where it was the other way round. It also shows the limit of
D527's gate: that gate reads the SEED's declared rows against the ranker's branches, and
the seed spells its ambience row `style/ambience`, so the gate was green while the
spelling the NLU emits was unreadable.

**The fix.** A branch for `ambience/quiet` and `ambience/lively` reading the boolean the
NLU emits, with the two attributes as either witness (D527's lesson: a matcher that
demands its own attribute answers None for every merchant the corpus leaves it out of).
Measured on this database after: a declared `ambience/quiet` at 0.9 scores the 188 quiet
merchants **0.9000** and the 282 loud ones **0.1000**.

**Verified, not claimed.**
`test_a_declared_preference_speaks_the_spelling_the_nlu_emits.py`: **6 passed** - the
declared preference reaches the quiet merchants, the lively one reaches the lively
merchants, a `value: false` refusal reads the other way round, the two spellings of one
fact answer alike, a merchant the corpus says nothing about stays unscored, and the
cross-plane gate: every (kind, key) the NLU emits has a stored branch. Live
(`test_live_the_declared_preference_speaks_the_nlu_spelling.py`): **3 passed** - the
corpus splits on both sides, the preference in the NLU's spelling is read, and the lane
is not flat. Proved to fail: removing the branch reddens **6** of the 9 checks (the probe
put back, the file byte-compared afterwards). Targeted regression (`-k "preference or
structured or occasion or personaliz or merge or refinement or state or polarity or
cuisine or transient or ranking or attribute or vocabulary or ambience"`) -> **1283
passed, 31 skipped**; (`-k "search or rank or card or score or facet or filter or avoid
or understand or intent or nlu"`) -> **1058 passed, 38 skipped**; `mypy nexus_ai` ->
**Success: no issues found in 59 source files**; `ruff check .` -> **All checks
passed**; eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**.

## 526. D532 · the seed derived the preference attributes from names the taxonomy does not carry (`data/seed/seed_pools.py`, `data/seed/generate.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_seed_derives_preferences_from_leaves_the_taxonomy_writes.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_spicy_word_speaks_the_seeds_own_leaves.py`)

**What was measured.** The seed derives seven merchant `attributes` from the merchant's
category, and every name it compared against was a name the taxonomy does not carry.
`restaurant`, `cafe`, `bar` and `hotel` are TOPS in `CAT_TREE`, not leaves - a merchant's
`leaf` is `sushi` or `ramen`, never `restaurant` - while `western`, `seafood`, `dim_sum`,
`malaysian`, `bakery`, `bbq`, `cooking_class`, `japanese` and `escape_room` are
respellings of leaves, and `attraction`, `park`, `rooftop`, `fast_food`, `sichuan`,
`hunan` and `mexican` name no leaf at all. Measured on the seed's own output (60
merchants): `solo_occasion` was True for **0 of 60** merchants and `scenic_view` for
**0** - the preferences the NLU emits (`occasion/solo`, `scene/scenic`) were inert on
every row - while `date_occasion` (4), `group_occasion` (1), `family_occasion` (1) and
`business_occasion` (1) sat barely above the 15% coin-flip the generator sprinkles for
variety. D528 had just wired the occasion matcher to its weight (D522's lesson), so the
matcher was weighting a flag that was always False: the user is told they have a
preference for somewhere quiet to eat alone, the corpus says nothing, and the ranking
lane answers from a constant. This is the D518 shape a fifth time - one fact, two
planes - with the writer and the reader on opposite sides of the seed.

**The fix.** The leaf sets moved into `seed_pools.py` beside the tree they name
(`DATE_LEAVES`, `GROUP_LEAVES`, `FAMILY_LEAVES`, `BUSINESS_LEAVES`, `SOLO_LEAVES`,
`SCENIC_LEAVES`, `SPICY_LEAVES`), the tops are read off the tree with `_leaves_under()`
instead of retyped, and the names that resolve to nothing were dropped. Measured on the
same 60 merchants after: `solo_occasion` **27 of 60**, `scenic_view` 2,
`date_occasion` 34, `group_occasion` 25, `family_occasion` 28, `business_occasion` 30.
`outdoor_style` stays at the generator's own fallback because the taxonomy carries no
outdoor leaf; that is now recorded in the set itself (`OUTDOOR_LEAVES = ()`) instead of
being left to look like a fact about the data.

**Verified, not claimed.**
`test_the_seed_derives_preferences_from_leaves_the_taxonomy_writes.py`: **21 passed** -
every member of every set is a leaf the tree writes, no set names a top, the generator's
derivation reads the set it was measured against, the sets are not vacuously small,
`OUTDOOR_LEAVES` is empty for the stated reason, and the generated corpus really does
carry each preference on both sides (the attribute is True for at least one merchant,
so the preference the NLU emits is not inert). The D526 spicy gate was re-read against
the named set and still holds: **9 passed**. Proved to fail: putting `restaurant` - a
TOP - back into `SPICY_LEAVES` reddens **2** checks (the probe was put back and the file
byte-compared afterwards); the same holds for a derivation naming a set `seed_pools`
does not write. Targeted regression (`-k "preference or structured or occasion or
personaliz or merge or refinement or state or polarity or cuisine or transient or
ranking or attribute or vocabulary or ambience"`) -> **1304 passed, 31 skipped**;
(`-k "seed or taxonomy or category or leaf or falsifier"`) -> **469 passed, 5 skipped**;
`mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 59 source files**; `ruff check .` ->
**All checks passed**; eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**.

## 527. D533 · a question was read as a refusal, and a refusal governed clauses it never sat in (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/understand.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_question_is_not_a_refusal.py`)

**What was measured.** The product names its question vocabulary in `ASK_MERCHANT_CUES` -
有無, 有无, 有冇 - and its refusal vocabulary in `NEGATION_CUES` - 冇 among them. Two
tables, one pair of characters, opposite meanings, and the reader that runs on the
sentence had to pick one. It picked the refusal. Measured on the live rule path:

    有冇辣            ->  spicy   -1,  cuisine_avoid=spicy    (the user ASKED about spicy)
    有冇海鮮          ->  seafood -1,  diet_avoid=seafood
    想問有冇嘈        ->  quiet   -1,  noise_avoid=嘈
    有冇安靜啲嘅餐廳  ->  quiet   -1

A question demoted the very merchants it asked about, in the preference lane and the
constraint lane alike - the D529 shape with the sign the other way round. The same unit
closes the other half of the rule the module's own docstring already claims (a cue must
GOVERN the token): a cue that merely sat somewhere later in the turn governed it, so
"想找個安靜的咖啡店，唔好辣" read quiet as -1 - a refusal of the quiet belonging to the
辣 clause.

**The fix.** A cue under the lead of the existential question governs nothing: the 有 of
有冇 / 有無 / 有没有 is the question's own verb. A cue governs a token it is attached to -
adjacent, modulo a short in-clause gap, with the Cantonese particles still reading as
same-clause - and a clause boundary (a comma, either spelling) ends the clause it sits
in. Both readers now walk every occurrence of a cue rather than the first, so a turn that
opens with a question and refuses later ("有冇辣，冇海鮮") still refuses the seafood. The
old attachment test was `_LOCAL_FILLER.match(between)` - a pattern whose `*` quantifier
matched the empty string, so ANY gap of three characters or fewer read as filler and the
boundary was never enforced at all.

**Verified, not claimed.**
`test_a_question_is_not_a_refusal.py`: **22 passed** - every 有-led question form the
product's own `ASK_MERCHANT_CUES` names leaves the preference it asks about positive and
writes no constraint; the same word without the 有 still refuses; a refusal later in a
turn that opens with a question still refuses, in both lanes; a cue that merely sits
later in the turn governs nothing; a cue attached after the token still negates it. The
contested-characters check fails the gate if the two tables stop disagreeing, so the gate
cannot go vacuous. Proved to fail: removing the question exemption reddens **5**, the
unconditional after-case **1**, the first-occurrence-only scan **6** (each probe put back
and byte-compared). Live (`test_live_preferences.py`,
`test_live_conversation_refinement.py`, `test_live_personalization_signal.py`): **13
passed, 1 skipped** (the skip is the test's own note: the live corpus predates the seed
generator that writes `date_occasion`). Targeted regression (`-k "preference or
structured or occasion or personaliz or merge or refinement or state or polarity or
cuisine or transient or ranking or attribute or vocabulary or ambience"`) -> **1304
passed, 31 skipped**; (`-k "search or rank or card or score or facet or filter or avoid or
understand or intent or nlu"`) -> **1058 passed, 38 skipped**; `mypy nexus_ai` ->
**Success: no issues found in 59 source files**; `ruff check .` -> **All checks passed**;
eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**.

**Residue measured and filed, not fixed.** `normalize_query` turns every clause comma
into a space, so by the time this reader runs "平, 唔要咖喱" and "平 唔要咖喱" are the same
string and no reader can tell the clauses apart. The normalizer owns that one.

## 528. D534 · the refusals the product could not read - 無, 沒有, 没有 (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_refusals_the_product_could_not_read.py`)

**What was measured.** The refusal table carried 冇 - the Cantonese character - and the
standard-written refusals were not in it:

    無素食     ->  vegetarian +1     (a LIKE of the very thing refused)
    沒有素食   ->  vegetarian +1
    没有素食   ->  vegetarian +1
    无素食     ->  vegetarian +1     (canonicalised to 無素食, same hole)

So a user who refused in the standard written spelling was answered with the opposite of
what they asked, and the ranking lane then boosted it - the D522 shape again, in the one
vocabulary the product has not finished.

**The fix.** 無 and 沒有 join the table. Adding them was NOT safe before D533, and the
reason is the point: 無 sits inside 無障礙 (the accessible token) and inside 貴都無所謂
(the premium pattern), and 有無 / 有没有 is the product's own question form - a naive
table entry would refuse the wheelchair users, refuse the premium diner who says price is
no object, and turn "is there any outdoor seating?" into a dislike of outdoor seating.
D533's attachment rule and its existential-question exemption are what make the entry
honest, and the gate pins the neighbours so they stay honest. 没有 is spelled out beside
沒有 because the canonical table has no 没 -> 沒 entry: canonicalisation cannot unify the
two scripts, and the Simplified user's refusal would otherwise go unread.

**Verified, not claimed.**
`test_the_refusals_the_product_could_not_read.py`: **15 passed** - each spelling is in the
product's own table (so a removal reddens the gate), each reads -1 in the preference
lane, each writes `cuisine_avoid=spicy` in the constraint lane, and the six measured
neighbours keep their positive polarity with only the constraints the sentence itself
legitimately writes. Proved to fail: removing 無 from the table reddens **3** (the probe
was put back and byte-compared). Live (`test_live_preferences.py`,
`test_live_conversation_refinement.py`, `test_live_personalization_signal.py`,
`test_live_the_refusal_does_not_flatten_the_lane.py`): **17 passed, 1 skipped** (the
test's own note about the pre-seed corpus). Targeted regression (`-k "preference or
structured or occasion or personaliz or merge or refinement or state or polarity or
cuisine or transient or ranking or attribute or vocabulary or ambience or refusal or
negation"`) -> **1355 passed, 35 skipped**; (`-k "search or rank or card or score or
facet or filter or avoid or understand or intent or nlu"`) -> **1058 passed, 38
skipped**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 59 source files**; `ruff
check .` -> **All checks passed**; eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**.

**Residue measured and filed, not fixed.** `CANONICAL_FORMS` has no 没 -> 沒 entry, so
`detect_language("没有素食")` answers **zh-HK** - a Simplified user is read as a Hong
Kong user, the D420 shape. Filling the map entry obliges 没 to vote Simplified on its own
(the D435 gate's locale invariant), which moves locale detection for every sentence
carrying it; that is the next unit's measurement, not this one's.

## 529. D535 · the clause is the unit of governance: a conjunction ends it, one verb bridge keeps it (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_clause_is_the_unit_of_refusal.py`)

**What was measured.** D533 enforced the boundary the punctuation marks. Two cases
survived it, because the normalizer turns a clause comma into a space while the OTHER
clause markers survive as words:

    cheap and no curry        ->  cheap -1     (the refusal is the curry's, not the cheap's)
    I do not want spicy food  ->  spicy +1     (a LIKE of the very thing refused)

The first is a conjunction: "X and no Y" coordinates two clauses and the refusal belongs
to the second. The second is a verb: "do not WANT spicy" keeps the refusal inside its own
clause across one verb, and without the bridge the most natural English refusal read as a
LIKE, which the ranking lane then boosted - the D522 shape, in English.

**The fix.** A conjunction ends a clause: a cue on the far side of one governs nothing
there. One verb may sit between a refusal and the thing refused. Both halves are the same
principle D533 stated - a refusal governs the clause it sits in - applied to the two
clause markers the punctuation rule could not see. The degree adverb 咁 joins the
particle vocabulary (`唔好咁嘈` - don't be SO noisy - refuses the 嘈 with the adverb in
between), which the vocabulary gate holds the package to.

**Verified, not claimed.**
`test_the_clause_is_the_unit_of_refusal.py`: **30 passed** - every conjunction the table
names ends the clause in both directions (the wanted half stays wanted, the refused half
stays refused, and the constraint still writes); every bridged refusal reads -1; and the
eight cases D533 fixed are held green so the two units cannot drift apart. Proved to
fail: removing the conjunction boundary reddens **17**, removing the verb bridge
**3** (each probe put back and byte-compared). Live (`test_live_preferences.py`,
`test_live_conversation_refinement.py`, `test_live_personalization_signal.py`,
`test_live_the_refusal_does_not_flatten_the_lane.py`): **17 passed, 1 skipped** (the
test's own note about the pre-seed corpus). Targeted regression (`-k "preference or
structured or occasion or personaliz or merge or refinement or state or polarity or
cuisine or transient or ranking or attribute or vocabulary or ambience or refusal or
negation or clause"`) -> **1387 passed, 35 skipped**; (`-k "search or rank or card or
score or facet or filter or avoid or understand or intent or nlu"`) -> **1058 passed, 38
skipped**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 59 source files**; `ruff
check .` -> **All checks passed**; eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**.

**Residue measured and filed, not fixed.** The CONSTRAINT lane's window is eight
characters past the negation, so "don't want spicy" (the value sits ten past the cue)
still writes no `cuisine_avoid` - the preference lane now reads the refusal, the filter
lane does not. Widening the window to sixteen was measured too: it then reads "no rush,
want spicy" as a refusal of spicy. That lane's grammar is the next unit's, not this
one's.

## 530. D536 · the constraint lane reads the clause, not eight characters (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/understand.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_constraint_lane_reads_the_clause.py`)

**What was measured.** The lane that writes the §7.1 constraints had its own idea of how
far a refusal reaches: eight characters past the negation, measured from the end of the
cue AFTER its trailing space was stripped - so a value had seven characters of room, and
the lane could not read the product's own vocabulary:

    no cilantro    ->  []        the value is eight characters
    no coriander   ->  []        nine, and in CONSTRAINT_CANON and in no rule
    唔要咖喱        ->  []        咖喱 / 咖哩 are in the canon and in no rule
    don't want spicy          ->  []    the value sits ten past the cue
    I do not want spicy food  ->  []

The preference lane read every one of these refusals; the constraint lane - the one the
§7.1 schema and the state merger carry - wrote nothing, so the refusal reached the
ranking lane and never reached the filter. Widening the window to sixteen was measured
and rejected: it then reads "no rush want spicy" as a refusal of the spicy, because
both clauses' words sit inside it. A window is not a grammar.

**The fix.** The clause is the unit of governance (D535), so the value is now read the
way the polarity lane reads a token: the cue governs a value in its own clause, and one
verb may bridge the two. `polarity._attached` is promoted to `clause_attached` and both
lanes read governance through it - ONE reader, so the two lanes cannot disagree about
what a refusal governs. Every gap the clause rule accepts fits inside the old window, so
nothing the old rule read is lost. The three surface forms the canon names and no rule
carried - 咖喱, 咖哩 (the Cantonese spellings of curry) and the English coriander - join
the values; `cilantro` was already there and is read now that the window stops
truncating it.

**Verified, not claimed.**
`test_the_constraint_lane_reads_the_clause.py`: **65 passed** - a census over the
product's own `CONSTRAINT_CANON`: all 27 surface forms must sit in some rule's values,
and each must be read, under the Cantonese cue and the English one, as the canon value
the test's own key map says it is (a new canon entry that declares no key reddens the
gate, so the semantic decision is made rather than inferred); the eight measured holes
are pinned to their exact constraint sets; and the two sentences the widened window
would have broken are held empty. Proved to fail: the eight-character window back
reddens **8**, the three surface forms out of the rules again reddens **10** (each probe
put back and byte-compared). Live (`test_live_the_refusal_does_not_flatten_the_lane.py`):
**4 passed**. The nine refusal/polarity/constraint gates -> **150 passed**; merger,
search-plan, lexicon and understand -> **235 passed**; the vocabulary gates -> **57
passed**; filtered regression (`-k "preference or structured or occasion or personaliz
or merge or refinement or state or polarity or cuisine or transient or ranking or
attribute or vocabulary or ambience or refusal or negation or clause"`) -> **1471
passed, 35 skipped**; (`-k "search or rank or card or score or facet or filter or avoid
or understand or intent or nlu"`) -> **1061 passed, 38 skipped**; `mypy nexus_ai` ->
**Success: no issues found in 60 source files**; `ruff check nexus_ai tests` -> **All
checks passed**; eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**. The whole `tests/` tree
was run once as well: **3656 passed, 43 skipped, 3 failed**, and all three failures
reproduce on the tree WITHOUT this unit's changes (`test_doc_paths_are_real.py`'s
`site.py`, `test_live_search_contract.py`'s refused-cuisine ranking, and a
seed-state-dependent `test_citations_resolve.py` case that passes in isolation).

**Residue measured and filed, not fixed.**
- The polarity lane's AFTER-case reads a cue that touches the token before it as
  governing that token, even when the cue has its own object after it: measured, "I want
  spicy no cilantro" answers spicy **-1** - a dislike of the very thing asked for, which
  the ranking lane then demotes. The rule to write is that a cue governs a preceding
  token only when it governs nothing after it; the constraint lane reads forward only,
  so the mirror case "咖喱唔要" writes no constraint at all.
- The clause gap admits a short filler and ONE verb, but not an adverb: "not very spicy"
  (the gap "very", four characters) reads +1 and writes no constraint, and "not really
  like spicy" reads the same. 咁 is in the particle vocabulary (D535); the English degree
  words are the missing half of it.
- `plan_from_intent` maps `cuisine_avoid` into `plan.avoid` and drops every other
  constraint key: `diet_avoid`, `smoking_avoid`, `noise_avoid` and `feature_avoid` never
  reach the search plan, while the corpus carries the facts they name (239 offerings
  carry a gluten tag, 15 a peanut one). "no gluten" is now read and then dropped between
  the Intent and the plan - the D517 shape, one lane over.
- `meat` is in no table at all: "no meat" writes no constraint and no preference, though
  the corpus carries the vegetarian merchants the refusal points at.

## 531. D537 · a cue with an object of its own does not reach back to the token before it (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_cue_with_its_own_object_does_not_reach_back.py`)

**What was measured.** D533 taught the polarity lane to read a cue that sits AFTER the
token it governs ("素食唔好" refuses the 素食), and the rule was attachment alone - which
is symmetric, and an empty gap is the most attached gap there is. So the lane read a cue
backwards whenever it touched the token before it, and the most natural way to refuse one
thing while asking for another came back inverted:

    I want spicy no cilantro   ->  spicy -1     (a dislike of the thing asked for)
    辣，唔要咖喱                ->  辣 -1        (the refusal is the curry's)
    quiet, no noisy please     ->  quiet -1

The "no" governs the object that follows it. Reading it backwards demoted the very thing
the user asked for, and the ranking lane then ranked on the inverted signal - the D522
shape, in the after-case.

**The fix.** A cue governs a preceding token only when it governs NOTHING after it: a cue
that still has words after it is speaking about those words. The Cantonese sentence-final
particles - 辣唔好呀 (spicy, no) - are part of the refusal and not words of their own, so
呀 㗎 喎 嘛 囉 嘞 咩 啩 join the filler vocabulary beside 咁 (D535); without them the new
rule would read "辣唔好呀" as a LIKE of the spicy, trading one defect for another.

**Verified, not claimed.**
`test_a_cue_with_its_own_object_does_not_reach_back.py`: **34 passed** - the five measured
inversions, the eight measured particles pinned in the table with the rest of the
vocabulary derived from it (so a particle added later is covered and one removed reddens
the pin), the four after-cases D533 fixed, and the five forward refusals. The gate's first
draft fed the raw comma'd string straight to `polarity_for` and went GREEN under the
probe; the lane is now fed the text it actually receives (normalised, then canonicalised),
which is what makes the Cantonese case load-bearing. Proved to fail: the clause-final
condition removed reddens **5**, the particles removed reddens **3** (each probe put back
and byte-compared). The eleven refusal/polarity/constraint gates plus the merger,
search-plan and live-refusal suites -> **433 passed**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no
issues found in 59 source files**; `ruff check nexus_ai tests` -> **All checks passed**;
eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**; filtered regression (`-k "preference or
structured or occasion or personaliz or merge or refinement or state or polarity or
cuisine or transient or ranking or attribute or vocabulary or ambience or refusal or
negation or clause"`) -> **1477 passed, 35 skipped**; (`-k "search or rank or card or score
or facet or filter or avoid or understand or intent or nlu"`) -> **1061 passed, 38
skipped**.

**Residue measured and filed, not fixed.** The constraint lane still reads forward only,
so "咖喱唔要" writes no `cuisine_avoid`. The backward direction is safe in principle now
that a cue with an object of its own cannot reach back - but the normaliser erases the
clause comma, and without a visible boundary "想食辣，咖喱唔要" would still smear the
refusal onto the 辣 (the gap "咖喱" is three characters, which reads as attached). The
same root cause costs the after-case its non-final clauses: "安靜的不好，要嘈" reads the 安靜
as wanted, because everything after the cue looks like the cue's own object. Both come
with the clause boundary that survives normalisation, not before it.

## 532. D538 - one locator, one reach, both lanes - and the clause boundary survives (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/matching.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/understand.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_refusal_is_read_once_by_both_lanes.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_clause_boundary_survives_normalisation.py`)

**What was measured.** Since D536 the polarity lane and the constraint lane read the same
refusal out of the same sentence and shared `clause_attached`, but the polarity lane kept
two private rules of its own: a REACH (a cue could not govern a token further away than a
fixed character count, fewer for a CJK token than for a Latin one, while the constraint
lane read the whole clause) and a LOCATOR (positions found with `str.find`, so a cue
inside a word was a cue here and not there). Measured at HEAD over sentences the product
answers with, three bilingual refusals wrote the filter and read the opposite in the
ranking:

    without 海鮮   -> constraint diet_avoid:seafood      polarity +1
    without any 奶 -> constraint diet_avoid:dairy        polarity +1
    avoid 二手煙    -> constraint smoking_avoid:smoking   polarity +1

The seafood was excluded from the results and boosted in their order, in one turn, from
six words. The same unit measured what the normaliser's flattening cost: a clause comma
arrived at both lanes as a space, so "想食辣，咖喱唔好" answered -1 for the 咖喱 - a refusal
of the very thing the clause before it asked for.

**The fix.** The positions now come from the ONE matcher (`cue_positions`) and the reach
is the clause, so a refusal the search filters for is never also a preference the ranking
boosts. `normalize_query` writes the ideographic space (`CLAUSE_SEPARATOR`) where the
clause punctuation was, and a line break becomes one too, with the ASCII whitespace
around it: it is whitespace, so every `\s*` in the field rules still reads across it, and
it is not ASCII whitespace, so the fold cannot flatten it back into one. Three readers
then read it - the clause boundary, the filler (a gap holding one is two clauses, not
particles), and the clause-final tail (`_clause_final` now ends at the separator, so
"安靜的不好，要嘈" refuses the 安靜 and "想食辣，唔好嘈，要安靜" refuses the 嘈 and asks for
the 安靜). The one place the separator is not a boundary is directly under a cue:
"唔好，辣" refuses the 辣, because there the comma is a pause after the refusal and not a
boundary between it and its object. That is `forward_gap`, and it is the forward
direction only - a cue that governs a token BEFORE it keeps every separator in its gap,
because there the comma really did end the token's clause.

**Verified, not claimed.**
`test_a_refusal_is_read_once_by_both_lanes.py`: **615 passed** - an agreement census over
the product's own negations, gap shapes and values, both directions charged;
`test_the_clause_boundary_survives_normalisation.py`: **84 passed** - the separator's
contract, a census of every punctuation the normalizer rewrites, the smears the comma
used to cause, the clauses the tail now reads, and the readings that must not move.
Proved to fail, each half put back and byte-compared: the separator demoted to a space
reddens **54**, the tail run to the end of the turn reddens **2**, `clause_attached`
stripping the separator again reddens **26**, `forward_gap` keeping the cue's own
separator reddens **2**. The eleven refusal/polarity/constraint gates plus merger,
search-plan and lexicon -> **1167 passed**; filtered regression (`-k "preference or
structured or occasion or personaliz or merge or refinement or state or polarity or
cuisine or transient or ranking or attribute or vocabulary or ambience or refusal or
negation or clause"`) -> **2092 passed, 35 skipped**; (`-k "search or rank or card or
score or facet or filter or avoid or understand or intent or nlu"`) -> **1077 passed, 38
skipped**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 59 source files**;
`ruff check nexus_ai tests` -> **All checks passed**; eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s),
0 failing**.

**Contract change, stated.** `normalize_query` writes `CLAUSE_SEPARATOR` where it used to
write a space, so "你好，世界" is now "你好<U+3000>世界" and "a.b" is "a<U+3000>b" (two
pins in `tests/test_lexicon.py` updated). Everything downstream reads it as whitespace;
the two lanes read it as a clause boundary.

**Residue measured and filed, not fixed.** The constraint lane still reads forward only,
so "咖喱唔要" writes no `cuisine_avoid` - the boundary is now visible, so the backward
direction is safe to write and is the next unit. `_has_constraint` still carries D536's
eight-character window, so "no cilantro" and "no coriander" write a constraint the intent
kind never sees: the intent comes back `unknown`. And the pause rule reads across a want
verb: "唔好，要辣" refuses the 辣 the next clause asks for, in both lanes - the separator
under the cue is read as the cue's own punctuation even when a verb follows it, which is
where a comma really did end a clause.

## 533. D539 - the constraint lane reads a refusal written the Cantonese way round (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/understand.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_value_before_the_cue_writes_its_constraint.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_clause_boundary_survives_normalisation.py`)

half-read, in the language most of its users type. 356 of the 490 read now; the 134
that still do not are two correct silences - the cue is not a word at all ("curryno"),

the 有 sits directly under the cue either way, so D533's one exemption reads both).

## 534. D540 - a verb after the comma opens the next clause (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_verb_after_the_comma_opens_the_next_clause.py`)

**What was measured.** D538 read the separator directly under a cue as the cue's own
punctuation, so a comma could never come between a refusal and its object - "唔好，辣"
refuses the 辣. That is right when the cue's OBJECT follows the comma and wrong when a
VERB does. Measured at HEAD, three sentences the product answers with read the refusal
onto the thing the next clause asks for:

    唔好，要辣        ->  辣 -1, cuisine_avoid:spicy    (the user asked for the 辣)
    辣嘅唔好，要咖喱   ->  咖喱 -1, cuisine_avoid:curry   (ditto)
    咖喱唔好，想食辣   ->  cuisine_avoid:spicy, on top of the curry

The search filtered for the very thing the user asked for and the ranking demoted it -
the D522 shape, from one character of punctuation.

**The fix.** A bare noun after the comma is the refusal's own object (the pause); a verb
opens a new clause's request. `forward_gap` now keeps the separator in the gap when one
was stripped and what follows opens with a verb, and `clause_attached` reads the boundary
it has spelled since D535. The control is the other half of the rule and the reason this
is not "a comma always ends the clause": with NO comma there is no separator to read,
and the verb is the clause's own bridge (D535) - "唔好食辣" and "don't want spicy" refuse
exactly as they did before. Only a STRIPPED separator arms the new reading, and only
against a verb.

**Verified, not claimed.**
`test_a_verb_after_the_comma_opens_the_next_clause.py`: **772 passed** - a census over
every verb the bridge table names x every surface the rules name, in BOTH shapes (the
separator'd one asks for the value and writes nothing; the comma-less one refuses it and
writes the constraint), plus a pause census over every surface, a punctuation census over
`CLAUSE_PUNCTUATION`, the line break, the three measured defects and the minimal pairs.
Proved to fail: `forward_gap` reverted to the unconditional strip reddens **382**, the

-> **285 passed**; filtered regression (`-k "preference or structured or occasion or
personaliz or merge or refinement or state or polarity or cuisine or transient or
ranking or attribute or vocabulary or ambience or refusal or negation or clause"`) ->
**2874 passed, 35 skipped**; (`-k "search or rank or card or score or facet or filter or
avoid or understand or intent or nlu"`) -> **1113 passed, 38 skipped**; `mypy nexus_ai`
-> **Success: no issues found in 59 source files**; `ruff check nexus_ai tests` ->
**All checks passed**; eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**.

**Residue measured and filed, not fixed.** A surface that sits inside another one ("煙"
inside "二手煙") can be further from the cue than the clause's reach, so it reads +1 while
the longer form is refused - the two lanes agree about it (no constraint is written for
it either), so it is the reader's reach, not a contradiction.

## 535. D541 - the intent kind answers its question with the ONE reader (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/understand.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_intent_kind_reads_the_refusal_the_lane_reads.py`)

## 536. D542 - the doc gate's exemptions were claims nobody checked, and one of them was already false (`apps/ai/tests/test_doc_paths_are_real.py`)

**What was measured.** D462's gate consults its exemption table BEFORE it looks for the
name, so a declared name that becomes real stays invisible to the rule written to catch
it: `embed.py` sat in `DECLARED_PROMISES` as "the platform's importer embeds them (not in
this repo)" while `apps/ai/nexus_ai/rag/embed.py` had been in the repository since
D510/D515 and `docs/RAG.md` names it as the lane's own Embed and Store stage - the
exemption had outlived its fact and nothing could see it. The table also had no way to
say the other thing a document does with a name: `docs/ENVIRONMENT_REPORT.md` names
CPython's `site.py` to explain the locale hazard that kills every interpreter launch
under a path the GBK codepage cannot decode - a fact about the machine, not a promise
about this repository, and a flat "not here" row cannot say which of the two it is.

**The fix.** The declarations are claims now, and each is held to what it claims: a
declared name may not be a file the repository has (the dead `embed.py` row is deleted -
the file is real); a declaration no judged document cites is a hiding place, not an
exemption; and a borrowed name must resolve, here and now, to a file the interpreter
produces OUTSIDE the repository root - `site.py` moves to its own `DECLARED_EXTERNAL`
table carrying the import name the sentence means.

**Verified, not claimed.**

and byte-compared: re-adding the `embed.py` row reddens the first new gate (**1 failed,**
**4 deselected**); a name no document cites reddens the second; a borrowed name that
resolves inside the repository and one the interpreter cannot produce at all each redden
the third. The vocabulary reference, the dead-constant census and the constraint table's
vocabulary gate beside it -> **28 passed**; `ruff check` -> **All checks passed**; `mypy`
-> **Success: no issues found in 1 source file**.

**Residue measured and filed, not fixed.** The new gates read NAMES, not sentences: a
declaration is green as long as some judged document still puts the name in backticks,
whatever the sentence now says about it. Measured: `docs/AI.md` describes the planner
(`orchestrator/planner.py`) in the present tense - "emits a typed `Plan`" - for a module
that does not exist, under a declaration that says it is not built yet. The row stays
green because the name is still cited; only a reader of the sentence could see the claim
flip.
## 537. D543 - the eat-less refusal puts the verb AFTER the cue, and the clause rule reads it (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_eat_less_refusal_puts_the_verb_after_the_cue.py`)

**What was measured.** D537's rule - a cue reaches back to a preceding token only when it
governs nothing after it - is right for a NOUN and wrong for a VERB, because the eat-less
refusal is written the other way round: "花生少吃" (peanut, eat less), "peanut 別吃",
"gluten 避免吃". The value sits BEFORE the cue and the verb after it, and the verb's
object is the value. Measured at HEAD, every one of these wrote nothing and came back
with the intent `unknown` - the user refused and the product heard nothing, in the
language most of its users type.

**The fix.** The tail after the cue may be ONE bridge verb, with the clause's own
particles hanging off it. The cue governs the verb, and the verb's object is the token
the backward arm already found, so the cue is final enough to reach back. A NOUN after
the cue is still the cue's own object (D537's "no cilantro" keeps the cilantro), a verb
with an object of its own after it is the forward refusal of that object ("辣唔好食咖喱"
refuses the curry), and the boundary, the separator and the existential exemption all
keep their teeth. Both lanes read the one rule, so "辣唔好食" now answers -1 and writes
`cuisine_avoid:spicy` with one voice.

**Success: no issues found in 59 source files**; `ruff check nexus_ai tests` -> **All
checks passed**; eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**.

**Residue measured and filed, not fixed.** The debt gate's four words are readable at the

## 538. D544 - a degree adverb between the cue and the value does not end the refusal's clause (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_degree_adverb_does_not_end_the_refusals_clause.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_refusal_is_read_once_by_both_lanes.py`)

**What was measured.** The gap rule reads anything up to three characters as the
refusal's own clause, which is why "not so spicy" and "唔好咁辣" already worked. The
English degree words are longer than that: measured at HEAD, "not very spicy" (the gap

like spicy" read the same - the ranking lane boosted the very thing the user refused,

modifies the value). A word that is neither still separates them, which is what keeps
D536's "no rush want spicy" unread, and a boundary or a coordinator ends the clause
wherever it sits. The seam door derives its gap population from these tables, so the
new words join it by itself.

noise_avoid:嘈" in the clause gate is re-spelled `noise_avoid:noise`: the window's
refusal is kept, under the canon's name.
## 540. D546 - every refusal the lane reads reaches the filter, and the filter reads the allergen column (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/service.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/sql.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_every_refusal_the_lane_reads_reaches_the_avoid_filter.py`)

**What was measured.** `plan_from_intent` mapped THREE keys into `plan.avoid` -
`cuisine_avoid`, plus the caller's own `avoid` / `exclude` - out of the FIVE the refusal lane
writes. A sentence the lane read therefore arrived at the plan with its refusal already
dropped: measured at HEAD, "唔食花生" wrote `diet_avoid:peanut` and the plan carried
`avoid == []`, and so did "no gluten", "唔好嘈" and "唔想排隊". The corpus carries what
those words name - 1,380 active offerings carry a `gluten` allergen tag and 57 a `peanut`
one - so the product read the refusal and then threw it away between the Intent and the SQL.
The keys that DID reach the filter were read by a clause that never looked at the column the
corpus writes the fact in: `avoid_terms` expands a word into the taxonomy's leaves, which is
right for a CUISINE, but an ingredient is recorded per OFFERING, in
`offerings.attributes->'allergens'`. Measured on the live corpus, `avoid=["gluten"]`
excluded **0 of 470** published merchants and **0 of 4,707** active offerings while 269
merchants and 1,380 offerings carry the tag. The clause read the merchant's tags, the
merchant's category and the offering's NAME - and an allergen is in none of them. Measured
beside it, an Intent carrying the same refusal twice under two spellings left
`plan.avoid == ['peanut', 'peanut']`; the merge below deduped it on the way into the filters,
so nothing downstream ever saw the duplicate, which is why it survived.

**The fix.** The planner DERIVES its key set from the lexicon's own `CONSTRAINT_RULES`
instead of hand-copying three of the five keys out of it, so a rule added to the table
reaches the filter by construction rather than because somebody remembered a tuple. The
value goes through the ONE canon reader (`canon_constraint`), the same reader
`_fill_constraints` uses, so a caller who hands the planner a surface form binds the term
set the lane's own reading writes. `plan.avoid` is deduped where it is assembled. Both
lanes' avoid clauses read `offerings.attributes->'allergens'` beside the tags they already
read, through the same bound term set, so one word has one set of spellings in both lanes.

**Verified, not claimed.** `test_every_refusal_the_lane_reads_reaches_the_avoid_filter.py`:
**52 passed** - the census walks every (key, surface) pair the rules carry and lands the
canon value in the plan, the key set is the table's own and nothing else, a surface form is
canonicalised, one refusal is written once, the caller's list still merges, both lanes name
the allergen column and bind the same terms, and the live measurement derives its population
from the corpus (every allergen tag a live offering carries, both lanes, the leak counted
rather than assumed). Proved to fail four ways, each restored and byte-compared: the
three-key tuple restored reddens **39**, the merchant lane's allergen leg deleted reddens
**1**, the offering lane's allergen leg deleted reddens **1**, the canon call dropped
reddens **29**. Measured on the live corpus after the fix: `avoid=["gluten"]` excludes 269
merchants / 1,271 offerings (was 0 / 0), `peanut` 22 / 44, `dairy` 245 / 1,022, `egg` 193 /
545, `soy` 213 / 1,247, `shellfish` 156 / 389, `fish` 106 / 295, `nuts` 97 / 171, `sesame`
57 / 82, `garlic` 51 / 118. The clause, vocabulary, canon, SQL-builder, plan and
soft-preference gates beside it -> **292 passed**; filtered regression (`-k "preference or
structured or occasion or personaliz or merge or refinement or state or polarity or cuisine
or transient or ranking or attribute or vocabulary or ambience or refusal or negation or
clause"`) -> **7051 passed, 4 skipped**; (`-k "search or rank or card or score or facet or
filter or avoid or understand or intent or nlu"`) -> **2404 passed, 11 skipped**; `mypy
nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 59 source files**; `ruff check nexus_ai tests` ->
**All checks passed**; eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**. One failure is
PRE-EXISTING on this plane and unrelated: `test_a_refused_cuisine_is_not_served_at_the_top`
reddens at HEAD with the same two slugs (this plane's corpus predates the seed generator
that writes the occasion rows it reads), and it was measured stashed as well as applied.

**Residue measured and filed, not fixed.** Three canon values still name nothing the corpus
writes, so the filter carries them and excludes nothing: `smoking`, `noise` and `queue` -
there is no smoking tag, no noise tag and no queue tag on any merchant or offering, though
the corpus DOES record a noise fact (`attributes.weak_aspects` can name `noise`, and
`quiet_ambience` is written from the same aspect) and a waiting-time one. `onion`, `ginger`
and `coriander` are named by the diet rule and absent from the corpus's allergen vocabulary,
so they exclude only what their spelling matches in an offering's name (6, 33 and 0
merchants). And the offline lane never reads `avoid` at all: `_filter_static` filters on
category, district and max_price and nothing else, so the fixture-backed backend answers a
different question about the same filter than the live one - the D488 shape, one lane over.

## 541. D547 - the negation the product did not know, in either spelling (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/canonical.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_negation_the_product_did_not_know_in_either_spelling.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_refusals_the_product_could_not_read.py`)

**What was measured.** Every other spelling of "did not" was a word the product understood -
唔食辣, 不吃辣, 不想吃辣, 不要吃辣, 讨厌吃辣, 冇食辣 and 無食辣 all wrote the refusal
and read it -1. 没 / 沒 was in NO table at all, and measured at D546 every sentence that
used it came back the opposite of what was asked: "没食辣", "沒食辣", "没吃辣", "沒吃辣",
"我没吃辣" and "我沒吃辣" all wrote no constraint, read the cuisine **+1** - a LIKE of the
very thing the user refused - and answered the intent `unknown`; "没素食" read vegetarian +1;
"没吃花生" wrote nothing at all. Not in `CANONICAL_FORMS`, so the two scripts could not meet.
Not in `NEGATION_CUES`, so neither lane read it. And because the locale markers are DERIVED
from the canon (`SIMPLIFIED_MARKERS = ... | frozenset(CANONICAL_FORMS)`), not in the detector
either - measured, "没有素食" was answered in the **zh-HK** locale for a user who typed
Simplified. D534 filed the canon hole in this exact sentence and predicted the row would
canonicalise into 沒有 and cost nothing when it was filled.

**The fix.** One canon entry (没 -> 沒) and one cue (the bare 没, which canonicalises into
沒). The two together reach three readers: the canon makes the two spellings one word, so
every table canonicalised at import (D447) holds one form of it; the cue joins
`NEGATION_CUES`, from which the constraint table derives its own negations, so ONE entry is
read by BOTH lanes rather than taught to each (D493's shape); and the locale markers gain the
pair for free, because they are derived from the canon rather than kept beside it. Measured
after: every one of the six sentences writes `cuisine_avoid:spicy` and reads the spicy -1, the
bare cue writes all five rules' refusals in both spellings, "没有素食" is answered in zh-CN,
and the refusal reaches `plan.avoid` - the whole chain the D541/D546/D547 units built.

**Verified, not claimed.**
`test_the_negation_the_product_did_not_know_in_either_spelling.py`: **28 passed** - the canon
entry is an equivalence, each spelling votes for the locale it belongs to, the bare cue is in
the product's own table in both spellings, the census walks every constraint rule's first
value under both spellings, the eight measured sentences read the refusal and not a LIKE, the
refusal reaches `plan.avoid`, and five neighbours (the cue inside 無所謂, the existential
question's lead, the refusal in another clause) govern nothing. Proved to fail twice, each
restored and byte-compared: the canon entry deleted reddens **11**, the bare cue deleted
reddens **21**. `test_the_refusals_the_product_could_not_read.py` is re-pointed at the
canonical form of its population - the hand-spelled 没有 row it carried was standing in for
the canon entry that now exists, and the bare 没 joins it - **18 passed**. The vocabulary,
canonical-coverage, canon, lexicon, negations, refusal-once, clause, seam, degree, question,
eat-less, state-merger and understand gates beside them -> **6953 passed**; filtered
regression (`-k "preference or structured or occasion or personaliz or merge or refinement or
state or polarity or cuisine or transient or ranking or attribute or vocabulary or ambience or
refusal or negation or clause"`) -> **7082 passed, 4 skipped**; (`-k "search or rank or card or
score or facet or filter or avoid or understand or intent or nlu"`) -> **2415 passed, 11
skipped**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 59 source files**; `ruff check
nexus_ai tests` -> **All checks passed**; eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s), 0 failing**. One
failure is PRE-EXISTING on this plane and unrelated, and it reddens identically at HEAD with
the changes stashed: `test_a_refused_cuisine_is_not_served_at_the_top`, the same two slugs
(`cove-house-0017`, `jade-stone-0321`) - this plane's corpus predates the seed generator that
writes the occasion rows the test reads.

**Residue measured and filed, not fixed.** The polarity lane reads a refusal of the WORD where
the user asked for its opposite: measured, "唔好嘈", "冇嘈", "無嘈", "没嘈" and "沒嘈" all write
`noise_avoid:noise` AND read the preference `ambience/quiet` **-1**, so the ranking lane demotes
the quiet merchants for a user who asked for a quiet one. The token 嘈 sits in the quiet rule's
own token list, and the cue negates the token it finds - the shape is the same whichever
spelling of the negation is typed, which is why it is filed rather than charged here. 不吃 is
the remaining word of the same family the polarity table lacks (D493's debt): measured,
"不吃辣" writes `cuisine_avoid:spicy` and still reads the spicy +1.

## 542. D548 - the outdoor vocabulary names the word a user actually types (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_outdoor_vocabulary_names_the_word_a_user_types.py`)

**What was measured.** The `style/outdoor` preference row answered 戶外, 户外,

露天座位, 露天, 露天座, 露天餐廳,

wrote `style/indoor +1`. The corpus carries the fact the row points at: measured on the live

the table answered a user in one spelling of a pair only - D416's lesson in a table that was
already half-fixed.

**The fix.** Two tokens in the row the reader already walks: 露天 and 室外. No new
rule and no new lane - the row IS the vocabulary the ranking lane asks with, so the two words
reach it whole.

## 543. D549 - the fixture lane answers the same avoid question the live lane answers (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/service.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_fixture_lane_answers_the_same_avoid_question.py`)

**What was measured.** `_filter_static` is the fixture backend's WHERE clause, and it read
`category`, `district` and `max_price` - and never `avoid`. The live SQL lane has excluded on
`avoid` since D517, so the two backends answered DIFFERENT QUESTIONS about the same hard
filter: measured at HEAD on the live plane (470 published merchants), `avoid=["seafood"]`
dropped **30** merchants in the live lane and **0** in the fixture lane; `avoid=["gluten"]`
dropped 269 and 0; peanut 22 and 0; dairy 245 and 0; egg 193 and 0; shellfish 156 and 0; soy
213 and 0; fish 106 and 0; spicy 66 and 0; meat 44 and 0; pork 120 and 0; beef 72 and 0; nuts
97 and 0; sesame 57 and 0; garlic 51 and 0; onion 6 and 0; ginger 33 and 0; vegetarian 9 and 0.
A test that asked the fixture backend whether a refusal filtered anything was answered "no"
for every word the corpus carries - the D488 shape, one lane over.

**The fix.** The live clause is four legs, and the lane only decides where the last two of them
look: the merchant lane reads the merchant's OWN offerings (`EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offerings
ao WHERE ao.merchant_id = m.id ...)`), the offering lane reads the offering's own name and
allergens. `_filter_static` now mirrors all four - `m.tags && terms`,
`m.category_primary = ANY(terms)`, and the row's own offerings or its own name and
`attributes.allergens` - reading the terms through the live lane's OWN expansion
(`sql._avoid_terms` -> `categories.avoid_terms`) rather than a second copy of it, so
`avoid=["seafood"]` still reaches the merchants tagged `seafood-grill`. `merchant_candidates`
hands the filter the backend's own offering list, because the EXISTS leg has nothing to read
otherwise.

**Verified, not claimed.**
`test_the_fixture_lane_answers_the_same_avoid_question.py`: **10 passed** - one test per leg,
the control that must survive every word, the word no row carries dropping nothing, an empty
list changing nothing, and two live cross-checks that run the predicate against the live SQL
over **20 words on both lanes** (470 merchants, 4707 active offerings, 5546 offerings of every
status) with **zero disagreements**. Proved to fail six times, each restored and byte-compared
(sha256 `e97a9d3b275b0524`): the avoid call dropped reddens **5**, the tag leg **3**, the
category leg **1**, the allergen leg **3**, the merchant lane's offering loop **3**, the
offering lane's own-words leg **2**. The search, sort, preference, structured, polarity,
vocabulary, canonical-coverage, canon, weak-preference, refusal and fixture gates beside them
-> **251 passed**; the filtered regression (`-k "preference or structured or occasion or
personaliz or merge or refinement or state or polarity or cuisine or transient or ranking or
attribute or vocabulary or ambience or refusal or negation or clause"`) -> **7096 passed, 4
skipped, 1 failed**; `mypy nexus_ai` -> **Success: no issues found in 59 source files**;
`ruff check nexus_ai tests` -> **All checks passed**; eval gate -> **PASS - 2 suite(s), 0
failing**. The one failure is PRE-EXISTING on this plane and unrelated, and it reddens
identically at HEAD with the changes stashed:
`test_a_refused_cuisine_is_not_served_at_the_top`, the same two slugs (`cove-house-0017`,
`jade-stone-0321`).

**Residue measured and filed, not fixed.** The same function's `category` leg is the next
instance of the same shape, and it is worse: measured on the live plane, `category_primary`
holds the taxonomy's leaf NES ("Cantonese", "Cha Chaan Teng", "Board Game Cafe" - 66 distinct
values, none of them a coarse bucket), while `_filter_static` compares the caller's bucket to
that column with `=`. So `filters={"category": "restaurant"}` keeps **184** merchants in the
live lane - which resolves the bucket into slugs through `categories.resolve` - and **0** in
the fixture lane, which matches none of them. The 57 fixture rows in the suite all write the
coarse bucket into `category_primary` themselves, so the lane is self-consistent on fixtures
and wrong on live-shaped rows. Filed rather than charged here because it is a different leg
with a different reader, and the D548 lesson is that one unit fixes one thing.


## 544. D550 - the seed gate forbade the embedding pass it had been waiting for, and a kind was a label instead of a claim (`data/seed/quality.sql`, `data/seed/falsifier_plants.py`, `data/seed/falsifiers.tsv`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/rag/embed.py`)

**What was measured.** Two defects one row apart in the same file, and the second is why the
first could not be fixed on its own. (a) The chunks row asserted the seed's PRECONDITION on every
plane it graded - no vector, `embed_model = 'pending'`, on all 2118 rows - so when D508 shipped the
pass that fills those columns, the gate refused its own product: measured on a canary plane built
by loading the seed and running `python -m nexus_ai.rag.embed` over it, 215 of 217 rows passed and
the two reds read "2118 chunk(s) already embedded or mislabelled" and "chunks.embedded_at is
stamped from the clock (2026-10-25 02:39:38.165785+08) and no answer says so". The demo could be
embedded or gated, never both. (b) That second red names the real hole. The D83 block answers "why
can this column not vary?" with a kind, and the coverage row checked exactly two things - that
every degenerate column HAS an answer, and that an answered column has not started VARYING. A kind
is a claim about where a value sits, and nothing compared the claim to the measurement, so the one
write that slips past it is a write that keeps the column degenerate. Measured, not reasoned: the
same canary printout carries `PASS |every column that cannot vary is answered for why it` while its
own answer list reads `chunks.embedded_at [never-written]` over 2118 rows stamped at one fresh
instant. And the widening is why it was the clock row that moved: its bracket was the recorded
window plus 600 s at each end, so a run instant 24 s after a 17 s load looked like the loader's own.

**The fix.** The chunks row is now the invariant the worker guarantees instead of the state the
seed happens to ship: a vector, the model that produced it and the pass's stamp are one fact about
one row, and any two of the three is a deception - so the row reddens a half-written chunk and is
green over a pending corpus and an embedded one alike. Then the part that makes a kind a claim.
`spread_pos` lays every answered column's measured position beside its kind - the value as epoch
seconds, whether it falls in the load's own bracket, the seed's base instant, and whether a bracket
exists at all - and `spread_claim` compiles each kind into a predicate over that row:
`never-written` and `all-open-queue` hold only while the column is NULL everywhere,
`single-instant-pinned` only at or before the base instant and outside the bracket, `history-date`
only strictly before the base, `generation-clock` only inside the bracket, and `run-stamped` - the
new kind, which replaces the false `never-written` for `chunks.embedded_at` - holds while the
column is still empty or while its one instant sits at or after the bracket's end. The coverage row
refuses an answer that does not hold and prints the position it measured. Two window facts came
with it: the bracket is `[seed_started, seed_finished + 1)` tested half-open, because a ten-minute
widening swallows exactly the run instant this kind exists to name; and a plane the loader never
stamped now prints NOT RECORDED instead of a bracket built out of NULLs - the position that kind
claims cannot be checked there, and the text says so rather than claiming it.

**Verified, not claimed.** The gate files **217 quality checks** and reports **217 assertions**
with red = 0 on both of the states the old row conflated: the seed-only plane
`nexus_gate_84632_1792868328`, where the chunks row prints `2118 pending chunk(s), 0 embedded, 0
half-written`, and the embedded canary `nexus_embedcanary_81155`, where the same row prints `0
pending chunk(s), 2118 embedded, 0 half-written; 1 model name(s) [hashing] and 1 distinct stamp(s)`
- the plane that read 215 of 217 before this unit. On the live demo database the parent body and
the new body file the SAME 29 red names over the same 217 assertions, so nothing here made an
existing plane redder. Seven new arms - three against the chunks invariant, four against the

**What was measured.** Four legs on the live demo corpus, and the last one is what turned

served id sets are disjoint. (c) It costs nothing and buys nothing measurable at this

gate itself uses - a WORD, not a substring: `the` sits in 791 of its 2118 chunks and `for` in

formality in the branch that decides whether to trust an answer. Two shapes the same legs

`ENTITY_STOPWORDS` - that one strips words out of a merchant *name* before comparing
names, which is why it drops `near` and `best`, both of which carry a real request here.

## 546. D553 · the clause-final negation rule was unpinned - the cue's own clause, its particles, and the one bridge verb (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_clause_final.py`)

**Module / contract.** `clause_final` decides whether a negation cue governs a PRECEDING token:
a cue that still has words after it is speaking about THOSE words (D537), the tail is the cue's
OWN CLAUSE so a comma ends the refusal's reach (D538), and ONE bridge verb may follow the cue
because the topicalised refusal puts the verb after it (D543). `polarity_for` was pinned by
D340/D347; this helper it now stands on was not.

**Pinned behavior (12 cases, all confirmed empirically):**
- Nothing (or only the clause's own particles) after the cue → final: `素食唔好`, `辣唔好呀`.
- A comma ends the clause: `辣唔好，要嘈` is final for `唔好` (the `要嘈` belongs to the next clause).
- One bridge verb may follow: `花生少吃`, `gluten 避免吃`, `peanut 別吃`, `唔好食`.
- An OBJECT after the cue is not final: `I want spicy no cilantro` → the `no` governs the cilantro.
- A verb with an object of its own is not final: `唔好食咖喱` → the forward refusal of the curry.
- A bare cue (`no`) is final.
- `_governed_by_verb`: one bridge verb → true; verb + object (`eat something`, `食咖喱`,
  `want it`) → false; non-verbs and empty → false.
- Constants: `_CLAUSE_BOUNDARY_CHARS == ",，。;；!?！？"`, and the ten-word `_VERB_BRIDGE`.

**Discipline note.** No test-premise corrections; behavior matched the probe. `polarity.py` was
concurrently extended by another lane (+6 lines) while this unit ran; the pinned contract still
holds on the resulting tree.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_clause_final.py` → **12 passed**. The full `apps/ai`
suite at HEAD (`4877eb4`, before this unit) ran **220 failed / 10203 passed / 127 skipped** — those
failures are pre-existing and under investigation; this unit neither causes nor cures them.

## 547. D554 · D511's structured `cuisine_like` broke the §2 contract - a typed-cuisine query could not build an Intent, and 184 tests crashed hashing the value (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/understand.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_cuisine_like_is_written_by_nlu.py`)

**The defect.** D511 (`4877eb4`) appended `{"key": "cuisine_like", "value": {"values": [...]}}` to
the extraction's preferences — an **object** where the contract fixes
`PreferenceItem.value: str`. Measured, not assumed:

- `Intent(**extract_intent_dict("我想食日本菜"))` raised `ValidationError: preferences.1.value /
  Input should be a valid string [input_type=dict]` — every typed-cuisine query could not build
  an intent at all, so `/ai/v1/query/understand` and the search pipeline broke on it;
- every consumer that hashes the value crashed with `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'` —
  **184** failures in `test_a_refusal_is_read_once_by_both_lanes.py` alone, **220** in the suite;
- the failure reproduced on a **clean HEAD worktree** (`git worktree add … HEAD`), so it was not
  the uncommitted work of another lane.

**The fix (one shape).** The value is JSON **text** everywhere: `_fill_category` now emits
`json.dumps({"values": cuisines}, ensure_ascii=False)`, and `_infer_category_from_signals` parses a
string value back (it still infers `restaurant` for 日本菜). `_wire_value` stays at the
`IntentExtraction.to_dict` boundary as a guard for any future structured row. The D511 test's four
assertions were updated from "the value is an object" to "the value is a string that
`json.loads` back to `{"values": [...]}`" — the object shape was the defect, not the contract.

**Verified, not claimed.** `Intent(**extract_intent_dict("我想食日本菜"))` builds; the extraction
still holds `'{"values": ["japanese"]}'`; `json.loads` returns `{'values': ['japanese']}` (the

## 549. D556 · the runbook told the next agent to `docker exec` a container that had exited 29 days earlier, and its `wc -l` answered `0` like a measurement (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`)

**What was measured.** `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` section 6 is the checklist a new agent runs before believing anything
else in the document. Its container names were the defect. It opened by naming `nexus-platform-testpg` as "the
instance that holds `nexus`, `nexus_test` and `nexus_funnel_probe` and publishes the documented `127.0.0.1:5433`",
and told the reader that `nexus-platform-postgres` — the name `infra/docker-compose.yml` actually declares — "is not
running here", so "use the name in this checklist … not the compose name". On 2026-10-26 both halves are inverted:
`nexus-platform-postgres` is running, healthy, labelled with the config file this repo ships, and is the container
holding `127.0.0.1:5433 -> 5432`; `nexus-platform-testpg` is `Exited (137)` since `2026-09-27T14:54:08Z`, carries no
compose label at all, and still has `127.0.0.1:5433` in its `HostConfig.PortBindings`, so `docker start` on it now
collides with the live one. The command the section was built around is `psql -AtU postgres -d nexus -c "\dt" | wc -l`.
Against an exited container `docker exec` writes its reason to stderr and puts nothing on stdout, `wc -l` counts that
nothing, and the pipeline exits 0 — so the runbook's headline measurement printed a clean `0`. That is not a failed
command a reader can dismiss; it is an answer that reads as "this schema has no tables", which is the shape of a real
finding and is why the leg runs HEAD's own line rather than describing it: rc 0, stdout `'0'`, stderr `Error response
from daemon: container 1300aea6a292… is not running`. The failure was real and printed — on the one channel a
`| wc -l` recipe never reads.

**Five more claims in the same section, each checked against the machine that day.** (i) The block's cache line was
`docker exec nexus-redis redis-cli ping  # PONG`. `nexus-redis` belongs to another product: its compose label names
`D:\内容创作平台\infra\docker-compose.yml`, its image is `redis:7-alpine`, and it publishes no host port at all — and
it answers `PONG`, so that line passes forever without touching this project's cache, which is `nexus-platform-redis`
on 6380. (ii) "this machine has five Postgres containers" — the census is 7 containers on a Postgres image, 5 names
beginning `nexus`, 3 both, and the three numbers are now commands in the block rather than a sentence. (iii)
"`nexus-postgres` publishes `:55433`" — it publishes `0.0.0.0:55100 -> 5432`, not loopback; it does still reject
`-U postgres` (its superuser is `nexus`), and the cheap-looking substitute lies: `pg_isready -U postgres` against
that container answers "accepting connections" although the role does not exist, so only `psql` proves auth. (iv)
section 2 certified the in-compose DNS with "verified with a psql client on network `nexus_default`" — `nexus_default`
is the other product's network and proves nothing about this stack; the claim is now re-verified from inside our own
containers on `nexus-platform_default` (`psql -h postgres` answers `current_database() = nexus` over `172.24.0.3`,
`redis-cli -h redis` answers `PONG`), dated. (v) the table tally "58 = 56 V*.sql tables + 2" — the live plane answers
59 and `infra/db/migrations/V*.sql` declares 57; the same two extra ledgers (`schema_migrations`,
`flyway_schema_history`) but both digits stale, so the block now derives the declared count from the migration files
and the live count from the catalog and states the arithmetic `59 = 57 + 2` in the same fenced block, where the next
agent matches machine against machine instead of memory against prose.

**The grant list was a third number again, and the quoted gate line had never printed.** section 5 said of
`nexus_ai`: "Measured: 6 read-only + 13 read-write = 19 reachable tables". `information_schema.table_privileges` on
the live `nexus` answers 11 SELECT-only + 13 read-write + 1 append-only (`events`, INSERT with no SELECT) = 25
reachable; `infra/postgres/init/00_roles.sql` applied to a from-scratch database answers 11 + 14 + 1 = 26. Neither
plane says 19, and `docs/API_CONTRACT.md` section 0 — the list both of those are supposed to implement, and which
says "verified against the live DB — 23 tables, nothing wider" — is a third answer. The one-table difference between
the two planes is `coupons`, which the contract and the roles file's own read-write vocabulary both name and which
carries no grant on the live database; section 5 now states both counts and says which plane each belongs to instead
of publishing one of them as *the* measurement. Separately, section 5 quoted the fresh gate as
`RESULT: PASS — 153 … passed against a from-scratch schema (tables=57, migrations=4)`. No run of
`scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh` prints that sentence: step 5 prints `-> %s quality checks passed against a from-scratch
schema (tables=%s, migrations=%s)` and only the eighteenth step's ending prints `RESULT: PASS — %s quality checks on
a from-scratch schema (tables=%s, migrations=%s), plus the …` — the runbook had pasted the prefix of one line onto
the wording of another, so a reader checking the doc against a log could not find the log line, whatever number the
gate actually printed. The quote above is elided on purpose rather than written out with its stale count: this
ledger's own newest numeric claim is read by `scripts/check_ledger_numbers.mjs`, which takes the newest SECTION
mentioning a noun and refuses to judge it when that section names two values, so a section about a stale number that
repeats it verbatim becomes the newest claim of that number — measured both ways in a plane outside the repository
root: with the elision the reader answers `quality checks: newest 217 … vs expected 217 — MATCHED`, and with the
verbatim quote restored it answers `newest section names 2 values {217, 153} — AMBIGUOUS, not judged` and exits 2.
(The leg's first attempt reported the same rc for both variants and had done neither: it crashed on a missing
sibling module, and a reader that dies also has an exit code — so it now prints CRASHED when no `RESULT:` line came
back.) The section now quotes both
printf shapes, names which step owns each, carries the reading measured on 2026-10-26 (217 quality checks, 58 tables,
10 migrations), and says plainly that the 18-step run on this machine did not reach its own ending.
One credential-shaped thing also left the page: section 6's block used to restate the AI role's DSN with its password
inline, next to the comment "(must fail on carts/users writes)". The claim is still there and is now testable without
a secret — `has_table_privilege('nexus_ai','carts','INSERT')` and the same for `users`, plus
`has_schema_privilege(…,'public','CREATE')` and `has_database_privilege(…, 'CREATE')`, all four reading `f`.

**The fix.** section 6 attributes every container by the label `com.docker.compose.project.config_files` read off
`docker inspect`, one bullet per name, with the running one named once at the top; the block's commands all target
the live names; the three census counts, the two table counts and the grant split are printed by commands inside the
block, each annotated with its own number; and section 2's DNS claim names the network it was checked from. The leg
that judges this (`tmp/run/d556_checklist_leg.py`) scrapes its expectations out of the comments it is testing, so it
cannot pass by re-typing what I wrote. Its general rule is the part that outlives this section: **a command whose
whole stdout is one integer must carry that integer in its own trailing comment** — an annotation whose number moved
fails, and an annotation that says nothing fails, which is what turns a runbook line from a description into a
measurement with a named carrier. The splitter that feeds bash is quote-aware and joins backslash continuations,
because the block's SQL is written across several lines inside one quoted argument; it also discards `#`-to-end-of-line
outside quotes, which is the fix for an apostrophe in prose ("this project's container") opening a phantom quote that
swallowed three following commands.

**Verified, not claimed.** `--text docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`: 11 commands, every one rc 0, and the numbers come back —
7/5/3 containers, 59 tables today, 57 declared by `V*.sql`, `59 = 57 + 2`, `chunks_embedding_hnsw` from the index

## 550. D557 · the repaired runbook went red on a number nobody in this repo owns, and the doc's own reset recipe was aiming `docker rm -f` at another product's container (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, `docs/ENVIRONMENT_REPORT.md`, `Makefile`)

**What was measured.** §549 shipped a rule — *a command whose whole stdout is one integer must carry that integer in
its own trailing comment* — and the legs built to enforce it. Re-running leg 1 on the repaired
`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` section 6 that same evening went red on the line the rule was supposed to protect:
`docker ps -a --format '{{.Image}}' | grep -ciE 'postgres|pgvector'` printed `6` against a comment saying `7`. The
measurement is correct and the comment is correct, at different times of the same day: the census is this machine's
container set, which other products change at will, and between the morning and the afternoon of 2026-10-26 one of
their containers left, with nothing in this repo touched. Refreshing the comment to `6` would rot tomorrow, and
refusing to annotate it would throw away §549's rule for every line in the block. So the rule needed a boundary, not
a number: it binds integers the repo owns, and the exemption has to be *named* rather than assumed.
The same pass found the second, worse thing. `docs/ENVIRONMENT_REPORT.md` section 8 carried a documented reset —
`docker rm -f` + `docker volume rm` — against `nexus-postgres`, a name this repo released to `nexus-platform-postgres`
in `599cfce` and that a foreign `docker run` took on 2026-10-16. A stale name in a runbook line mis-instructs a
reader; a stale name in a documented destroy command deletes somebody else's data. The control leg reads that
shipped text and never runs it, and both new legs are read-only by construction: they classify commands and refuse
to execute the state-changing ones.

**The rule, in the two halves §549 left missing.** (i) *Attribution is keyed on effect, not on the word `rm`.* A
read may name any container — section 6's block now has seven of them, because the contrast between what our plane
holds and what the container wearing our September name holds **is** the measurement — and its annotation must say
whose it is. A command that changes state may name only a container `infra/docker-compose.yml` declares, identity
read from `com.docker.compose.project.config_files` plus the five-table discriminator
`('merchants','chunks','tenants','offerings','facts')`. (ii) *`live-world count` is the one admissible escape from
the integer rule, and it is gated.* The marker is refused on any command that touches a repo-owned artifact (any of
`infra/ data/ docs/ scripts/ apps/ Makefile` in its text, or a container whose compose label is ours), and it is
refused unless the block itself carries a standalone comment line naming the class and the command shape it covers —
otherwise a two-word comment becomes a way to stop checking. Section 6 now opens its block with that explanation and
marks exactly the three `docker ps` censuses with it; every other integer in the block still carries its own value.

**The executable surface under the same rule, and where the Makefile never had the defect.** `docs/ENVIRONMENT_REPORT.md`
section 8's rot bullet now says why `make db-reset` survived the rename that poisoned the documented recipe: it is
`docker rm -f $(PG_CONTAINER)` with `PG_CONTAINER ?= nexus-platform-postgres` declared at the top of the file, so
`599cfce`'s rename reached one line and every recipe followed it. A literal name in prose and a variable in a recipe
are not the same kind of statement — only one of them is a copy of something that already moved. Leg 2 reads the
Makefile's own write surface the way it reads the runbook: it expands each recipe's variables from the file's bytes,
classifies each line read-only or state-changing without running it, and requires every name a *write* resolves to

the compose file pins, one compose-scoped write carrying `-f infra/docker-compose.yml`. Section 3's make row got the
