## 555. D558 · the evidence pack certified a home page whose card artwork never appeared, because its opacity marker read inline styles and the hide was a class (`packages/ui/src/trust/Renderers.tsx`, `apps/web/scripts/collect-evidence.mjs`, `tests/e2e/specs/consumer/card-media.spec.ts`)

**What was measured.** The pack answered `5/5 surfaces captured`, `rendered_opaque: true`,
`broken_images: []` for every surface, and the screenshots it writes are what this lane reads to decide
what a consumer sees. `01-home.png` showed the rails' names, prices and badges over a grey block where
each card's artwork should be: 28 card images, 28 placeholders that never lifted. `CardMedia` paints its
`<img>` at `opacity-0` and moves it to `opacity-100` from React's `onLoad`. On a server-rendered page the
browser has usually fetched and decoded the tiny local SVG before hydration attaches the handler, and a
load event that already fired never fires again — so `loaded` stays false for the life of the page. This
is the stranded-opacity family STATUS §450 named for `Reveal` — same shape, the thing that lifts the opacity
never runs; different cause, a load that predates its handler rather than a preference the markup
ignored. The split by population, read off the live dev plane before anything changed: home 28/28 images
`complete` with computed opacity 0, cold and warm, at 3 s and at 8 s; a merchant detail page 12/12 the
same; the streamed search surface 8/8 opaque. Same component, two outcomes — the search results are
client-rendered, so React creates those elements with the handler already attached. That difference is
why the search case is the witness's control rather than a fourth thing to fix.

**The fix.** A ref callback runs on every mount, so it reads the completion the event missed:
`node.complete && node.naturalWidth > 0`. The second term keeps `onLoad`'s success-only contract — a
failed image still keeps its skeleton, exactly as before — so the fix cannot turn a broken URL into a
visible frame. Nothing else in the tree reads `onLoad`, and the three call sites that render artwork
(`EntityCard`, `merchant-view`, `offering-view`) all reach it through this one component, so the repair
is not per-surface.

**The second finding: the pack could not see the class it was certifying.** `rendered_opaque` comes from
`settled()`, which waits on `[style*="opacity"]` — elements carrying an **inline** opacity. `CardMedia`
hides with a Tailwind **class**, so the marker's population never contained the artwork and its `true`
was read as a verdict about the page. STATUS §450 had already written that sentence — "visibility is a layout
fact and opacity is a paint fact; which is also why the pack captured a blank hero" — and left the pack
unchanged. It is changed now: the manifest carries `artwork_invisible`, every decoded, on-screen `<img>`
still under `0.99` opacity after a 15-second deadline, named by src, and a non-empty residue fails the
surface the way `broken_images` already does. `settled()`'s comment now states its own population
instead of letting the key's name over-claim; the key itself keeps its spelling because no reader in the
tree opens the manifest — the collector writes it and nothing consumes it. The same file carried a
dead binding that predates this unit — `const home = await snap({ … })`, whose value no later line reads
(the summary works off `pages`) — and `npm run lint:web` answers it with one error and exit 1. It is removed here rather than left for the next author to meet as a pre-existing red: a
collector that cannot be linted cleanly is a collector nobody re-runs.

**Verified, not claimed.** Two arms, both against the running dev plane, both splicing the same three
lines (the ref callback's body becomes `void node;`) and restoring from a byte capture rather than
`git checkout`, because the fix is uncommitted work in a shared tree.
`tmp/run/d558_arms.py` drives the witness: arm open → 2 failed / 1 passed, home charging `28/28 of home's
card images are loaded and still invisible` and merchant charging 7/7, with the streamed search control
green; arm shut → 3 passed; restored bytes equal capture. The merchant count is 7/7 there and 12/12 in
the pack because the spec follows the home page's first merchant link rather than pinning a seeded slug,
and the collector reaches the merchant the search returned — neither number is a fixture, so each carrier
prints its own.
`tmp/run/d558_evidence_arm.py` drives the pack: arm open → `FAIL home … artwork loaded but stayed
invisible (28)` and `FAIL merchant … (12)`, while search and both consoles still capture; arm shut →
5/5 captured with every residue empty. The pack then regenerated on the fixed bytes, and `01-home.png`
now shows the artwork.

**Two readings that were harness noise, not verdicts.** The first arm run reported FAIL for a reason of
my own making: two `open()` calls, each with a 15-second settle, do not fit Playwright's 30-second
default, and every failure text was `page.waitForTimeout: Target page, context or browser has been
closed`. A timeout that arrives before the assertion is not evidence about the assertion, so the three
tests now carry `test.slow()` and the red that arrives is the charge. The same file's `networkidle`
waits never resolve against `next dev` — the HMR socket keeps the network busy — which is why `open()`
waits on the surface's own card hook plus a deadline instead. Both traps are recorded in the spec's own
comments, because the next author of a browser test here will reach for the same two idioms.

**Left open.** With JavaScript disabled the artwork still never appears: the component's start state is
invisible and only a script lifts it, which is the boundary STATUS §450 closed for `Reveal` in CSS and this
unit does not close here — the demo's whole flow needs JS anyway, so it is disclosed rather than
repaired. Task #211: the suite's `mobile` project is `devices['iPhone 13']`, which is WebKit, while
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs `--with-deps chromium` and this machine's `webkit-2359` download
times out twice — so all 12 mobile reds in `specs/consumer` read
`browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist`, in both environments, and the phone-size verdict had to
come from a Chromium probe at 390×844 instead (home 28 images, 28 decoded, 0 invisible; search 8/8;
`/m/silver-table-0147` 7/0). Task #212: that harness sets `locale: 'zh-HK'` while the page renders its
rail labels in Simplified, which is why `vertical-slice` waits for `附近熱門` and finds nothing — that
spec on desktop is 7 failed / 1 passed focused and 6 failed in the combined run, so its count moves and
none of its reasons are about artwork. Task #210, from the same harness: `playwright.config.ts` and
`lib/fixture.ts` resolve their URLs to `:3000`/`:8080`/`:8000` while the Makefile declares
`3002`/`8090`/`8010` and `make e2e` exports none of them — CI boots its own stack on the defaults, so
the defaults are a second copy of a coordinate the Makefile owns, and on this machine they point at
another product's frontend. #207, #208, #203, #204, #205, #196 and #195 stand as filed.

- readers: the witness green on the bytes this section describes (3 passed, desktop) and `npm run lint:web` at 0 errors · step 8 0 strict offenders on the working-copy plane · step 9 0 offenders, with no citation total quoted because that count moves with other lanes' uncommitted comments in the same tree · step 10 every committed heading still on disk, duplicate 0, uncommitted 1 (this section) · step 12 every spelled `STATUS §NN` in the tree resolves, this section's three among them · the line-ending census PASS with mixed 0, this section uniform LF like the section it follows · step 15 103 of 179 line citations still name the line they were written against, strict=none, and every MOVED and NOT-UNIQUE site lies outside this section · step 17 census-only, no `--expect`, because no fresh 18-step gate was filed in this unit: the database-backed steps were not re-run here, and the figures above come from the readers this change can actually reach

## 556. D559 · the from-scratch gate was aborted by its own CLEANUP - the host's safe-delete shim refused a `C:\…` temp path at three EXIT traps (`data/seed/load.sh`, `scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh`, `scripts/seed_truncate_probe.sh`)

**The defect.** D552 fixed the gate's step 2 (migrations ran V10 before V1). With that fixed, the
gate reached step 4 and stopped — not on a data check, but on a **cleanup**. `mktemp` on this host
returns a `C:\…` path, and the node runtime's safe-delete shim refuses to `rm` it. Under `set -e`
(and the gate's `pipefail`) a refused `rm` in an EXIT trap turns a **successful** step into a
non-zero exit, so the run died with no failing assertion anywhere:

- `data/seed/load.sh`: `cleanup() { rm -f "$stream"; }` on an EXIT trap — the seed load finished
  (facts 5688, chunks 2118) and then exited non-zero, aborting the gate after step 4;
- `scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh`: the step-5 `trap 'rm -f "$GATE_OUT" …'` could fail at exit and
  corrupt the gate's own exit code;
- `scripts/seed_truncate_probe.sh`: two traps (`REFUSE_OUT`, `CLEAR_OUT`) — step 6 passed its four
  arms and then died on the cleanup line.

**The fix.** Every one of those cleanups is now `rm -f … 2>/dev/null || true`. A cleanup is not a
check: it must never be able to fail a step that succeeded, and it must never hide a real failure
behind a shim's refusal.

**Evidence (the run with the first two fixed).** step 2: V1→V10 in order, tables=58, migrations=10 ·
step 3: generate PASS (FK integrity, bounds, naming, density, language mix) · step 4: seed loaded
(facts 5688, chunks 2118, reviews 11000, availability_slots 32492) · step 5: **217 quality checks
passed** and the ledger's newest claim MATCHED · step 6: truncate probe PASS (the empty stranger is
cleared, the one holding rows refuses by name, and the refusal costs nothing). The run stopped at
the probe's own cleanup `rm` — exactly the third fix above.

**Full 18-step run pending.** Docker Desktop went down again before the third fix could be exercised
end-to-end; the next unit with the daemon up runs `bash scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh` to completion.

**Suite state.** The `apps/ai` suite ran to 100% with **0 FAILED** (`grep -c '^FAILED'` = 0) across
10550 collected tests; pytest's non-zero exit came from its **tmp_path cleanup** being refused by
the same shim (`SAFE_DELETE_BULK_CONFIRM_REQUIRED`), not from a test. Run it with
`--basetemp` on a relative path to get a clean exit code.

**The same pattern outside the gate.** `scripts/db_schema_drift.sh` (`mktemp -d` + `rm -rf` in its
EXIT trap) and `scripts/check_launcher_log_mode.sh` (`mktemp -d` + `rm -f "$root/…"` in its
cleanup) carried the identical defect. Neither is called by the 18-step gate, but both are CI
scripts that would fail on this host for the same reason, so both cleanups are tolerant now.

## 557. D561 · the party-size reader's normalisation step was unpinned - the counter-only rewrite, and the canonicalise-first guarantee that makes Simplified input work (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/understand.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_party_text.py`)

**Module / contract.** `party_size_of` is pinned by the party-size tests; this unit pins the helper
it stands on: `party_text` rewrites a Chinese numeral to a digit **only when a party counter
follows it** (`_PARTY_MARKERS` = 個/位/人). The numeral table holds only the Traditional spellings
(D435: one spelling per character), so Simplified input works **only because the pipeline
canonicalises before it matches** — and that guarantee had no end-to-end row.

**Pinned behavior (13 cases, all confirmed empirically):**
- A numeral before a counter becomes a digit (`三個人` → `3個人`, `二人` → `2人`, `十三個人` →
  `13個人`); an Arabic digit is left alone; the rest of the sentence is untouched
  (`三個人食飯` → `3個人食飯`).
- A numeral with no counter after it is left alone: `星期三` stays a weekday, and a numeral before a non-counter (the hour marker) stays put.
  The rule is the **following** character, not the word before it (`星期三人` → `星期3人`).
- Empty → empty; the marker set is exactly the three counters.
- **Canonicalise-first, end to end:** `extract_intent("四个人").party_size == 4` and
  `extract_intent("两位").party_size == 2` — Simplified input is read even though the table has no
  `两`/`个` — while `四個人` → 4 and `2位` → 2 agree, and a turn naming no party → `None`.

**Discipline note.** A direct `party_size_of("四个人")` returns `None`, which looked like a
Simplified-input gap; the real pipeline canonicalises first and returns 4. The probe was wrong, not
the product — and the test now pins the pipeline's guarantee so the distinction cannot be lost.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_party_text.py` → **13 passed**.

## 558. D562 · the two response helpers were only covered through TestClient - the degraded HEADER and the §1 error envelope (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/degraded.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/errors.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_response_helpers.py`)

## 559. D563 · the distance expression was unpinned - the float8 casts and the clamp that keeps `acos` in its domain (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/sql.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_haversine_expr.py`)

**Module / contract.** `haversine_expr` returns a SQL string the query builder splices in, so its
shape IS the contract: every parameter and column is cast to `float8` (asyncpg will not infer a
numeric type for `radians`), the cosine is clamped to `[-1, 1]` **before** `acos` (rounding can push
it just outside the domain and turn a whole page into an error), and the result is cast back to
`float8`.

**Pinned behavior (8 cases, all confirmed empirically):**
- `EARTH_RADIUS_M == 6371008.8`.
- Every placeholder/column is `::float8` (`radians($1::float8)`, `radians(m.lat::float8)`, …), and
  other column names are threaded through (`o.lat`/`o.lng` replace `m.` entirely).
- The clamp `greatest(-1.0, least(1.0, …))` is present; the expression starts
  `(6371008.8 * acos(` and ends `::float8`.
- Each placeholder appears the expected number of times (`$1` twice for cos/sin, `$2` once), and
  both the cosine and sine terms are present.

**Discipline note.** No test-premise corrections; behavior matched the probe. Code unchanged.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_haversine_expr.py` → **8 passed**.

## 561. D565 · the provider pool factory was unpinned - the configured-first/mock-last order, the cache, and the degrade that keeps the product serving (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/models/factory.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_factory_pool.py`)

  (`["anthropic", "mock"]`, `["openai", "mock"]`).

  object); a different provider is a different object.
- An anthropic pool with an **empty key** degrades to `["mock"]` — a misconfigured live provider
  never stops the product.
- `get_router` returns a `ModelRouter` carrying the pool's adapters and the settings'
  `max_llm_calls` (7); `get_adapter` is the first of the pool.

**Discipline note.** The probe first read `router.providers` (0); the attribute is `adapters`.

## 562. D566 · the SSE serializer's two bottom pieces were unpinned - compact JSON and the async byte encoder (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/sse.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_sse_bytes.py`)

**Module / contract.** `test_sse.py` pins `sse_frame` / `parse_frames` /
`assert_canonical_stream` / `plain`; this unit pins the two underneath: `json_compact` (compact
separators, no ASCII escaping, insertion order preserved — the browser forwards upstream bytes
verbatim) and `sse_bytes` (one UTF-8 frame per event, in order; a non-canonical name raises **at
iteration time**).

**Pinned behavior (8 cases, all confirmed empirically):**
- `json_compact` → `{"a":1,"b":2}` (no spaces); `{"a":"中"}` keeps the CJK unescaped; insertion
  order survives (`{"b":1,"a":2}`); nested structures are compact too.
- `sse_bytes` yields exactly `b'event: status\ndata: {"stage":"searching"}\n\n'` and
  `b'event: done\ndata: {"agent_run_id":"r1"}\n\n'`, in order; a CJK payload is UTF-8 bytes, not
  `\u` escapes; an empty iterator yields nothing; `("bogus", {})` raises `NonCanonicalEvent` when
  the stream is consumed (not at construction).

**Discipline note.** No test-premise corrections; behavior matched the probe. Code unchanged.

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_sse_bytes.py` → **8 passed**.

## 563. D567 · the jsonb-reads falsifier held 3 of 38 arms only because its FIXTURES were stale - the checker was right all along (`scripts/falsify_quality_seam.mjs`, gate step 7)

**What the gate said.** With D552/D559 fixed, `db_gate_fresh.sh` ran through steps 1-6 (migrations
V1→V10, generate PASS, seed loaded, **217 quality checks PASS** + ledger MATCHED, truncate probe

`falsify_quality_seam.mjs` over `check_jsonb_reads.mjs`.

- **Arm "a default root still reaches every declared read"** narrowed to ONE root
  (`services/platform/src/main/java`) and required every declared read to stay reachable. The plane
  now also carries a read in `apps/ai` (`offerings.attributes.allergens`), so narrowing to one root
  **must** miss it — and that is the CORRECT behaviour, already tested by the `--roots=scripts` arm
  (rc 1 with `outside-the-census-roots`). The arm pinned a premise the plane has outgrown, so it is
  **retired** (38 → 37 arms). Historical "38 of 38" claims stand as written; this section supersedes
  the count.
- **Arm "a root that opens files and finds no read is refused"** pointed at `apps/ai/nexus_ai`, which
  now holds **3** jsonb reads (it held none when the arm was written). Re-pointed at
  `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api` — measured: **16 files opened, 0 jsonb reads** — which is exactly what the
  arm needs.
- **Arm "a kind no row carries reddens"** re-filed ONE `reachable` row; the plane now has **two**
  (the platform row and the `apps/ai` read of `offerings.attributes.allergens`), so the branch was
  not emptied. It now re-files **both** via `plantMany`.

**The checker was correct throughout.** Manually re-filing both rows made it print
`ANSWER KINDS UNUSED (1)`, `1 classify no row on this plane (reachable)` and
`REPORT COMPLETE — 1 reason(s) to redden, this run exits 1` — the behaviour the arm expects.

## 564. D568 · the console-a11y falsifier called `rmSync` without importing it - gate step 14 died on a ReferenceError, not on a red arm (`scripts/falsify_console_a11y.mjs`)

**What the gate said.** With step 7 fixed (D567), the full 18-step run passed steps 1-13 and reached
step 14. `check_console_a11y.mjs` itself printed **PASS** (landmarks, names, focus rings, and every
printed contrast ratio), and then the step died with:

```
ReferenceError: rmSync is not defined
    at Object.apply (scripts/falsify_console_a11y.mjs:171:19)
```

**The defect.** The module imports `copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync,
statSync, writeFileSync` from `node:fs` — and **not `rmSync`** — while three arms use it (the README
removal at :171 and the two console-page trees at :185-186). A falsifier that throws is not a missed
arm: the step cannot tell "the checker is right" from "the harness is broken", which is exactly the
distinction these arms exist to make.

**The fix.** All three calls use `safeRemove` (already imported from `spawn_guard.mjs`), which also
handles this host's safe-delete shim: a bulk recursive `rmSync` is refused, so `safeRemove` unlinks
in batches and then removes the empty directories. The arm's meaning is unchanged — it still removes
the README / the console page trees and still requires the checker to redden for that reason.

**Verified, not claimed.** `node scripts/falsify_console_a11y.mjs` → **RESULT: PASS — 13 arms · 13
held · 0 missed** (fixture root `nexus-d186-falsify`).

## 565. D569 · the line-citation re-aimer had TWO defects of its own - it could not read a `yml` row, and it lost every rewrite but the last per file (`scripts/apply_line_cite_reaim.mjs`)

**What the gate said.** With steps 1-15 passing, the 18-step run stopped at step 16:
`RESULT: FAIL — --strict MOVED,NOT-UNIQUE on MOVED 72 + NOT-UNIQUE 3 of 179 judged citation(s)`.
The project ships `scripts/apply_line_cite_reaim.mjs` for exactly this; it did not work.

**Defect 1 - the applier's grammar was narrower than the reader's.** Its `CITE` regex accepted
`mjs|py|sh|java|ts|tsx|json|sql` while the drift reader also judges `js`, `yml` and `yaml` (its own
census prints that difference). The three `.github/workflows/ci.yml` rows were therefore refused
forever: `no citation to … on that line`. Fixed by adding the three extensions.

**Defect 2 - a lost update.** `planJobs` grouped rows by **site** (`ledger:line`), read the whole
ledger once per site, and wrote it once per site. With 70 sites in two files, every write after the
first restored the file as it was read, so only the **last** site's rewrite survived: measured,
`RESULT: APPLIED — 72 site line(s) rewritten` while `git diff --stat` showed **2 lines changed**.
Fixed by grouping by **file**: one read, all its rows applied, one write.

**The result.** `node scripts/check_line_cite_drift.mjs --reaim` now produces 70 rows, all validated;
after `--apply`, `git diff --stat` shows **71 insertions / 71 deletions** across the two ledgers and
the strict reader reports **MOVED 0**. `--selftest` → **PASS — 13 case(s), 0 mismatch(es)**.

**What is left, named.** Step 16 still reddens on **NOT-UNIQUE 3** - citations whose quoted text
occurs on more than one line, so no tool can choose: `docs/STATUS.md:4421 -> data/seed/load.sh:161`
(2 lines hold `"DO \$\$"`), `docs/STATUS.md:22178 -> search/sql.py:131` (2 lines hold
`wsq = f"websearch_to_tsquery('`), `docs/STATUS.md:23747 -> search/service.py:1072` (3 lines hold
`if attrs.get("outdoor_style")`). Each needs the citing sentence read against the candidates.

## 566. D570 · "don't be noisy" was read as a DISLIKE of quiet - the antonym surface inverted the ranking for 40% of the plane (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`)

**What was measured.** `extract_intent("唔好嘈")` (don't be noisy) produced
`{"key": "ambience", "value": "quiet", "polarity": -1}` — the user asks for quiet and the ranking
lane is told to demote it. On the live corpus `quiet_ambience` is true on **188 of 470** published
merchants, so the inversion reached **40%** of the plane. The constraint lane was right all along
(`noise_avoid: noise`); only the preference was reversed.

**Why the obvious fix does not work.** Removing 嘈 (noisy) from the quiet rule fixes the refusal,
but `有無嘈` (is it noisy?) must still read quiet **+1** — the existential question asks about the
thing (D533) — and the tests pin that. The rule must keep the surface; what must change is what a
**refusal** of it means.

**The fix.** `lexicon.ANTONYM_TERMS` names the surfaces that are the OPPOSITE of a value
(`("ambience","quiet") -> {"嘈"}`), and `apply_polarity` inverts a **-1** on such a surface to
**+1**. `polarity_for` is untouched: it is a pure cue reader and still answers -1, which its own
tests pin. The two layers now say different, correct things:

| turn | quiet preference |
|---|---|
| `唔好嘈` (don't be noisy) | **+1** — wants quiet |
| `唔好安靜` (don't be quiet) | **-1** — refuses quiet (the control) |
| `有無嘈` (is it noisy?) | **+1** — the question (D533) |
| `唔想太嘈` (don't want it too noisy) | **+1** — the phrase |

**Verified, not claimed.** `pytest tests/test_an_antonym_refusal_means_the_value.py` → **8 passed**;
the affected nine files (preference polarity, clause unit, canon spellings, constraint lane, clause
boundary, question-not-refusal, avoid filter, the 184-arm two-lane file) → **930 passed, 1 skipped**;
the vocabulary gate + the new file + three neighbours → **129 passed**.

## 567. D571 · the browser harness resolved its three service URLs to the ports another product owns, and `make e2e` exported none of them (`Makefile`, `tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`, `tests/e2e/lib/fixture.ts`, `tests/e2e/package.json`, `scripts/check_plane_coordinates.mjs`)

**Why this is D571 and not D559.** A concurrent lane landed its own D559–D570 into this ledger while this
unit was being measured, so the number this unit was carrying was taken. The id moved rather than the
content: the measurements below are the same ones, re-read after the ledger moved, and the section
number is derived from the file rather than asserted.

**What was measured.** The harness reads each service coordinate from the environment and falls back to
the framework default: `NEXUS_WEB_URL` → `http://127.0.0.1:3000` (`tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts:6`),
`NEXUS_PLATFORM_URL` → `http://127.0.0.1:8080` and `NEXUS_AI_URL` → `http://127.0.0.1:8000`
(`tests/e2e/lib/fixture.ts:4` and `:5`). The Makefile's own dev plane is `WEB_PORT ?= 3002`,
`PLATFORM_PORT ?= 8090`, `AI_PORT ?= 8010` (`Makefile:20-22`), and the `e2e` recipe exported nothing at
all: it ran `cd tests/e2e && npx playwright test`. So the documented local entry point read the fallback
plane while `make dev-*` had started a different stack — the run was real, it started, it reported a
verdict, and the verdict was about services nobody in this repository had started. The CI job is not
wrong to own those defaults: it boots Spring on 8080, uvicorn on 8000 and Next on 3000 and waits on
all three (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:266-270`), and it exports no `NEXUS_*` either, so CI's fallbacks
are exactly its plane. The defect is that the defaults were the **only** copy the local path could
read. On this machine the three fallback ports belong to a different product: `:3000` answers
`<html lang="en">` with a hashed Next bundle, `:8000` answers `{"detail":"Not Found"}`, and `:8080`
answers `{"success":false,...,"code":"UNAUTHORIZED"}` — none of them ours. Ours answer `lang="zh-HK"`
on `:3002`, a `{"code":"not_found",...,"request_id":...}` on `:8090` and `{"service":"nexus-ai",...}`
on `:8010`. The harness would have driven another product's frontend and reported it as NEXUS.

**The second finding: a fourth copy of the web port, and a promise the file never kept.**
`tests/e2e/package.json`'s `codegen` script hard-coded `playwright codegen http://localhost:3000` — a
fourth copy of the web coordinate, in the one file of the harness with no env guard at all, so no plane
could move it. And the config's docstring promised three things the file did not have: a `webServer`
block ("webServer is opt-in via `NEXUS_E2E_AUTOSTART=1`") that exists in no line of the file, a knob
`NEXUS_E2E_AUTOSTART` that no line of the harness reads, and `make dev-stack` — a target the Makefile
has never declared (24 `^target:` lines read, none of them `dev-stack`). It also told the reader the
stack lived on "platform :8080, ai :8000, web :3000", which is the CI plane, so the local reader was
sent to the wrong plane by the file that explains the harness.

**The fix.** The `e2e` recipe now exports the three URLs, derived from the knobs above rather than
retyped: `NEXUS_WEB_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$(WEB_PORT)`, `NEXUS_PLATFORM_URL=…$(PLATFORM_PORT)`,
`NEXUS_AI_URL=…$(AI_PORT)`. A change to `WEB_PORT` therefore moves the coordinate the harness reads
and the coordinate the harness's own docstring names, together. The config's docstring was rewritten to
say which plane each fallback is — the framework defaults, which is the plane CI builds its own stack
on — and to state plainly that there is no autostart in the file. `package.json`'s `codegen` no longer
names a port at all: `playwright codegen` reads the URL from the config, which reads it from the
environment. `tests/e2e/README.md` now says that `make e2e` exports all three, derived from the
Makefile's own `WEB_PORT` / `PLATFORM_PORT` / `AI_PORT`, so a run through make reads the stack make
started.

**The door.** `scripts/check_plane_coordinates.mjs` reads the Makefile, the CI workflow and the harness
directory as text and holds five rules: **R1** every env-guarded fallback in the harness must be
exported by the `e2e` recipe, and derived from a declared `*_PORT` — a retyped literal does not pass;
**R2** where the CI e2e job exports no variable, the fallback ports and the job's port set must be the
same set; **R3** a URL literal may not be naked, and a line that quotes a variable may not contradict
the code's own default; **R4** a backticked or fenced `make <target>` in the harness must be a declared
target; **R5** a `NEXUS_*` token the harness names must be read on a `process.env` line somewhere in the
population. The door runs in CI before any service exists, because it reads text and starts nothing.

**Verified, not claimed.** Nine arms in `tmp/run/d559_arms.mjs`, each splicing one needle into one
shipped file and restoring from a byte capture rather than `git checkout`: the export removed (3
offenders), the export retyped instead of derived (1), the export derived from an undeclared variable
(1), CI's AI port moved off the harness's set (2), the fourth copy of the web port back in
`package.json` (1), the phantom target back in the config comment (1), the phantom knob back in the
config comment (1), the Makefile's own `WEB_PORT` moved from 3002 to 3012 (0 — a derived coordinate
must stay silent), and the README's row drifting from the code it documents (1). All nine matched the
predicted offender count, and the tree hash was unchanged at rest afterwards
(`fb54c0d4d48e`).

Two behavioural legs, run against the live stack and driven by the shipped recipe rather than a
retyped copy of it (`tmp/run/d559_expand_recipe.mjs` expands the Makefile's own `e2e` body, because
`make` is not installed on this machine). With the export in place: **3 passed** (28.2 s). The first
attempt in that shape was 2 passed / 1 failed — the streamed search surface, whose AI service had
booted seconds earlier — and the second attempt with the services warm was the 3 passed that is quoted
here. With the export removed, so the harness fell back to the defaults: **3 failed**, each on
`toBeVisible` for `article[data-card-type]` — the card the suite is about — and exit 1. That is the
defect in one line: the documented local entry point was red against a stack that was not ours, every
one of those failures read as a NEXUS card defect and none of them was, and the same suite is green
against the stack `make dev-*` started.

The reverse control is the HEAD bytes, extracted to a plane outside the repository
(`D:\获客平台-planes\d559_head`, 42 files) and graded by the same door: **6 offenders, exit 1** — the
three "make e2e exports no …" rows, one naked URL in `package.json`, the `make dev-stack` target and the
`NEXUS_E2E_AUTOSTART` knob. The working copy grades 0 offenders, exit 0. The two planes differ only in
the bytes of this unit, and the door reads both.

**Left open.** The door compares port **sets**, not service↔port pairs, because the workflow text
declares no role for `:3000`/`:8080`/`:8000` — it says so in its own output rather than implying more.
`infra/docker-compose.yml`, `scripts/e2e_fresh.sh` and the `verify_*` scripts carry their own copies of
these coordinates and are outside this population. R4 reads backticks and fenced blocks only, so an
unbackticked `make target` in prose escapes it — a sentence about making sure is not a coordinate. Task
#211: the `mobile` project is `devices['iPhone 13']`, which is WebKit, while CI installs
`--with-deps chromium` alone, so the phone-size verdict still needs a browser the workflow does not
install. Task #212: the harness asks for `locale: 'zh-HK'` while the page answers in Simplified, so
`vertical-slice` waits for `附近熱門` and finds nothing — its reds move for that reason and not for
this one. Task #210 is closed by this unit.

- readers: the door green on the bytes this section describes (0 offenders, exit 0) and the reverse
control red on the HEAD bytes (6 offenders, exit 1) · the arm battery 9 of 9 matched with the tree at
rest `fb54c0d4d48e` · the behavioural legs 3 passed with the export and 3 failed without it · the
reachability reader 15 of 15 first-party readers invoked, 0 unreached, and the new door is one of the
15 · step 8, step 9, step 10, step 12, step 15 and step 16 all exit 0 on this tree, step 10 with

## 568. D572 · the citation reader could not hold the repository's own extensionless build entry point — D571's `Makefile:20-22` was filed FILE NOT FOUND by the index, not by the ledger (`scripts/source_index.mjs`, `scripts/check_ledger_citations.mjs`, `scripts/citation_blank_census.mjs`, `scripts/citation_blank_sites.mjs`, `scripts/falsify_ledger_text.mjs`)

**What was found.** D571 (§567) landed a row that cites the build's own entry point — "the Makefile's own dev
plane is `WEB_PORT ?= 3002`, `PLATFORM_PORT ?= 8090`, `AI_PORT ?= 8010` (`Makefile:20-22`)" — and the commit
that carried it left two gates red on the tree it landed:

- gate step 8 (`check_ledger_citations.mjs`) filed **FILE NOT FOUND** for `Makefile:20-22` — "no indexed file
  has that name or path";
- gate step 16 (`check_line_cite_drift.mjs --strict MOVED,NOT-UNIQUE`) filed **MOVED** for three
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml` cites that D571's own commit had pushed down six lines.

The two have different causes, and the first one is not the ledger's.

**The first red was the reader's, read from the producer rather than inferred.** The file is real, tracked
(`git ls-files Makefile` names it) and holds exactly those three knobs on exactly those lines: `Makefile:20-22`
reads `WEB_PORT ?= 3002`, `AI_PORT ?= 8010`, `PLATFORM_PORT ?= 8090`. The reader's index could not name it.
`LEDGER_EXT` names a file by its extension and `Makefile` has none — while the reader's own grammar admits the
citation anyway, because `isCitation()` takes a capitalised extensionless word for a class stem (the same
grammar that reads `EventsController:63`). So the citation was one the reader had promised to judge and then
could not open. The class that fired was the honest one; the finding was about the index.

**Two ways out, and why neither was taken.** Spelling the cite `./Makefile:20-22` takes the path branch, whose
last segment is not a held file, so the citation would have been dropped from the census rather than judged —
a green that says nothing, which is the D193 chain. Putting a second private copy of the walk predicate inside
one reader repeats D166's failure: two readers of one claim resolving two file sets, which is how one sentence
came to be quoted with three different counts.

**The fix — one list, one predicate, four readers.** `scripts/source_index.mjs` now holds the repository's
extensionless root files (`EXTENSIONLESS`, `scripts/source_index.mjs:114`) and the one predicate that says what
a ledger may cite (`LEDGER_FILE`, `scripts/source_index.mjs:123`): extensioned by `LEDGER_EXT`, one of those
extensionless names, or a dot file the repository owns. The three readers that walk the ledger population point
at it (`scripts/check_ledger_citations.mjs:222`, `scripts/citation_blank_census.mjs:96`,
`scripts/citation_blank_sites.mjs:48`), and so does the falsifier that witnesses the reader's own index
(`scripts/falsify_ledger_text.mjs:766`), which had kept a private copy of the same predicate and would have
counted one file short of the reader's — the root `Makefile` its extension test cannot name.

**The second red was D571's own commit, and the ledger is where it is corrected.** D571 added six lines to

## 569. D573 · the four §8 growth routes answered HTTP 500 in live mode — the platform serves `title` as a localized pair and the web rendered it raw (`apps/web/src/lib/platform-guides.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/data.ts`, `apps/web/app/guides/page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/collections/page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/guides/[slug]/page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/collections/[slug]/page.tsx`)

**What was found, and how.** The D572 live leg widened from the home page to the navigation routes and found
that four of them answered **HTTP 500**: `/guides`, `/collections`, `/guides/sha-tin-date-night` and
`/collections/tai-wai-under-100`. The server said it in one line:

```
Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {en, zh}).
```

The page was not broken by its own markup and not by a missing fixture. It was broken by a field the
platform serves and the web renders without projecting.

**The cause, read from the producer rather than inferred.** `CollectionsController.summary()` is ONE
projection shared by `/api/v1/collections`, `/api/v1/guides`, both detail routes and the draft-create
answer, and it puts a **pair** in `title`
(`services/platform/src/main/java/com/nexus/catalog/CollectionsController.java:217`):

```java
out.put("title", Json.map("en", Json.str(row, "title"), "zh", Json.str(row, "title_zh")));
```

Two columns, one field: `collections.title` and `collections.title_zh`. The contract documents it that
way — "`collections.slug`, `title` (+ `title_zh` for the zh-HK locale)" (`docs/API_CONTRACT.md:397`), inside
`API_CONTRACT §8`'s growth surface. The web's view-model declares `title: string`
(`apps/web/src/lib/types.ts:247` for a collection, `apps/web/src/lib/types.ts:262` for a guide) and the
read cast the payload raw, so the page handed React a map and React refused it. Every growth route in the
navigation was unreachable in live mode, and the two index pages were the ones the nav links to.

**Why the mock plane never showed it.** `DEMO_GUIDES` and `DEMO_COLLECTIONS` are written in the view-model
shape, with plain-string titles. The two planes disagreed about the same field and only one of them was
ever exercised — the same failure as the `body_blocks` defect this module already carries, one layer
down. A green mock run was not evidence about a live run.

**The fix.** The pair is resolved **by the page's locale**, in the one module that already owns the wire →
view-model crossing for this surface (`apps/web/src/lib/platform-guides.ts`):

- `toLocalizedTitle(value, locale)` (`apps/web/src/lib/platform-guides.ts:71`) reads the column the locale
  asks for — `zh-HK` reads `zh`, `en` reads `en` — falls back to the other column when the locale's own is
  absent, and passes a plain string through so the mock plane and any future wire that serves one keep
  working. An absent title answers `''`, never a map.
- `toGuide(payload, locale)` (`apps/web/src/lib/platform-guides.ts:174`) and `toCollection(payload, locale)`
  (`apps/web/src/lib/platform-guides.ts:201`) apply it, and project the fields whose wire type differs from
  the view-model's declared type: `description`, `cover_image` (the wire allows a null `alt`; the
  view-model declares a string, and an empty alt is the honest spelling of "this image carries no alt
  text"), `city` and `category`.
- `toCollection` derives a collection's `items` from the wire's resolved `cards`, not from `items`. The
  detail view serves both, and `items` holds the stored references the author wrote
  (`{subject_type, subject_id, note, card}`) while `cards` holds the same walk with the merchant resolved.
  Rendering the stored array would have produced a grid of references with no title and a `JsonLd` whose
  `name` was undefined — a page that answers 200 and says nothing.
- `toGuidePage` and `toCollectionPage` project a list page item by item, as `toGuidePage` already did.

The locale reaches the read: `guideBySlug`, `guideList`, `collectionBySlug` and `collectionList` now take it
(`apps/web/src/lib/data.ts:287`, `apps/web/src/lib/data.ts:306`, `apps/web/src/lib/data.ts:316`,
`apps/web/src/lib/data.ts:329`) and the four pages pass the one they already resolve. `app/sitemap.ts`
resolves it too — the sitemap carries paths and timestamps rather than titles, but its reads project the
same field, so it must not be the one place that guesses.

**What it does not do.** It does not change the platform: the pair is what `API_CONTRACT §8` documents and
what `title_zh` exists for. It does not pick a language by guessing — the page's locale is the only input,
and a locale with no column of its own falls back to the other rather than to nothing. It does not drop a
card the platform could not resolve: `dropped_item_ids` still names them and the resolved array still omits
them, which is the `API_CONTRACT §8` rule that an unresolvable id drops the item and never renders a
placeholder card.

**Evidence.** The unit cases in `apps/web/src/lib/platform-guides.test.ts` are written from the wire shape
the platform actually serves — the pair, the null `alt`, the stored references beside the resolved cards —
and not from the mock plane's plain strings: 17 cases, green, in a file that held 8 before this unit. The
live leg re-visited the four routes on the running stack (`http://127.0.0.1:3002`, live mode against the
platform on `:8090`): **all four answer HTTP 200**, against four HTTP 500s before this change, and the
browser console is clean on three of them. The fourth — the guide detail route — logs one React error,
"Encountered two children with the same key", which is the defect the next unit takes; it is named below
rather than counted as clean. The rendered heading is the platform's `zh` column read by the page's own
locale (沙田情侶約會路線), and the collection detail renders nine resolved merchant cards — names, ratings,
prices — where the stored array would have rendered nine references with no title. `npx tsc --noEmit` over
`apps/web` is clean, and the whole web suite is 160 cases in 12 files, green.

**Left open, named here rather than left to be discovered again.** The guide detail route now answers 200
and still logs one React error: "Encountered two children with the same key". The seeded Sha Tin guide
cites ten merchants over nine shops — `bramble-spoon-0001` appears at position 1 and position 9 of the
resolved cards, and the platform's own comment says the repeats are kept on purpose, because a `cards`
array one shorter than the items it came from reads as a lost item. So the data is right and the web's
`key={card.id}` is wrong; that is the next unit, not this one. Separately, the seeded guide's description
carries a broken template placeholder — `"由{d2}分鐘步程內嘅安靜餐廳…"` — where a distance number belongs,
and that string is what the page renders as its description.

- readers: the four growth routes answer HTTP 200 live — `/guides`, `/collections`,
  `/guides/sha-tin-date-night`, `/collections/tai-wai-under-100` — against four HTTP 500s before this
  change · the browser console is clean on three of the four; the guide detail route logs one React
  duplicate-key error, which the next unit takes and this section names rather than counting as clean ·
  the rendered heading is the platform's `zh` column read by the page's own locale, and the collection
  detail renders nine resolved merchant cards where the stored array would have rendered nine references
  with no title · `apps/web/src/lib/platform-guides.test.ts` is 17 cases green in a file that held 8 ·
  `npx tsc --noEmit` over `apps/web` is clean and the whole web suite is 160 cases in 12 files, green ·
  gate step 10 reads this section as one more heading with missing 0 and duplicate 0, and step 8 reads
  its eleven citations against the working tree with 0 strict offenders

## 570. D574 · the client plane's multi-child slots could render an unkeyed list member — React's missing-key warning fired on the home page and no reader could see it (`scripts/check_slot_keys.mjs`, `scripts/falsify_slot_keys.mjs`, `packages/ui/src/primitives/Badge.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/primitives/Input.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/primitives/Layout.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/primitives/Select.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/primitives/Tabs.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/primitives/Floating.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/feedback/States.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/trust/EntityCard.tsx`)

**What was found, and how.** The live home page rendered and the browser console still carried a React
error: `Each child in a list should have a unique "key" prop` — naming `EntityRail` as the slot's owner
and `HomePage` as the component the child was passed from. The page itself looked right: hero, search,
four rails, 24 cards, the footer. Nothing in this repository could see the defect. Every reader that
reads the web tree reads TEXT — the accessibility reader reads the render tree, the i18n reader reads
the copy — and none of them asks whether a slot React walks as a LIST carries the keys React asks for.
The console warning is the only place the answer exists, and nothing was reading it.

**The mechanism, read from the runtime rather than inferred.** React's `validateChildKeys` marks a
PLAIN element `validated = 1` the moment the element enters a children array, so an element created in
the same pass never draws the warning. An element that crosses the RSC boundary arrives as a
`React.lazy`, and the runtime Next vendors has NO lazy branch in `validateChildKeys`: the lazy is
never marked, and when the reconciler resolves it the element behind it is still unvalidated, so React
asks the slot's owner for a key. The SERVER plane never warns, and that is not luck: there the element
is a plain element created in the same pass, and the array-creation loop marks it validated before the
server renderer walks the array. The defect therefore belongs to the client plane and to no other.

**The rule, in the shape the compiler emits it.** SWC sets `isStaticChildren = true` exactly when a
slot's children compile to an ARRAY, which is exactly when the slot has two or more real children: JSX
text is trimmed the way the JSX transform trims it, so whitespace on its own line is not a child. Every
member of such an array is a list member and React asks each one for a key. A slot with ONE child
compiles to `false` and asks nothing.

**The fix.** Thirteen sites in nine files: the bare node-typed prop is wrapped in a keyed fragment. A
keyed fragment turns "element in an array" into "single child of a fragment", and a single child is not
an array, so React asks for no key at all. The thirteen are:

- `packages/ui/src/primitives/Badge.tsx:61` — `Badge`'s `children` in a two-child `<span>`.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx:64` — `Button`'s `leadingIcon` in a three-child `<span>`.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx:65` — `Button`'s `children`, the same span.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx:66` — `Button`'s `trailingIcon`, the same span.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/Floating.tsx:187` — `ToastProvider`'s `children` in a two-child
  `<ToastContext.Provider>`.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/Input.tsx:40` — `FieldShell`'s `label` in a two-child `<label>`.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/Input.tsx:48` — `FieldShell`'s `children` in a three-child `<div>`.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/Input.tsx:52` — `FieldShell`'s `error` in a two-child `<p>`.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/Layout.tsx:127` — `Section`'s `children` in a two-child `<section>`.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/Select.tsx:132` — `Select`'s `label` in a two-child `<span>`.
- `packages/ui/src/primitives/Tabs.tsx:140` — `Tab`'s `children` in a two-child `<button>`.
- `packages/ui/src/feedback/States.tsx:78` — `ErrorState`'s `retryAction` in a two-child `<span>`.
- `packages/ui/src/trust/EntityCard.tsx:212` — `EntityRail`'s `action` in a two-child `<header>`, the one
  the console named.

**The reader.** `scripts/check_slot_keys.mjs` reads the same render tree from the other end — the
question React asks, asked of the source:

- the population is three source roots (`scripts/check_slot_keys.mjs:79`), and it REFUSES with exit 2
  when a root is absent or the population is empty: a tree this reader cannot see is not a tree whose
  slots are safe.
- the client plane is the modules whose FIRST statement is the `'use client'` directive
  (`scripts/check_slot_keys.mjs:118`) plus their transitive import closure — and the closure follows
  RE-EXPORTS as well as imports (`scripts/check_slot_keys.mjs:152`), because `packages/ui/src/index.ts:26`
  is a barrel: `export * from './primitives/Layout'` pulls that module into the client bundle through the
  re-export, not through an import statement. The reader's own header records the measurement that
  forced the change — the first version of the closure put 53 modules in the plane and `Layout.tsx` was
  not among them.
- the slot is a JSX element or fragment whose REAL children number two or more.
- the prop is read from the component's own declared props type: an inline type literal, a named
  interface or type alias in the same file (following `extends`), or the type argument of `React.FC<…>`;
  the node-typed test is `ReactNode`, `ReactElement` or `ReactChildren`
  (`scripts/check_slot_keys.mjs:192`).
- the `children` fallback: React's JSX contract makes every component's children a ReactNode, so a slot
  that renders `children` bare is read as node-typed even when that member's type lives in the
  platform's own `React.*Attributes` declarations, which this reader does not resolve
  (`scripts/check_slot_keys.mjs:384`).
- the verdict names every offender and exits 1 (`scripts/check_slot_keys.mjs:422`), or prints PASS and
  exits 0 (`scripts/check_slot_keys.mjs:425`).

**What it does not do, stated rather than implied.**

- It does not decide whether a slot's prop is actually handed a server-created element. It asks the
  question React asks — can this shape warn? A prop that only ever receives a client-local element is
  reported anyway. That direction over-reports, which is the direction this project accepts.
- It reads the BARE-IDENTIFIER form only. A conditional (`{action ? <X/> : null}`), a logical
  (`{action && <X/>}`) or an array literal compiles to an element the SLOT creates itself, and the
  reader says so rather than guessing.
- It does not check the DUPLICATE-key warning. React raises that one on the client only and no source
  scan can decide it — two cards may legitimately carry the same id. That is D575, named below and not
  answered here.
- It does not run a browser. It reads the source and reasons about the shape the compiler emits; the
  live measurement that anchors it is the console A/B below.

**Evidence.** The census on the HEAD bytes: 13 node-typed props in multi-child slots, 13 offenders, exit
1, one line per site. On this working tree: 0, exit 0. The population is identical on both planes — 125
JSX/TS files under the three roots, 56 client-plane modules of which 26 carry the directive, 69 files
that render on the server, 242 multi-child slots — so the difference between the two readings is the
thirteen wrappers and nothing else.

`scripts/falsify_slot_keys.mjs` is 15 arms, 15 held, 0 missed. The census reddens on a bare node-typed
prop; it keeps quiet when the same prop's declared type is changed to a non-node type; it keeps quiet
on the SERVER plane; it keeps quiet on a conditional; it follows the barrel's `export * from` and goes
quiet again when that re-export is deleted; it refuses with exit 2 on a missing source root, on an
unknown flag and on `--plane` given twice; and the last three arms aim it at a planted tree in both
spellings — `--plane <dir>` and `--plane=<dir>` — while the `--report` arm prints the offender and still
exits 0.

The reachability census reads 16 of 16 first-party readers invoked by a surface, 0 unreached, and all
12 CI steps that pipe a checker into `tee` declare `shell: bash` — this reader and its own arms are two
of those twelve. The CI wiring is in the `lint-type` job and not in `contract-drift`, because that job
installs NOTHING: a reader that cannot import its own parser dies with MODULE_NOT_FOUND, which is a
crash and not a verdict.

`npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present` exits 0 across all four workspaces, and the workspace
suites are 234 tests green — the web's 160 in 12 files, the SDK's 43 and the types package's 31. The
live A/B is the console itself: before the wrappers the browser console on `http://127.0.0.1:3002/` carried exactly one
React missing-key error naming `EntityRail` and `HomePage`; after them a cache-bypassing reload of the
same page carries no console message at all — no error, no warning — while the page renders in full:
hero, search, four rails with 24 cards, the "一次搜索做了什么" section and the footer.

**The ledger's own readers.** Gate step 16 was RED when this unit started: five MOVED citations, all of
them rows D572's own commit had made stale by editing `scripts/check_ledger_citations.mjs` and
`scripts/falsify_ledger_text.mjs` — two and five lines of drift. They were re-aimed from the reader's own
`--reaim` output, each target line read by hand before it was accepted. Then this unit's own commit did the

and 6 to `scripts/falsify_reader_reachability.mjs`, and those three files are cited by ten committed

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:314-335` is the three steps that pipe a checker into `tee`,
`.github/workflows/ci.yml:299` is the note that says why they declare `shell: bash`,
`.github/workflows/ci.yml:266-270` is the block that boots Spring on 8080, uvicorn on 8000 and Next on
3000 and waits on all three, `scripts/falsify_reader_reachability.mjs:169-175` is the arm that used to

## 571. D575 · the guide detail page rendered two cards with the same React key — the platform keeps repeats on purpose and the web keyed by identity (`scripts/check_duplicate_keys.mjs`, `scripts/falsify_duplicate_keys.mjs`, `packages/ui/src/trust/cardKeys.ts`, `packages/ui/src/trust/EntityCard.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/trust/CompareTable.tsx`, `apps/web/src/components/cards.tsx`, `data/seed/generate.py`)

**What was found, and how.** The guide detail route on the running stack (`http://127.0.0.1:3002/guides/sha-tin-date-night`) carried exactly one React error in the browser console: "Encountered two children with the same key". The page itself looked right — the heading, the description, and ten merchant cards with names, ratings and prices. §569 named the defect and §570 left it open; what no reader could see was the RULE behind it, and the rule turned out to say that the DATA was right and the KEY was wrong.

**Why a list may hold the same card twice.** The platform resolves a guide's items in the author's order and keeps every reference — it resolves each item and adds the card it resolved — so a guide that cites one shop in two places yields that shop's card twice. That is deliberate: `CollectionsController`'s own comment says "Item order, repeats included", the row's `item_count` says ten, and a `cards` array one shorter than the items it came from reads as a lost item. The web keyed the list members by `card.id` — the card's IDENTITY — and an identity is not unique inside a list that holds that card twice. React's reconciler keeps the keys it has already seen in the children array it is walking, and when a key comes round twice it logs the warning and the second member takes the first one's place on update: the list duplicates or drops a member.

**Why no reader could have caught it.** The warning lives in the CLIENT reconciler alone: it is absent from every `react-dom-server` build, and `renderToStaticMarkup` emits nothing for a list whose members share a key. No server render can witness it, and D574's reader — which reads the render tree from the source — was the right instrument for the OTHER warning and the wrong one for this. So the reader here runs the real component and reads the tree it returns.

**The fix — a key names the OCCURRENCE, not the identity.** `packages/ui/src/trust/cardKeys.ts:22` is the whole rule: the first appearance of an id keeps the bare id, and a repeat is suffixed with the number of EARLIER appearances of that same id (`dup`, then `dup#1`). The suffix counts appearances of the same id rather than positions in the list, so a list of distinct cards keys exactly as it did before the helper existed — no remount, no churn — and a card keeps its key when an unrelated card joins the list. Four sites now call it:

- `apps/web/src/components/cards.tsx:41` — `CardGrid`'s `<li>`, keyed by `keys[index]`.
- `apps/web/src/components/cards.tsx:113` — the compare tray's `<li>`, keyed by `keys[index]`.
- `packages/ui/src/trust/EntityCard.tsx:216` — `EntityRail`'s keyed fragment, `keys[index]`.
- `packages/ui/src/trust/CompareTable.tsx:60` — the compare table's `<th scope="col">`, keyed by `keys[index]`.

**The reader.** `scripts/check_duplicate_keys.mjs` asks the question React asks, of the real component rather than of the source text:

- the population is the components that take a LIST OF IDENTITY-BEARING OBJECTS — a prop whose declared type is an array of a type that declares `id: string` — and the identity-bearing types are resolved through the imports, so `EntityCardModel` in the web and `EntityCard` in the UI package are the same type and both are found;
- the fixture is built by `identityList` (`scripts/check_duplicate_keys.mjs:424`): one list member per identity, and one identity twice, so a list keyed by identity gives `dup` twice and a list keyed by occurrence gives `dup` and `dup#1`. The other props are furnished from their DECLARED types — strings become `'en'`, functions become no-ops, the labels object becomes the real `trustLabels('en')`;
- the client plane is the modules carrying the `'use client'` directive plus their transitive import closure; the same shape in a server module is not this defect, because the warning does not exist there;
- a REQUIRED prop whose type the reader cannot furnish is a REFUSAL, not a verdict: the component was not run, and "did not run" is not "found nothing";
- it refuses with exit 2 when one of the three `ROOTS` is absent (`scripts/check_duplicate_keys.mjs:93`) or when the population is empty: a tree this reader cannot see is not a tree whose lists are safe.

**What it does not do, stated rather than implied.**

- It does not decide whether a list really can hold the same card twice; it asks whether the shape CAN warn. A prop that only ever receives distinct cards is judged the same way. That direction over-reports, which is the direction this project accepts.
- It does not check the MISSING-key warning — a list member with no key at all. That is D574's subject, `scripts/check_slot_keys.mjs`.
- It does not run a browser. The live measurement that anchors it is the console A/B below.

**The seed's half — the copy was claiming a route its members did not make.** The guide's description shipped the literal placeholder `由{d2}分鐘步程內嘅安靜餐廳…` — `{d2}` was a template slot that was never filled — and its members were eight Sha Tin shops plus two drawn from every merchant whose noise rating was high enough, so the route's copy named restaurants, dessert and bars while its members were heritage tours, tailors and photo studios. The old code computed that quiet list and never used it; that is how the copy and the membership came apart. Both are now derived from the CLAIM:

- `data/seed/generate.py:1572` — the membership is the published merchants that satisfy the collection's own DECLARED claims (in Sha Tin, quiet, and of a kind the route can name), so every member is a stop the route can name. D576 moved this derivation into the claim vocabulary the generator and the reader now share, and the quiet threshold is now the seed's own `quiet_ambience` attribute (noise ≥ 4.2) rather than the 4.3 this line carried when it was written;
- `data/seed/generate.py:1580` — the members are taken round-robin over the kinds they come in and the first member is then cited twice on purpose: ten references over nine shops, because the platform keeps repeats and a reader with no repeat to witness cannot see the defect;
- `data/seed/generate.py:1658` — the distance in the copy is `max(m["mtr_min"])` over the members, the seed's own walking-minutes field, so "within N minutes" is true of every stop and false of nothing;
- the kind nouns in the copy are the members' own kinds, and a small merchants plane that produces no qualifying member gets a copy that says the route has no stops rather than a copy that claims a distance.

The regenerated dataset answers the guide over HTTP with 200 and no placeholder: `由14分鐘步程內嘅安靜餐廳、咖啡店同酒吧組合而成的示範路線。全部商戶均為虛構。`, ten items over nine distinct merchants, every one of them in Sha Tin.

**The correction §569 and §570 owed.** Both rows name `bramble-spoon-0001` as the repeated shop, at positions 1 and 9. That was true of the seed this unit replaced and is false of the seed that ships now: the route's repeated member is `umber-ridge-0029`, at positions 1 and 10, and `bramble-spoon-0001` is no longer a member of the route at all. The shape of the finding is unchanged — ten references over nine shops, one identity twice — and the slug in those two rows is stale.

**Evidence.** The reader on this tree: PASS, 126 JSX/TS files under the three roots, 57 client-plane modules of which 26 carry the directive, 69 files that render on the server and are out of scope, 5 card-list components run, 0 duplicate keys. `scripts/falsify_duplicate_keys.mjs` is 16 arms, 16 held, 0 missed: the census reddens on a list keyed by the card identity, and it reddens in the RAIL and in the COMPARE TABLE too; it keeps quiet on the SERVER plane, where the warning does not exist; it keeps quiet on a list member with NO key at all, which is D574's warning and not this one; and it refuses with exit 2 on a component whose required prop it cannot furnish, on a tree missing one of the three source roots, on an unknown flag and on `--plane` given twice. ## 572. D576 · the three collections §571 left open advertised what their members were not — the claims now live in one vocabulary the generator writes from and a reader holds against the rows (`data/seed/claim_vocabulary.json`, `scripts/check_collection_claims.mjs`, `scripts/falsify_collection_claims.mjs`, `data/seed/generate.py`, `scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`)

**What was found, and how.** §571 named the other three collections and left them open. This unit did not re-read those descriptions and reason about them; it wrote the question down as a program and let the program answer it. Run against the plane the previous unit shipped — 520 merchants, full scale, `data/seed/out` as it stood when this unit began — the census files **57 failures and exits 1** (`sha-tin-date-night` 2, `quiet-meals-near-me` 19, `tai-wai-under-100` 13, `weekend-family-sha-tin` 23); the same generator at ci scale files **64** with the same split except the itinerary's 30. Nearly every row is one sentence wearing a different member's name: the copy says something about the list and the list is not that thing. The guide's two rows are the shape rows only, because §571 had already derived its membership from its claim.

**Why the claim was nowhere checkable.** D575's route fix put the derivation in Python — the filter that chose the members and the sentence that described them were now one computation — but the *claim itself* existed only as that code. A reader that wants to hold a sentence to its rows needs the claim as data: which members are being asserted, in what words the assertion is said, and which value the copy states. Before this unit each collection had a hand-written description and a hand-written pool and no third place where either was recorded, so a sentence could only be checked against the generator's memory of what it meant to say.

**One file, two readers.** `data/seed/claim_vocabulary.json` is that third place. It declares 12 check names (`:6`), the vocabulary the words come from — 15 districts, 10 kinds, 3 attributes, 2 bands, 3 stages — 9 slots (`:67`), 11 sentence templates (`:79`) and 4 collections (`:93`), each with its membership claims, its title claims, the phrase ids its body is made of, and the fixed values its slots cannot derive. The generator selects members by the checks (`data/seed/generate.py:1572`) and renders the copy from the templates (`:509`); the reader (`scripts/check_collection_claims.mjs`) reads the same file, parses the SHIPPED copy back out of the same templates, and holds every claim against the SHIPPED rows. A claim that is not written here cannot be said; a claim that is written here is checked against the data.

**The check set is closed on both sides.** `data/seed/generate.py:447` implements the seven member-scoped checks and raises on a name it does not know at `:472`; `scripts/check_collection_claims.mjs:88` declares the same set and refuses at `:94` when the vocabulary names a check the reader does not implement. The two lists are not compared by hand anywhere — each side refuses the file rather than silently ignoring an entry, because a check one side knows and the other does not is a check one side can answer wrongly. The same closure runs on the slot table: an unknown render kind, an unknown derivation, a slot that carries no check at all (`:103`, `:105`, `:107`) and a phrase naming a slot the slot table does not declare are refusals, not verdicts. So is a rows file the census needs (`:156`): a plane it cannot see is not a plane whose claims hold.

**A sentence is parsed back, not trusted.** `phraseRegex` (`scripts/check_collection_claims.mjs:335`) turns `全線都係{minutes}分鐘步程內嘅{kinds}。` into an anchored regex — a number slot captures digits, every other slot captures `[^。]+?` so a capture cannot run past the sentence it belongs to — and the copy is split into sentences whose count must equal the declared phrase count (`:493`). A sentence that is not its declared template is a failure, which is how the pre-D576 guide's single fused sentence reads as two rows rather than as prose.

**Each claim is held twice.** The value the copy states must equal the value the rows support, AND every member must satisfy the claim the value encodes. `:514` recomputes the members' own distinct count, maximum walking minutes, kinds present and stages offered from the shipped CSVs; `slotProblem` (`:569`) compares the stated value against it — so `全線共9個站` over ten distinct members reddens on the NUMBER, not on a sentence-matching trick — and then asks the member-scoped check of every member: a stated walk bound must be the members' own maximum, a stated price must clear every member's `avg_price_hkd`, a kind list must name exactly the kinds the members have (`named bar which no member is`), a stage list must be offered by members' own slots, and an attribute word must be the vocabulary's spelling carried by every member. `:413` asks the membership claims member by member and `:436` holds the title claims, which additionally have to be *said*: the title must carry the claim's own word in both languages, a district or attribute word must be the vocabulary's spelling, and a price title must carry the number.

**"Near me" is a claim about a person.** `quiet-meals-near-me` says 我附近嘅安靜用餐位, and §571's complaint — "seven districts from Sha Tin to Tsim Sha Tsui and Stanley, which is not near me" — has no support in a merchant table. The vocabulary declares the check `home_district`, and `consumerHomeDistrict` (`scripts/check_collection_claims.mjs:288`) reads it from the author's own `04_user_preferences.csv` row: exactly one `home_district` row, whose English value names a declared district. The generator renders the same claim from `self.consumer_home_district()` and refuses a home district the vocabulary does not name, so the title's "我附近" is held against the consumer the seed actually ships. `weekend_slots` is held the same way as a title claim (`:321`): the itinerary says 週末 and the members must have slots on both a Saturday and a Sunday.

**What the generator now refuses to write.** A claim whose pool is empty (`data/seed/generate.py:1577` — on a small merchants plane that leaves no qualifying member the collection says it has no stops rather than claiming a distance); a title claim its own members do not support (`:1715`); a body phrase the vocabulary does not declare (`:1724`); a title that does not carry the word its claim needs (`:1694`); a vocabulary whose district list disagrees with `seed_pools.DISTRICTS` (`:538` — the two lists of the same names are compared on every run, because a reader that trusted a stale copy would name a district the generator never writes); and a disclaimer that is two strings that look alike rather than one (`:548`). The membership is taken round-robin over the kinds it comes in (`:1589`) so a route whose copy names a cafe and a bar is not nine restaurants, and the guide's deliberate repeat survives (`:1581`) for D575's reason.

**The copy that ships now.** Every sentence below is the declared template, and every value in it is re-derived from the members the census then walks:

- `sha-tin-date-night` (guide) — 全線都係14分鐘步程內嘅餐廳、咖啡店同酒吧。全部成員都係安靜嘅商戶。全線共9個站。全部商戶均為虛構。 — 10 items over 9 distinct merchants, kinds restaurant/cafe/bar, every one in Sha Tin and quiet;
- `quiet-meals-near-me` — 全部成員都係安靜嘅餐廳同咖啡店。全部成員都喺沙田區。清單共有10間。全部商戶均為虛構。 — 10 members, kinds restaurant/cafe, max walk 16, and the consumer whose title says 我附近 does live in Sha Tin;
- `tai-wai-under-100` — 全部成員都喺大圍區，人均低於100蚊。清單共有9間。全部商戶均為虛構。 — 9 members, all in Tai Wai, all below HK$100. Its members also include a `service`, and the copy does not name kinds: the sentence says what the list supports and stays silent about what it does not;
- `weekend-family-sha-tin` (itinerary) — 由午餐、活動同晚餐組成嘅示範一日行程。全部成員都係親子嘅商戶。行程包含週末供求時段。全線共9個站。全部商戶均為虛構。 — 9 members, kinds restaurant/activity/experience, all in Sha Tin, all carrying `family_occasion`, all with Sunday slots and Saturday-and-Sunday pairs.

**Wiring, and the CI step that was failing on its own command line.** Gate step 3 runs the census and then its arms immediately after generation (`scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh:172`, `:175`), placed after the `if` so it also runs under `--skip-generate` — the census judges the bytes step 4 loads, so a plane someone else generated is exactly the plane worth checking. CI runs it in both jobs that load the seed: `ai` after its generate (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:180` → `:185`, which needed a `setup-node` step because that job had none) and `e2e` before `load.sh` (`:257` → `:262`); the `changes` filter now counts `data/seed/` as an input to the `ai` job (`:48`) because the seed *is* that job's input. While wiring `e2e` this unit read the generate command already there and found it dead: `python data/seed/generate.py --counts merchants=80,offerings=600,reviews=1200`. `--counts` takes a preset NAME — `full|ci|smoke` — so argparse refused the value, the step failed on its own command line, and the "Start data stores + schema + demo data" step was generating nothing for the suite that followed it. The three separate scale flags carry the numbers that line meant, and the plane they produce now self-checks PASS and reads PASS through the census.

**What it does not do, stated rather than implied.**

- It reads the seed's CSVs, not the served database. A collection row changed after load is not this census's plane; inside the fresh gate that is the same run's own bytes (step 3 checks what step 4 loads), and outside it the seam is named rather than assumed.
- It does not decide whether a claim is worth making, only whether the rows support it. A collection that says only 全部商戶均為虛構 passes as honestly as one that says nine true things.
- It holds the two implementations of each check equal by the shared NAME, not by a differential test. Python's `merchant_satisfies` and the JS `memberSatisfies` are two programs that can disagree while each staying self-consistent; nothing yet hands both the same row and requires the same answer. That is this unit's named residue.
- It judges only the four collections the vocabulary declares — and it files a fifth shipped collection as a failure (`:681`, "a copy nobody declares is a copy nobody checks"), so the population cannot shrink in silence.

**Evidence.** Measured on planes generated for this unit OUTSIDE the repository root, so the shared `data/seed/out` was not emptied under another lane (the hazard #205 names): full scale, 520 merchants — PASS, exit 0, 4 declared / 4 shipped, 37 distinct members, 16 sentences parsed out of 11 templates, 144 claims checked, and the generator's own self-check PASS (FK integrity, bounds, naming, density, language mix) on the same plane; ci scale, 120 merchants — 35 members, 140 claims, PASS; the e2e scale this unit's CI fix produces, 80 merchants — 27 members, 116 claims, PASS; smoke scale, 30 merchants — 8 members, 53 claims, PASS. The reverse control is the same reader on the same vocabulary over the previous generator's bytes: 57 failures at full scale and 64 at ci scale, both exit 1. `scripts/falsify_collection_claims.mjs` is 17 arms, 17 held, 0 missed in about 27 s — one control, nine red plants (stop count edited by one, a Sha Tin member planted in the Tai Wai list, a title that drops its price word, a dropped disclaimer, an undeclared collection, a missing collection, a stage no member offers, a kind no member is, a moved consumer home district), four refusals (a check the reader does not implement, an absent rows file, an unknown flag, `--out` given twice) and three seam arms (`--report` prints the failure and still exits 0; `--out <dir>` and `--out=<dir>` both reach the planted plane). The reachability census reads 18 of 18 first-party readers invoked by a surface, 0 unreached, and its verbose list names this unit's reader as reached by two of them — `reached check_collection_claims.mjs  gate, ci`.

**The ledger's own readers.** This unit moved `data/seed/generate.py` by several hundred lines, which makes every committed citation into that file stale, and the drift census is the reader that says so: 4 lines in `docs/STATUS.md` (two D89/D90 rows now naming `:1123`, §571's three route bullets now naming `:1572`/`:1580`/`:1658`, and §571's re-aim sentence), 5 lines in `docs/DECISIONS.md` (`:968`→`:1123` three times, `:2085`→`:2377`, `:1749`→`:2041`), and 3 `site` strings in `data/seed/quality.sql` (`generate.py:1368`, `:1136`, and the pair `:293`/`:1729`) that `check_jsonb_reads.mjs` charges by the line's own words. Each target was read on the committed tree before it was accepted, and §571's route bullets carry the clause that says what moved them and why the quiet threshold no longer reads 4.3.

**Left open, named here rather than left to be discovered again.**

- The differential test the two implementations still lack: hand `merchant_satisfies` and `memberSatisfies` the same merchant row and the same claim and require the same answer, for all seven member-scoped checks.
