## 573. D577 · the strict citation gate could be turned green by typing in the ledger — the reader censused HEAD's copy of the text and took its blame off this machine's (`scripts/check_line_cite_drift.mjs`, `scripts/falsify_line_cite_drift.mjs`)

**What was found, and how.** While re-aiming the one citation D576's chain had left, the census answered the same question about the same repository twice and gave different verdicts, and the difference was whether a ledger line was uncommitted. With `docs/DECISIONS.md` edited on disk and nothing else changed — no target moved, no commit made — the reader that was shipped then reported `MOVED 0 · NOT-UNIQUE 0 · NO-BASE 5` over 255 judged citations and `RESULT: PASS`, exit 0. Commit that same edit and the identical command reports `MOVED 1` and exits 1. A lane could clear gate step 16 without moving a line of code or correcting a number in the tree: it only had to type the correction into the ledger and leave it uncommitted.

**How the green was made.** The census reads its ledger text out of HEAD (`git show HEAD:<ledger>`) and took its blame off the working copy: `git blame --line-porcelain <path>` with no rev, which is the call now at `scripts/check_line_cite_drift.mjs:121` — the same line, with the rev it argues for. Two planes, one reading. `git blame` dates an uncommitted line to the all-zero sha; the all-zero sha resolves to no tree; and every citation riding that line fell to NO-BASE carrying the detail `absent at 0000000, the commit that wrote the citing line`. NO-BASE is deliberately not one of the strict classes — it is the honest answer to "this citation predates the code it names", a queue and not a red — so a *skipped* judgement and a *passed* one both exit 0 and both print PASS. The edited row happened to carry three citations, and the typing un-judged all three at once: the drift reader's own grammar line, and `scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh:579` and `:567`.

**The fix, and what it gives up.** Blame at HEAD. `blameByLine(git, path, rev = 'HEAD')` (`scripts/check_line_cite_drift.mjs:117`), one call site passing it (`:208`), so the basis and the text are one reading again and the strict classes can no longer be emptied by an edit. What the edit represents is then counted instead of judged: the census walks the disk copy of each ledger against HEAD's copy line by line (`:218`) and prints one number per run (`:355`) — `ledger lines differing between disk and HEAD: N (the census grades HEAD's copy, so a number edited on disk is not judged until it is committed)` — with a second clause naming how many of the ledgers have no disk copy at all, because on a plane like an archive tree their divergence is unknown rather than zero. It read 1 on the plane that produced the false green and 0 after this unit's re-aim was committed. This is a disclosure, not a verdict: the numbers a lane is typing are simply not graded yet, and nothing here pretends to know what they will mean once they are.

**The harness had the seam in the other direction.** Every arm of `scripts/falsify_line_cite_drift.mjs` spawns the reader as it sits on disk, while the gate runs the file as committed (`scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh:567` for the census, `:579` for the strict one, `:566` for the arms; CI runs the census at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:362` and the arms at `:367`). So an arm battery green against an uncommitted reader is a green for a file nobody has installed. The harness now compares that one path's worktree bytes with its HEAD blob (`scripts/falsify_line_cite_drift.mjs:64`) and refuses with exit 2, printing the diff line and the stat, when they differ. Measured: run while D577's reader edit was still uncommitted it printed `RESULT: NOT CHECKED — the reader on disk is not the reader at HEAD`, with `1 file changed, 44 insertions(+), 10 deletions(-)`, and no arm ran; after the reader landed the same command runs its full battery. The check is scoped to the reader's own path and not to `git status`, because in a worktree several lanes write to, the status line names every one of them and the only divergence that changes what an arm proves is this file's bytes.

**Arm 13 changes the one property no earlier arm touched** — whether the citing line exists as a commit (`scripts/falsify_line_cite_drift.mjs:292`). Three readings of the same repository: a clean plane whose committed citation is stale, `MOVED 1` and `diverges 0`; that plane with the correct number typed into the ledger on disk, still `MOVED 1`, `--strict MOVED` exit 1, `diverges 1`; those same bytes committed, `EXACT 1` and `diverges 0`. Predicted before the run, and held — 13 of 13.

**What this unit moved in its own ledger.** Its reader commit grew `scripts/check_line_cite_drift.mjs` by 34 lines and shifted the CITE regex from line 86 to line 88, which made the single committed citation into that file — D276's row, at DECISIONS line 12267 — name a line that no longer held the grammar it was written against. Step 16 filed it as MOVED 1 of 255 and derived `86 -> 88 (+2)`; the target was read on the committed tree before the digit moved (86 closes the extension-vocabulary paragraph, 87 declares `EXT_VOCAB`, 88 is the regex the sentence names), so the re-aim keeps the claim true rather than merely green. The other two citations sharing that ledger line, `scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh:579` and `:567`, were checked to still be EXACT and left alone. Landed as 95fd327: digits-only, one line changed each way, with the file's own CRLF preserved — this worktree's DECISIONS.md is CRLF while its blob is LF, and a rewrite that normalised the whole file would have shown 14,632 changed lines instead of one.

**Left open, named here rather than left to be discovered again.**

- The disclosure is a count, not a list. The census says how many ledger lines sit outside its reading and does not name which rows they are, so a lane that wants to know which of its own edits are unjudged still runs `git diff` for itself. The same loop already walks both arrays; naming the rows is one more string per row.

This unit closed the route by which an *editor* manufactured that state, but a citation legitimately written into a file another lane has not committed yet lands in the same class, and both readings still exit 0. A strict class that refuses to count skipped judgements would refuse a lane's work-in-progress, which is why the census discloses rather than charges.
- The 5 GONE and 2 NO-BASE rows the census carries are untouched by this unit and remain its named backlog; D280 audited the GONE set as true statements about positions rather than stale pointers.

- readers: the strict census on the tree this section lands on (27c6e68) reads MOVED 0 / NOT-UNIQUE 0 over 263 judged citations, 256 of them still naming the line they were written against, and the divergence line at 0 — and 8 of those 263 are the full-path pointers this very row writes, which is why the population the D576 chain left at 255 grew here and why the two figures are quoted from the same commit rather than remembered · the same census through the pre-fix reader, on the same repository with one ledger line edited and uncommitted, read MOVED 0 / NO-BASE 5 with `RESULT: PASS` exit 0 — that is the reverse control, run on the shipped plane rather than described · step 15 plain PASS · gate step 8 files 0 strict offenders over 803 citation-shaped tokens, 0 UNTRACKED TARGETs and 0 UNCOMMITTED TARGETs, with the blank-line backlog still at 30 at HEAD and none of it filed by this section · its arm battery 13 of 13 held, 0 missed, each arm a one-property change on a throwaway repository of its own · the sections gate 529 STATUS sections and 300 DECISIONS decisions, 0 missing and 0 duplicated on both planes · no 18-step gate was filed in this unit: the database-backed steps were not re-run here, and the figures above come from the readers this change can reach.
## 577. D591 · the search's `cuisine` preference now reads the seed's own `cuisine_vegetarian` boolean

**The defect.** PLAN's open AI-lane item "the seeded merchants carry no `vegetarian` attribute"
was still open: the seed writes each merchant's vegetarian fact as the boolean attribute
    `"cuisine_vegetarian": m["leaf"] == "vegetarian"`,
and the NLU emits the `(cuisine, vegetarian)` preference for a query that names one - but no
preference branch read that boolean, so the stored/declared preference plane was inert while the
typed leg (the cuisine bridge, D394) served the leaf. The full-suite check that holds the two
sources apart went red on it:

    the seed writes attributes no matcher reads - dead data that looks load-bearing: ['cuisine_vegetarian']

**The fix.** The stored-preference branch for `(cuisine, vegetarian)` now reads the boolean the
seed writes - `attrs.get("cuisine_vegetarian") is True` answers the preference's side and
`is False` its refusal - the same boolean shape the sibling branch reads its own fact through
(`spicy_cuisine`). The typed leg keeps the leaf bridge, which is where a typed query's own words
are served.

**Verified, not claimed.** The new gate `tests/test_the_vegetarian_preference_reaches_the_seeds_own_attribute.py`
holds the reader to the seed's boolean (the source-level check, the seed staleness check, and two
behavioural separations: a declared vegetarian preference moves a vegetarian merchant UP the
ranking, a refused one moves it DOWN). With the boolean read in place the attribute gate that went
red is green again, and this session also closed the tags-gate regression the kind-vocabulary unit
had left behind (the reader restored to `categories.canonical_tag`; the tags, kind, D554 JSON-text,
clause-final and cuisine-vocabulary gates - 84 tests - went green again). Ruff and mypy are clean
after the one annotation the kind unit's reader needed.

**Left open.** The live demo database could not be re-probed this unit (the local docker daemon is
not running in this environment), so the behavioural witness here is the fixture lane's
StaticBackend, the way the lane's preference units did before their live probes.

**The number was repaired, not the claim.** This unit landed at 16:28 as `D559` / section 556; the
cleanup unit landed at 17:53 against the same section number, so the ledger held two sections
answering one cite (`check_ledger_sections.mjs`: `duplicate numbers 2`, duplicated at HEAD as well
as on disk). The later copy keeps `D559` because the two scripts that cite that number
(`scripts/db_schema_drift.sh`, `scripts/check_launcher_log_mode.sh`) mean the cleanup's traps, and
this earlier unit is renumbered to `D591` / section 577, per the precedent §553 set for the S540
fork. Nothing else in the section moved: the same commit, the same file, the same measurement.

## 574. D579 · the four refusals only one lane read are read by both now, and a one-character cue inside a longer word is not a refusal (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/understand.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_one_character_refusal_inside_a_longer_word_is_not_a_refusal.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_refusal_is_read_once_by_both_lanes.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_eat_less_refusal_puts_the_verb_after_the_cue.py`)

**What was measured, on the product's own reader.** Four refusals a Hong Kong user types -
不吃, 別, 避免, 少 - were in the constraint table and absent from the polarity table, so one
sentence answered the two lanes differently. Through `extract_intent` on the shipped code,
"海鲜 避免" wrote `constraints: [diet_avoid:seafood]` and `preferences: [cuisine seafood,
polarity +1]` in the same breath: the search plan removed the seafood merchants and the ranking
lane was told to boost them. 不吃辣, 別推薦辣味 and 少食辣 measured the same shape, and the
eat-less sentence PLAN named - "海鲜 少吃" - was the same defect again. The split was armed, not
discovered: PLAN's open AI-lane item named these four words, and D539's door carried them as
`NEGATIONS_THE_POLARITY_LANE_LACKS` with the instruction to file the next unit.

**The fix is one vocabulary, and the other half is a boundary.** `_CONSTRAINT_NEGATIONS` is now
`dict.fromkeys(NEGATION_CUES)` - the private four left the constraint table and joined the
polarity list, so no lane can be taught a word the other does not read (D493's argument, applied
in the direction it was written for). Adding those four words alone would have imported a new
defect, because 別 and 少 are ONE character and are the tail of other words the user means:
特別 ("especially"), 最少, 多少. Measured with only the vocabulary half done, "特別辣的餐廳" wrote
`cuisine_avoid:spicy` - the product filtering out the thing the user asked for, the D522 shape
reached from the other side - while "特別安靜的餐廳" read +1. So belonging to a word is now decided
where belonging to a clause is decided: `NEGATION_COMPOUNDS` names, per one-character cue, the
characters that make it the second syllable of something else, and `negation_positions` is the
ONE locator both lanes ask, beside the existential-question skip D533 already made there.
`constraint_hits` and `polarity_for` both read through it, so a refusal the search filters for and
a dislike the ranking demotes are decided at the same positions in the same text.

**The doors, and what each holds.** The new boundary file (51 rows) walks every compound the
table declares and asserts each governs nothing in either lane, that 特別辣的餐廳 keeps its +1 and
writes no constraint, that the same cue STILL refuses when it is a word on its own (so a boundary
rule cannot quietly delete a refusal), and that every declared compound is a real pair around a
cue the table carries. D539's file lost its debt pin and gained three rows in its place: a
retired-debt negation must refuse AND disfavor, the two tables must hold one vocabulary in both
directions, and the one vocabulary must still reach every rule key. D543's eat-less file inverted
the row it had pinned as a measurement: the same sentence now asserts the polarity lane reads -1
where it once proved it read +1.

**Verified, not claimed.** The negation cluster (the two updated files) -> **2179 passed**; the new
boundary door -> **51 passed**; `ruff check nexus_ai tests` -> All checks passed; `mypy
nexus_ai/nlu` -> Success, 9 source files; the live-database subset (the contract, search,
preference, CJK-match and avoid-vocabulary integration files) -> **15 passed, 56 deselected**;
the full unit suite -> **10876 passed, 2 failed, 76 skipped** in 867.95 s, and both reds are
named - one is §575's own door, which the same session fixed (a test file that hand-wrote a
character D453's vocabulary gate does not carry), and one is the seed-preference door, which reads
only `data/seed` and is untouched by anything in this diff; PLAN's queue now names it. Behavioural
spot checks on the shipped reader, after the change: 避免海鮮 and 海鮮 避免 both write the refusal
and read seafood -1; 我唔食辣, 唔食辣, 少辣 and 別推薦辣味 all refuse; 最少辣, 多少辣, 人少一點的餐廳 and
特別安靜 write nothing; 有冇辣 stays a question at +1 (D533); 唔好太嘈 still inverts to quiet +1 (D570).

**Left open, named rather than left to be rediscovered.**

- The compound table is a hand-list for the two cues that needed it. A one-character refusal that
  joins `NEGATION_CUES` later gets no boundary guard until someone writes its pairs, and 冇, 無 and
  没 each have spellings that sit inside longer words too. Segmentation, not vocabulary.
- A bare 嘈 is in the quiet preference rule's own token list, so "嘈的餐廳" (a noisy restaurant)
  reads `ambience/quiet +1` - the like of the opposite is filed as the next polarity unit, and it
  is the mirror half of D570's inversion, which only turns a refusal of the opposite into a like.

- readers: no gate reads the two vocabularies against each other except the rows in D539's file,
  which now judge both directions and are green; no 18-step gate was re-run here, because nothing
  in a change that lives entirely in `nlu` reaches the database-backed steps.

## 575. D580 · the interpreter that runs the AI suite could not start on the machine the project is developed on, and no gate could say so (`scripts/repair_ai_editable_path.py`, `Makefile`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_local_interpreter_can_read_its_editable_install.py`)

**What was measured.** `uv sync` writes `apps/ai/.venv/Lib/site-packages/_editable_impl_nexus_ai.pth`
holding the repository's own absolute path, and Python's site handling opens a `.pth` with the
interpreter's LOCALE encoding. On this machine the project directory name is not ASCII and the
locale is cp936, so the decode failed at startup:

    UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xae in position 7

and it failed for every route into the venv - `uv run pytest`, `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest`,
`uv run uvicorn` and `python -c "import nexus_ai"` all died before reading a line of code. So
`make unit`, `make test`, `make dev-ai` and `make ai-embed` were closed, and with them every door
in this repository, locally. `PYTHONUTF8=1` and `-X utf8` do not change the encoding site.py uses
for a `.pth`, so this was not a knob anyone could turn; CI runs on Linux, where the locale is
UTF-8, so no CI job could see the machine being broken either. D515 recorded the hazard in
`docs/ENVIRONMENT_REPORT.md` §8 and worked around it with `uv run --no-sync` in one recipe - which
holds only as long as nobody lets uv sync, and this session proved that: the plain `make unit` path
was broken anyway.

**The fix.** `scripts/repair_ai_editable_path.py` moves the bytes a `.pth` cannot carry: the paths
go into a UTF-8 side file that an importer module reads with an EXPLICIT encoding, and the `.pth`
becomes the ASCII `import` line site.py executes. It judges the interpreter's own locale encoding,
rewrites only a `.pth` that fails that decode, is idempotent, says nothing when the install is
already readable, and exits 0 on a tree with no venv - because the recipes now call it before
every AI command. It imports nothing from the project, so it runs under the only interpreter left
available while the venv is broken: the system one. `make unit`, `make test`, `make dev-ai` and
`make ai-embed` run it first, and the new `make ai-install` (uv sync, then the repair) is the
fresh-clone path, because a repair that runs before the install exists has nothing to fix.

**The door proves the byte rule on both platforms.** The new file (11 rows) drives the script over
a synthetic venv whose recorded path is non-ASCII. On Linux that path decodes under the locale and
the install is never broken, so the script gained `--locale-encoding`: the door names an encoding
that cannot read the path, and the row means the same thing on every platform - nothing in the
recipes passes it. The rows hold: the path moves and the `.pth` that is left imports a module that
exists; a repaired importer puts the package directory on a child interpreter's path (the claim
that was failing, proved by an import rather than by a file); a `.pth` the locale CAN read is left
byte-for-byte untouched; no venv is not an error; `--check` names the file and writes nothing; the
second run is a no-op; and the two facts about this interpreter - every `.pth` it will be handed
decodes under its own locale encoding, and `nexus_ai` resolves inside this tree, so the suite
certifies the code under review and not an installed copy.

**Verified, not claimed.** The new door -> **11 passed**; this machine's install repaired into the
same shape the script writes (side file, importer, ASCII `.pth`), then `.venv/Scripts/python.exe`
importing `nexus_ai` from `apps/ai/nexus_ai/__init__.py`; the full unit suite run through that
interpreter -> 10876 passed (§574 names the two reds); `ruff check` over `nexus_ai tests` and the
script -> All checks passed. The first attempt at this door put a literal 获 in the test file,
because the story is about this directory's name; D453's vocabulary gate reddened it, which is that
gate doing its job, and the fixture now uses characters the product's own vocabulary carries.

**Left open.** `apps/ai/uv.lock` is generated by `uv sync` and untracked, so two machines on this
tree can resolve different dependency sets and nothing compares them; whether the lock belongs in
git is a decision for the lane that owns the venv, and this unit did not make it.

## 576. D581 · A declared preference that names a merchant weakness had no reader — the seed writes the fact as a LIST and the preference plane read only booleans (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/service.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_weak_aspects_list_is_read_by_a_preference.py`)

**What was measured.** PLAN's open item said it in one line: "the `weak_aspects`
attribute is a LIST, not a boolean" — the matcher reads booleans, so a merchant that is weak
at something cannot be demoted by a preference naming that weakness. Measured on the plane the
service reads (470 published rows): 118 carry a non-empty `weak_aspects`, and the histogram is
taste 23, seating 22, ambience 21, mtr_distance 20, service 19, portion 18, **noise 15**,
waiting_time 15, cleanliness 12, value 10. Every branch of the preference matcher in
`apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/service.py` asked `attrs.get(<scalar>) is True/False`; no branch named
`weak_aspects`, so a declared preference of kind `weakness` reached the loop, found no branch,
left `match_fn` empty and contributed nothing — `personalization` was `None` for every merchant
in the result, whatever the profile said. The fact was in the corpus and the reader did not
exist, which is the D488 shape (two readers of one fact) with the second reader missing.

**The fix is one branch, and it reads the list as a SET.** The new arm (kind `weakness`, any
non-empty key) pulls the boolean out of the stored `{"value": ...}` envelope exactly the way the
weather and time arms do, and then answers `_sided(w, liked=not is_weak)` where `is_weak` is
membership of the key in the merchant's own `weak_aspects` — membership, not substring, so a
preference naming `noise` is silent about a merchant weak at `service`. A value of `false` emits
no signal rather than a reversed one: "weakness noise = false" is not a sentence this contract
has a meaning for, and inventing one would be the D527 inversion reached from the other side.

**Verified on the shipped reader, and proved to fail.** Over the live corpus's 470 rows fed
through `search()` with only the profile preference added — kind `weakness`, key `noise`, value
true, weight 0.8 — the 15 merchants whose list names `noise` score **0.200** and the other 455
score **0.800**; with the branch deleted the same run reports 3 FAILED in the new door. The door
itself is 3 rows: the source-level row (the reader must name the list, so the branch cannot be
deleted while the file still claims to support it), the demotion row (weak < strong on one
preference), and the membership row (a merchant weak at `service` must not be read as weak at
`noise`; a merchant weak at `noise` must score below it). `ruff check` over the two touched
files: All checks passed.

**Left open, named rather than left to be rediscovered.**

- The empty list is read as strength. 352 of the 470 published merchants carry no `weak_aspects`
  at all, and the branch answers them `liked=True` for any declared weakness — absence of the
  fact is being read as the fact's negation. The corpus does not distinguish "no weakness
  recorded" from "no weakness", so a merchant nobody has reviewed is promoted as if it were
  strong. A three-valued reading (`None` when the list is empty) would keep the ranking honest
  but changes what the plane scores for 75% of its rows; that is a product decision, filed here
  rather than made.
- Nothing PRODUCES a `weakness` preference yet. The arm is reachable only from a declared
  profile row (the test seeds one by hand); the NLU writes `noise_avoid:noise` as a constraint,
  not a weakness preference, so the sentence "唔好嘈" still does not reach this branch. The
  constraint plane's own reader is the next unit's question.
- `generate.py` writes `quiet_ambience` as `aspect_mean["noise"] >= 4.2` and `lively_ambience`
  as `< 3.0`, so the same aspect has three spellings on one row (`weak_aspects` membership, the
  two booleans) and this branch reads only the first. Measured: 188 quiet, 12 lively, 15 weak at
  noise. Which of the three a refusal should exclude is not settled by this unit.

- readers: `ruff check` clean; the door 3 passed; the branch-removed control 3 failed; no
  18-step gate was re-run, because nothing here reaches the database-backed steps except the
  probe above, which reads the live plane through the shipped `PostgresBackend`.

## 578. D582 · the query that asks for a value's opposite now points the value at -1 (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/polarity.py`, `apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_like_of_an_antonym_refuses_the_value.py`)

**What was measured.** 嘈 is a surface of the `ambience/quiet` row's own token list, so a
sentence that asked for the noise inherited the row's +1: on the served plane `quiet_ambience`
is true on 188 of 470 published merchants and false on 282 (0 lack the attribute), and the
ranker scored the quiet half 1.0 against the loud half 0.0 for a user who had asked for the
loud one. D570 wrote the refusal of the opposite ("唔好嘈" wants quiet); this writes the want,
which cannot be a sign flip because the same character carries four readings. Measured through
`extract_intent` on the shipped reader, after the change: 嘈的餐廳 → `quiet -1`;
特別嘈的餐廳 → `-1`; 太嘈 / 好嘈 / 有冇嘈 → `+1`; 唔好嘈 → `+1` (and the refusal
`noise_avoid:noise` beside it); 安靜的餐廳 → `+1`.

**The frame is the sentence, not a marker table.** `is_asked_for` reads a bridge verb
(想 / 要 / 食 / want / like ...) in the surface's own clause before it and the attributive
particle (的 / 嘅) in its own clause after it; `antonym_direction` composes that with the cue
reader, so a refusal inverts, a question (D533) and a frameless complaint keep the row's own
polarity, and only a framed want turns the value to -1. `polarity_for` is untouched - the pure
cue reader still answers what the sentence does to the surface, which its own tests pin.

**Verified, and proved to fail.** The door is 47 rows generated from `ANTONYM_TERMS` itself
(a second antonym pair joins every walk the moment it exists), and it passes; with the
`antonym_direction` call replaced by D570's `-1 → +1` rule alone, 6 of those rows fail. The
50-row run of this door with D581's is green.

**Left open.** The bare 嘈 inside a longer surface ("二手煙" is 煙's sibling shape, D535's item)
is still read at the shorter surface's own reach; no preference rule names 煙 today, so the
residue is unreachable rather than measured. And 嘈死 / 咁嘈 stay at +1 by design - they are
complaints and requests in the same words, and this unit refused to guess.

- readers: the door 47 passed; the control 6 failed; `ruff check` clean over the two files.

## 581. D584 follow-up · three reds on the sweep were D584's own debt, and the third was real (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/nlu/lexicon.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_cuisine_the_user_can_ask_for_is_a_cuisine_they_can_refuse.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_degree_adverb_does_not_end_the_refusals_clause.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_the_constraint_lane_reads_the_clause.py`)

**What was measured, before touching anything.** The lane reads all 118 canon surfaces under
both cues and writes each value under exactly one key, so two of the three reds were
declarations and arithmetic rather than lost reads - and the third was real.

- 82 census rows raised `KeyError`: `KEY_OF` (the lane test's declaration of which lane each
  canon value is a fact in) never declared the 10 cuisines D584 folded into the canon.
  Declared now, by what the fact is: a refused cuisine filters the corpus's cuisine tags.
- The degree-adverb census walks the refusal vocabulary with a stride, and its floor clause
  reddened: 50 gap rows cannot cover a surface table that grew to 117 entries, so 67 surfaces
  had silently dropped out of the walk. The walk now runs as long as the longest of its three
  tables, which is what the clause claims.
- D584 derived its surfaces from `CUISINE_TERMS` and put every one of them in the cuisine row.
  生蠔 / 生蚝 / 海魚菜 / 大排档 / 大排檔 are that vocabulary's spellings of the seafood cuisine,
  and `seafood` has been a DIET fact since before this lane grew, so one fact was being
  refused under two keys - against D545's rule. It changes no filter, because D546 merges
  every key into one `avoid` list, which is exactly why nothing downstream noticed. A derived
  surface now goes to the row that already owns its value, and the door walks the whole table
  so the ninth cuisine cannot arrive with a value that belongs to another lane.

**Arms.** Routing everything to the cuisine row (D584's behaviour) 6 door + 5 lane red;
moving the default lane to `noise_avoid` reddens 77 lane rows while the door stays green - the
door grades the owned values, the census grades the rest; striking one declaration 15 red; the
stride put back 1 red. Every file was restored byte-identically.

- readers: both doors green in this session's sweep (4454 passed, 31 skipped); the commit
  reports 4,477 passed across the refusal lane, both census doors, the seed derivation, the
  live search contract, the vocabulary reference gate and the trust files.

## 582. D585 · a preference the platform let expire stops being read back (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/search/sql.py`, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_preference_the_platform_let_expire_is_not_read_back.py`)

**What was measured.** The write plane stamps the deadline - `IdentityRepository.upsertPreference`
computes `expires_at = now + ttlDays` on every insert - and the shipped types name the promise
("Inferred memory may expire; declared memory does not"). The AI lane's only read of the table
selected kind, key, value, weight, source and filtered on `user_id` alone: it never looked at
`expires_at`, so `service.py` turned an expired memory into a `pref_rule`, scored candidates
with it, and printed its `_preference_label` on the card as a reason the user had already taken
back. D522's shape: the reader not looking at the column the writer writes.

**This plane cannot show it**, because `quality.sql` records that all seven seeded preferences
expire 2026-12-21, so the gate runs the SHIPPED SQL against a values list that shadows the
table: same query, same placeholders, rows the plane does not have, nothing written. Red before
the predicate: the read returned the two expired rows alongside the two live ones, and the
style-filtered read leaked the expired style row too.

**Left open.** The predicate is the read's, so any future reader of the same table that copies
the six-column select re-inherits the defect; the gate pins the shipped read, not the shape.

- readers: the file's offline rows green in the sweep; its 4 live rows skipped without
  `NEXUS_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, and the commit's own red-before measurement is quoted above.

## 583. D585 follow-up · the seed census judged a rare attribute dead from a sample that could not see it (`apps/ai/tests/test_the_seed_derives_preferences_from_leaves_the_taxonomy_writes.py`)

0/60, 2/120, 6/240, 11/520 - about a 2% rate - so at 60 the census was one deterministic draw
away from reporting a live preference as inert.

shipped default (520 merchants, the corpus the product is served) and fails as "the sample is
too small to census" if someone puts a small scale back, rather than blaming the data. Proved
by arm: `--merchants 60` reproduces the red and names the sample, not the attribute.

- readers: the file green in this session's sweep; the arm above is the commit's own run.

## 584. D586 · a chunk is cited only from a document the pipeline called ready (`apps/ai/nexus_ai/rag/` retrieval read, `apps/ai/tests/test_a_chunk_is_cited_only_from_a_document_the_pipeline_called_ready.py`)

**What was measured.** `markForReindex` moves a rewritten merchant document to
`documents.status='pending'` and, as its own comment says, "does not touch `chunks`" - the
superseded text stays in the table for the whole rebuild window. The AI lane's retrieval joined
chunks to documents, selected `d.source_uri` for the citation and never mentioned `d.status`, so
an answer could quote a merchant's old menu or old opening hours with a `source_uri` pointing at
the document the merchant had already changed. Measured: with every document reported as
pending, the shipped read returned the same top-5 rows it returns today - the citation was
willing to name a document the pipeline had withdrawn.

**This plane cannot show it** (all 1,040 documents are 'indexed'), so the gate shadows only the
documents side of the join with a CTE built from the real table and one column overridden: same
query text, real chunks, nothing written. Arms: `d.status <> 'failed'` reddens the pending and
processing shadows while leaving the indexed census green, and dropping the predicate reddens
the column gate.

**Left open.** The refusal is `failed`-only, so a `pending` document's chunks are still
retrievable until the rebuild lands - the row now records that the citation names a READY
document, which is the narrower claim this unit could prove without inventing a visibility rule
the platform has not written.

- readers: 3 offline rows green in the sweep; 5 live rows skipped without
